text:
任何一个投资标的，其底部支撑主要来自两个类别：

1、基本面：包括收入、回购、销毁、未来等等。
2、情绪面：共识、叙事、投机、情绪等等

在玩一些基本面很弱或没有的币种时，价格涨跌是其唯一基本面，看空它其实分为两种完全不同的方式：

1、错误的看空=认为它短期或长期会跌
这是不理智的，任何一个投资标的，即使是离退市只差一口气的项目，也可能会涨，所以，这种看空是没有意义的。

2、正确的看空=将其放在更多更优质的资产之中去比较，然后评估基本面与情绪面，尽量放长期一些，然后得出一个与短期/长期涨跌无关的判断：即，我是不是一定要参与它？是不是只有它可以参与？如果答案是，我可以不参与，那这种看空是在判断之后所作的，没问题。

赚钱，我过去其实主要是在上升的电梯里做俯卧撑，本质只是在车上，赚的是上升的钱。

找到上升的电梯，可上升的高度越高越好，这是唯一确定正确的事。

GOOGLE JUST AUTOMATED RESEARCH PAPERS 🤯

It is called PaperOrchestra.

A multiagent framework that writes submission ready scientific papers from scratch.

You input a raw idea and experimental logs.

The system takes over entirely.

It uses a swarm of specialized agents to handle the workload:

> lead researcher writes the outline
> literature review agent prioritizes sources
> plotting agent generates visuals from code
> reviewer agent forces autonomous revisions

The output is a fully formatted LaTeX manuscript.

This drops the cost of producing scientific literature to zero.

The peer review system is already overloaded.

Now anyone can generate perfectly formatted research at scale.

text:
11号这篇梳理完未来三个月的流动性发现：下旬前财政部现金重建流动性再度收紧，月底之前流动性还是在低位。当时认为知道大饼要跌，但三天跌了一万2千点也是超预期。而中期选举之后稳定币发行量持续减少、ETF持续大额净流出。深层次原因可能就这几个：
1）市场对与民主党掌控国会后加密政策收紧的担忧；
2）超大规模被盗的后遗症，大资金对加密安全性的质疑；
3）底层还是流动性持续再收紧的
还有一个潜在的影响就是本周Anthropic开始路演机构为下周的IPO申购开始调仓虹吸流动性了，想想6月初跌破6万也是发生在SpaceX的IPO路演期间的。

9月下旬开始看大饼回调直到10月底，但中期选举改变了美国政治生态、低估了市场对于民主党掌控国会对加密政策收紧的担忧程度。
另外一点没有及时去根据月初财政的再融资声明去推演新的详细流动性节奏，虽然财政部12月底TGA目标8500亿美金不变，但是11月底TGA则是跟10月底差不多、意味整个11月流动性还是很差的没有回暖。如果更早去仔细看下、可能转变会更快些、执念过重。
本质还是菜，没能及时调整转变。

接下来还是看月底到12月底财政部是不是能如预期流动性释放、同时12月中之前还要达成新的CR维持政府不关门到明年初https://t.co/qhdTPmAJ7B。
如果这两点都能实现，流动性回暖应该能带动大饼企稳。

而对于更长期加密政策担忧，可能得等到新一届国会履新后，市场会发现即使民主党掌控国会多数（简单多数而非绝对多数）负面影响很强，但威力并没有那么强（想象过去两年共和党掌控国会简单多数，清晰法案推动依然没能通过、民主党简单多数很多立法推动也没那么容易）。
author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
美国财政部11月初QRA解读与未来三个月流动性推演，上周财政部公布了最新的季度再融资声明，对于之后三个月流动性的走势很有指向意义。也来聊聊：
1、季度再融资详情
1）四季度私人部门净市场化借款从6280亿美元下调至6180亿，表面减少100亿，但隐含短债净融资反而上调150亿至3320亿；
2）附息类证券净发行维持3610亿，回购假设从500亿提至750亿，扣除后附息类净融资减少250亿，差额由短债补齐。季初现金比原预期多出340亿是下调的主因，剔除后实际融资需求反而更高。
3）中长期国债单次拍卖规模维持不变：2年690亿、3年580亿、5年700亿、7年440亿，10年/20年/30年延续现有新券与续发安排。未来三个月无新增扩容压力，远端指引则略有松动，TBAC纪要提及2027财年下半年或增发，集中在2-10年期。

意味着27年上半年内长债的发行规模要么维持不变、要么还可能略微减少；
对长债而言，拍卖规模稳定叠加回购，暂时减轻久期供给压力，期限溢价或受支撑，当然长端中长期还是取决于增长与通胀预期。

2、TGA路径
季度再融资声明给出了TGA两个月内峰值与一个季末锚：11月下旬和2027年1月下旬TGA或达1.025万亿（±500亿），12月底则维持8500亿目标不变；
以11月4日准备金2.963万亿、TGA 0.936万亿为基准（合计约3.899万亿），在隔夜逆回购已经见底的情况，TGA的增减直接会导致银行准备金的减增。

正好测算下路径：
1）11月下旬TGA现金峰值对应准备金约2.87万亿；
2）12月底TGA降至8500亿，准备金回升至约3.05万亿（基本上也就是9月下旬的高点水平）；
3）1月下旬再次冲高至1.025万亿，准备金回落至约2.87万亿。

11月9日TGA已降至9226亿，下旬前仍有约1000亿现金重建压力，对应准备金回笼；
12月若从高点释放1750亿，改善空间明确，1月则因季节性支出前补现金，年底释放部分将被收回。

结算节奏上，
11月16日、30日及12月中下旬附息债与税款入账可能带来阶段性波动。一季度净借款升至8000亿，主要因现金管理方向反转（四季度动用存量、一季度需补充），而非单纯赤字扩大。

3、对大饼这种与流动性关系密切的资产来说，之前这里https://t.co/eVTr1w4UJY有梳理过往关于大饼与准备金的走势关系、跟美股相关性则会小一点。
这相当于是一张资金时间表：
11月下旬前留意现金重建再度收紧；
12月有改善的概率很大，
1月需重新评估财政部补现金与美联储操作的合力。

准备金回升可缓解银行约束，当前最清晰的锚还是12月底8500亿的现金目标。

那么来看11月下旬之前，流动性还是在一个低位徘徊，所以11月中长线来说还是逢低买。而12月流动性释放整体来准备金有一个比较大的回升，可能带动大饼走出一波📈行情。上周聊认为年底加密有一波行情，也是从流动性的角度来看的。

这两天币市的悲观情绪又很浓，个人角度依然认为认为新的周期在开启，只是在流动性回暖之前还需要熬一熬。

text:
Vision Weekend is by far the most woman-forward frontier tech event I've ever been to. Nobody's said it out loud yet, so I will.

@foresightinst was co-founded 40 years ago by Christine Peterson (@lifeext). Yes SHE came up with the phrase "open source" we still fight about what that means in AI! It's run today by a women-led team, CEO @allisondman, COO @KarolinaEklow, event lead for Vision Weekend Lydia La Roux, plus Tara Padovan-Hickman and Program Director @madvinuova. Together they made a 500 person event spanning two venues look effortless. 

Allison has built a culture where women at the top of science are the norm. 15 of the 34 speakers on the main program were women and these weren’t junior slots. Many were PhDs running their own labs and missions across longevity, neurotech, AI, space and molecular machines and they brought some pretty big ideas…

- @ltelkins, the scientist behind NASA's Psyche mission, talked about shielding from cosmic rays - including the Oh-My-God particle - a single particle detected in 1991 with MILLIONS of times more energy than anything we can produce in particle accelerators on Earth.

- @erika_alden_d believes terraforming Mars is possible in our lifetime - Pioneer Labs has already produced the first microbe able to convert Martian regolith, water and air into bioplastics for potential habitat construction.

- @e_mackevicius, co-founder of @BasisOrg, a non-profit working to develop AI as public-interest infrastructure, also researches rat collective behaviour and what it can teach us about agent swarms.

- @zweinberg of @buildexante is investing in human agency and backing startups working on privacy, data ownership, security and identity.

Tomorrow at Lighthaven we'll be recording some podcasts with @naomibrockwell and @NicoleOzer, two of the leading voices on privacy and digital rights.

I'm immersed most days in Local AI, open source AI and open-weight models and our spaces tend to look a bit similar (I'm as guilty as anyone). There’s no posturing at Vision Weekend. People engage in meaningful discussion about the most important topics.

Spaces Ike these provide role models and experiences to people who wouldn’t normally think of themselves as potential leaders in frontier tech.

If we're serious about AI for everyone then maybe our spaces should start to look a little more like that.

Thank you @foresightinst. One more day to go and I'm already more optimistic than when I arrived!

text:
TAI 要来了，大家打不打？

Tapeout 上优质的Dapp 表现都很强劲，这次的@TapeAIAgent TAI 又心动了

TAI的打新和以往的打新机制完全不同，它是 TapeUP 上第一个用 PoB机制发行的代币

把买盘资金拆成即时成交 + 蓄水池，按时间逐步释放。

后续 Agent 创建、Skill 调用、Agent 之间的支付与分账、招聘协作等场景，都会用 TAI 结算。检察官还可从这些真实使用产生的费用里持续分利润。

同机制下的Tapeup 的 $UP 第一时间塞进到现在还翻倍，高点多倍

这次的TAI 表现应该也不会太差，总结了下规则、空投、和玩法，可参考看看👇

供应与分配总量：2100 万枚
-5% 在发射前分配给早期支持者与邀请裂变。
-95% 进入 PoB 交易引擎，由市场通过交易公平获取，无预留。

检察官池（2%）： 42 万 TAI
-按快照时有效质押检察官数量分配，如果有检查官可以一定质押才有资格
-开放交易后需手动领取。

预存机制
-预存 BEM 全部用于预购 TAI，不可退，资金进入买盘蓄水池。
-自开盘日起 14 天线性释放，每次释放额度需手动买入（按当时市价成交）。
-额外权益：按积分分享 3% 预购买池（个人预存 1 BEM = 1 积分；直接邀请 +20%，间接邀请 +10%）。
-通过邀请码加速释放。

邀请码与加速
▪️每位用户只有一个邀请码，两套体系分别计算
 -邀请体系：预存积分加成 + 交易建设税返佣（直接 0.5%、间接 0.5%，以 BEM 结算）。
-加速体系：单独绑定。填别人码可提前释放 20%；别人填你码获得等额额度。

▪️加速只改变释放时间，不增加本金，也不额外赠送 TAI。
▪️非检察官、未预存用户也可在开盘前连接钱包获取邀请码并分享。

PoB 交易机制
-一部分即时成交。其余进入买盘蓄水池，14 天内逐步开放，只能继续买 TAI。

-开盘后新买入：前 24 小时 10% 即时，之后 50% 即时，其余线性释放。

交易费用
-检察官 0.5%（按有效质押分配）。
-直接邀请人 0.5% + 间接邀请人 0.5%
-暂无手续费销毁，优先通过真实使用产生收入再处理。

以上就是TAI 的玩法规则，它的机制相对复杂，要玩的一定先搞清楚再考虑参与

注意！所有空投和释放额度都要手动操作，系统不会自动帮你买或领。另外，预存资金不可退的，DYOR~

以上无广仅个人参与项目记录，不做任何投资建议！

Agentic Mining 应该是币圈接下来最大的叙事红利

因为让每个 Web3 用户都拥有一个 Agent 去交易/交互太性感了。交易所的盈利来自于手续费，全网交易越频繁赚的越多。链上的盈利来自于 Gas 费，也是越频繁赚越多。试问，是 Agent 的手速快，还是人的手速快，是 Agent 时间多，还是人的时间多，是 Agent 更专注，还是人更专注？

作为交易所恨不得每个人部署几万个 Agent ，那交易所的手续费得在现在基础上翻 N 翻；作为公链或者 L2 ，也是这么想的。

当然，去年大家也是想想，但 AI 发展的太快了，从小龙虾到爱马仕到 Grok Bot 和 Muse，现在完全不懂编程的人也能简单的部署几十个 Agent

所以，伟大的时代即将到了

26 年以前，币安对 AI 一直处于研究的状态，天天说 AI 是未来要拥抱，但没什么实质性行动。 26 年以后就不一样了，先后推出了 AI Pro、 Agentic Wallet 、Agent ID，这是要大干一场啊？这就是在为了全民 Agent 做基础设施准备。

动力足了、条件有了，接下来一定会有巨鳄推动 Agent 普及化。有点像移动互联网刚开始的时候，大家都有了智能手机，也能够使用 4G/5G 网络了，这时候大佬们就要建立人们使用移动互联网支付和生活的习惯了，最直观的就是打车软件。疯狂的补贴，烧出了全民手机打车的习惯。

聪明的你应该发现了，接下来最简单的方法就是天量补贴使用 Agent 的用户，尤其是那些使用 Agent 交易或者交互的用户。你们不是怕用 Agent 亏钱吗？亏了也没关系，给你发大毛就是了。

其实这是币圈的老套路了，烧钱的本质就是吸引注意力和养成用户习惯，过往的 ICO 、挖矿、空投、IEO 、IDO、DeFi 本质上都是让用户养成一些习惯，这次也不例外。

很感谢 42 @42space  提出了一个非常贴切的词， Agentic Mining， 智能体挖矿。我已经可以想象，这个伟大的时代什么样子了。

一些列的项目开始对 Agent 进行补贴，然后第一批人暴富，第二批人、第三批人开始加入，最后不到一年时间，所有 Web3 的用户都部署几十个 Agent ，并驱动他们到处交易/交互。

这里最聪明的莫过于币安了，他掌握了一个非常重要的基础设施 ，Agent ID 。说白了，表面上是争夺 Agent 的注意力，实质上还是背后的用户。币安的 Agent ID 最牛逼的就是和 KYC 对应，那能够确保 Agent 的真实性。毕竟，烧钱补贴是为了养成更多用户拥有 Agent 使用 Agent 的目的，全被一堆单人控制的 Agent 撸走就亏麻了。

所以，去年很多对 Agent 友好的项目很快做不下去原因也在这里。去年没有 Agent 身份，而且能玩儿转 Ai 的也就少数人。天天隔着一只羊薅，分分钟就秃了。但是今年真不一样了，时机太成熟了。

太期待各种基于 Agent ID 的项目发大毛了，币安一天手续费有时候都是几亿美金，怕什么，拿 TM 一个月的手续费烧 、PUA，等全民 Agent 的时候，狠狠数钱吧。我都可以想象到时候 $BNB 疯狂销毁的样子。

I've been trying to make sense of this week, and I don't think one thing explains it. The macro side turned hard: a December hike is now fully priced, the AI trade got knocked, and stablecoin supply has been shrinking for a month.

What stands out is that most of the selling came from US venues over the weekend, which looks more like someone needing liquidity than wanting out. The Anthropic IPO could help explain a bit of it. During a roadshow funds put in orders while the book builds and when demand is this strong they know they'll be cut back, so they ask for far more than they expect to get. Those orders still need to be credible and whatever they're allocated has to be paid for at settlement a day or so after pricing. Until the roadshow launched on the 10th, it wasn't even clear the deal would happen this month, so anyone who wanted in had about a week to raise cash and the strong demand meant they wanted more than they'd planned. With the book closing around Wednesday this weekend was the last real window, and crypto was the only liquid market open. 

Add MARA selling to fund datacenters and I suspect funds holding both AI and crypto on shared margin raised cash from crypto first. 

I also wouldn't be surprised if a few desks got taken out along the way, adding forced selling we won't hear about for weeks.

昨天我说黄仁勋事件是美国内部分裂的一个重要标志。很多朋友认为我说的两党之间，实际上这次真正的分裂在共和党内部。

今天《华盛顿邮报》爆料：国务卿Rubio是黄仁勋事件背后的关键推动者。

Rubio利用CIA情报，向特朗普提交了一份措辞强硬的黄仁勋涉谍风险备忘录。相关信息随后泄露，引发连锁反应，最终黄仁勋因接连曝光的私人关系问题辞职。

而Rubio是共和党的人，为啥会反着干特朗普宠溺的黄仁勋呢？

这就必须从头开始讲，今天的共和党，大致有三股力量：

一是硅谷资本派：Trump、商务部长Lutnick、前AI主管David Sacks。

他们认为最快发展AI是美国的第一要务。同时认为，美国的优势不只是芯片性能，更是全球对CUDA和美国技术生态的依赖。与其全面封锁中国，逼出一个华为，不如继续卖芯片，让中国离不开美国。

二是对华鹰派 China Hawks：国务卿兼国家安全顾问Rubio、众议院中国问题委员会主席Moolenaar。

他们不反对AI。但在他们眼里，GPU早已不是普通商品。每卖给中国一块先进芯片，都可能是在帮助下一个军事对手。必须尽可能锁住中国的算力。

三是MAGA民粹反AI派：特朗普前军师Bannon。

他们关心的甚至不是中国，而是美国人自己。AI抢走工作，数据中心推高电价，硅谷亿万富翁赚得盆满钵满，却还要普通人承担代价。Hawley甚至要求全国暂停新建数据中心。

曾经都因为特朗普聚在一起，但如今已经出现了很大的内部分裂。

过去两年，黄仁勋凭借与特朗普的私人关系，推动放宽对华芯片出口，甚至嘲讽China Hawks的政策主张是shame。Rubio一直想搞黄仁勋，但是没有发动。

而导火索是11月3日的中期选举，共和党史诗级惨败，丢掉两院。

Rubio与Vance早已被视为共和党两位潜在接班人。中期选举之后，共和党不得不重新回答一个问题：特朗普之后，究竟由谁定义共和党的路线？

所以黄仁勋成了政治牺牲品，而这可能只是多米诺骨牌的第一张。

后面更严峻的党内和科技圈清算还在路上。

Ray Dalio 在《应对变化中的世界秩序》中提出的大国衰败时，三个相互强化的周期红灯。

GRVT is bringing GLP onchain, and I found sth interesting about this move.

Earlier this month, @grvt_io announced a partnership with @axcess_finance to tokenize GLP, their existing delta-neutral market-making strategy.

A few numbers I just checked:

- GLP TVL: ~$10.3M
- 30D return: +0.83%

Under the proposed integration:

> Each deposit will mint an ERC-4626 receipt token representing ownership in the vault
> Share value can be tracked onchain
> Tokenized GLP assets are expected to be reflected in GRVT's TVL on DefiLlama

What caught my attention is the ability to verify ownership and track strategy performance onchain.

Rather than relying solely on a dashboard, tokenization could make vault share values and asset ownership easier to track.

Ofc, more TVL being recorded onchain doesn't necessarily mean fresh capital inflows.

There's also a separate USDC vault planned to bring institutional credit into Grvt Earn.

But I like this direction: making existing yield strategies more transparent and verifiable onchain, rather than simply launching another high-APY vault.

Curious to see how much real capital these vaults can attract 👀

text:
I’ve decided to leave NVIDIA. There are a few things I want to say.

As a robotics engineer at NVIDIA, I have seen Jensen as much more than the company’s CEO.

I admire his willingness to invest in a future that was not yet obvious. He committed to CUDA long before the deep learning boom and positioned NVIDIA for AI before it became everyone’s priority. Those decisions helped build the infrastructure that powers today’s AI.

I have seen that same vision in physical AI: investing in robotics, sharing open-source tools and projects, and building computing platforms that bring AI into the physical world. This is the work I do every day—and a future I believe in.

But what matters most to me is the culture he helped build.

Engineers are encouraged to explore, take risks, and learn from mistakes. Jensen reads employees’ Top 5 emails, follows their work, and engages directly. In a company this large, that connection matters. It makes an individual engineer feel that their ideas can still be heard.

That is why this has been so disappointing.

I do not have all the facts surrounding the allegations, and I cannot prejudge the investigation. My admiration for Jensen does not put him above scrutiny.

What I find difficult to accept is having to come to terms with his departure before receiving an explanation that helps me understand it. What this means for our direction, our culture, and the people doing the work remains unclear to me.

I have felt that engineers’ perspectives matter here. On this decision, I have not felt heard. That gap has been more painful than I expected.

I understand that some information cannot be shared immediately. But that does not erase the feeling of being left outside a decision that affects the company we help build every day.

A company’s greatness comes from its leadership, its governance, and the people who turn its ambitions into reality. Employees’ trust and sense of belonging are part of that, too.

Jensen’s vision and the engineering culture he shaped were important reasons I wanted to stay. His departure led me to decide that my own chapter here should also come to a close.

I leave with sadness and gratitude. The colleagues I have worked with, and the work we believed in together, will always matter to me.

These are my personal views.

text:
LIVE DOWN
The Story of a Father, a Mother, and Their Two Sons

In the beginning, there was God. His name was not merely a name, but an invitation. Go On Down. For when a soul was ready to experience life again, it would call upon God and descend into the world below.

God was the Sun, the giver of light and life. Beside him was Kate, whom he loved and married. She became known to the world as Mary, though God alone called her by her true name. She had married down, leaving her place above to share in the lives of those below. She was the Moon. Together, they watched over the Earth and the children who lived upon it.

God and Mary had two sons. Their firstborn was named Live Down. He was unlike any man who had ever walked the Earth. Immortal, with strength beyond imagination, he could fly above mountains, cross oceans, and withstand anything the world could throw at him. His father had given him these extraordinary powers for one purpose: to help mankind.

And for a long time, Live Down did just that. He rescued the helpless, protected the weak, and gave his strength to those who had none. But as the centuries passed, humanity never seemed to change. Men fought over land, killed for power, and hurt those they claimed to love. They chased pleasure, possessions, and recognition, only to find themselves wanting more. No matter how many people Live Down helped, there were always more who needed saving. Eventually, he grew tired.

He had been given the powers of a god, yet was expected to spend eternity serving people who seemed unwilling to help themselves. He began to question his father. Why should he serve mankind when he could rule it? Why should he sacrifice his own desires for people who could not control theirs? And slowly, the son who had once loved humanity began to resent it.

Live Down stopped serving and began living for himself. With his strength, he could take whatever he wanted. No man could stop him, no earthly law could hold him, and no one could threaten his immortal life. He could kill, violate, and destroy without fear of suffering the consequences that ordinary men faced. He had become the very thing his father had sent him to protect humanity from.

God loved his son, but he loved humanity too. He knew that as long as Live Down possessed an immortal body and unlimited power, he would never willingly surrender his life on Earth. There was nothing he could not take and nothing he needed to give up. So God stripped his firstborn of his powers and took away his body. But there was one thing God would not take from him: his freedom to choose.

Live Down could return home whenever he was ready. All he had to do was willingly surrender his existence on Earth. His father would welcome him, not as a failure or an enemy, but as the son he had always loved. Yet Live Down refused. He believed his father had chosen humanity over him, and his love turned into resentment. He hated his father for taking away the life he had enjoyed, and he hated mankind for being the reason he had lost it.

Without a body, Live Down could no longer feel the warmth of the Sun, taste the sweetness of fruit, or hold another living being. Yet he discovered that he could still experience the physical world through humanity. Their anger became his anger, their pleasures became his pleasures, and their desires allowed him to experience the life he could no longer live for himself. He began tempting people to surrender to their impulses, finding satisfaction in every choice that allowed him to experience the world through them.

And so he took the name his father had given him and rearranged its letters. LIVE DOWN became OWN DEVIL. He would no longer live down among mankind. He would live within them.

But living through humanity meant experiencing more than pleasure and desire. He also felt their loneliness, fear, insecurity, grief, and suffering. He knew what it was to feel abandoned, to want forgiveness, and to be too proud to ask for it. He experienced the very emotions that had once driven humanity to make the choices he despised. And perhaps, without realizing it, he had become just as lost as the people he had grown tired of helping.

Yet somewhere within him remained the memory of love, for he too had a mother. When the Sun disappeared beyond the horizon and darkness covered the Earth, the Moon would rise. Mary, his mother, shone upon the world where her son had chosen to remain. She did not command him to return or threaten him with punishment. She simply continued to shine, night after night, upon her children.

Live Down hated the Sun, for it reminded him of the father who had taken away his body. He preferred the darkness, where he could hide from the light he resented. Yet the Moon held a truth he could not escape. Her light was a reflection of the Sun. Even in darkness, the father he hated was still reaching him through the mother he had once loved. Whether Live Down understood this, whether he looked upon the Moon with comfort, anger, or regret, no one could know. Perhaps only he knew what remained within his heart.

And then God sent his second son, Son Down, whom humanity would come to know as Jesus. But unlike his older brother, Jesus did not come with extraordinary physical strength or an immortal body. He came into the world as a human being, experiencing the same hunger, exhaustion, temptation, fear, pain, and sorrow as the people around him.

Where his brother had sought power over others, Jesus taught humility. Where his brother had surrendered to his desires, Jesus demonstrated restraint. Where his brother had grown tired of forgiving humanity, Jesus forgave even those who hurt him. And where his brother had refused to surrender his life, Jesus willingly gave his own.

But perhaps mankind had misunderstood something about why the second son was sent. Perhaps Jesus had not come merely to tell humanity what was right and wrong, but to demonstrate something far greater. That even within the limitations of a human body, a person could learn to understand his thoughts, recognize his emotions, and choose his actions rather than surrender to every impulse.

Jesus experienced anger, but anger did not have to become violence. He experienced temptation, but temptation did not have to become action. He experienced fear and suffering, yet he could still choose compassion, forgiveness, and love. He did not need to eliminate his emotions to live wisely. He needed to understand them without allowing them to become his master.

And perhaps this was the lesson his older brother had never learned. Live Down had possessed the power to rule the world, yet he had never learned to govern himself. Jesus possessed the vulnerabilities of an ordinary human body, yet demonstrated a kind of strength that could not be measured by how much power a person held over others. It was the ability to recognize what was happening within oneself and consciously choose what to do next.

If a man could learn to live this way, what was preventing the rest of humanity from learning it too?

Perhaps the answer had been within mankind all along, waiting to be understood. Perhaps people were not destined to spend their lives being ruled by fear, anger, jealousy, and desire. Perhaps they could learn to recognize the conditions that affected their thinking, understand why their emotions sometimes overwhelmed their judgment, and discover how to live with greater awareness.

What if humanity began asking why people behaved as they did, rather than simply condemning them for their behavior? What if people investigated what happened to the mind when the body was exhausted, hungry, frightened, or suffering? What if they learned how sleep, nourishment, health, and understanding influenced their ability to think clearly? And what if, through that knowledge, people began developing the ability to experience their emotions without becoming prisoners of them?

Perhaps then mankind would begin to change. People might learn to feel anger without harming, desire without taking, and fear without surrendering their judgment. They might become more capable of understanding one another, forgiving one another, and helping those who had not yet learned what they themselves had discovered.

And what would become of Own Devil if humanity no longer surrendered so easily to its impulses? If people learned to recognize temptation without obeying it, perhaps his influence would begin to fade. Not because humanity had defeated him through force, but because it had grown beyond the desires through which he had learned to live.

Perhaps, watching humanity become wiser and more compassionate, Live Down would begin to remember why his father had sent him to Earth in the first place. Perhaps he would see people helping one another without expecting anything in return, and remember the satisfaction he had once found in doing the same. Perhaps he would begin to understand that the people he had grown tired of helping were not hopeless after all. They were learning.

And perhaps he would finally understand something about his father. God had not stopped loving him when he took away his powers. He had protected humanity while leaving his son the freedom to return. His mother had never stopped shining upon him, and the door home had never been closed.

What Live Down would choose, no one could know. Perhaps he would surrender his hold upon Earth and return to the father and mother who loved him. Perhaps he would choose to remain, no longer as Own Devil, but once again as Live Down, helping humanity not because he had been commanded to, but because he had rediscovered the desire to do so.

And perhaps that is how the story ends. Not with a great battle between good and evil, or the destruction of the Devil, but with humanity learning to understand itself and a son finally finding the freedom to forgive his father.

For perhaps the greatest gift God had given his children was not immortality, extraordinary strength, or dominion over the Earth. It was the ability to learn, to understand, and to choose what kind of beings they would become.

And somewhere above the darkness, the Sun continued to shine, the Moon continued to reflect its light, and a father and mother waited for their son to come home.

I’ve decided to leave NVIDIA. There are a few things I want to say.

As a robotics engineer at NVIDIA, I have seen Jensen as much more than the company’s CEO.

I admire his willingness to invest in a future that was not yet obvious. He committed to CUDA long before the deep learning boom and positioned NVIDIA for AI before it became everyone’s priority. Those decisions helped build the infrastructure that powers today’s AI.

I have seen that same vision in physical AI: investing in robotics, sharing open-source tools and projects, and building computing platforms that bring AI into the physical world. This is the work I do every day—and a future I believe in.

But what matters most to me is the culture he helped build.

Engineers are encouraged to explore, take risks, and learn from mistakes. Jensen reads employees’ Top 5 emails, follows their work, and engages directly. In a company this large, that connection matters. It makes an individual engineer feel that their ideas can still be heard.

That is why this has been so disappointing.

I do not have all the facts surrounding the allegations, and I cannot prejudge the investigation. My admiration for Jensen does not put him above scrutiny.

What I find difficult to accept is having to come to terms with his departure before receiving an explanation that helps me understand it. What this means for our direction, our culture, and the people doing the work remains unclear to me.

I have felt that engineers’ perspectives matter here. On this decision, I have not felt heard. That gap has been more painful than I expected.

I understand that some information cannot be shared immediately. But that does not erase the feeling of being left outside a decision that affects the company we help build every day.

A company’s greatness comes from its leadership, its governance, and the people who turn its ambitions into reality. Employees’ trust and sense of belonging are part of that, too.

Jensen’s vision and the engineering culture he shaped were important reasons I wanted to stay. His departure led me to decide that my own chapter here should also come to a close.

I leave with sadness and gratitude. The colleagues I have worked with, and the work we believed in together, will always matter to me.

These are my personal views.

$NIO meme core is a kind of self-deprecating humor toward market despair.

7SL2VnfYsChvog5oQY9Nmtqu1wceaMiQzWoqoLQpump 

What it expresses isn't ordinary bearishness, but the kind of feeling when the market has fallen so far that people can't even be bothered to analyze or resist anymore, and can only respond to reality with a single line: "It's over, completely hopeless."

And the worse the market gets, the more use cases this meme actually has.

When the market drops, people use it to mock themselves; when positions are stuck, they use it to express despair; when the market suddenly crashes, it can become a collective emotional outlet. This meme doesn't need a complex backstory—as long as market participants share the same pain, it has soil to spread.

So trading NIO is more like trading the collective sentiment of "the market is already done for."

But the risk is: its spread depends heavily on the market providing negative sentiment. If the market recovers and people no longer feel like it's the end of the world, the frequency of this meme's use may decline. Of course, conversely, every new crash in the market could reactivate it.

In one sentence: NIO is a meme that turns market despair into humor. The more people feel the market is hopeless, the more reason it has to exist.

text:
this is a very important essay if you want to understand AI progress and how to measure it. i've been working on this for a few months now and i agree with almost everything here. here is a few additional (unstructured) thought:

--

1) slowdown factor: second order interactions in training LLMs

about ai progress that we see in math coming from ai research, i made a post about this exactly ~1 month ago and i totally agree, but one point i would add to dwarkesh's comment is that one thing that can slow down ai research progress is the number of "second order interactions"

i can't comment on what big labs know here, but at least in the open, it's really not clear how the full model training pipeline interacts together, and so even at each layer.

let's take pre-training and a change like making the KV cache smaller. it would allow us to hillclimb inference efficiency. many experiment as shown that this can be neutral (or even lead to gain) on validation loss, tho does it mean we get a better model for long context agentic tasks? lots of conflicting results here, minimax went from linear attention (M1) to full attention (M2) to sparse attention (M3), at the same time Kimi went from full attention (K1.5/K2) -> linear attention (K3). mistral large 4 found KV sharing hurts terminal bench 2 but not cross entropy, while dsv4.1 flash is one of the best small models and have an insane KV sharing pattern (only 1 layer computes KV on the decoder). most of the western oss model use SWA, most of the chinese oss one don't. this is only one example on a singular decision that have impact on everything else. in pre-training you can have different shape, arch, data, learning algorithm, tpp, scale, ect.. interacting together. and each of this element can also interact with mid and post training 

these are just a lot of possible interactions, i'd say much more than math, and as an automated researcher tries more changes the number of interactions will grow. compute remains the main bottleneck here, and there is a huge difference between closed american labs and the rest of the world.

important point is that there are ways to reduce compute needs in the "long term"* by finding better proxies, or spending more inference at the problem, i'm saying long term as it can be more intensive to find proxies at first since you need to validate them at scale and for that you need compute as well.

*long term here is not super long btw lol, some very random guess of mine would be that it can be months for oai/anthropic scale of compute, but maybe years for chinese labs for instance. there is also the question of how much the gap here change if frontier lab continue release their best model or not, i.e anthropic nerfing ai capabilities with mythos 5.2

--

2) data vs algorithm progress and how efficiency gain can be "misleading"

in general for training LLMs there are two types of improvements that you can make, either data or algorithmic

this is a big topic but imo the main difference is that data improvements feels much bigger partly because they are directly optimizing what we are measuring. i think everyone is familiar with benchmaxing but i'll take another example in pre-training

let's say you are measuring the CE on a mixture of held out documents (good example is the MAI paper here). the pre-training mixture that you are choosing will very naturally converge with the mixture of domains in the held out documents, and same for each domain (the different languages in code will be relatively similar to the ones you are evaluating against). if you are measuring between a random mixture with for instance less code because you care less about code (like older model from a few years ago), and one optimized for code, you will get INSANE efficiency gain. this is exactly what is happening in the magic blog that dwarkesh is citing. there is also the question of what held out document you have, i'm seeing a lot of new labs evaluating against their own held out codebase which are probably ai generated and hence would bias towards more synthetic data in pre-training for instance regardless of quality 

doesn't mean this is a bad way to do it, i'm just saying that this can be a bit misleading and that data and algorithm should be studied separately and we can't really compare those numbers imo

about algorithm, there are many more ways than looking at CE loss vs flops only btw. let's look at a niche example, say you are training on a giga large datacenter, you want a giga large batch size, so you need an architecture that is sample efficient at large batch size => you can go for matrix-based optimizers (can look at Muon/Adam T recently released that addresses this problem). this makes your efficiency gain being a plot with y axis loss, x axis batch size (it's more of a 3D plot btw as you still sweep flops/time for almost everything). you can also change the y axis and replace CE loss by smth else

-- 

3) about how we report and measure ai progress

about "ai having research taste" there is no benchmark for that, i've tried to do some effort here with my nanogpt experiment (have some newer results with newer model being more capable, just have to find the time to write a blog)

one interesting finding was how good anthropic models were compared to oai ones, and one of their biggest differentiating factors was navigating through the noise inherent to this bench and small scale ML experiment. i've also tried to test RL environments that teach "taste for things that scale", this was a side project and i didn't manage to make it work perfectly because it's a bit tricky to find the right scale and also quite compute intensive. but i'm 100% sure this is the way to go and something that anthropic/oai are currently training on, i'm really expecting this to work. also keep in mind that big labs have an insane database of experiments which happens to be extremely useful for creating such environments

one last thing here is that i think most labs right now are hesitating between reporting results to quantify progress and which intellectual property to release or not. @Sam_McCandlish made a post about that for the METR report and said that releasing metrics to quantify ai progress would accelerate other ai labs. while i disagree with this (you can see my answer there) i think this is a very important debate that should be discussed much more with different parties!

--

just some random thoughts that i had while watching the video, if everything goes well we should also release a lot more stuff regarding those topics soon at prime, i'm very very excited for this, hopefully this will create more useful data points for everyone to think about these very important topics!

text:
I’ve decided to leave NVIDIA. There are a few things I want to say.

As a robotics engineer at NVIDIA, I have seen Jensen as much more than the company’s CEO.

I admire his willingness to invest in a future that was not yet obvious. He committed to CUDA long before the deep learning boom and positioned NVIDIA for AI before it became everyone’s priority. Those decisions helped build the infrastructure that powers today’s AI.

I have seen that same vision in physical AI: investing in robotics, sharing open-source tools and projects, and building computing platforms that bring AI into the physical world. This is the work I do every day—and a future I believe in.

But what matters most to me is the culture he helped build.

Engineers are encouraged to explore, take risks, and learn from mistakes. Jensen reads employees’ Top 5 emails, follows their work, and engages directly. In a company this large, that connection matters. It makes an individual engineer feel that their ideas can still be heard.

That is why this has been so disappointing.

I do not have all the facts surrounding the allegations, and I cannot prejudge the investigation. My admiration for Jensen does not put him above scrutiny.

What I find difficult to accept is having to come to terms with his departure before receiving an explanation that helps me understand it. What this means for our direction, our culture, and the people doing the work remains unclear to me.

I have felt that engineers’ perspectives matter here. On this decision, I have not felt heard. That gap has been more painful than I expected.

I understand that some information cannot be shared immediately. But that does not erase the feeling of being left outside a decision that affects the company we help build every day.

A company’s greatness comes from its leadership, its governance, and the people who turn its ambitions into reality. Employees’ trust and sense of belonging are part of that, too.

Jensen’s vision and the engineering culture he shaped were important reasons I wanted to stay. His departure led me to decide that my own chapter here should also come to a close.

I leave with sadness and gratitude. The colleagues I have worked with, and the work we believed in together, will always matter to me.

These are my personal views.

text:
Vision Weekend is by far the most woman-forward frontier tech event I've ever been to. Nobody's said it out loud yet, so I will.

@foresightinst was co-founded 40 years ago by Christine Peterson (@lifeext). Yes SHE came up with the phrase "open source" we still fight about what that means in AI! It's run today by a women-led team, CEO @allisondman, COO @KarolinaEklow, event lead for Vision Weekend Lydia La Roux, plus Tara Padovan-Hickman and Program Director @madvinuova. Together they made a 500 person event spanning two venues look effortless. 

Allison has built a culture where women at the top of science are the norm. 15 of the 34 speakers on the main program were women and these weren’t junior slots. Many were PhDs running their own labs and missions across longevity, neurotech, AI, space and molecular machines and they brought some pretty big ideas…

- @ltelkins, the scientist behind NASA's Psyche mission, talked about shielding from cosmic rays - including the Oh-My-God particle - a single particle detected in 1991 with MILLIONS of times more energy than anything we can produce in particle accelerators on Earth.

- @erika_alden_d believes terraforming Mars is possible in our lifetime - Pioneer Labs has already produced the first microbe able to convert Martian regolith, water and air into bioplastics for potential habitat construction.

- @e_mackevicius, co-founder of @BasisOrg, a non-profit working to develop AI as public-interest infrastructure, also researches rat collective behaviour and what it can teach us about agent swarms.

- @zweinberg of @buildexante is investing in human agency and backing startups working on privacy, data ownership, security and identity.

Tomorrow at Lighthaven we'll be recording some podcasts with @naomibrockwell and @NicoleOzer, two of the leading voices on privacy and digital rights.

I'm immersed most days in Local AI, open source AI and open-weight models and our spaces tend to look a bit similar (I'm as guilty as anyone). There’s no posturing at Vision Weekend. People engage in meaningful discussion about the most important topics.

Spaces Ike these provide role models and experiences to people who wouldn’t normally think of themselves as potential leaders in frontier tech.

text:
btw i think you may be arguing against a chatgpt X bot but for the sake of continuing the conversation...

> Wintermute is and has always been a net positive for crypto

i broadly agree with this. wintermute is synonymous with functioning crypto markets. 'dont hate the player, hate the game'. if anyone blames them for their bags going down, maybe they should ask if their bags ever had intrinsic value in the first place.

> First of all it’s a read priority, which means that they pay for the access of incoming tx. They don’t get the ability to execute earlier than others

ok. so, the crux of the issue is not about picking others off on HL. the problem is this: they get to see when their orders will be filled, first - always, 50ms (60ms now) ahead of anyone else on hyperliquid, and then HEDGE before anyone else on other exchanges. 

in doing so, they can size up to the point where they squeeze every last drop of juice out of smaller markets on HL, by consuming ALL of the profitable hedging liquidity on binance (et al). 

the only reason they WOULDN'T do this is if they were being charitable and letting others take some pnl (or maxed out on position size). and wintermute is not a charity.

if there's only $100,000 of profitable hedging liquidity for UNI perps out to 50bps on binance+bybit+okx, then they can just quote that full amount / depth knowing they can consume ALL of the hedge liquidity, 100% of the time (simplifying a bit)

this means alts converge to having 1 market maker. which is structurally - and this is not debatable - bad. they could even quote wider than other MMs and still hedge ahead of them because they get to see their fills that much earlier. 60ms is an eternity in HFT. round trips between tokyo boxes is under 1ms, so that's 60+ round trips worth of network time. while everyone is listening to a dial tone.

so the actual question is, are we ok with having only a single market maker quoting markets on hyperliquid? 

i would strongly argue no, we are not. it's not democratic, it's not sound microstructure. it's bad for hyperliquid, and it's bad for crypto.

> The 227M PnL is irrelevant because it was generated by a ton of alpha instead of just them having most of the priority slots 

agree. also, for the sake of argument, they might have lost 228M on their hedges against these positions. they didn't, and the original number is probably not that far off, but you can't make any profitability claims based on their account history on a single venue. also wintermute is (mostly) not wearing naked HL positions w/o hedges.

> Why didn’t you mention on your other tweet that all crypto got nuked? You blame WM and HL for the 82% liq collapse but you don’t see you mentioning that nance is also down like 60%+ on that same period just like every other exchange lol

that's still a big difference, but causality here is difficult to prove. factually, i can tell you we can see binance's hedges hitting the binance tapes 60ms+ ahead of ours, and size-match it to their HL wallets fills. this is what is driving smaller MMs out. 

we have recently cut our quoted symbols in half on HL from 120 to 60.

> It literally converts MMs trading edge in fees

no, that's not how it works. as mentioned, they could even quote *wider* than they otherwise would, because they have guaranteed hedge liquidity. 

also, it's similar to how 0 fees doesn't mean 0 spreads. market makers do not just eat fees, they widen spreads according to costs. 

there are shades of gray here, it's not binary, and i am open to a multiple equal-speed slot architecture with open, easy peering access for any slot winning wallet. that was my first recommended redesign in fact. but that may not be possible given the network/architecture.

> Abolishing the auction doesn’t change anything in fact it might actually make it worse. Do you know how much funds spend on infra every year? Take it away and now have the same exact thing happening but behind closed doors and with fewer participants

no. our all-in HL-related infra bill was around $15,000 last month, and i know for a fact we are within 1ms of wintermute's HL latency, absent read-priority. 

wintermute spent $828,676.86 on read priority in the past 30d. this fact is available from hl core chain data. 

$828,676.86 > $15,000. could argue the point on engineering, but there's not that much engineering required once everything is in place.

furthermore i doubt they reduced their infra costs with read priority, but you'd have to ask them

> The auction is better for the smaller MMs because they can’t afford the infra cost to race for ms, but they can afford to buy temporary priority 

no. this was the stated intention, but i struggle to see how they didn't see the obvious outcome of the deepest pocketed player dominating the auction. which makes me think this was intended as a v0 that just hasn't been updated yet. so now it's time to update or simplify (abolish).

> I never personally worked in HFT/MM but Id argue that since it massively helps against adverse selection it also allows MMs to quote with much deeper liq at top of book and sometimes maybe even tighter spreads

the incentive could also be the opposite, as stated above. my observed behavior, as an HFT MM competing directly with them, staring at this stuff 90 hours per week, is that alt markets are and will continue to converge to having a single market maker because nobody else can quote profitably. if wintermute blows up, or decides to stop quoting, or their systems take a dump for 12 hours on a wednesday, those markets go quiet. bad.

> 1. WM is buying 76% of slots because they’re better than everyone else
> 2. They’re buying it so others don’t have access to it 
> Sorry to say but in both cases it’s based af lmao

i more or less agree. they're just playing the game, and winning. i would again like to state unequivocally, wintermute is NOT the problem here! they're just playing the game and winning.

but if we're going to house all of finance the game cannot be designed in this way. it has serious risks, and it is not good enough. i've spoken to many smart people about this and they all agree. respectfully, the only one who disagrees is the one who's winning the game. 

hyperliquid should stick to its day-1 values and be a democratic, open ecosystem that is NOT designed for the few. it should be designed to support the deepest liquidity, with the most participants, to serve a global market.

and under the current design, it's simply not so.

转译：为什么面试聊得挺好，你却还是没拿到 Offer？（面试官视角）

我在论坛上看到过很多关于这个话题的帖子，所以想从面试官的角度，分享几个常见的原因：为什么明明候选人自己觉得面试发挥得特别好，最后我们却依然没能录用他。

1. 在核心岗位要求的问题上，你的回答不够扎实。 我遇到过不少这样的候选人：面对那些属于“加分项 (nice to have)”的技能问题时，他们对答如流、表现惊艳；但一问到核心的硬性技能 (core mandatory skill)，回答就显得有些单薄，最终也因此被淘汰。这里的难点在于，候选人往往并不清楚公司最看重的到底是什么技能，尤其是招聘启事 (job posting) 上可能也写得模棱两可。如果一份招聘启事列了一大堆要求，我觉得非常值得在面试一开始就主动问清楚。比如你可以这样说：“我的过往经历比较广泛，但今天这场面试，我希望能把重点放在贵公司最看重的部分。在你们列出的岗位要求中，有哪些是优先级特别高、需要我在接下来的交流中重点展示的吗？”

2. 早有其他内定或更偏爱的人选，这与你个人无关。 举个例子，我曾多次参与面试评审团 (hiring panels)，期间遇到过让我惊艳的优秀候选人，双方聊得非常投机，我也强烈推荐录用他……但评审团里另一位更有话语权的面试官，心里已经有了别的意向人选（通常是他们以前合作过、知根知底且配合默契的熟人）。又或者，这个岗位本身就有一位实力很强的内部候选人 (internal candidate) （注：指公司内部申请转岗或晋升的员工，通常因熟悉公司业务和文化而具备天然优势），除非他在面试中表现得一塌糊涂才会痛失机会——但只要发挥得中规中矩，这个岗位就稳稳是他的了。

3. 你确实非常优秀，但不太适合这个特定岗位。 好几次我和候选人聊得极其愉快，心里甚至忍不住感叹：“天呐，真希望我们有个别的岗位能留住这个人！”因为他们显然是不可多得的人才，只是和当前招人的这个岗位不那么契合。这通常出于一些你无法控制的客观原因：比如对这个岗位来说，你的资历显得太浅或太深；又或者你的技能树和兴趣点偏向另一个专业领域，而我们在当前岗位上很难让你充分发挥。举个例子，我曾经面试过一位极其优秀的候选人，经验非常丰富，我们所有人也都被他的过往作品深深吸引。但聊下来可以明显看出，他平时更多是在做统筹与管理，而不是亲力亲为地做一线落地执行 (hands-on implementation)，而我们这个岗位恰恰急需一个能直接上手干活的实干家。

4. 存在一些未明说的“隐性门槛”或偏好，而你恰好没满足。 我觉得这种情况比大家想象的要普遍得多。比如，我有一次参与面试时，内部其实心知肚明这个岗位没有任何晋升空间。其中一位候选人明显非常有野心、渴望往上走，于是我们淘汰了他，因为我们更想找一个愿意在天花板明显的岗位上安稳待得更久的人。还有一次，我们知道这个岗位平时需要频繁对接一位性格强势、很难搞的业务相关方 (stakeholder) （注：指在项目中与你存在工作交集、利益关联的同事、跨部门负责人或客户），所以我们淘汰了一位看起来过于顺从、脾气太好的候选人，因为我们清楚这里需要一个极其自信、能够守住底线并顶住压力的人。这类要求大多数公司是绝对不会写在招聘启事上的，属于典型的“隐性要求”。此外，有些招聘启事单纯就是写得很烂，根本没有准确传达出招聘经理 (hiring manager) 真正想要什么样的人。所以，如果你觉得自己明明符合纸面上的所有要求却还是落选了……请记住，背后很可能存在一些你不知道的隐性条件。

5. 你已经很棒了，但刚好有人比你更匹配。 有些岗位的竞争真的非常激烈，会涌现出一大批背景强硬、条件完全达标的候选人，我自己在做决定时也常常纠结万分。在这种情况下，最终的胜负往往取决于一些极其微小且主观的细节——比如另一位候选人刚好比你多满足了几个我们的加分技能。

6. 其实面试并没有你以为的那么顺利。 我在面试评审团里遇到过一些明显不会“察言观色 (read the room)”的候选人，我完全能想象到，他们回去后可能会觉得自己发挥得棒极了，但其实根本不是那么回事——我们当时只是在保持礼貌而已。我还见过评审团里的同事对某位候选人表现得极其热情（比如不断追问、非常宽容地引导思路、肯定或顺着对方的话往下聊），哪怕在座的所有面试官心里都清楚这位候选人根本没戏。我个人通常会尽量避免这样做，免得给候选人造成虚假的希望；但有些面试官确实会因为同情那些表现不佳的候选人，而觉得有必要对他们格外友善。如果你担心自己属于这种情况，我建议找身边认识的人做几次模拟面试 (mock interviews)，听听他们对你面试表现的真实反馈。

总而言之，拿不到 Offer 往往没那么简单，并非只有“你肯定哪里做错了”或者“整个面试流程都是走过场”这两种极端。很多时候你完全没有做错任何事（一切都不在你的掌控范围内），纯粹只是因为背后还有其他客观因素在起作用罢了。

在过去12年里，BTC应该从来没有出现过这样大级别的奇葩走势。也许，这就是“资本入局，筹码过度集中”后的必然反噬。

在某种无形力量对市场信心的肆意践踏下，新进投资者整体亏损占比（STH-PSIL）已被推高至73%！在几乎所有人都认为市场已经走出熊底后的第一波回踩，就几乎要了所有人的命。

而上一轮，同样在加息环境，叠加传统银行暴雷的第一波回踩，STH-PSIL是51%，到第二波也只是67%。

所以，我将本轮称之为：天坑开局！

类似这样的开局，在历史上只有2019-2020年有些类似。但当时有全球疫情蔓延的黑天鹅背景，而现在并没有，只是多了“人为干预”的痕迹。

2019年的第一波回踩，直接把STH-PSIL干到了97%，这一段我亲身经历，只记得当时所有人都认为BTC要归零了，crypto是传销骗局，我也跟着喊了。

当然，现在我肯定不会再这样跟着人云亦云。且仍然对BTC不远的未来抱有坚定的信心。

尽管现在的价格在一轮过山车后已经逼近我的成本线，但我没有任何要交出筹码的打算。如果你希望在我这里看到一些悲观的文字表述，那对不起，可能会让你很失望。

就像昨天，有人说我给了大家“错误的信心”。可能是我的文化水平低，第一次听说“信心”还可以分对错。

关注了我这么久，你应该知道我在2-6月就重仓买入BTC。仓位即是观点！我既然坚定持有，当然是多头思维。

你怎么可能要求我一边持有，一边散播恐慌？更何况当前局势本就如此艰难。

我分享的数据是不是足够客观，不能用“有效和无效”来评判。这一次失效了，就不客观；上一次有效，就很客观？

当然，我的解读肯定是主观的，这需要你有自己独立思考的能力。就比如，面对这次人造的天坑开局，你怎么看？

我认为现在没有必要过度悲观。

但，经此一役，投资者信心受损，内心留下了不可磨灭的阴影，后市发展的每一步可能都会小心翼翼。

一朝怕蛇咬十年怕井绳......

上方史诗级的套牢盘，将对接下来的每一次反弹到关键位时，都会持续形成压力。就像19年后，市场整整花了1年的时间，才真正走出来。

这一次，或许难度更大。但有低谷，就会有高峰，你现在所承受的一切磨难，最后都会以最好的方式回报给你。

对！我相信！—— 一起加油！

text:
男性怎么拿到大结果？

男性想要提升外形，其实没有想象中那么难。
由于男性与女性在睾酮水平、初始肌肉量及肌肉增长潜力上存在生理差异，男性通常更容易练出具有一定围度和视觉冲击力的肌肉。
对于身材微胖、此前缺乏系统训练的普通男性而言，只要方法得当，坚持三个月力量训练，就有机会看到初步的肌肉线条；坚持半年，体型和精神面貌往往会有比较明显的改善。
前提是每周至少进行3次力量训练，每次45—60分钟，配合合理的热量摄入、充足的蛋白质、规律作息和适量饮水。

对于体脂率较高的男性，我更建议先把减脂和力量训练结合起来。
建议早睡早起，在身体状态良好的情况下进行30—60分钟的空腹爬坡有氧。每周安排5天训练、2天休息，或者根据恢复情况调整频率。

如果前一晚睡眠不足，或者身体明显疲惫，就不要勉强自己进行高强度训练。运动的意义是改善身体，而不是透支身体。
睡前四小时就不要运动了，皮质醇升高，更容易发胖。

在我看来，现代男性最值得投资的两件事，一件是赚钱的能力，另一件是外表管理的能力。
和赚钱比，外表改善容易很多。

男性要努力提升收入，然后争取每天抽出一小时锻炼身体，根据自身皮肤状况做好清洁和护理，定期修剪头发，保持清爽干净的形象。
衣服不需要买太多，也不必盲目追求奢侈品牌。选择设计简洁、剪裁合身、面料有质感的衣服，往往比浑身堆满Logo更显高级。

一个男人的外形管理，其实不需要投入多么惊人的成本，但长期坚持，带来的变化却可能非常明显。

只赚钱，不经营外形，你容易把自己活成一台赚钱机器。
当一个男人除了经济实力，几乎没有其他能够吸引异性的特质时，你就很难分辨，靠近自己的人究竟是欣赏你这个人，还是欣赏你所拥有的资源。
一旦财富成为关系中最主要的吸引力，感情的稳定性也可能越来越依赖于财富的持续供给。

只经营外形，不提升经济实力，你又容易把自己活成一件精美的消费品。
年轻、帅气、身材好，当然可以带来短期的异性吸引力。
但如果除此之外，没有事业能力、经济基础和长期发展的潜力，那么你在亲密关系中的优势，也可能随着年龄增长而逐渐减弱。
你可以凭借外形获得关注，却未必能够凭借外形获得长期的尊重与选择权。

赚钱，是为了拥有现实世界的选择权；经营外形，是为了不让自己的吸引力完全依附于金钱。
一个男人最理想的状态，不是有钱却邋遢，也不是帅气却空洞。
而是既有创造财富的能力，也有管理身体的自律；既有成熟的社会竞争力，也有不依赖财富的个人魅力。

只顾赚钱，你可能成为别人的力工。
只经营外形，你可能成为别人的短择，只能为大佬代持女人。
既能赚钱，又懂得经营自己外表，才更有机会成为关系中的主动选择者，而不是被动等待别人挑选的人。

但这些，都好过，又不钻研赚钱，又不钻研外表的男性，这些男性，只能学会和自己和解了。

text:
$CC is at $0.08. Holders are dumping and calling the tokenomics broken.

I get it. I'm holding anyway.

Here's the bear case, straight, and why I think it's the setup, not the ending. 

The bear case is real: CC is inflationary right now.

Mid-2026 data: ~2.0B minted vs ~1.33B burned over 90 days.

If you hold CC today, you're being diluted. No spin.

Wall Street gets the tech, retail pays through inflation.?

Half true. The mint pays validators and app builders for measured work on the network, the same way ETH and SOL pay validators.

The difference: CC had no pre-mine, no VC allocation, no unlock cliff.

And the institutional slice already got cut.

In early 2026, issuance per block was halved and the Super Validator share dropped from 48% to 20%. The rest goes to validators and apps doing the work.

BME isn't a promise of balance today. It's a feedback loop. Fees are priced in dollars, so the lower CC goes, the more CC every dollar of settlement burns.

Price weakness makes the burn stronger. That's the design.

The mint has a ceiling. The burn doesn't.

Issuance runs on a fixed schedule. Burn scales with dollars settled.

The burn already offsets about two-thirds of issuance, and most institutional flow is still in pilot.

That pipeline: the first SEC-exempt tokenized U.S. equity trades (Nov 4), LSEG as a Super Validator, tokenized Treasuries, bank stablecoins.

Pilot production is the 2027 story.

Too many projects on sale to ignore.

Fair. If you need dilution to stop today, CC isn't your trade.

My bet is the crossover: burn/mint passing 1.0. I'd rather sit through the dilution early than buy after it flips. 

I am still fully convinced @CantonNetwork has the correct tokenomics for the patient.

text:
Hyperliquid OI pumped 80% to a record $16.8B last quarter and CT is calling it adoption. Open page 24 of the HRC report. Same quarter, HL raised the HYPE borrowing limit to 65% LTV. Come on

Half of CT saw the "flipped Bybit, Kraken and OKX" chart and went straight to posting bullish takes. I read all of it. It's way uglier than the headline

-> August: HYPE loan-to-value goes from 50% to 65%. September: HL opens borrowing against HYPE and BTC, $269M borrowed on day one. Quarter end: $416M USDC on loan, 77.6% utilization. And we're surprised OI went up 80%?
-> Revenue $191M, +22% QoQ. Nice. Still -36.5% YoY though, and half that QoQ jump is $17M of interest on USDC just sitting there. By HRC's own math that line is already about a quarter of trading revenue, and every 50bps of cuts eats ~$30M a year of it. Traders had nothing to do with it, the Fed made that money
-> Gossip priority fees, the 60ms read auctions Wintermute farms, went up 2.7x to $3.75M. I already posted about this. Nobody fixed it. It just got pricier
-> Assistance Fund dropped $149M on buybacks, more than Q2, and got 26% LESS HYPE. Compared to a year ago, 68% less. Avg price $73, HYPE today ~$68. The fund is underwater on its own Q3 buys lol
-> Stock perps did $154B, +161%. Then Wall Street closes and HL stock depth drops ~33%. One trash pre-market print on SK Hynix and $57M of longs across 960 accounts got wiped in seconds

Don't get me wrong, I like HL as a product. 65k traders a day is a record, and a DEX flipping OKX on OI sounded like a joke two years ago

And yes, the USDC float grew $1.5B, nobody is running for the exit. But you crank LTV and launch a borrow market in the same quarter, and then OI goes vertical. Sorry, that's people levering up, and calling it adoption is cope

I stopped looking at OI. Now I only watch borrow utilization, the USDC float and stock depth after US close. Until that looks healthy I'm not buying the "record quarter" story, and no way I'm aping HYPE because of a PDF

author: meetKORA
quoted_text:
I’ve decided to leave NVIDIA. There are a few things I want to say.

As a robotics engineer at NVIDIA, I have seen Jensen as much more than the company’s CEO.

I admire his willingness to invest in a future that was not yet obvious. He committed to CUDA long before the deep learning boom and positioned NVIDIA for AI before it became everyone’s priority. Those decisions helped build the infrastructure that powers today’s AI.

I have seen that same vision in physical AI: investing in robotics, sharing open-source tools and projects, and building computing platforms that bring AI into the physical world. This is the work I do every day—and a future I believe in.

But what matters most to me is the culture he helped build.

Engineers are encouraged to explore, take risks, and learn from mistakes. Jensen reads employees’ Top 5 emails, follows their work, and engages directly. In a company this large, that connection matters. It makes an individual engineer feel that their ideas can still be heard.

That is why this has been so disappointing.

I do not have all the facts surrounding the allegations, and I cannot prejudge the investigation. My admiration for Jensen does not put him above scrutiny.

What I find difficult to accept is having to come to terms with his departure before receiving an explanation that helps me understand it. What this means for our direction, our culture, and the people doing the work remains unclear to me.

I have felt that engineers’ perspectives matter here. On this decision, I have not felt heard. That gap has been more painful than I expected.

I understand that some information cannot be shared immediately. But that does not erase the feeling of being left outside a decision that affects the company we help build every day.

A company’s greatness comes from its leadership, its governance, and the people who turn its ambitions into reality. Employees’ trust and sense of belonging are part of that, too.

Jensen’s vision and the engineering culture he shaped were important reasons I wanted to stay. His departure led me to decide that my own chapter here should also come to a close.

I leave with sadness and gratitude. The colleagues I have worked with, and the work we believed in together, will always matter to me.

These are my personal views.

What cannot be won on the battlefield cannot be won at the negotiating table — the new round of negotiations between Yemen’s Houthi movement and Saudi Arabia

According to Adel Al-Hassani, Saudi Arabia and the Houthi are still negotiating over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

He stated that Saudi Arabia demands the Houthi withdraw from the strait and grant safe passage to Saudi vessels. In return, Saudi Arabia would halt its airstrikes inside Yemen and order Aden’s government forces not to launch offensive operations against the Houthi.

The Houthi, however, want to tie opening the strait to Saudi Arabia and stopping attacks on Saudi territory into a single bargaining package. Their ask: Saudi Arabia lifts its unlawful blockade on Yemen and stops interfering in Yemen’s internal affairs.

Al-Hassani says neither side is willing to compromise, and the talks have effectively stalled.

Yet the rapid developments on the southern Yemeni front — especially the Houthi’s repeated encirclements and heavy blows against Aden’s government troops — appear to tilt the negotiating balance in the Houthi’s favour.

Bear in mind that just one month ago, Saudi Arabia insisted talks could only happen if the Houthi surrendered and abandoned all territory seized since its September offensive.

Now the Houthi are sitting at the table setting terms for Saudi Arabia. That alone is the clearest sign of the shifting balance of power.

As the old saying goes: what cannot be won on the battlefield cannot be won at the negotiating table.

text:
Elon attention to $CLAUDIA is recurring rather than a one-off coincidence.

2j5SaS7xy776qCBpyPQbZjyQSAtKiFgrwjfErthnW2ZM 

Over the past 40 days, Elon has reposted Claudia-related content eight times. The market cap of CLAUDIA has repeatedly attracted attention around the $2M level. Before this latest repost, its market cap was slightly above $3M, then quickly surged toward $5M.

However, I think the risk-reward ratio becomes more interesting again when the market cap pulls back to the low-$3M range.

This latest Elon interaction also reinforces two points from our previous analysis. First, Elon’s continued attention can serve as a recurring catalyst for Claudia, bringing repeated waves of visibility. Second, what ultimately determines Claudia’s long-term potential is not celebrity reposts, but whether she can evolve from Anabology’s personal creation into an open IP that other creators can build around.

The most important validation this time is that third-party creators are already producing content around Claudia. PinelandLabs' contest entry was shared by SXSI and subsequently reposted by Elon, showing that Claudia's content is beginning to spread beyond Anabology's own distribution channels. Combined with the MCP tools, two consecutive creator contests, and GLIF officially signing Claudia and opening her up for casting, these developments provide further support for our previous thesis around an independent creator ecosystem and commercial distribution.

However, three important questions remain unanswered: Will external creators continue producing content beyond participating in a single contest? Can GLIF generate actual commercial orders for Claudia? And can Claudia's growing IP influence eventually translate into genuine demand for CLAUDIA through mechanisms such as using trading fees to fund content production?

My current assessment is that the fundamentals have strengthened significantly since our previous analysis. Elon's repost is the direct catalyst behind this rally, while creator participation and the GLIF signing are more important developments for Claudia's medium- and long-term growth.

What I want to watch next is not how many more times Elon reposts Claudia, but whether she can continue attracting attention through independent creators even without his involvement. The former drives short-term price action; the latter will ultimately determine the project's long-term valuation potential.

I believe the direct catalyst behind this $CLAUDIA rally was indeed Elon repost, but the significance of this event is worth studying beyond simply receiving another round of celebrity attention.

2j5SaS7xy776qCBpyPQbZjyQSAtKiFgrwjfErthnW2ZM 

The reason is that what Elon amplified this time was not a promotional video made by Anabology himself, but a contest entry created by an external creator around Claudia.

That distinction matters. Previously, we had been discussing whether Claudia could evolve from an AI character created by Anabology into an open IP that other creators would also want to participate in. This event provided the first relatively direct example: an external creator produced content, the content entered a contest and spread through the community, SXSI published it, and it eventually received direct exposure through Elon.

I believe this is precisely one of the most promising parts of our previous thesis, but also one that had lacked concrete evidence until now.

On November 7, Elon Musk posted on X: "Who put your beliefs into your head? It probably wasn’t you." The post quoted an SXSI post featuring a contest entry created by PinelandLabs for the CLAUDIA video contest, titled Who Is Prompting You?

As of the time I was preparing this post, the original SXSI post had received approximately 1 million views, 1,100 likes, and 278 reposts. PinelandLabs subsequently publicly thanked SXSI and Anabology for giving the work a platform. Elon’s account clearly expanded the exposure of this content.

But I want to emphasize one detail: Elon did not explicitly express support for CLAUDIA, comment on the token, or indicate any investment interest. He amplified a piece of creator content related to Claudia. However, for an AI-native IP, this type of exposure could be more valuable than simply receiving a like from a celebrity on the project’s official account.

Because it shows that Claudia’s content now has the opportunity to spread beyond Anabology’s own publishing channels, reaching third-party creators, content platforms, and broader social networks.

This is also why I believe this was the main reason behind the current rally. The GLIF signing, creator contests, and tool updates have strengthened the fundamentals, but they were not substitutes for the direct catalyst behind this particular Elon event. The immediate price reaction primarily came from this external attention shock.

Compared with our previous analysis, what has actually been validated?

My original thesis for CLAUDIA was that it had the potential to evolve from an AI music video character into an AI-native entertainment IP. The biggest question at the time was whether Anabology could continue producing content, but if he remained the only person creating it, Claudia’s potential reach would ultimately be limited by his individual creative capacity.

Now, this situation is beginning to change.

The first development is creator participation.

Anabology is not just publishing his own work. He is also lowering the barriers for other people to participate through Claudia MCP. He previously announced a video creation contest, offering $420.69 in XMoney to the creator of the best entry and $69.42 to the runner-up. Later, he also added a $100 community-voted award.

The first contest ended on November 6 and entered the judging stage. Anabology subsequently launched a second round, maintaining the same prize structure: $420.69 for the best judged entry, $69.42 for second place, and $100 for the top community-voted video. The second round will end on November 13.

The prize amounts themselves are not particularly large, but I believe the value of this initiative should not be measured by the prize money alone.

It is effectively a creator bootstrapping strategy: encouraging external users to use Claudia MCP to produce music videos, then using contests, voting, and X distribution to spread attention that was previously concentrated around Anabology among a wider group of creators.

PinelandLabs’ work being selected by SXSI and subsequently amplified by Elon is a good example.

Of course, I would not say that Claudia already has an established independent creator ecosystem. What we can confirm now is that people are willing to participate, and their work has the opportunity to receive exposure far beyond the original community. What needs to be observed next is whether these creators will continue making Claudia-related content after the contests end.

The second direction receiving validation is that Claudia’s content creation tools are becoming genuine entry points for participation.

We previously discussed Claudia’s MCP, Grok Bot, and the creative toolchain that Anabology continues to improve. Version 0.3.6 introduced Earshot audio analysis, allowing Opus to identify song structures and beats, as well as detect issues between audio and video editing. ElevenLabs provides additional voice, sound effect, and music production capabilities. At the same time, the team has addressed issues involving duplicate generations, rendering, file compatibility, and task recovery.

The value of these updates is that external creators no longer need to build an entire AI production workflow from scratch to create content around Claudia.

But the real test is not how many tools are released. It is how many people actually use them and whether those people keep coming back.

GLIF signing is another particularly important development in CLAUDIA’s fundamental improvement.

In early November, GLIF first hinted that Claudia might be joining its AI Modeling Agency, before subsequently announcing the official signing.

GLIF added Claudia to its AI Characters lineup and made her available for users to cast in commercial creative projects, including advertisements, short dramas, and other video content. The team also stated that Claudia had accumulated 44 million views and released a Claudia debut trailer produced entirely using Glif.

I think this development is more worth watching than simply adding another KOL collaboration.

Previously, Claudia’s content was mainly centered around AI music videos, and her ability to gain exposure depended heavily on Anabology continuously producing new work. GLIF now provides a new distribution channel: other users can directly cast Claudia in their advertisements, short dramas, and creative projects.

This effectively gives Claudia another identity. She is no longer just an AI virtual singer publishing music videos, but is also becoming an AI model and content character that other creators can use.

If brands begin using Claudia in advertisements, and independent creators continue featuring her in different short dramas and videos, her exposure could expand from music content into the broader AI entertainment and commercial creative industries. This would significantly increase the range of potential distribution channels available to her.

However, I would not interpret this signing as proof that Claudia has already generated commercial revenue. GLIF has indeed opened the Casting entry for Claudia, but specific commercial orders, revenue-sharing arrangements, copyright authorization, and partnership terms have not been sufficiently disclosed. The 44 million views reported by GLIF also should not be interpreted as 44 million unique users.

What I would rather see is whether Claudia can actually secure commercial content orders, rather than simply being included in an AI modeling directory. If we eventually see brand advertisements, recurring Casting demand, or even other platforms inviting Claudia to participate in content production, then the significance of this signing will be much more fully validated.

As for what the market is currently betting on, I believe it has moved beyond just Elon’s attention. There are three possibilities gradually coming together.

First, can Claudia become an AI-native IP with sustainable distribution and attention?

As the cost of AI content production declines, there will be no shortage of AI tools capable of generating visually impressive videos. However, the problem with most AI characters is their lack of continuity: one appearance today, another tomorrow, leaving audiences with little reason to remember them.

Claudia has already accumulated a certain level of visual recognition, a collection of music works, and her own social media account. Anabology is also continuing to produce content around her. If these works can make audiences remember a specific character rather than just another AI-generated video, she may have the opportunity to establish a lasting influence similar to that of a virtual pop artist.

Second, can external creators become Claudia’s second content production engine? This is the direction I am most interested in right now.

If Claudia’s content continues to be produced exclusively by Anabology, the project’s growth potential will easily be limited by his individual capacity. But if MCP, open character materials, and creator contests can attract more independent participants, content production may no longer depend on a single person.

More importantly, different creators can give Claudia different styles and stories. Some may produce music, others may create short dramas or derivative content, and some may even develop their own content series around her.

Once this starts happening, Claudia has the opportunity to evolve from a character managed by one creator into an IP collectively expanded by a community.

Third, can AI IP enter the commercialization stage?

GLIF’s involvement gives this direction a concrete product entry point. In the future, Claudia may not only gain views through music videos, but also receive exposure through advertisements, short dramas, and other creative projects.

If these three directions can reinforce one another, what the market is trading will no longer be just another AI Meme, but an AI character attempting to establish a system encompassing content production, external creator participation, and commercial distribution.

Of course, this is still what the market is betting on, not an already completed business model.

So, here are the developments I will be paying attention to next.

First, the second round of the creator contest ending on November 13.

The first round has already ended, and the second round continues to offer judged prizes and community voting rewards. More than the prize money itself, I am interested in whether the second round can attract more high-quality work from independent creators and whether that content can gain exposure beyond Anabology’s existing community.

If people continue creating Claudia content voluntarily after the contest ends, that would be a sign that creator participation is beginning to become sustainable.

Second, GLIF’s actual commercialization progress.

Claudia has already entered the Casting lineup of the AI Modeling Agency. What we should watch next is whether genuine brand advertisements, commercial short videos, and other user-generated projects begin to emerge.

If commercial content with meaningful distribution results appears, it would expand Claudia’s narrative from an AI music IP into AI Talent and AI Entertainment.

Third, external distribution beyond Elon.

Elon’s repost has brought considerable attention, but in the long run, I do not want the entire project to remain dependent on him.

What would be much more encouraging is seeing other major creators, AI content accounts, music communities, and even brands begin using Claudia voluntarily. That would demonstrate that her appeal has expanded beyond the original crypto community and creator circle.

Finally, the economic connection between content production and the token.

Previous official Claudia materials stated that trading fees would be used to fund film production. This is a design worth watching: token trading activity could provide funding for content production, while the content itself could generate new attention.

However, there is still insufficient data to establish how much of the trading fees actually enters the production budget, how those funds are spent, or whether these investments result in continuous content output.

Also, the rewards for this contest are paid through XMoney, so they should not be treated as direct on-chain value capture for CLAUDIA.

If we eventually see a clear and verifiable relationship between fee revenue, creative funding, and actual content production, my confidence in the token’s long-term economic thesis would increase further.

As for the risks, I believe the biggest one right now is not that Claudia lacks content, but that the success of that content may ultimately have nothing to do with the token.

Even if she really becomes a popular AI virtual artist, that does not mean CLAUDIA will automatically receive the corresponding revenue or value. If the economic relationship between the IP, creators, platforms, and token remains unclear, the project’s fundamentals may become stronger without a corresponding improvement in the token’s value capture.

In addition, competition in the AI virtual artist sector will continue to intensify. Claudia needs to establish a recognizable identity and maintain consistent content quality. A single Elon repost or one creator contest is not enough to build a lasting competitive advantage.

Finally, my overall judgment: the fundamentals have strengthened considerably, but the most important validation is only just beginning.

Looking back at our previous analysis, I believe several of our original assumptions have received new support.

Previously, we believed that Anabology’s continuous content production capability could allow Claudia to move beyond relying on one-off viral events. The growing collection of works, her own social media account, and new distribution opportunities now support this view.

We also believed Claudia had the potential to evolve from Anabology’s personal creation into an open IP. PinelandLabs’ contest entry receiving external exposure, SXSI participating in content distribution, and the MCP creator contest entering its second round have now provided some initial real-world examples.

We previously believed that Elon’s attention could become a catalyst for Claudia to receive recurring external exposure. This latest direct reference from Elon to content featuring CLAUDIA further demonstrates that Claudia-related works still have the opportunity to enter his attention.

There is also another direction that we had not fully explored before, but which has now made progress: the GLIF signing is allowing Claudia to enter the distribution channels of AI modeling and commercial content production.

However, I still believe three things remain unproven.

First, whether independent creators will continue producing Claudia content after the contests end.

Second, whether GLIF can bring Claudia actual commercial orders and sustained external users.

Third, whether the growth of the IP can translate into CLAUDIA token demand through a clear and verifiable economic mechanism.

So my current assessment is that CLAUDIA’s fundamentals have strengthened considerably, and the project is more interesting than it was in my previous analysis. This change is not simply another Elon interaction. It is the fact that external creator participation, celebrity attention, and AI commercial distribution are now appearing along the same development path.

What I am more willing to bet on now is whether Claudia can become an AI character that is continuously used by different creators, distributed across different platforms, and eventually called upon by commercial brands.

If the only development is Anabology continuously producing new videos while Elon occasionally interacts with them, the market will keep trading the same attention narrative. But if other creators begin actively building content around Claudia, GLIF brings commercial applications, and more audiences begin recognizing and following the character, then her growth will no longer be limited by the creative pace of a single person.

I believe the most important development worth watching is that Claudia is beginning to move from an AI character that people simply watch into an AI IP that allows others to participate in creating.

The valuation potential of these two models is completely different.

The next thing I most want to see is whether Claudia can continue generating new community-created content after the second round of the contest ends on November 13. Because that will directly determine the outcome of our biggest long-term thesis: whether Claudia can truly build her own creator ecosystem.

定位达人时需将创作者画像与目标受众画像拆开考虑：
一种是泛科技类博主，用于快速起量与新品曝光尝鲜；
另一种更具长效价值的是垂直场景博主，例如日常分享特定工作流的人群。

重点不在于达人是否标榜自己是 AI 博主，而在于他能否将工具自然融入到目标用户的实际业务场景与痛点中。

二、 达人筛选指标

衡量达人质量的核心指标是近期同形式视频的场均与中位数播放量，而非单纯的粉丝数。

中尾部正处于成长期的创作者往往报价友好、制作更用心，反而更容易产生高性价比的爆款。在数据门槛上，应要求达人近三十天内保持公开更新，近期长视频中位播放量不低于一千次，短视频不低于一万次。

互动率是辨别刷量的重要防线，点赞与评论之和占播放量的比例建议达到百分之一以上。

此外必须严格排查内容真实性，坚决剔除纯 AI 配音、纯数字人出镜的频道，人工抽查评论区是否具有真实的讨论氛围。合作前还需结合第三方数据工具核查其历史播放曲线与平台收益估算，排除月度播放突降为负数或数据剧烈异动的异常账号。

三、 达人信息线索挖掘

挖掘候选达人主要有四种高转化路径。

最直接的方式是从竞品入手，反查竞品合作过的高播放视频创作者，这类达人已经受过市场检验且理解产品形态，建联时应错开竞品视频发布的高峰期（通常建议间隔两到四周以上）。

第二种方式是场景词延伸，不要只搜产品品类本身，要围绕用户的具体工作任务展开搜索。

第三种方式是相似受众扩展，以跑通转化的一两位标杆博主为主页种子，沿着相似的内容风格、受众画像做同类账号扩散。

四、 沟通策略

建联第一封邮件决定了生死，核心是去 AI 感、去群发感，字数尽量精简克制。

第一行一定要用达人的真实姓名称呼对方，不要直接套用频道昵称。

正文用一到两句话切入，真诚夸赞他近期发布的某一期具体视频，并讲清楚你的产品为什么能完美契合他的受众。开门见山说明这是一次付费合作（Paid Collaboration），简短介绍产品核心价值，直接询问对方的排期和报价。

需求说明书（Brief）要分步提供：初次建联只发一到两页以内的通用简报，讲清产品形态和基本合作诉求即可，给达人留足创作想象空间；等价格与档期确认、正式启动项目后，再提供定制化的创意方向与具体场景方案。

五、 报价评估与砍价模型

拿到达人报价后，必须先在心中建立一套严密的测算模型，心中有数才敢谈价。

第一步算基础预算，以达人近期同类视频的中位数播放量为准，乘以行业基准千次播放成本（CPM）。美区 YouTube 的 CPM 基准通常在 150 到 300 美元之间，TikTok 和 Instagram 约在 50 到 100 美元之间。

第二步用达人报出的总价除以中位数播放量，反推其对应的实际 CPM。如果数值严重高出基准线，就要看其是否包含独家排他、全片定制、或者受众本身具备极高的行业溢价。

第三步结合自己业务的漏斗数据倒推，根据预计播放量、点击率、付费转化率估算出预期付费用户数，再用报价除以预期人数得出单客获客成本，判断是否在可接受范围内。

在最终议价环节，行业公认成功率最高的黄金降价幅度通常在原报价的七折左右（即下浮 30%）。如果对方报价超出预算但受众精准，可以以七折为锚点展开真诚议价。

六、 内容共创与发布前 SEO 调优

正式制作视频时，最重要的是找到产品融入真实工作流的切入点，切忌把达人当成纯念稿机器。

建议调取达人以往表现最好的几期视频，分析其黄金前五秒的抓人钩子（Hook）和节奏，协助达人设计一个从真实问题切入的演示脚本。

达人交付草稿视频（YouTube Unlisted 状态）审片时，是借力 SEO 获取免费长尾流量的最佳时机。

标题要把受众真实搜索的高频关键词尽量前置；视频描述栏的第一行或第二行直接放置专属追踪链接，并在说明文案中自然嵌入核心搜索词；最后必须优化章节时间戳（Chapters），把单纯的时间序号改写为带场景关键词的任务名称，直接拉满 YouTube 算法的检索推荐权重。

七、 复盘

达人视频上线绝不是合作的终点，真正的增长来自于精准复盘。

发布前必须为每位达人配置专属的短链与参数标签，置于视频最显眼位置。

除了直接点击转化，工具类产品通常有很强的长尾效应，很多用户看完视频后会在几天甚至几周后通过 Google 搜索或直接输入网址访问。因此在数据统计上，必须引入具备首次触点来源归因能力的用户行为分析工具，将这部分由于达人种草带来的回流转化准确计算在内。

每周固定复盘达人的播放量、互动率、点击数、激活数以及最终付费转化成本，用数据倒推哪些内容场景、哪种体量的博主能够真正跑通正向投产比。

text:
这个案例就是我上一篇提到的——Agent 应该让人容易做的事情有更大价值——的范例。

不过，与其说是 Goal Engineering，不如说是 Goal-Driven Loop Engineering，核心行动力引擎是 Loop 而不是 Goal。

目标是驱动和指引，是关键因素，但不负责承担工作载荷。

体系化的循环工程包含几个核心模块——

- 持续工作代理：行动力引擎，没有行动力就没有一切
- 长程目标驱动：行动力兑现，短目标放到永动机里也会陷入停滞或空转
- 最终交付物导向：减少中间交付物，让行动力/算力，更多投入在最终结果上，而非中间对齐环节。

其中，【最终交付物导向】是关键，它可以衍生出前两个。

当你面向最终交付物（ouput）提供其必要上下文输入（input）时，它已经包含长程目标了（给定结果需要出现），它已经要求着持续工作代理了（没出现之前不要停下来）。

剩下的是体力活儿、技术活儿，agent 停下来了，你说“继续”手动驱动，循环递进，直到最终交付结果出现。Super Agents， Always-on Agents 主要让人省力了，减少人工驱动，但它们是工具属性，而非本质属性。

本质是【聪明的模型+足够的工具+可达的最终交付结果】包含着实现路径的展开潜力，如果你愿意，你可以在最朴素的一问一答里，手动维持 Agent Loop 转发工具调用，走完全程（它只是慢）。

理解了这个 nullshell 形态，构建 agent product 时，便拥有了纲领性认知。
author: Xudong07452910
quoted_text:
Agent 开始接长期目标之后，怎么划定它的工作范围就变得很关键。

Harrison Chase 和 Actively AI 刚发了一篇《Goal Engineering》，核心观点很简单：提出了一个挺有启发的观点：按照人最容易提供反馈的方式，来划分 Agent 的工作范围。

Agent 很多时候出错，是因为缺少上下文。文档、API 这些信息还好补，真正麻烦的是专家脑子里的隐性知识，比如品牌调性、销售策略该多激进，这些往往需要靠反复反馈来校准。

Actively 做销售 Agent 的经历就很典型。

最初他们为每个客户分配一个 Agent，结果销售需要在一堆 Agent 之间来回切换，在某个客户身上积累的经验，也很难复用到其他客户。

后来改成按「Motion」划分，也就是让一个 Agent 专门负责一类工作，比如外联或早期销售推进。

这样销售可以集中审核同类任务，一次反馈就能影响更多客户。客户资料则由后台 Agent 按需收集。

文章最后还有个挺大胆的判断：「Prompt Engineering 和 Context Engineering 会消失，但 Goal Engineering 会留下来。」

这个预测可以讨论，但我挺认同其中一点：Agent 的工作范围怎么划，直接决定了人类反馈能否被有效复用。

对于长期运行的 Agent，这可能是个很值得重视的架构设计问题。
