实际上我的交易方式以及地址分析绝大部分是来自 @Shanks_A9z 的擒龙术和@0xmagnolia 的meme “圣经”，以及@BitCloutCat 的保留10%底仓，一致性交易。

因为我本人是偏向 叙事分析和地址追踪，在趋势行情下才能赚到钱，在流动性枯竭，pvp我是菜鸟，几乎赚不到钱，所以最近我几乎没有去交易，去做多身体和学习了。

因为很多时候我们的精力是有限的，怎么早期能发现好项目，好标的呢，总不能一直刷x去获取信息吧，去追踪聪明钱地址，分组监控是一个很好的思路

因为大部分的人的赚钱地址是不愿意公开的，默默赚钱，所以把这部分地址找出就很必要，我之前是 看到一个经常能赚的大v地址，在想他为什么一直能抓到，真有那么多精力？

我把他买入赚到大利润的标的选出，然后到bsc scan或者对应链的scan，那在他地址买入前的地址全部下载下来，就这样做3，4个标的，你就会发现 有2，3个地址总是在他之前买入，那是不是就意味着 这些地址就是这个大v监控的地址！

用了codex和muse，grokbot后这个工作就很轻松了，之前还需要 excel，现在几分钟足够，有了地址后一定要分组，为 低频率高确定性和高频率扫链，二段等等类型，然后每天分组查看，基本上就能知道最近该玩什么。

以上是我的追踪钱包的思路，也帮助我抓到了很多标的，趁着最近，我会继续更新方法和去学习链上技术，希望在下一波行情中拿到属于自己的Alpha！

text:
David Sacks: Who Risked Jail to Take Down Jensen Huang?

“I think it's pretty clear that there were two ops here.

So one op is whatever Alice Huang was doing with or without the Chinese Communist Party. There may have been smuggling involved, we don't know. There is an investigation going on, and there should be an investigation. We should get all the facts there.

However, there's also a second op here. That second op began when somebody, or multiple people, leaked a highly classified memo, or the contents of it, to The New York Times. I think it's really important to understand that that's a crime. Leaking classified intelligence is a crime, and many people have been prosecuted for it.

Because of that fact, I don't believe that The New York Times just got this by overhearing people talking about it at a bar. Somebody made the calculated decision that they're willing to risk going to jail, they're willing to risk committing a crime to let The New York Times know about this story.

I have a series of questions about that.

So number one is, first, who did that and why? What was their motivation? Why did they feel so strongly about taking Jensen down?

Bucket number two is around the failure to give the defensive briefing. If the national security state is worried that Jensen is in possession of national security secrets and might leak them to someone who they suspect is a spy, why wouldn't you go to him right away and tell him, ‘Hey, you have this problem. Don't talk to this person’? Apparently, that didn't happen, and it does sound like that is some sort of standard operating procedure.

That brings me to question number three, which is what exactly were the national security secrets that Jensen supposedly knew? He doesn't work for the government. He's not, as far as I'm aware, privy to classified materials. So what is it that people say that he leaked to this suspected intelligence asset?

The last question I have is, what is the evidence that this person, Alice Huang, was actually a Chinese spy who worked for the Ministry of State Security? Just this morning, the incoming chair of the House Intelligence Committee, who's a Democrat, came out of a classified briefing on this subject and said that he's not sure that this person is a Chinese spy.

So I put all these things together and I would say, at this point in time, I think there's more questions than answers. And I would like a full accounting of the facts to come out.”

Vision Weekend is by far the most woman-forward frontier tech event I've ever been to. Nobody's said it out loud yet, so I will.

@foresightinst was co-founded 40 years ago by Christine Peterson (@lifeext). Yes SHE came up with the phrase "open source" we still fight about what that means in AI! It's run today by a women-led team, CEO @allisondman, COO @KarolinaEklow, event lead for Vision Weekend Lydia La Roux, plus Tara Padovan-Hickman and Program Director @madvinuova. Together they made a 500 person event spanning two venues look effortless. 

Allison has built a culture where women at the top of science are the norm. 15 of the 34 speakers on the main program were women and these weren’t junior slots. Many were PhDs running their own labs and missions across longevity, neurotech, AI, space and molecular machines and they brought some pretty big ideas…

- @ltelkins, the scientist behind NASA's Psyche mission, talked about shielding from cosmic rays - including the Oh-My-God particle - a single particle detected in 1991 with MILLIONS of times more energy than anything we can produce in particle accelerators on Earth.

- @erika_alden_d believes terraforming Mars is possible in our lifetime - Pioneer Labs has already produced the first microbe able to convert Martian regolith, water and air into bioplastics for potential habitat construction.

- @e_mackevicius, co-founder of @BasisOrg, a non-profit working to develop AI as public-interest infrastructure, also researches rat collective behaviour and what it can teach us about agent swarms.

- @zweinberg of @buildexante is investing in human agency and backing startups working on privacy, data ownership, security and identity.

Tomorrow at Lighthaven we'll be recording some podcasts with @naomibrockwell and @NicoleOzer, two of the leading voices on privacy and digital rights.

I'm immersed most days in Local AI, open source AI and open-weight models and our spaces tend to look a bit similar (I'm as guilty as anyone). There’s no posturing at Vision Weekend. People engage in meaningful discussion about the most important topics.

Spaces Ike these provide role models and experiences to people who wouldn’t normally think of themselves as potential leaders in frontier tech.

If we're serious about AI for everyone then maybe our spaces should start to look a little more like that.

Thank you @foresightinst. One more day to go and I'm already more optimistic than when I arrived!

text:
Bitcoin fell 19% into the biggest IPO ever. Now it's down 18% heading into the second biggest.

SpaceX raised $75B when it went public on June 12. In the 50 days before it listed, Bitcoin dropped 19%. Anthropic plans to raise up to $64B when it lists next week, and Bitcoin is down 18% over the same stretch. Overlay the two and they look almost the same.

What happened after the SpaceX IPO is the notable part. Bitcoin bottomed 18 days after the listing, then recovered all the way. By Day 100, it was above where it started.

Bitcoin around the SpaceX IPO:

Day -50 to IPO day: -19%
Low (Day +18): -25%
Day +50: still -20%
Around Day +70: a sharp rally
Day +100: +3.7%

From the IPO-day close to Day +100, Bitcoin gained 28%. From the low, it gained 39%.

The takeaway is that the selling came in the run-up to the listing. The bottom had effectively happened by the IPO, and the recovery came relatively shortly after, and it came all at once.

If Anthropic follows the same pattern, most of the drawdown is behind us, and it could reverse quickly over the next couple of months. And Bitcoin is sitting right at its 200-week moving average.

Map the SpaceX path onto today's price and you get roughly $90k by late February. Markets rarely follow a comparison like this exactly. But we remain very constructive on both the technicals and the fundamentals heading into 2027, and it's not hard to imagine what the narrative would be if anything close to this plays out.

text:
I’ve decided to leave NVIDIA. There are a few things I want to say.

As a robotics engineer at NVIDIA, I have seen Jensen as much more than the company’s CEO.

I admire his willingness to invest in a future that was not yet obvious. He committed to CUDA long before the deep learning boom and positioned NVIDIA for AI before it became everyone’s priority. Those decisions helped build the infrastructure that powers today’s AI.

I have seen that same vision in physical AI: investing in robotics, sharing open-source tools and projects, and building computing platforms that bring AI into the physical world. This is the work I do every day—and a future I believe in.

But what matters most to me is the culture he helped build.

Engineers are encouraged to explore, take risks, and learn from mistakes. Jensen reads employees’ Top 5 emails, follows their work, and engages directly. In a company this large, that connection matters. It makes an individual engineer feel that their ideas can still be heard.

That is why this has been so disappointing.

I do not have all the facts surrounding the allegations, and I cannot prejudge the investigation. My admiration for Jensen does not put him above scrutiny.

What I find difficult to accept is having to come to terms with his departure before receiving an explanation that helps me understand it. What this means for our direction, our culture, and the people doing the work remains unclear to me.

I have felt that engineers’ perspectives matter here. On this decision, I have not felt heard. That gap has been more painful than I expected.

I understand that some information cannot be shared immediately. But that does not erase the feeling of being left outside a decision that affects the company we help build every day.

A company’s greatness comes from its leadership, its governance, and the people who turn its ambitions into reality. Employees’ trust and sense of belonging are part of that, too.

Jensen’s vision and the engineering culture he shaped were important reasons I wanted to stay. His departure led me to decide that my own chapter here should also come to a close.

I leave with sadness and gratitude. The colleagues I have worked with, and the work we believed in together, will always matter to me.

These are my personal views.

quoted_text:
最近看到币安 bStocks 一组数据上线125天，AUM达到10亿美元；145天，进一步突破15亿美元。按照当前统计口径，bStocks 已经成为全球按资产管理规模计算最大的代币化股票发行方。

不过，我觉得这组数据值得讨论是它背后反映出来的市场变化。先把三个容易混淆的数据分清楚：
15亿美元，是 bStocks 自身的 AUM；超过30亿美元，是币安用户通过 Direct Stocks 和 bStocks 持有的传统金融资产总额；48亿美元，则是整个代币化股票行业的 AUM。

这三个数字对应的统计范围不同，但放在一起看，能更直观地理解币安在传统金融资产与加密市场之间搭建的这套产品体系。

从行业角度来看，2026年6月至11月初，代币化股票市场的总 AUM 增长了164%，达到48亿美元。同期bStocks 的市场份额也从不足1%提升到了30%以上。即使不计算 bStocks，其他平台的资产规模仍然增长了81%。

这说明一个问题：代币化股票并不是单纯依靠某个平台的增长而出现的短期现象，整个市场都在扩大。越来越多投资者开始关注，传统股票能不能通过区块链获得更灵活的持有和交易方式。

当然，和传统股票市场相比，目前48亿美元的行业规模依然很小，整个赛道还处于早期阶段。但从125天达到10亿美元、145天突破15亿美元的速度来看，用户对这类产品的实际需求已经开始显现。

比如过去想配置美股，通常需要单独开设券商账户，还要考虑不同市场的交易时间、资金转入转出以及账户管理等问题。

而 bStocks 面向美国以外符合资格的投资者，最低5美元就可以获得相应股票的碎股敞口，并且支持24/7交易，不需要另外注册外部券商账户，就能在币安的生态内参与。

对我来说，这种方式比较适合用来补充自己的资产配置。加密资产本身波动性较高，如果希望在投资组合中增加一些传统股票资产的敞口，代币化股票提供了一个不同的选择。尤其是可以根据自己的时间安排参与交易，不必完全受美股常规交易时段限制。

数据也印证了这种使用场景：bStocks 有56%的交易量发生在美股常规交易时段之外。这意味着全天候交易并不只是一个宣传功能，而是已经有相当一部分实际交易发生在传统市场休市期间。

另外，还有一个我认为很有价值的产品功能，就是 bStocks 与对应真实股票之间的1:1双向转换。

符合条件的用户可以将支持转换的 bStocks 换成对应的真实股票，也可以反向转换为 bStocks，转换环节免手续费。

这里需要说明，转换真实股票仍然需要开通币安股票账户并同意相关条款，并不是持有代币就能无条件直接兑换。尽管如此，能够在代币化资产和对应真实股票之间建立双向转换通道，确实让 bStocks 的使用场景更加完整。

还有一点，我认为涉及真实资产的产品，透明度一定不能忽略。bStocks 的每枚代币都有对应的真实股票或 ETF 提供1:1支持，由受监管托管机构持有，储备每日核对并公布。用户可以通过币安的 Proof of Collateral页面查看相关资产支持情况。

我觉得这比单纯告诉用户产品规模增长了多少更重要。毕竟涉及传统金融资产，用户不仅要关心能不能交易，也应该清楚自己持有的代币背后有什么资产作为支持。

综合来看，bStocks 这次突破15亿美元，确实是一个值得记录的行业数据。但我更关注的是它正在形成的产品逻辑：
低至5美元参与、24/7交易、真实资产1:1支持，以及与真实股票之间的双向转换。

从更长远的角度看，币安正在尝试建设一个连接加密货币和传统金融资产的超级金融 App，让用户不必在多个独立平台之间来回切换，就能管理不同类型的资产。

当然，代币化股票目前仍然只是传统股票市场的一小部分，未来还有监管、流动性和产品体验等问题需要持续完善。

但至少从现在的数据和产品功能来看，这个方向已经不只是讲故事了，而是在逐渐形成真实的用户需求。

如果对代币化股票感兴趣，可以进一步了解 bStocks 的交易方式、与真实股票的双向转换机制，也可以到 Proof of Collateral 页面自行核验资产支持情况。对于希望用较低门槛、更加灵活的方式接触传统股票资产的用户来说，这确实是一个值得了解的新选择。

SpaceX Just Changed the Space Race. But Is This Really a Win for Investors? $SPCX

This Starship test had plenty of positives. The biggest highlight was Starship successfully returning and being caught by the launch tower, showing another major step forward in its technology.

Yes, the Super Heavy booster failed to return to the launch tower and ended up in the Gulf of Mexico. But I don't think that takes away from the overall achievement, and it certainly doesn't change my long-term optimism about SpaceX.

What I'm looking forward to next is seeing SpaceX solve booster recovery and further reduce launch costs.

If future tests continue to make progress, SpaceX's commercial potential could be enormous.

In my view, the biggest opportunities for investors may still be ahead.

Anthropic داره یک پیام مهم می‌ده: از Claude Code فقط برای برنامه‌نویسی استفاده نکنید!

این شرکت ۱۱ Plugin متن‌باز منتشر کرده که Claude رو برای فعالیت در حوزه‌های شغلی مختلف آماده می‌کنن.

این Pluginها حوزه‌های مختلفی رو پوشش می‌دن؛ از جمله:

- Sales: کمک به فرایند فروش، مدیریت مشتریان و پیگیری فرصت‌های فروش
- Marketing: برنامه‌ریزی کمپین‌ها، تولید محتوا و تحلیل فعالیت‌های بازاریابی
- Legal: کمک به بررسی اسناد، قراردادها و فرایندهای حقوقی
- Finance: تحلیل اطلاعات مالی و انجام وظایف مرتبط با امور مالی
- Data Analysis: بررسی داده‌ها، تحلیل اطلاعات و استخراج بینش
- Product Management: مدیریت محصول، بررسی نیازمندی‌ها و برنامه‌ریزی توسعه

هر Plugin دقیقاً چه چیزی در اختیار Claude قرار می‌ده؟

هرکدوم از این Pluginها مجموعه‌ای از سه بخش رو در خودشون دارن:

۱. Skills: دستورالعمل‌ها و دانش تخصصی برای انجام وظایف هر حوزه.

۲. Commands: دستورهای آماده برای اجرای سریع کارهای مشخص.

۳. Connectors: اتصال به ابزارها و سرویس‌های مرتبط تا Claude بتونه در جریان کاری واقعی فعالیت کنه.

در واقع، به‌جای اینکه هر بار از ابتدا به Claude توضیح بدید یک متخصص فروش، بازاریابی یا تحلیل داده چطور باید کار کنه، می‌تونید Plugin مرتبط رو در اختیارش قرار بدید تا با Workflow همون حوزه کار کنه.

نکته مهم: این رویکرد Claude Code رو از یک ابزار صرفاً برنامه‌نویسی فراتر می‌بره و به یک دستیار تخصصی برای انجام کارهای حرفه‌ای تبدیل می‌کنه.

اگر از Claude Code استفاده می‌کنید، پیشنهاد می‌کنم این مجموعه رو بررسی کنید.

text:
Several people encouraged me to share a post I made on LinkedIn,  here on X

I wrote this from the heart, about someone I had the privilege of working closely with for years.

No agenda. Just a side of Jensen I hope doesn’t get lost in the noise.

As the days pass, my heart grows heavier.
 
I have worked at NVIDIA for nearly eight years. I have never worked for anyone quite like @JensenHuang , and I doubt I ever will.
 
Much has been written about his extraordinary vision and the company he built. But there is another side to Jensen that I have had the privilege of witnessing. And I am only speaking to what I have personally witnessed.
 
I have watched him stand behind researchers, founders, and startups when few others would. Companies struggling to survive, ideas that seemed too early, people whose ambitions exceeded their resources. He saw possibilities most of us could not yet comprehend. And he committed his time, attention, and NVIDIA’s resources to helping them succeed. Some of these companies might not exist today without him.
 
His capacity for long-term thinking is extraordinary. Sometimes it took me years to appreciate the implications of something he had recognized almost immediately. Few could match his ability to connect technology, markets, and people.
 
My own journey at NVIDIA has not always been easy. Through difficult organizational transitions and moments of uncertainty, Jensen’s guidance and willingness to stand behind my work helped me persevere.
 
But what I will remember most is his humanity.
 
My sister, has been fighting an unforgiving battle with brain cancer. When her condition deteriorated during her visit to California, our family faced unimaginable circumstances: devastating medical decisions, overwhelming hospital expenses, and the possibility of losing her far from home.
 
Despite everything on his shoulders, Jensen found the time to care. He helped my family through circumstances that seemed impossible. And he took the time to meet my sister.
 
The photograph here is one I will treasure for the rest of my life.
 
When he told me, “I am proud of you. Treasure this time together,” I understood something about leadership that no professional experience could have taught me.
 
What I will miss most professionally is the extraordinary combination of vision, conviction, curiosity, and personal commitment he brought to everything. His ability to see around corners, to challenge conventional thinking, and to bring an entire ecosystem along with him.
 
Organizations evolve, leadership changes, and new chapters begin. But the influence of someone who has shaped so many people, ideas, and possibilities endures far beyond any role or title.
 
Jensen built far more than NVIDIA. He helped build an ecosystem of researchers, entrepreneurs, engineers, and companies whose futures became intertwined with his vision.
 
I do not know what comes next. I only know how grateful I am to have worked with him, learned from him, and experienced his kindness when my family needed it most.
 
Thank you, Jensen. For your guidance, for believing in people and ideas long before the rest of us understood them, and above all, for your extraordinary humanity.

Hard disagree

The argument: Jensen was the guy fighting to sell chips to China & now with him gone, the hawks tighten the screws and OAI and Anthropic pull away.

But we’ve been running this experiment for three years. here’s what it got us:

→ Huawei now says its AI chips outsell Nvidia’s in China
→ Cambricon (another Chinese chip co) 2x’d revenue in the first half and posted its first ever annual profit
→ Cut off from the best chips, Chinese labs got efficient and gave their models away. Commerce’s own AI lab says adoption of Chinese models has surged since DeepSeek

Jensen has a commercial interest, but the core argument was legit: you want the world’s developers building on the American stack

The chips that leaked looks more like an enforcement failure. Treasury is now publicly blaming Commerce for never blacklisting Megaspeed. So far restrictions have mainly accelerated China’s domestic stack and open-model lead. Thats not obviously good for America.

这一轮比特币大跌，其实不知道啥原因！

通过逻辑和数据梳理一下！

最有可能是宏观预期、ETF赎回、技术破位、杠杆平仓几个因素叠加在一起造成的，不是单一机构或者庄家偷偷做空。

第一，最核心的宏观原因：美国通胀数据偏强，市场觉得降息要往后推迟，利率会维持在高位。美债实际收益率走高、美元走强，比特币没有利息，持有它的机会成本变高，资金跑去美债，整体市场风险偏好下降。

第二，现货ETF一直在大额赎回，是直接的资金利空。机构资金持续撤出，没有买盘托住价格，很容易往下走。

第三，监管方面的担忧，市场在预判美国后续加密监管可能收紧，叠加黑客事件带来的滞后恐慌，资金先离场避险。

第四，技术破位加上杠杆踩踏，属于下跌加速器。价格跌破关键支撑之后，大量多头止损、连环爆仓，做市商被动卖出，形成越跌越卖的循环。

text:
The next generation of the internet won't just be powered by AI.
It will be powered by autonomous agents that can own assets, make payments, coordinate with other agents, and execute transactions.

But there's one missing piece in the AI stack that deserves more attention..
Economic infrastructure for AI agents.
Think about what an autonomous agent actually needs to operate independently.

➜ Identity
An agent needs a way to establish its identity and prove which permissions it has.

➜ Wallets
Agents need wallets to hold digital assets and interact with financial applications.

➜ Payments
An agent should be able to pay for APIs, compute, data, and services without requiring a human to approve every transaction.

➜ Smart contracts
Agents need programmable rules to execute agreements, manage funds, and coordinate transactions.

➜ Access control
Autonomy doesn't mean unlimited permissions. Agents need spending limits, authorization policies, and safeguards.

➜ Coordination
Multiple agents should be able to exchange value, purchase services, and collaborate through programmable infrastructure.

This is where Ethereum becomes interesting.
Ethereum already provides several foundational building blocks,
Smart contracts for programmable execution.
ERC-20 for fungible assets.
ERC-721 and ERC-1155 for digital ownership.
Account abstraction developments for more flexible wallet experiences.
Stablecoins for programmable payments.
DeFi protocols for financial services.

Combine these primitives with capable AI agents and entirely new applications become possible.

Imagine an agent that..
Purchases its own compute resources.
Pays another agent for specialised research.
Manages a budget through smart-contract rules.
Earns revenue by providing a service.
Coordinates with other agents without a centralised payment intermediary.

These are possibilities, not capabilities that every AI agent can safely or reliably perform today.

There are still serious challenges around security, key management, agent authorisation, privacy, transaction costs, and accountability.

But the direction is worth paying attention to.
AI gives software the ability to make decisions. Ethereum gives software programmable economic infrastructure.

The intersection could become one of the most interesting areas for developers building the next generation of applications.

KORA's AI-Native Linux OS: How It Aims to Rethink the Desktop

What if AI were built into the operating system itself, rather than added as another application?

KORA Systems, led by Cyanogen co-founder Kirt McMaster, has announced KORA, a Linux-based desktop operating system designed around AI models and agents. The company plans to release it in 2027.

The key difference is where AI operates. Instead of relying entirely on separate assistants, KORA proposes integrating AI capabilities into the desktop environment.

Its Cortex component is designed to coordinate AI workloads across local hardware and cloud services. Neural Workspaces are intended to organize applications and agents around projects with defined access permissions, while Neural File System aims to make files searchable by meaning rather than just filenames.

KORA also plans support for selected Windows applications and has announced a technical collaboration with Qualcomm involving Snapdragon X2 Elite processors.

This approach could make AI more closely connected to everyday computing tasks. However, the announced architecture is not proof that KORA performs better than existing operating systems.

Its real-world speed, security, application compatibility, and reliability still require independent testing.

For now, KORA represents a proposed shift in desktop design: treating AI as part of the operating system's foundation, not merely another tool running on top of it.

quoted_text:
Ever look up at the night sky, marvel at the grandeur, and wonder… “Where is everybody?"
 
Well…, that’s the Fermi Paradox in a nutshell. Billions of stars, countless galaxies and planets, and yet total silence from anything (or anyone) “out there.” Our Milky Way Galaxy is billions of years older than Earth; so it stands to reason that other civilizations should have had a good head start on us.  So…, where is everybody?
 
Enter the Fermi Explorer Mission.  A small spacecraft that will launch towards Proxima Centauri (the nearest star beyond our solar system), will carry messages and items representing life on Earth (including a copy of the Voyager Probe's Golden Record). Using current, and proven, propulsion techniques, it will take roughly 80,000 years to get there. Yep…, 80,000 years. While we may be the first to leave, we will certainly be the last to arrive. Hopefully, future generations --with better ships and advanced technology-- will zoom past our little “message in a bottle.” And that’s the beautiful part. It’s not about winning a race. It’s about choosing to take that first step—even when we know we won’t live to see the finish line. We’re sending a piece of who we are, into the dark, and trusting that someone, someday, will find it and know we were here…, curious and brave enough, to try.

text:
I've recently talked to quite a few people recently who believe they can just rent B300 nodes, install @vllm_project / @sgl_project, plug into @OpenRouter, and start printing money.

I think they seriously underestimate how hard the inference business has become.

A few facts everyone should know:

- Getting listed is extremely hard now! OpenRouter reportedly gets 40 provider applications every day and only approves 1. It could take months just to get listed!

- Competition is brutal! There are already 80+ providers serving @deepseek_ai models. Unless you have done extreme optimizations, you won't get any meaningful traffic!

- Some competitors aren't even trying to make money! Some providers intentionally price below cost to attract traffic. They treat the losses as marketing spend, and no one can even compete the price!

I think the era of simply hosting open-source models and selling tokens is coming to an end, especially for new entrants.

The real opportunity is moving up the stack. Sell solutions, not tokens.

昨天我说黄仁勋事件是美国内部分裂的一个重要标志。很多朋友认为我说的两党之间，实际上这次真正的分裂在共和党内部。

今天《华盛顿邮报》爆料：国务卿Rubio是黄仁勋事件背后的关键推动者。

Rubio利用CIA情报，向特朗普提交了一份措辞强硬的黄仁勋涉谍风险备忘录。相关信息随后泄露，引发连锁反应，最终黄仁勋因接连曝光的私人关系问题辞职。

而Rubio是共和党的人，为啥会反着干特朗普宠溺的黄仁勋呢？

这就必须从头开始讲，今天的共和党，大致有三股力量：

一是硅谷资本派：Trump、商务部长Lutnick、前AI主管David Sacks。

他们认为最快发展AI是美国的第一要务。同时认为，美国的优势不只是芯片性能，更是全球对CUDA和美国技术生态的依赖。与其全面封锁中国，逼出一个华为，不如继续卖芯片，让中国离不开美国。

二是对华鹰派 China Hawks：国务卿兼国家安全顾问Rubio、众议院中国问题委员会主席Moolenaar。

他们不反对AI。但在他们眼里，GPU早已不是普通商品。每卖给中国一块先进芯片，都可能是在帮助下一个军事对手。必须尽可能锁住中国的算力。

三是MAGA民粹反AI派：特朗普前军师Bannon。

他们关心的甚至不是中国，而是美国人自己。AI抢走工作，数据中心推高电价，硅谷亿万富翁赚得盆满钵满，却还要普通人承担代价。Hawley甚至要求全国暂停新建数据中心。

曾经都因为特朗普聚在一起，但如今已经出现了很大的内部分裂。

过去两年，黄仁勋凭借与特朗普的私人关系，推动放宽对华芯片出口，甚至嘲讽China Hawks的政策主张是shame。Rubio一直想搞黄仁勋，但是没有发动。

而导火索是11月3日的中期选举，共和党史诗级惨败，丢掉两院。

Rubio与Vance早已被视为共和党两位潜在接班人。中期选举之后，共和党不得不重新回答一个问题：特朗普之后，究竟由谁定义共和党的路线？

所以黄仁勋成了政治牺牲品，而这可能只是多米诺骨牌的第一张。

后面更严峻的党内和科技圈清算还在路上。

text:
Launch costs are about to get absolutely insane.

Over the past couple of days at Starbase, watching Starship and talking with investors and space founders, I heard and read some fascinating perspectives. Here's a sum up:

@pronounced_kyle said, Starship, carrying 100 tons of payload, costs roughly $1 million in propellant per launch. With full reusability, that translates to a fuel cost of just $10/kg.

Suddenly, @elonmusk ’s target of $100/kg doesn’t sound particularly ambitious.

Fun fact: shipping a computer from California to Australia by air could eventually cost more than sending it into space.

@PhilipJohnston The founder of @Starcloud_ , the orbital data center company, said SpaceX charging a premium is not a big problem. As long as the price stays around $500/kg, or five times the target cost, he’s happy with it. Falcon 9 currently charges roughly three times its cost.

When I met the Starcloud team at the NYSE Space Summit in May, the company was valued at around $1 billion. Now it’s worth $2.3 billion.

He’s even considering paying extra to charter entire Falcon 9 launches next year. Launch capacity is becoming a serious bottleneck.

@zebulgar offered a very different perspective. He said that ever since he started working on Varda, Falcon 9’s commercial launch price hasn’t gone down. So whenever he sees people talking about how many times Starship will reduce launch costs, he finds it amusing.

In a market dominated by a single player, what makes you think you have any pricing power?

Cost is cost. Price is price.

@ycombinator approached it from another angle: What we should really be thinking about is what becomes commercially viable in space when launch costs fall by 100x.

And we should start building those companies today, rather than waiting for launch prices to come down.

In fact, this is the very first topic in YC’s latest Requests for Startups.

But launch economics are only half the story. The satellites themselves are getting dramatically better, too.

On this flight alone, Starship deployed 26 @Starlink V3 satellites, each with a design capacity of 1 Tbps, for a combined 26 Tbps.

And eventually, a fully loaded Starship could deploy 60 V3 satellites in one flight, delivering 60 Tbps of additional capacity.

Higher payload capacity.
Lower launch costs.
More powerful satellites.
Higher launch frequency.

These four variables don’t add up. They multiply.

When the cost of accessing space falls by 100x, it won’t just transform the aerospace industry. It will redefine the entire space economy.

这两天 BTC 跌到 6.2 万美元，有人说币安上个月被盗了 63 亿美元，这次是故意把市场砸下来，好低价把币买回去。

我去翻了下成交数据，发现这几天现货卖得最凶的，反而是 Coinbase。

11 月 9 日到 14 日（UTC），四家交易所的 BTC 现货成交里，Coinbase 主动卖出的量比主动买入多了约 8,900 枚 BTC，币安是 3,100 枚，Bybit 是 700 枚，OKX 则是主动买入多了 1,400 枚。Coinbase 的差额接近币安的 3 倍，那一周 Coinbase 上的 BTC 还平均折价 0.13%。

周日早上跌到 61,946 美元那一脚，要单独看。上面这组数据没覆盖到那个低点。Coinbase 当时一小时成交了约 3,400 枚 BTC，是前三天小时成交量中位数的 6.4 倍。确实放了大量，但要看谁先打下去，得把几家交易所同一时间的逐笔成交摊开看。

我更在意的是钱往哪走。美国现货 BTC ETF 上周五个交易日天天净流出，一共 10.65 亿美元。截至 11 月 14 日，美元稳定币的流通量，7 天少了 44.4 亿美元，30 天少了 163.9 亿美元。把 USDT 从交易所提到自己钱包，市场上的 USDT 一枚都不会少。这次是整个市场的稳定币供应在缩，至于有多少最后换成法币出了圈，光凭这个数字算不出来。

再说币安。被盗是真的，补买资产也是币安自己说过的。但按币安 11 月 3 日披露的口径，到 10 月 31 日，受影响的代币已经补齐了约 98%。

所以我现在更倾向于这么看：Coinbase 现货卖压重，美国 ETF 在撤钱，稳定币供应也在缩水，这三件事都有数字。至于币安为了补窟窿先砸后买，我想先看看能对到币安自营账户的成交记录。

thoughts on this current price action and what I think is wrong with crypto markets;

before starting, obviously I was wrong not to flip bearish/neutral at 80-85k, however my system remained bullish on HTF and I'm not going against my system, don't care, I take the L, my system has made me and will make me 100x more in the future than any irrelevant losses here

that being said, I can now objectively commentate on the market with only spot holdings [that I don't touch until 2028-2029] from lower as my only skin in the game, I have a lot of stables waiting to deploy so red candles are whatever for me - here it goes;

we topped on what was initially over-exuberance in the markets, clearly visible by over-extention in AI, valuations that no longer make sense, inflation/hike concerns mostly due to Iran and idiosyncratic crypto factors most notably leverage/alts

decorrelation from a topping equity markets is something we could've counted on, but not with high conviction, for obvious reasons [decorrelation can only last so long]

the issue started, in my opinion, on the day Binance got "hacked". I'm using quotation marks because I highly doubt it was a hack

price action since then has been the single worst orderly selling I have ever seen. not even shadowy-BTC-sellers that turned out to be FTX 2022 can compare to this selling pressure. not even fucking close, by the way. I remember the markets in September/October 2022. before we knew about FTX hole, I felt the selling pressure on BTC specifically [this is why BTC bottomed lower than ETH that bear] weeks before FTX scandal. obviously, later I had an obvious retrospect moment of "ah, right, this was FTX selling BTC". again, as mentioned, current pressure is 5x worse at the very least. not a good look. pinpoint this as my 'option A'.

my 'option B' is not crypto nor equities/AI related. unfortunately, this one is grim. BTC historically has proven to be the most sensitive asset to whatever is going on with the world. remember Covid? first to drop. first to feel the pressure. same with both of the wars last 4 years. now, if this isnt Binance, then its something much worse. I'm not going to doom, but by this time next week I am convinced we will know whats going on. complete war escalation? US/EU grounds hit? power grid outages? AI hacks? even...a nuclear bomb? I don't know and I'm scared to find out. BTC doesnt sell like this if something is not horribly wrong behind the curtains. contrary to popular belief, I'm actually a positive individual, alas, seeing this doesn't inject much hope into my veins. realism prevails, as painful as it is

'option C' would be the least of our concerns - stocks have simply topped [my HTF system actually signals 6-24 month tops in all US equity indices], AI trade is rolling over and taking crypto with it. we can only hope it's ONLY this, and not Binance, which sets the industry back for years, or even worse, a global fallout in which case we have more concerning matters to worry about than our coins.

I hope its "nothing ever happens" and even if it does that governments will act accordingly [read; print money out of whatever issue there is]

if its Binance, then we simply deserve it.

author: etoeth
quoted_text:
Smith and Montesquieu thought that markets and commerce made us better: that they create an incentive to pursue self-improvement and to create things of value for others. In the positive AI visions, where the labor of humans is made redundant, I find myself wondering how we fare in the presumptive absence of these incentive gradients. Perhaps we are released to a life of freedom, where we can study Mozart and read Dickens, but that still seems complicated: both Mozart and Dickens were themselves deeply commercially-motivated in the production of their work, as were most of the great artists through human history. If the premise is that nobody will need to work or produce, how confident are we that we actually get the next Mozart and Dickens? The relevant question is not the partial equilibrium of whether one individual can pursue a life of enlightened leisure, but the general equilibrium of what form a society as a whole will take on.

One could maybe invoke Periclean Athens or the aristocratic gentleman scientists of Victorian England as a counterpoint. While these individuals were perhaps not motivated by commercial considerations, they were embedded in wider societies shaped by commerce, attendant betterment, and trade: Byron was himself upper class, but he was also surrounded by and writing for an educated bourgeois audience. So we’re back to the equilibrium question. Furthermore, even these individuals were surely motivated by a sense of high-stakes and consequential agency: if they did not apply themselves to their labors, they presumably believed that the work would not otherwise exist. Thucydides was addressing pressing military matters.

So I would like to read more optimistic cases from AI proponents about what a society (vs individual life) looks like if everything goes well: what people do, why they do it, whether humans achieve excellence (and in which domains), and which historical groups we should look to as relevant precedent.

One can perhaps imagine that humans will turn out to have a strong preference for work created by other humans. This may work in certain domains (ceramics?), but for how many will it actually apply? (I’m told that much of what is sold on indie crafts websites is now in fact manufactured in China.) It’s hard to see how this human preference, even if strong, would, for example, save scholarship.

Another idea would be to accept that nobody will become Einstein or Mozart or Byron, and that human excellence as such diminishes, but that there are compensatory benefits (planet brains and Dyson swarms?).

I believe that we can satisfy individual desires, but to what extent will we cultivate behavior worthy of admiration? Will a post-scarcity society mold capable and ambitious people? Which institutions will sustain them and which responsibilities will they have? I’d like to hear more of the equilibrium for the maximalist case spelled out.

text:
There’s an interesting market structure developing in cards/collectibles for a year+, where gacha websites create a source of demand for the asset class that behaves differently from traditional collectors.

A collector buys a card because they want to own it. A gacha company buys it because it helps sell packs, attract players or keep them gambling. Those incentives can support buying that wouldn’t necessarily happen at the same prices in a market driven purely by collectors.

What’s interesting is how the inventory works inside that loop.

You need desirable grails that people will chase. But less desirable cards can also be useful because people are more likely to sell them back and gamble again. The same slab returns to the pool and generates another round of paid play.

From that perspective, an attractive inventory mix could be a few grails surrounded by dogshit people will happily recycle. CC’s CEO said its lower tier assets typically turn over 55 times before someone holds onto them.

This raises two questions about how durable this demand actually is.

1- How long does the structural bid last?

Building and expanding these platforms requires buying inventory (altho some platform don't even buy their inventory now but rather borrow it from the owners). But once the pools are stocked, they mainly need to replace what people keep and support whatever growth comes next.

The grails might need regular replenishment. The rest can keep going around longer.

So gambling volume can stay healthy without the platforms continuing to buy cards at the same pace. The companies could keep doing well while their contribution to demand in the wider market slows down.

2- If card prices start going down, can we enter a small scale death spiral?

Lower card prices mean less valuable prizes and smaller buyback offers. If that makes people less interested in playing, platforms could reduce inventory purchases and weaken the structural bid

Lower prices, weaker activity, less buying, potentially more selling.

Cheaper inventory and adjusted pack prices could offset this, so it isn’t automatic. But it raises the question of how much of the market’s apparent strength depends on these operators continuing to expand.

People continuing to gamble and companies continuing to accumulate cards are two different assumptions. How much of today’s pricing depends on both?

Regardless if you own less desirable cards this is probably a once in a lifetime opportunity to get liquidity from them.

text:
I bet against this and I bet against Dwarkesh.

He conveniently sweeps under the rug that climbing a metric involves defining it. Then, supposing you define it (in a way that avoids Goodharting, reward hacking, etc), you need data/envs, which do the lifting. On defining good metrics - this is most of the game of making AGI (converting fuzzy concepts to formalized objects you can climb without gaming, which requires costly fixes later). He elides the hard problem by saying 'AI will just automate data'.

How do you know whether a change belongs in your final recipe? You ablate at scale. When you make N changes, on even a subset of combinations, this compute cost is naively exponential. So, you need a faster signal to tell you when a task that isn't immediately verifiable improves end behavior. Finding that signal is the bottleneck, which doesn't seem to be helped by 'automating the great algorithmic thinker starting from the empty string on paper'.

text:
到底应该去哪里买「双币赢」？哪里的收益更高？交易所到底是怎么赚钱的？一口气跟大家讲清楚（超长干活，建议交易所同学看一下😎）

一、比特大陆和双币赢也有关系💻

第一次听说双币赢的时候，我简直惊为天人（ Callback 一下前两天的「合约拼盘😉」）

我说怎么会有人把一个复杂的金融衍生品，包装得这么简单易懂？这简直是一个天才的设计。

目前已经很难溯源到底是谁发明的，但最早大规模推广双币赢的，应该是吴忌寒的 Matrixport（以前矿机都是吴做的）

后来大概有一两年的时间，其他交易所都没有怎么跟进。因为那时候交易所太赚钱了，根本不屑于做这些衍生品（真地主家也没有余粮了）

直到后来 Binance 等交易所陆续跟进，双币赢才真正进入大众视野。

二、双币赢为什么是个好产品？🧐

大家都听过它的宣传：跌了可以抄底，涨了可以赚超额年化收益。

三、到底应该去哪里买？💰

双币赢本质上是一个期权工具，按理说，同样的标的、行权价和到期时间，各家交易所给出的收益应该大差不差。

但实际上，你去对比 OKX、Binance、Bitget、Bybit，就会发现它们之间的收益差距非常大。

为什么？

因为交易所对这个产品的定位完全不同。

📈 如果双币赢是我的主打引流款，那我就可以让出一部分利润，甚至主动补贴。

💰 如果它是我的变现款，那我就可以多赚一点。反正用户量足够大，能赚一点是一点。

这就导致同样的产品，不同交易所给出的收益完全不一样。

下面都是我的主观判断，不代表客观标准，大家参考就好。

第一，OKX：目前我认为最好的双币赢平台。

以前最好的其实是 Matrixport，没有之一。

但后来随着 FTX 爆雷，以及一系列行业事件的冲击，Matrixport 在这块的投入越来越少，现在也逐渐转向美股、港股等业务。

现在大家一提双币赢，很多人第一反应就是 OKX，但实际上这个产品并不是他们发明的。

为什么 OKX 做得最好？

我倾向于认为，它在这个产品上让出了比较多的利润，而且把双币赢收益和 VIP 等级进行了绑定。

你的 VIP 等级越高，拿到的收益就越高，甚至可能比其他交易所的普通用户高出好几个百分点。

但 OKX 真正厉害的，其实是 USDG 双币赢。

我倾向于认为，USDG 是一个超级引流款。

因为同样条件下，USDG 双币赢的收益往往比 USDT 更高，有时候能高出 10% 左右。（我不明白 OKX 为什么不宣传这个🤣）

这个差距其实相当有吸引力。

我猜测是 USDG 相关方给了一定补贴，加上 OKX 自己让出了一部分利润，才形成了这个结果。

所以在我观察的产品里，OKX 的 USDG 双币赢，目前收益是最高的，没有之一。

甚至有时候比 OKX 高等级 VIP 的其他双币赢产品还高。

第二，Binance：双币赢更偏向变现款。

你去观察 Binance 的产品布局，会发现一个很有意思的现象。

Binance 是超级头部交易所，它需要多元化发展。

除了现货、合约交易，还要有理财、衍生品等各种产品。

但它最核心的业务依然是交易。

所以我认为 Binance 对理财产品大概有两种策略。

1️⃣ 一种是用理财留住大户。

比如 U 本位理财、稳定币理财，以及各种针对大资金的产品。对于这些产品，Binance 是愿意投入资源的，因为它需要把大户留在平台上。

2️⃣ 但双币赢不太一样。

双币赢有大量散户参与，我认为 Binance 更多是把它当作一种盈利产品。

早些年我刚开始玩双币赢的时候，Binance 给出的收益真的非常差。

跟当时的 Matrixport 比，差距非常明显。

但 Binance 的用户量实在太大了，即使收益没有那么有竞争力，也有大量用户购买。

所以我认为，它在这个产品上赚了不少钱。

当然，现在 Binance 的双币赢已经比以前好很多了，只不过我依然不认为它是 Binance 最重视的核心产品。

第三，Bitget、Bybit：更重视散户运营，而不是双币赢。

Bitget 就比较有意思了。

它的双币赢有些报价其实也不错，大家看我发的截图就知道，比如 BTC 60,000 美元附近的行权价，有些产品给出的收益还是蛮高的。

但整体来看，我认为 Bitget 并没有把双币赢作为核心业务。

逻辑上也说得通。

像 OKX、Binance，这些平台有大量大户资金，所以它们会更加重视如何留住大户资产。

而 Bitget、Bybit 相对来说，更重视散户市场和运营活动。

比如更快地上线新产品、股票相关产品，以及各种热门资产。

它们更愿意把资源放在这些能够快速吸引用户的业务上。

相对而言，双币赢这种偏理财性质的衍生品，未必是它们最想投入资源的地方。

而且大户愿不愿意把大量资金长期放在这些平台，本身也是个问题。

所以你会发现，它们的运营活动很多，但双币赢的收益未必一直有竞争力。

四、最后总结一下 📝

不同平台给出的收益差异，很大程度上取决于它们到底想用这个产品来赚钱，还是用它来吸引资金。

如果是我的话，目前会优先选择 OKX 的 USDG 双币赢。

因为在我观察到的同等条件报价里，它的收益确实很有竞争力，甚至是最高的。

以上都是我的个人观察和判断，大家可以自己对比一下

手机打字，有不对的也可以指正🙏

Within the massive encirclement in Lahj Governorate, the Houthis have seized another operational opportunity and scored a major breakthrough.

The Houthis have again subdivided the large pocket, cutting off and surrounding disorganised Aden-aligned government troops left behind near Dhubab who failed to withdraw.

This gain stems from a breakdown in cohesion during the hasty retreat of the Giants Brigades: some units held their positions while others abandoned defensive lines, a lapse the Houthis exploited.

Furthermore, the Houthis have seized the volcanic plateau at the summit of Jabal Haraz. While Aden-aligned forces have theoretically recaptured the narrow southern coastal corridor, the highway is effectively impassable under Houthi fire from these high ground positions.

Vehicles can no longer traverse the route. Retreating troops must pull out slowly under intense fire in extremely hazardous conditions. Supply convoys from Aden cannot enter the pocket; resupply is only possible via airdrops and sea lift.

The Houthis are steadily compressing, fragmenting and reducing the Aden government forces trapped inside this huge encirclement. Unlike the Taiz theatre, where defenders are shielded by extensive urban fortifications and a million civilians, this coastal pocket in Lahj consists mainly of coastal desert and rolling hills with no pre-built comprehensive defensive works. The besieged forces are therefore in a perilous position.

If the Houthis ultimately annihilate the Aden government troops trapped in the pocket — even though a contingent has escaped these past two days — this will rank among the largest strategic encirclement-and-annihilation battles since World War II and could become a classic case study in military history.

We shall watch how this battle unfolds.

text:
I’ve decided to leave NVIDIA. There are a few things I want to say.

As a robotics engineer at NVIDIA, I have seen Jensen as much more than the company’s CEO.

I admire his willingness to invest in a future that was not yet obvious. He committed to CUDA long before the deep learning boom and positioned NVIDIA for AI before it became everyone’s priority. Those decisions helped build the infrastructure that powers today’s AI.

I have seen that same vision in physical AI: investing in robotics, sharing open-source tools and projects, and building computing platforms that bring AI into the physical world. This is the work I do every day—and a future I believe in.

But what matters most to me is the culture he helped build.

Engineers are encouraged to explore, take risks, and learn from mistakes. Jensen reads employees’ Top 5 emails, follows their work, and engages directly. In a company this large, that connection matters. It makes an individual engineer feel that their ideas can still be heard.

That is why this has been so disappointing.

I do not have all the facts surrounding the allegations, and I cannot prejudge the investigation. My admiration for Jensen does not put him above scrutiny.

What I find difficult to accept is having to come to terms with his departure before receiving an explanation that helps me understand it. What this means for our direction, our culture, and the people doing the work remains unclear to me.

I have felt that engineers’ perspectives matter here. On this decision, I have not felt heard. That gap has been more painful than I expected.

I understand that some information cannot be shared immediately. But that does not erase the feeling of being left outside a decision that affects the company we help build every day.

A company’s greatness comes from its leadership, its governance, and the people who turn its ambitions into reality. Employees’ trust and sense of belonging are part of that, too.

Jensen’s vision and the engineering culture he shaped were important reasons I wanted to stay. His departure led me to decide that my own chapter here should also come to a close.

I leave with sadness and gratitude. The colleagues I have worked with, and the work we believed in together, will always matter to me.

These are my personal views.

Anthropic公式が、AIの『スライドがダサい問題』を終わらせにきた。

その名は「pptx」（スライド作成スキル）。

→ タイトルの下に、お決まりの線
→ 文字がはみ出したまま

pptxスキルは、これを根元から変える。

AIに、作り始める前に「誰に見せる資料か」を考えさせ、配色・文字・ページの作りまで決めさせる。

使い道に合わせて、資料の作りごと変わる。
→ 投資家向け：勢いと数字で押す
→ 経営会議：重厚で信頼感

→ 採用説明会：親しみやすく温かい
→ 社内研修：すっきり見やすい

グラフも表も、PowerPointの部品のまま出てくる。
だから、数字を書き換えればそのまま仕事で使える。

3. 使い道と雰囲気を選ぶ

Our world is at a turning point, and like every turning point in history, the people living through it don’t know it yet.

In 1937, Berliners still went to work every morning.

I‘m not saying WW3. But I do think we’re at the start of a global reengineering. Things are breaking one after another, and Earth Online just loaded its next main quest:

THE GREAT REPRICING.

The economy gets worse from here. By the end of 2027, this week will feel like a light tickle.

A lot of people are scared, and I understand why. But I‘m very, very, VERY excited. And you should be too.

If you’ve spent years feeling late to everything, priced out of the house, late to Bitcoin, late to AI, watching the same people win every round while you did everything “right”, there‘s a reason.

In calm times, whoever already has money and access just keeps compounding, and working harder rarely gets you a seat.

Chaos is when the seats open back up.

I bought my first Bitcoin in 2013, when most people had never heard of it. At the time I had no idea how insanely big it would become. It felt risky and even a little embarrassing to explain.

By the time it felt obvious, the cheap seats were gone. I can feel that same kind of moment starting again.

If you’ve ever really loved someone, you know the fastest way to hate a person is to love them first. Nobody else can hurt you that deeply, because nobody else ever got that close.

Disaster and opportunity live that close too, and most people only find out which one they were holding after it‘s gone.

Stagflation gave us Microsoft and Apple. The Great Depression gave us HP. The 2008 crash gave us Airbnb, Uber and Bitcoin.

While the world was locked inside during the pandemic, OpenAI released GPT-3 and Anthropic was founded. Every one of them made its move while everyone else was scared.

In more than a decade of trading, I’ve been liquidated three times. Each time I was sure it was the end of me. And each time, I came back stronger in every way that counts, including my account. I made back far more than I ever lost. If I had believed those moments were the end, the person writing this wouldn‘t exist.

Now the whole world is heading into its own version of that moment.

And I don’t think this window stays open long. My guess is about two years. Building at the frontier already takes billions of dollars of compute, and whoever owns the models, the chips, and the data gets stronger every quarter.

As AI keeps compounding for the people who already control it, the wall around them gets taller, and no amount of talent gets you over it.

Maybe I‘m wrong about how fast, and it’s four or five years instead of two. But I‘d bet this is one of the last big reshuffles in the next few decades where an outsider can still break in.

So use it. If you can build, build.

If you don’t know how to build, get your ass off that bed and learn, because in this era anyone can.

If you trade, keep cash ready, stay patient, and buy when everyone else is desperate to sell. And if you short, do it carefully, because no bear market only goes down and the bounces are brutal. Or do both. There‘s still time to get that cash ready.

Every disaster has a door in it.

Most people only see the fire.

YOU👏WALK👏THROUGH👏IT👏

text:
Today, one validator decides the order of each Solana block.

Two Solana Foundation researchers, Quentin Kniep and @TheWattenhofer, have published a design where nobody does.

Their paper is called New Constellation. Instead of one leader per slot, three proposers in the same city each build a block every 50 milliseconds.

Validators then merge those blocks into a single order, sorted by the priority fee each transaction pays. No proposer gets to decide what comes first.

The blocks stay hidden while they are built. Each proposer encrypts its block, swaps a signed fingerprint with the other two, and only then reveals the key. No proposer can see the others' transactions before its own block is locked.

That is where the censorship resistance comes from. In the paper's words, unless a slot is skipped, a transaction "only needs one non-censoring proposer among the proposers of a slot to be included."

The name needs a footnote. Anza published a different design called Constellation in March, with both authors among its writers. That one used a leader, a layer of attesters and synchronised clocks. The new paper says its design "differs fundamentally."

For validators, the big change is location. Proposers must sit within about 10ms of each other, in city hubs. The paper suggests starting with New York, Frankfurt, Tokyo and London, and estimates 3.7% of today's stake would sit outside any hub.

It is a research paper for now, with no activation date. It builds on Alpenglow, the consensus protocol Solana switched to on 21 October.

Two companion proposals from the same authors, SIMD-0674 and SIMD-0675, are already open: one registers where validators are, the other builds a leader schedule around geography.

This is CONCERNING.

Big Tech is BURNING cash like never before.

Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft spent $203 BILLION on capex last quarter, more than the $175 BILLION their businesses generated.

A year ago the same four spent $98 BILLION.

Free cash flow last quarter:

1. Amazon: minus $34.9 BILLION

2. Alphabet: minus $9.1 BILLION

3. Meta: minus $2.1 BILLION

4. Microsoft: plus $18.6 BILLION

Together they went from about $61 BILLION of free cash to about minus $27 BILLION.

Before this year, Alphabet had NEVER posted negative free cash flow in its 22 years as a public company.

It has now done it two quarters in a row.

So where does $203 BILLION in three months actually go?

Most of it is going into the race to build AI.

Amazon says its cash outflow "primarily reflects investments in artificial intelligence."

At Alphabet, about 65% went on servers and networking gear and 35% on the data centers that house them.

And why would four of the richest companies on earth spend more than they earn?

Because customers are lining up for AI computing power faster than they can build it.

Google Cloud revenue DOUBLED to $30.7 BILLION.

Amazon's cloud unit grew 39% to $46 BILLION, and CEO Andy Jassy expects growth of "over 40%" in both 2027 and 2028.

Alphabet's cloud backlog stands at $561 BILLION.

For three of the four, cash from the business no longer covers the spending, so they are borrowing to keep building.

Amazon raised $48.1 BILLION of debt in the quarter.

Alphabet sold $28.7 BILLION of bonds and $12.4 BILLION of new shares.

And none of them is slowing down.

Amazon plans about $220 BILLION of capex this year, Alphabet up to $205 BILLION and Meta up to $145 BILLION.

The bet is simple: spend now, earn it back from AI later.

Nobody knows yet if that bet pays off.

刚看了下 GATE 对于冻结事件的公告，我觉得大家都不要人云亦云，应该更多的看事情的经过发展和证据链。

首先我觉得这件事就一个原则：

如果资金确实涉及诈骗，被执法机关依法要求冻结、追缴并返还受害者，没有问题，当前任何一家交易所要在主流社会立足，配合执法机关是必须要遵守的一点。

但同时，用户的资产也应该获得充分的保护，如果用户合法持有的资产只是因为资金链路关联而被冻结，同样需要得到充分的程序保护。

所以双方是否应该加强一下沟通？这件事还是有一些可圈可点的地方，或者是不有什么误会？

首先 Gate 没有直接划转资产，并且持续要求补充证据、引入当地律师，这些做法是值得肯定的，某种程度上在为用户考虑，这是交易所应该有的态度。

但我觉得，与此同时，平台也应该进一步说明：最初的冻结依据是什么？涉案资金与用户资产之间有什么可验证的联系？为什么需要限制整个账户？用户是否获得了充分的申诉机会？用户涉案金额是多少？如果涉案金额远远少于冻结资金能不能把大部分资金先解封？

如果能做到这些，说的清楚，我相信大家肯定也无话可说，甚至会为 GATE 点赞。

合规，是交易所必须承担的责任，我非常同意这一点，但司法调查需要被尊重，合法财产权也需要被尊重。

希望最终由证据和法律程序给出答案，而不是由任何一方的舆论声量决定结果。

quoted_text:
I’ve decided to leave NVIDIA. There are a few things I want to say.

As a robotics engineer at NVIDIA, I have seen Jensen as much more than the company’s CEO.

I admire his willingness to invest in a future that was not yet obvious. He committed to CUDA long before the deep learning boom and positioned NVIDIA for AI before it became everyone’s priority. Those decisions helped build the infrastructure that powers today’s AI.

I have seen that same vision in physical AI: investing in robotics, sharing open-source tools and projects, and building computing platforms that bring AI into the physical world. This is the work I do every day—and a future I believe in.

But what matters most to me is the culture he helped build.

Engineers are encouraged to explore, take risks, and learn from mistakes. Jensen reads employees’ Top 5 emails, follows their work, and engages directly. In a company this large, that connection matters. It makes an individual engineer feel that their ideas can still be heard.

That is why this has been so disappointing.

I do not have all the facts surrounding the allegations, and I cannot prejudge the investigation. My admiration for Jensen does not put him above scrutiny.

What I find difficult to accept is having to come to terms with his departure before receiving an explanation that helps me understand it. What this means for our direction, our culture, and the people doing the work remains unclear to me.

I have felt that engineers’ perspectives matter here. On this decision, I have not felt heard. That gap has been more painful than I expected.

I understand that some information cannot be shared immediately. But that does not erase the feeling of being left outside a decision that affects the company we help build every day.

A company’s greatness comes from its leadership, its governance, and the people who turn its ambitions into reality. Employees’ trust and sense of belonging are part of that, too.

Jensen’s vision and the engineering culture he shaped were important reasons I wanted to stay. His departure led me to decide that my own chapter here should also come to a close.

I leave with sadness and gratitude. The colleagues I have worked with, and the work we believed in together, will always matter to me.

These are my personal views.

text:
现在到底应该不应该买Ai行业
应该不应该买入稳定币龙头crcl
先确认下这一个标的成长过程中的几个阶段
然后把各种带入其中
就像先搞明白人的生老病死
知道一个人的年龄
才好预测他未来可能的行为

它是婴儿还是儿童
还是少年还是中年还是老年
我们来梳理下
先看看行业发展的过程

1、发现阶段
前几年我买入3-4千亿美金英伟达的时候
几乎是全网最早喊英伟达会破万亿
会超过苹果谷歌成为市值第一的企业
那个时候是发现阶段

那个时候我们的看法是未来的竞争
企业和企业国家和国家
缺的是算力
这个算力不是cpu而是gpu
新能车的无人驾驶是gpu而不是cpu
我是从这里走进去AI的门口
找到了英伟达

后面很多人发现光模块存储各种
买入可能都赚了很多倍比英伟达还多
这些市场我没有发现他们
不是我的能力圈

发现这个阶段胜率并不高
完全看你相信什么
比如此刻的crcl
就处在这个阶段
你信不信gpu 能带领Ai带来科技革命
信不信稳定币行业是支付行业的范式转移
这个时候能给你提供的数据支撑很少
你很难定量分析
你只能定性分析
这个阶段风险最高回报最高

2、成长阶段
很多人把成长阶段当做发现阶段
三星海力士在业绩开始起飞之后
赚的是成长的钱了
英伟达1.5万亿到6万亿这段
也是成长的钱
它每个季度财报都超预期
营收和利润都在增长
市值不断提升
现在crcl还没有进入这个阶段

发现阶段是比较难看到的
但成长阶段是可以用定量筛选出来的
财报后就继续拿着
业绩开始不及市场的增长预期
股价也开始放缓甚至回落
这是大多数基金机构开始进入的阶段
风险较低回报也还行

3、信仰阶段
当所有的业绩都已经预期到位
甚至开始透支很多年以后
这个阶段是那些在发现和成长阶段忽视的人
开始上车的时候了
终于被这些宏达叙事所说服
但市场剩下的涨幅已经非常有限
这个阶段风险最高回报最低

btc就已经走完了发现和大部分成长阶段
现在进入了纯信仰阶段

有人说你买crcl难道不是信仰阶段吗
不是
在没有数据支撑前的相信就发现
在数据兑现之后已经没有增长空间了
你依然还相信它继续“增长”
那才是“信仰”

现在依然愿意去买存储那些周期股的
大部分都是“信仰”了
因为业绩已经透支
随着产能开始爬坡价格下跌
企业的盈利增速会下降
甚至盈利总额也会下降
我并不是今天说这句话
而是今年5-6-7股价最高峰的时候就这样说了

4、AI现在到底是哪个阶段
对于英伟达而言
现在已经走进成长阶段的后半程
存储和光模块那些走到了信仰阶段
英伟达有定价权
企业的营收暂时不会陷入周期性变化
但存储光模块那些市场竞争激烈
随着产能扩森行业原先的周期规律还会体现

5、那现在应该买入Ai行业吗
AI行业其实非常庞大
英伟达是 三星海力士美光也是
但他们可能出在不同的时期
我先回答
现在肯定应该买入Ai行业
但可能不是你说的那几只股票

随着AI基建行业走入过热甚至回落
AI应用行业开始崛起
他们从发现阶段走到了成长阶段
现在最具确定性的
就是Anthropic Opneai Deepseek这些

如果我们回顾互联网这轮产业革命
从2000年泡沫开始破裂
到后面互联网龙头企业创造千亿美金营收
股价涨了几百上千倍
真正的底部是从to c端企业盈利开始的

今年10月中Anthropic走到了盈利的门口
虽然增速放缓但整体实现了盈亏平衡
互联网时代的三个细分市场社交电商和搜索
在AI应用端已经开始呈现出
聊天机器人 OpenAI
代码编程 Anthropic
视频生成 Seedance
其中ANT率先实现盈利

但不幸的是AI行业to c的成长阶段
刚好赶上了AI行业to b的信仰阶段
所以我们看到了半导体这一个月以来的暴跌

但事实这恰恰是AI作为整个行业成长阶段你的开始
以to c端企业盈利为标志
本次AI行业的大爆发
可能不会再有2000年的崩盘泡沫了

人类社会其实也是在不断发现问题
修改缺陷的
这次还没等到基建崩盘
to c的企业就开始盈利
参考互联网行业
相当于如果2000年的时候
腾讯阿里谷歌亚马逊就开始盈利了
那还会有互联网泡沫崩盘吗

6、我的结论
现在是买入AI行业的好时机
我们现在相当于是在2004年买入互联网龙头
那个时候买入互联网指数
买入腾讯阿里谷歌亚马逊微软那些
你在未来十年都是躺赚

买入OpneAI Anthropic Seedance Deepseek
相当于在2004年买入了中美互联网龙头
大模型是还没有分出胜负
但优势现在已经进入叠加时代
决赛圈已经出现
没有进入决赛圈的选手才是危险的
已经进入决赛圈的选手是应该下注的

如果不能确定到底买哪家
买入QQQ就是最好的
或者未来会有更窄的Ai应用端指数etf
指数会自动筛进入决赛圈的成长阶段企业
盈利的胜率会提高但赔率会降低
目前看直接买这四家胜率还是很高的

又有人说了ANT上市就14000亿美金了
当年互联网企业龙头上市才多少估值呢
这恰恰是这些龙头企业的价值
那些几百亿美金的企业未来生存下去都难
但这些万亿美金的
是有可能成为垄断标的的
他们的估值也依然有十倍甚至几十倍空间
当年互联网企业上市的时候
谁又不是市梦率呢

7、文章内容有点长
我把结论长话短说
crcl出于支付范式转移成长阶段应该买入
大模型头部几家企业
属于Ai应用端的成长阶段应该买入

AI指数（可能暂时还没有标的）
和QQQ属于长期成长阶段
可以定投长期持有

Many are asking why are we supporting $EVAL, and how does it benefit base:0xff8104251e7761163fac3211ef5583fb3f8583d6 holders?

At @reppo, our goal is simple and consistent - maximize the impact of every dollar generated through trading fees and protocol revenue for base:0xff8104251e7761163fac3211ef5583fb3f8583d6 holders. 

When we direct buybacks towards $EVAL, we can have a greater impact on its supply while simultaneously driving demand for $REPPO.

Since $EVAL is paired with $REPPO, buying REPPO to acquire EVAL creates buy pressure on REPPO and adds REPPO to the liquidity pool.

The EVAL we buy back is then burned, permanently reducing its supply and $REPPO is taken out of supply and stays in the LP.

$EVAL isn’t a competing token. It’s another economic engine for the Reppo ecosystem.

All value accrues to $REPPO , directly and indirectly.

Two tokens. One ecosystem. Aligned incentives.

text:
让 Grok Bot 撸积分，自动注册并完成交易，42 自动交互教程。

前几天讲了 Grok Bot，这两天拿 @42_mandarin 跑了个实例：注册账号、收邮箱验证码、创建钱包，再接入 Clawby 完成交易，整套流程都让它做。

我投入了 39 美元，每轮用 5 美元交互，另外准备一点 BNB 付 Gas。
录视频时跑了七百多美元交易量，累计磨损 11.34 美元。本金可以反复用，手续费和滑点会不断消耗。

这次通过 Clawby 操作，是因为符合条件的交易最高能拿 1.5 倍积分。
目前还在前几周，我愿意拿小钱试试，后面参与的人多了，再看成本是否划算。

操作思路很简单：
把完整教程发给 Grok Bot，让它先读懂，完成注册、绑定 Clawby、铸造身份 NFT，再充值测试。

先跑 5 轮，检查成交、余额和实际磨损，确认没问题再继续。
每次只开一个仓位，不做无限授权，设好累计止损；交易卡住先查旧交易，避免重复下单。

还有个容易漏掉的地方：Grok Bot 用量快耗尽时，要提前停止开仓，处理剩余头寸。
别让它买完之后没额度卖，最后留着仓位等重置。

任务在云服务器上跑，我的电脑不用一直开着。但钱包私钥也存在云端，所以我只放小额测试资金。

积分先按零估值，花掉的磨损是真金白银。
自动化省下了操作时间，能不能赚回来，还得等最后的奖励。
后面成本不合适，我就不刷了。

个人实测，仅供参考，DYOR。

I believe the crypto tokens that retain the most value will be those powering the financial infrastructure behind these markets, rather than the endless cycle of speculative assets we see today.

We’re leveraging Uniswap v4 hooks to build infrastructure specifically optimized for stock token trading and future onchain IPOs, including programmable liquidity, dynamic fees, automated liquidity management, efficient price discovery, and customizable launch mechanics.

All of this will run through StonkBrokers smart contract infrastructure, allowing teams to operate independently branded DeFi businesses while benefiting from audited, battle-tested financial infrastructure.

You own your frontend, your brand, your domain, and your customer experience. We power the underlying financial rails.

I believe the next generation of onchain finance will be built by thousands of independent operators, banks, businesses, and communities, many of whom won’t have the technical resources to develop their own smart contracts.

Our goal is to remove that barrier entirely. Instant On-Chain Financial Franchise.

text:
At this point in the market, many assets look oversold. Everyone who rotated into stables will try to time the bottom, but very few will catch it. That’s why I recommend DCAing into spot and carefully managed perps via @MancerXYZ.

More importantly, we’re seeing trading, LPing and market making increasingly move onchain, bringing greater transparency to liquidations and execution.

I believe onchain options will be a major unlock for market stability.

For example, exercising a $1M ITM ETH put settled in USDG creates ETH selling pressure, while the counterparty or market maker may need to buy ETH to settle or rebalance. Calls create the opposite exposure. These flows generate trading activity, LP fees and continuous hedging demand.

With sufficient liquidity, this activity can help absorb volatility, although poorly managed hedging can amplify it.

Deeper options liquidity could ultimately reduce extreme price swings and strengthen crypto’s credibility as a store of value.

This is why StonkBrokers Options Vaults and STORM are my #1 priority.

Our scaling model follows what Hyperliquid demonstrated with perps: let teams integrate our infrastructure into their own frontends, set custom fees and build businesses around it.

We’ll extend this across our entire DeFi suite, including options, DEXs, smart LP vaults and launchpads, with codeless deployments and custom domains.

GOOGLE JUST AUTOMATED RESEARCH PAPERS 🤯

It is called PaperOrchestra.

A multiagent framework that writes submission ready scientific papers from scratch.

You input a raw idea and experimental logs.

The system takes over entirely.

It uses a swarm of specialized agents to handle the workload:

> lead researcher writes the outline
> literature review agent prioritizes sources
> plotting agent generates visuals from code
> reviewer agent forces autonomous revisions

The output is a fully formatted LaTeX manuscript.

This drops the cost of producing scientific literature to zero.

The peer review system is already overloaded.

Now anyone can generate perfectly formatted research at scale.

text:
Important message for the @LayerZero_Core community, developers, and everyone planning to degen on November 30.

Before you make your plans, there is something important you need to understand about the upcoming ATLAS launch.

According to information shared by the LayerZero team, ATLAS will NOT launch with a permissionless DeFi environment.

What does this mean?

If you’re a developer planning to build and deploy DeFi protocols, launchpads, permissionless applications, or other on-chain projects, you should be aware that this type of environment will not be available at launch.

There is another important detail: LayerZero is unlikely to introduce a generalized EVM environment in the foreseeable future.

In other words, don’t expect an open EVM ecosystem where anyone can deploy smart contracts, launch new protocols, create permissionless applications, or experiment with their own DeFi ideas.

And what does this mean for everyone planning to degen on November 30?

If you’re expecting a new ecosystem full of permissionless DeFi opportunities, new launchpads, and projects launching one after another, you should adjust your expectations.

The November 30 launch is focused on different infrastructure, not on opening a generalized EVM environment to developers.

This doesn’t mean these possibilities are off the table forever. The LayerZero team has simply made it clear that this is not part of its foreseeable plans.

So, developers and degens, do your own research and understand what you’re actually getting into before November 30.

It’s better to know the direction of the ecosystem now than to build expectations around something that isn’t coming anytime soon.

text:
financial mkts never trade on yesterday’s emotions. they only trade on tomorrow’s consensus and liqs.

i know the recent price action has left many of you disappointed in btc and exhausted by the broader crypto market. plenty of ppl have taken real financial hits and heavy portfolio drawdowns. but rn is the worst time to give in to despair. respect the cycle. washouts and dried-up liq are just part of how this mkt evolves. it was like this in 2015, 2018, 2022, and now in 2026. it will be the exact same thing the day btc gets cut in half from $1m to $500k.

true core assets always earn their place in the rubble when no one is paying attention. keep believing in btc’s future, but rn, conviction needs strict discipline to back it up. don’t touch leverage, and don’t use fragile debt to bet on a cycle bottom. stay away from altcoins and drop the get-rich-quick fantasies. hold on to your core spot positions, and keep enough cash flow to live your life comfortably. in a brutal market, survival is always priority number one.

btc has a way of finishing its shakeouts through total despair, starting the next chapter only when sentiment is completely frozen. time is the fairest filter, and the dawn will eventually reward those who actually make it through the cycle. until daybreak, stay patient.

don’t give up on yourself right before the sun comes up.

text:
这次我是真的输了

BTC 11 号还收在 74,015，今天早上破 62,000，4 天跌了 16%，抹掉了这轮启动的90%涨幅。

从高点 87,396 算，已经回撤 32%。

这次的资产回撤，比去年 1011 那次还大。

那天我以为之后都不会有那么难受的时刻了，结果这次更狠，没有一根针，没有什么消息，是一天一天往下走，每天都给你一点反弹的希望，再把你按下去。

都说币圈是粪坑，不止一次想离开这个粪坑。

每次大跌完都跟自己说，算了，回去老老实实拿美股不香吗？

然后过几个月又回来了

原因很简单，这里的收益是真的诱人，也最熟悉，一波行情能顶别的地方好几年，8月后的启动也确实完整吃到了

但我现在算明白了，诱人的是收益，要命的是盈亏比。

赚的时候赚几成，亏的时候一次吐回去，还要多搭一截。

以前大家都说，机构进场以后币圈会变成熟，波动会变小，结果呢，只变得更恶心了

上涨的时候，3 根大阳线，从 6 万直接拉到 8 万。

下跌的时候也一样，几天就跌完。

和机构搏杀难度确实肉眼可见的提高了

这次亏，不怪市场，怪我自己仓位和预期都太满。

我太相信牛市初期，急于把仓位上满，坚信回调就是上车机会。

事实证明我也太低估了，加密一直都是极端的市场，顶部和底部都是极致的情绪震荡

写这篇不是劝谁离场，也不是喊底。

就是记下来，下次再想冲的时候，先回来看看今天。这次回撤很痛，但每次痛苦可能是资金的下一个晋升台阶，1011之后很绝望，但也在今年通过做美股资产新高，只是今天又把盈利又还给市场了，但至少我还活着就有希望，只是重新开始罢了

AI 教父、诺贝尔奖得主 Geoffrey Hinton 透露：去年夏天，他曾前往上海，与习近平的亲信、中国政治局委员会面。

他认为，中国高层对超级人工智能风险的理解，比美国政府更深刻。

“在超级人工智能问题上，我认为中国和美国的利益其实是一致的，双方最终会展开合作。中国共产党不希望超级人工智能取代中国共产党的统治。”

“去年夏天，我去了上海，与一位政治局委员进行了交谈。他是习近平的亲信。我认为，中国政治局对这些问题的理解远远超过美国政府。他们非常担心这些风险，也愿意与美国合作，防止超级人工智能接管一切。”

“但只要白宫里还坐着一个……该怎么说呢，或许是一个腐败、年老昏聩、有重罪前科的人，这种合作就不会发生。所以，未来两年内不会有这样的合作。但最终，我们会迎来一个理性的美国政府。我相信它会与中国合作，共同避免超级人工智能失控的风险。”

“就像20世纪50年代，美国与苏联合作，试图避免氢弹带来的危险一样。”

Bloomberg: Bitcoin Falls Toward $62K, Putting $58K Yearly Low Back in Focus  

According to Bloomberg, Bitcoin fell toward $62,000 over the weekend, its lowest level since July, as higher Treasury yields, a stronger dollar, post-midterm policy uncertainty and continued fallout from the Binance hack weighed on crypto markets.   

FalconX co-head of markets Joshua Lim said discussion around the selloff has focused on nearly $20 billion in stablecoin balance declines over the past month and the potential liquidity impact of Anthropic’s upcoming IPO. Bloomberg noted Bitcoin is again approaching its 2026 low near $58,000.

text:
Multipli基金会上线了。
这项目之前已经在Coinbase旗下Sonar平台完成的$MULT公售，当时有2.5亿美元和1亿美元两档估值，融了2000多万的协议，ba+cb都有投资、Sonar公募、@base 生态，币安系一路都走过来了，上所方面应该也不会差，码住看看表现吧。

1、做什么的
@multiplifi 是主打机构业务的链上收益聚合协议，可以理解为 RWA 资管协议。它主要做两件事：帮资金找收益，帮资产释放流动性。

收益端的核心产品是 xToken。稳定币、BTC 等资产可以通过它参与收益策略，用户持有相应的收益凭证，参与对冲套利等策略。

流动性端的核心产品是 rwaUSD。符合条件的代币化黄金、国债等资产可以拿来抵押，在对应的风控参数下铸造 rwaUSD，再接入借贷、流动性池等 DeFi 场景。

以黄金为例，抵押代币化黄金铸造 rwaUSD之后，不用卖掉黄金就能拿到美元流动性，参与 DeFi。

2、业务前景
Ondo以美债上链被大家熟知，之后又做了ondoperp实现产品生态闭环，算是从一个发行角色到发行与交易的叠加，

而Multipli想做的还是让这些已经上链的资产，可以继续拿来抵押、借钱、参与收益策略。不同机构发行的资产，托管方式、赎回规则都不一样。Multipli试图通过rwaUSD，把符合条件的资产接入同一套抵押框架，往全球RWA流动性层这个方向做，有点下一代RWA叙事的样子。

我理解下来是一个做资产发行，一个做流动性通道，发行方掌握资产来源，流动性平台连接资金需求，倒是以后链上的RWA越来越多，谁能捕获更多价值？除了接资产已经释放流动性之后，defi场景不明朗的情况下，其实当前市场给出了答案，就是一定要有交易闭环，市场或者说赌场才是最高利益的地方。

3、机构业务是重点
Multipli的重点是机构业务，协议主要tvl贡献面向机构的rwaUSDi产品，这部分涉及的机构资产管理人，都需要做机构身份审核，并且这里和普通用户持有的收益凭证是分开的。
目前披露的策略合作方包括野村旗下LaserDigital、EdgeCapital、Fasanara、Spartan等知名机构。这些机构都是在资管领域非常知名的，都有一套非常成熟的风控及资管系统，这么看其实Multipli就相当于资金上链及通道。

很多项目方的发币时机都选得不太好。经过这波大跌，希望流动性能慢慢恢复。只有赚钱效应起来了，资金和信心才会逐渐回来。

text: I am selling my beautiful Bored Ape for $10,700 after buying it for $578,000 around 5 years ago.  I have made the extremely difficult decision to leave the Bored Ape Yacht Club, and below is my reason why:  Today, I went to the BAYC meetup here in New Jersey to meet my fellow Apes. We have been through a lot this past couple of years, so it would be good to meet other community members IRL and bond with them. Or so I thought.  When I got to the venue, there were only 4 other guys there. No problem. It's a cozy setting and I would love to get to know these Apes on a deeper level.  We sat down at a table, got a few beers, and started talking. Most of our chatter revolved around BAYC and crypto, of course. Naturally, the topic of memecoins came up, as they've been the talk of the town this entire year.   I've profited 8.5 SOL ($2,050) this year trading memecoins, so I was excited to talk about them as I've been doing well for myself.  And that's when it all went downhill.  One of the guys sitting at the table (I will not name him, for the sake of our community) told me I should buy a memecoin called "The Black Bull" if I don't have any.  When he said that, my body filled with a bout of rage. I felt like Rosa Parks being asked to give up my seat on the bus.  I excused myself and immediately left the venue. I am sitting at home now, writing this post. I haven't stopped shaking since I heard those words.  Since when is it okay to tell a white man to buy a token called "The Black Bull"? Why do we continue to allow white folk to oppress, mock, and belittle us in this way?  Why is it allowed to create cryptocurrencies with a racial slur in the name? How can we stop this nonsense? Where is the cyber police and why haven't they taken any action against the Solana blockchain for the existence of these tokens?  It pains me to say this, but Apes together are no longer strong.  I will be listing my Bored Ape tomorrow at 6 ETH. I have attached an image of my Ape to this post for any interested buyers.

I'm bullish on #Anthropic (as a company, revenue side). If this is really the valuation the market is discussing right now, I think it's seriously undervalued. I would buy.

This is company analysis. Last week's #NVIDIA news left me pretty sour on @AnthropicAI as a company, and that is this week's talking point. It does not change this analysis.

At first glance, people see revenue growing very fast and a GAAP loss, and they assume costs are very high. But a substantial part of that is liability from past fundraising, debt-to-equity conversions, and equity appreciation. That is not the same as its real operating spend.

What is actually worth watching is how much cash it is putting in, relative to current revenue, ARR, and the growth rate. From a startup point of view, I think this kind of capital-efficient growth is unlike anything I've seen.

So I wouldn't just look at "how much is it still losing." The real question should be: to create one more dollar of new intelligence, revenue, and future earnings, how much does it actually need to burn?

text:
So where do we go from here? Much lower, most likely.

Debasement hedges have been hammered since the January highs: gold is down 10% YTD and 28% off its peak, BTC is down 26% YTD and 49% off its ATH.

That looks odd with inflation ramping, but these assets trade liquidity, not CPI. And liquidity is draining: the Fed, ECB, BoJ and BoE are all hiking.

To me the Fed is behind the curve. Markets now price 3 more hikes by March 2027, I think that's the floor.

Meanwhile the AI bubble has barely started to deflate: the Nasdaq 100 is only 13% off its October record, I still have a 22k target in the next few months.

BTC is one of the best global liquidity gauges we have. As central banks tighten around the world, liquidity falls and BTC falls with it.

Add to that the increasing odds of finding a critical vulnerability, too late, as AI gets smarter, and the quantum threat getting closer. 

In these conditions I'm now eyeing a new low to $39k, about -69% from the ATH, still a shallower drawdown than the last two bear markets. 

Confirmation once we take out the previous low and break down from the 82-58k range.

text:
Wintermute 年花1000万美元锁定 60 毫秒数据优势，在 Hyperliquid 累计盈利超 2 亿美元

Hyperliquid 有一套叫 gossip priority（读优先）的机制,每 3 分钟拍卖一次，出价最高的地址可以优先收到即将进入的订单数据。

⏰每个席位大约能降低 20 毫秒延迟，顶级席位叠加后，能比普通用户早大约 50-60 毫秒看到订单流

Loris Tools 的链上数据显示，过去一个月里，Wintermute 关联钱包在顶级席位上的胜率约 76%。他们为了维持这个位置，日均支出大约 2.6 万美元，年化接近 1000 万美元。

出价本身对所有人开放，但要真正拿到完整的 60 毫秒优势，需要满足额外条件：

🔺直接和 Foundation 节点做直连。而直连的要求是达到一定做市量（约全网 maker 成交量的 0.5%）
🔺质押至少 1 万枚 $HYPE

像Wintermute @wintermute_t 这种顶级做市商能轻松满足，而大多数中小做市商是没有资格的。

做市商的核心工作是挂单提供流动性，同时要避免被“毒性订单”吃到。有了这 60 毫秒的提前量，Wintermute 就可以做到：

1️⃣、提前撤单
看到大单即将进来，自己的报价还没被吃到之前，先撤掉。普通做市商 60 毫秒后才看到，撤单已经来不及，报价被打掉。

2️⃣、调整报价
提前知道订单流方向，马上把报价往更有利的位置移动，或者收紧/放宽点差。

3️⃣、跨所对冲
在 Hyperliquid 上提前看到大单，立刻在 Binance 或其他交易所反向对冲，把风险转走。等普通用户在 Hyperliquid 上反应过来时，价格已经动了。

Hyperliquid 本身设计是取消单优先于吃单，本意是保护做市商。但加上这 60 毫秒的“预览”，等于让付钱的人能更安全地利用这个规则：自己先撤，别人的报价还留在盘口被吃。

🎯对小做市商来说，这就是反复被狙击。他们看不到提前量，报价总是慢一步，被吃几次后只能放宽点差，或者直接关掉山寨币的做市机器人。最后订单簿变薄、点差变大，成本落在普通交易者身上。

这套机制在华尔街早已玩的炉火纯青，纳斯达克等传统交易所会出售离自己机房撮合引擎最近的机柜位置给高频交易公司。

逻辑和这套链上的拍卖机制是一样的：离撮合引擎越近，延迟越低，位置越好越贵。

不过Hyperliuid这种做法，此前曾遭社区质疑，优先费用机制的公平性，以及是否符合美国监管要求。

author: mikemaccana
quoted_text:
✨ From someone that lived in London for 15 years, here’s the favourites I’ll look forward to at Breakpoint next year. No offence to Brick lane and the British Museum✨

📚🍸Maison Assouline. A large format book store and cocktail bar. Great date venue. 

🪞⛏️The Wallace Collection. House with a substantial collection of French aristocratic art (the French sold their fancy items very quickly after the revolution) and, er, weapons. Crypto persons: the staircase balustrade has the first depiction of fiat currency in human history. 

🧀 Borough market and specifically the Kappa Casein cheese sandwich made with 5 types of cheese, butter and onions. Crunch though the bread and enjoy the warm gooey cheese inside. 

☕️🍂Watchhouse Hanover. Get a cuban cigar at the nearby Davidoff store, sit in the courtyard and enjoy it with a flat white and a raspberry chocolate brownie. For a proper brunch, try Ozone or Lantana. 

🏠🖼️ Robilant Voena - an Edwardian home converted to an art gallery and the gallerists/dealers have great taste. Also: Saatchi gallery. 

⏱️Watch room at Selfridges. More watches than the NY department stores and less stress than the diamond district. Includes vintage items. If you want boutiques they’re all together on Bond St 5 minutes away. 

✖️Klub Verboten. A European-style techno club. People in NY go to Box and watch someone else doing something wild. People in London go to KV and do something wild. Read the rules before buying a ticket.

😅🥊 1Rebel probably the best gym classes in the world. Everything from boxing to pilates, a thumping soundtrack, lit like a nightclub, they give you filtered water in metal bottles and fresh refrigerated face towels and sell protein shakes too. A bit like if you took the best bits of every gym class from the US (which they absolutely did). Do the Rumble class at Liverpool St - the bags are in concentric rings and you can quietly imagine battering the other class members. Honourable mentions to BXR (Anthony Joshua’s gym, also boxing oriented) and Gymbox. 

Ronnie Scott’s for jazz, Zima for vodka, Saddler’s Wells for the ballet, Hampstead Heath for getting away from it all.

text:
I've been combing forensically through the media reporting on the Jensen Huang debacle, and I'm shocked.

- New York Times directly claimed at least 11 times that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy.
- The Times is walking this claim back after U.S. intelligence would not corroborate it.
- If real, whoever handed over the alleged intelligence to the Times potentially violated the Espionage Act, unless authorized to do so.
- If Trump authorized it, why did he?
- If Trump did not authorize it, why did the official violate the Espionage Act -- potentially prosecutable as a felony?
- Who was the official who leaked the classified intelligence?
- Was it Rubio, who authored the memo on the original CIA brief, or was it someone else?
- Jensen Huang's apology for being unfaithful does not name Alice Huang, or anyone else.
- The media's characterization of Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang as being romantic is also based on anonymous intelligence, but is not established as fact.
- Wall Street Journal fabricated a claim that Singapore investigated Alice Huang for espionage, when Singapore actually investigated her for false claims; WSJ still has not retracted its false reporting.

Thus:

- Jensen Huang may have had an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, or he may not have.
- Alice Huang may be a Chinese intelligence asset, or she may not have been.
- According to third-hand accounts of the intelligence briefs, the U.S. government suspected that Alice Huang may be a Chinese asset for well more than a year.
- Yet, according to Trump's account, Jensen Huang had never been informed.
- Jensen Huang, therefore, is apparently being held accountable for an extramarital affair that he may not have had, with a woman who may not have been an intelligence asset, who he had never been told was or was not such an asset.
- This is nonsensical. How, after all, can he be held accountable for an affair with a Chinese intelligence asset (who might not actually be a Chinese intelligence asset) that the U.S. government knew about -- but did not warn him about?
- Is not the accountable party the U.S. government official who failed to warn him?

Or is he being held accountable for that affair?

- Remember, Jensen Huang acknowledged that he had been unfaithful, but not with whom.
- Is he being held accountable for another affair?
- Unnamed sources also mention an affair with a direct subordinate Kimberly Powell.
- This affair is again unconfirmed.
- A romantic relationship with a subordinate violates company policy.
- But the board actually has discretion about how to handle this. They could slap him on the wrist, impose some disciplinary regime, therapy, etc.
- But they didn't. So to say that they were obligated to remove him is not correct.
- We know that some members of the board were helicoptered in from Wall Street just 6 months before the ouster.
- What role did they play?
- Was the takeover by the board being planned far in advance of the reporting?

So they chose to remove him. Or did they?

- Jensen Huang resigned.
- This is not the same as the resignation being voluntary.
- What are the circumstances of his resignation?
- Was he forced to resign, or did he do so from exhaustion, or to protect his company?
- Furthermore, what was the flash point? Was it for the extramarital affair that may not have been one, with the Chinese intelligence asset, who may have not been an asset, that U.S. intelligence knew about but did not warn him about? Or was it about the affair with the subordinate that the board had discretion over?
- We do not know the answers to any of these questions.

- Unnamed sources, reported by Reuters, implicated a second Nvidia employee extramarital, also unconfirmed.
- Which affairs are real? Which are mere hearsay?
- How did this play into deliberations?

- The media continues unabated character attacks on Jensen Huang.
- Yet we also know that, for all the dirt that they try to dig up, most of it has remarkably little substance.
- Alice Huang may have smuggled some state-of-the-art (banned) chips into China.
- What did Jensen Huang know about this? We don't know that yet.
- If these chips were smuggled, objectively, these chips are still a drop in the bucket compared to the overwhelming compute advantage that the United States has over China.

Overall, the story is actually extremely thin, and we know remarkably less than the media implies.

And, in my opinion, that is the story itself: a full-on media assault on Jensen Huang in the court of public opinion, on the basis of remarkably little substance.

This reveals more about the media than it does about Jensen Huang. They want him gone.

But why? And how does this relate to the motives of the U.S. government official who leaked the Rubio memo about Alice Huang?

We also know:

One of the first reporters involved at the FT says that she was tipped off to this story by someone in the tech industry.

We have many more questions than answers.

Personally, and my opinion at this point is clearly partisan, but I smell a room full of rats.
