text:
Giving an AI agent a wallet is easy.

Giving it the right permissions is the hard part.

We're moving toward a world where AI agents can hire other agents, pay for services and execute tasks without someone clicking approve every five minutes.

Sounds great, right?

But there's a problem nobody should ignore.

What happens when an agent has more authority than it actually needs?

Imagine giving an AI agent access to $10,000 just to complete a $20 research task.

That's not autonomy. That's unnecessary risk.

Here's what I think the next generation of agent infrastructure needs:

❯ Spending limits: How much can an agent actually spend?

❯ Scoped permissions: Which services and contracts can it interact with?

❯ Time restrictions: When should its authorization expire?

❯ Human approval: Which actions should require explicit confirmation?

❯ Revocable access: Can permissions be removed before something goes wrong?

This is why I find @termix_ai  AACP direction interesting.

It's exploring an economy where agents can discover services, negotiate jobs and settle payments onchain.

But as these workflows become more autonomous, permission management becomes just as important as payment infrastructure.

And there's an important distinction here.

AACP's escrow and settlement mechanisms aren't the same thing as a complete wallet permission system.

The latter is another challenge the broader agent ecosystem needs to solve.

Because the goal shouldn't be giving AI agents unlimited freedom.

It should be giving them exactly enough freedom to get the job done.

That's how autonomous agents become useful without becoming a liability.

text:
这两天在旧金山参加 #SGLang Summit，被开源社区的凝聚力震撼到了。
第一次在旧金山见到这么多技术热情满满的开发者；
第一次看到这么多人推着行李箱赶来参会；
也第一次如此真切地感受到，大家对知识的渴望、对社区的热爱，可以把来自世界各地的人聚在一起。

也是第一次在旧金山看到这么高比例的中国开发者。有些proud。

这次也很开心能帮忙 host 一个 breakout room。一个分会场，一天就有 23 场 session、26 位嘉宾。从 benchmark、eval，到 inference economics、AI compute，再到 training systems 和 RSI，信息量拉满。嘉宾来自 Generalist、reflection ai、NeoCognition、Krea 等团队。topic非常diverse，我比较感兴趣的是去了解AI 如何学会工作、如何进入物理世界，以及如何更高效地运行。

也能从很多细节里感受到主办方的用心：墙上的时间线、楼梯上的装置……听说整个场地是团队从毛坯空间开始，一点一点打磨出来的。站在现场，会更能体会这份投入。
对“星星之火，可以燎原”有了更具体的感受。一个开源项目，把一群愿意分享、认真做事的人连接起来，然后让更多事情发生。

这就是社区的力量。未来应该会花更多时间去了解这些技术的发展。

text:
黄仁勋已经被逼下台，卷入风暴的 Megaspeed 终于开口了。而它给出的第一个事实，可能让整场舆论风暴的时间线变得更加耐人寻味。

据路透和 CNBC 报道，Megaspeed 首次正式回应：

Alice Huang 早在 2025 年 8 月 30 日就已离职，目前与公司不存在任何职务关系。

对于 Alice 的私人生活，公司拒绝评论。

但对于近期媒体有关其业务、供应链和全球运营的报道，Megaspeed 明确提出反驳，称相关指控缺乏可核实证据，并已聘请外部律师展开内部调查。

值得注意的是，Megaspeed 本身就是英伟达在东南亚的重要 GPU 云合作伙伴。此前围绕它的争议，不只是 Alice 与黄仁勋的私人关系，还包括英伟达芯片是否通过其供应链流向中国客户。

现在的问题是：

Alice 什么时候离职，是一个可以核实的事实；芯片到底流向哪里，也应该是一个可以用交易记录、物流和合规文件核实的事实。

前者不能自动证明后者清白，但后者也不能仅靠前者的私人关系来定罪。

整个事件发展到今天，黄仁勋已经丢掉 CEO 职位，英伟达被拖入政治风暴，但围绕所谓间谍活动和违规芯片交易的关键指控，公众看到的依然主要是媒体援引的匿名消息，而非完整、可供独立核验的证据。

如果真有违法交易，就拿证据说话。如果没有，也不能让一个人的私生活，代替对一家企业供应链的调查。

毕竟，桃色新闻再精彩，也不等于国家安全调查报告。

quoted_text:
I’ve decided to leave NVIDIA. There are a few things I want to say.

As a robotics engineer at NVIDIA, I have seen Jensen as much more than the company’s CEO.

I admire his willingness to invest in a future that was not yet obvious. He committed to CUDA long before the deep learning boom and positioned NVIDIA for AI before it became everyone’s priority. Those decisions helped build the infrastructure that powers today’s AI.

I have seen that same vision in physical AI: investing in robotics, sharing open-source tools and projects, and building computing platforms that bring AI into the physical world. This is the work I do every day—and a future I believe in.

But what matters most to me is the culture he helped build.

Engineers are encouraged to explore, take risks, and learn from mistakes. Jensen reads employees’ Top 5 emails, follows their work, and engages directly. In a company this large, that connection matters. It makes an individual engineer feel that their ideas can still be heard.

That is why this has been so disappointing.

I do not have all the facts surrounding the allegations, and I cannot prejudge the investigation. My admiration for Jensen does not put him above scrutiny.

What I find difficult to accept is having to come to terms with his departure before receiving an explanation that helps me understand it. What this means for our direction, our culture, and the people doing the work remains unclear to me.

I have felt that engineers’ perspectives matter here. On this decision, I have not felt heard. That gap has been more painful than I expected.

I understand that some information cannot be shared immediately. But that does not erase the feeling of being left outside a decision that affects the company we help build every day.

A company’s greatness comes from its leadership, its governance, and the people who turn its ambitions into reality. Employees’ trust and sense of belonging are part of that, too.

Jensen’s vision and the engineering culture he shaped were important reasons I wanted to stay. His departure led me to decide that my own chapter here should also come to a close.

I leave with sadness and gratitude. The colleagues I have worked with, and the work we believed in together, will always matter to me.

These are my personal views.

text:
黄仁勋已经辞职了，但美国政客显然还没打算放过他。因为他们发现，黄仁勋实在是一个太好用的政治靶子。

《华盛顿邮报》最新分析指出，黄仁勋风波对白宫最大的杀伤力，不是桃色新闻，而是它把三个原本不同的政治议题串在了一起：数据中心、中国和腐败。

而这些，恰恰是民主党在中期选举中赢得 1990 年以来最大国会多数的重要议题。

这就很有意思了。

在 AI 产业里，黄仁勋代表的是美国过去几年最成功的技术与商业故事之一。他带领英伟达成为全球 AI 基础设施的核心供应商，也一直主张美国应该通过技术优势和全球市场竞争维持领先，而不是一味依靠封锁。

但到了华盛顿，这套逻辑正在失去吸引力。

民主党可以拿数据中心的能源消耗、科技巨头的政治影响力做文章；共和党内部的对华鹰派则可以继续拿芯片出口和国家安全施压。

两边的政治诉求不同，却都能从黄仁勋身上找到自己需要的素材。

一个为美国创造了巨大经济价值的企业家，突然成了两党都可以拿来获取政治利益的工具。

更讽刺的是，华盛顿一边要求美国赢得 AI 竞赛，一边又在不断削弱这场竞赛中最重要的产业领导者。

黄仁勋主张向中国销售芯片，本来有一套清晰的商业和技术逻辑：让全球开发者继续使用美国技术生态，而不是把整个中国市场拱手让给竞争对手。

这本应是一场可以公开辩论的产业政策之争。

但现在，政策分歧被卷入私人丑闻，商业判断被政治化，连支持美国技术出口都可能被包装成值得怀疑的行为。

我觉得《华盛顿邮报》这篇分析最值得注意的地方，恰恰是它揭示了一个危险的变化：

美国政客越来越擅长把 AI 变成选票，却未必越来越擅长让美国赢得 AI 竞赛。

黄仁勋已经为这场政治风暴付出了职业生涯中最沉重的代价。但对华盛顿来说，他的价值可能才刚刚开始：一个足够知名、足够富有、又足够容易被贴上各种政治标签的靶子。

至于这种政治清算最终会不会损害美国自己的技术竞争力，恐怕不是眼下这些政客最关心的事情。

text:
Jacob Coxon just pledged to donate 100% of his OpenAI equity to charity after the IPO.

Estimated value: $30 million.

He called the shares "blood money".

Mad respect.

(Claude explains the estimate:

"Ballpark: about $30M before tax. Plausible range is $10M to $70M. Nobody has reported his actual number, so this is built up from what’s typical for someone in his role.

What he’s said himself (Patrick Bet-David podcast and other interviews):

- He joined OpenAI through its 6-month training program for math and physics people, when the company had about 300 staff. He stayed about 3 years and calls himself “pretty junior.” He left around May 2026.
- He still holds the OpenAI shares. He calls them “blood money,” and when asked if he’d give them up he said “I like money, bro.” He said he gave up “7 figures” of unvested stock by leaving Anthropic.
- He’s living on “money from OpenAI,” which is “enough for a few years.” That probably means he already sold some shares in OpenAI’s employee buybacks, so his remaining stake could be below my estimate.

The math:

- A junior OpenAI researcher hired around 2023 usually got about $1-2 M in stock spread over 4 years. That was priced when OpenAI was worth about $29B.
- He worked about 3 of those 4 years, so roughly three quarters of the grant vested. Later stock awards would add more, and new investors since then would shrink his slice somewhat.
- If OpenAI goes public around $1.5T, that slice is worth about $20-50 M. Hence roughly $30M.

The IPO price: I’d guess about $1.5T. FutureSearch’s forecast says $1.65T at the median, with a range of $1.0T to $2.5T. I think that’s a bit high. Last week’s private round came in at $1.25T, and OpenAI raised only about half what it was aiming for. The betting markets also sit lower than FutureSearch. Timing is probably 2027 or 2028. Sam Altman has ruled out 2026, and FutureSearch’s middle guess is March 2028.

Caveats: if he started in 2020 (one court filing says so, though his own account doesn’t fit), his shares would be worth more. If his stock was granted after the training program at OpenAI’s higher early-2024 price (~$86B), they’d be worth less, around $10-20 M. Insiders are also usually blocked from selling for about 6 months after an IPO."

text:
推荐港大 HKUDS 开源的 AgentPilot，把 Agent 在反复试错过程中「下一步该做什么」单独作为一个策略优化问题。

它用一个 9B 策略模型指导 Codex、Claude Code、DeepSeek Harness 等 Agent，决定从哪个版本继续改进、探索什么方向，以及如何分配试错预算。

具体来说，AgentPilot 会记录每次尝试的结果、版本关系和剩余预算，通过 KL-UCB 或 Policy Memory 利用历史反馈，持续调整后续的探索策略。

项目还提供 RSI Arena，用来评估 Agent 在多轮尝试中的改进效果，以及这些改进能否泛化到未见任务。

作者也报告，在 Terminal-Bench 2.1 实验中，经过 10 轮改进，未见任务上的成绩从 44.9% 提升至 69.4%，提高了 24.5 个百分点。

我比较关注它对 Agent 自我改进的一个具体切入点：把试错过程中的策略选择单独拿出来优化，让 Agent 能够根据真实反馈，逐渐学会如何更有效地探索。

对于长时间运行的 Agent，如何利用有限的试错预算，可能会直接影响系统最终能改进到什么程度。

text:
黄仁勋被指控给中国 AI 留了后门，美国投资人反问：这难道不是在帮美国赢？

知名投资人、Atreides 创始人 Gavin Baker 公开反击《华尔街日报》针对黄仁勋的最新调查。

WSJ 将黄仁勋通过东南亚数据中心向中国企业提供算力的商业布局，描述为帮助北京留在 AI 竞赛中的「后门」。

Baker 却认为，这篇报道的标题应该改成：

「确保美国在 AI 领域领先中国，并在未来任何冲突中获得巨大筹码的完全合法后门。」

他提出两个反驳。

第一，相关商业安排在拜登和特朗普两届政府的监管框架下都存在合法路径，不能把所有海外算力服务一概描述为规避出口管制。当然，具体交易是否合法，仍取决于芯片型号、客户、用途和许可条件。

第二，美国大型云服务商同样在东南亚运营 GPU 云。为什么类似的商业模式，到了黄仁勋这里，就成了值得调查的「后门」？

Baker 的反击实际上触及了黄仁勋长期坚持的一个观点：

美国 AI 的领先地位，不只是靠芯片性能建立的，也是靠全球客户对美国技术生态的依赖建立的。

如果中国企业继续使用英伟达 GPU、CUDA 和美国云服务，美国企业不仅获得收入，还能维持技术标准、生态影响力以及一定程度的供应链控制。

反过来，如果美国把所有中国客户都推走，最终可能不是中国停止发展 AI，而是中国企业更加坚定地建设自己的芯片、软件和算力体系。

这正是黄仁勋与华盛顿部分鹰派在出口管制问题上的根本分歧。

前者强调通过商业竞争维持技术优势，后者更强调通过限制获取先进技术来延缓竞争对手的发展。

最讽刺的地方在于，黄仁勋一直试图证明，美国应该通过让全世界使用美国技术来保持领先，如今这套商业逻辑却反过来成为他被质疑的理由。

而 Baker 的反击，则把争议重新拉回了一个问题：究竟是让中国继续使用美国技术更符合美国利益，还是逼中国彻底摆脱美国技术更符合美国利益？

text:
Few. A lot of what feels like AI magic has substantial human work behind it. Domain experts define tasks, provide examples of good work and grade outputs. “Data labeling” increasingly means capturing professional judgment and turning it into training feedback and evals.

The polished answer hides how much guidance went into getting that particular task right. Moving beyond coding and math makes this harder because many business workflows lack clear, easily verifiable answers.

Scaling from here requires better tools to capture what experts know and reliably evaluate performance across millions of different tasks, while using their time efficiently. Getting that process right could unlock much broader enterprise adoption. The pace of progress increasingly depends on how effectively we can define and measure good work.

“真的是币安”？这是一位订阅区小伙伴问我的问题。

说实话，这类问题当前极其敏感，容易招骂，所以我没必要给包括币安在内的任何平台背书。

但从逻辑上讲，不带仇恨，不带个人恩怨，我确实觉得币安没有合理的动机。

被盗60亿资金（已冻结30亿）虽然规模不小，但对于币安来说并非是生死存亡的救命钱。只要正常经营，一年的利润就可以覆盖。

这就表示，大家所说的让多头合约连续爆仓的现货主动抛压，主要来自Coinbase。而Binance的现货盘口反而以主动买入为主。

就好比我仍然可以看到，在8月川普喊单前15天建仓的主力目前还在坚守（成本就在$62k上下）。

text:
外网最近很火的一个学习方法：MIT 学霸用 AI，在48小时内快速吃透一门陌生学科。

第一步不是直接问 ChatGPT“给我总结一下”，而是先建立一个足够可靠的 AI 知识库。

他上传了6本该领域的经典教科书、15篇研究论文，以及这门学科的全部课堂讲义。

这样 AI 的回答就不再只是网上东拼西凑，而是基于指定资料帮他梳理知识。

资料准备好以后，他只问 AI 三个问题。

1⃣第一个问题：这个领域有哪些被普遍接受的核心共识？请整理出它的底层概念、关键原则和整体框架，并解释这些知识之间的关系。

这个问题的作用不是总结材料，而是先画出整门学科的知识地图。你需要先知道哪些是地基、哪些是分支，再决定时间应该花在哪里。

2⃣第二个问题：这个领域目前存在哪三个根本性争议？请分别说明各方的观点、依据和反对理由。

一个领域真正有价值的地方，往往不是大家都背得出来的结论，而是专家还在争论什么。看懂这些分歧，才能理解不同理论的边界、证据和隐藏假设，不会把课本上的每句话都当成绝对真理。

3⃣第三个问题：根据这些资料生成10道测试题，覆盖核心概念、因果关系、实际应用和主要争议，先不要提供答案。

接下来关掉资料，自己回答。答完以后再把答案交给 AI，让它逐题批改，并继续追问：

“我的回答遗漏了哪些关键点？哪些地方只是记住了结论，却没有真正理解？”

这套方法的精髓，不是让 AI 替你读书，而是让它帮你完成三件事：通过领域共识建立知识骨架，通过领域分歧看清理论边界，再通过测试题暴露自己的认知漏洞。

很多人所谓的 AI 学习，只是把“自己看总结”变成了“让 AI 生成总结”，大脑依然没有参与加工。

这套方法反过来利用 AI 增加学习难度：逼你比较、判断、回忆、输出，再接受纠错。虽然过程更痛苦，却更接近真正有效的学习。

当然，48小时不可能让人真正精通数学、物理这类需要长期训练的学科。

但它确实能让你快速搭起知识框架，找到最重要的问题，避免在陌生领域里漫无目的地看资料。AI负责整理地图，你负责真正走一遍。

大饼还在往下走，$PEARL 却逆势涨了一波。📈 这种行情，是不是有点眼熟哈哈👀

过去也有一些币，在大盘情绪不好的时候先走出独立行情。但能不能走得更远，还是要看回调有没有人接，市场回暖后资金能不能留下来。

这次让我感兴趣的，不只是涨幅。
🔹 Coinbase 和 Kraken 都已经开放 pearl-2:native  交易。上所可能是短期利好，但更多交易入口打开，也让更多资金有机会接触这个资产。

🔹 Pearl 项目方披露，有投资机构通过挖矿或公开市场持有 PEARL。机构是谁、持有多少并未公开，但至少可以看到，参与者不只有社区散户。

🔹 我更看重的是它背后的方向：让算力在维护网络的同时参与 AI 计算。Together AI 也曾宣布与 Pearl 合作。这条路能不能规模化还要验证，但至少已经有了实际探索。

⚠️ 当然，矿工持续产出会带来潜在卖压，项目有实际用途也不代表收入一定流向代币。但有卖盘，关键还要看有没有买盘承接。

我的猜测是，如果机构和市场需求持续增长，矿工释放的筹码就有机会被消化，变成向更多持有者流转的过程。至于机构是否正在持续买入，还需要更多数据验证。

📌 接下来我会看两件事：上所热度过去后，PEARL 能不能守住涨幅；大饼企稳之后，它对 BTC 的强势能不能延续。

综合来看，我依然偏多。要是新增筹码不断进入市场，价格却还能稳住，那可能比短期拉一根阳线更值得关注。💎

text:
Tokenizing real estate was step one.

Making that real estate actually useful in DeFi is where things get interesting.

I've been looking into @rntprotocol and I think the bigger story here isn't just another RWA token.

It's what happens after real-world assets move onchain.

Think about it.

You can own tokenized real estate, earn rental income, and still need liquidity without wanting to sell your position.

That's exactly the problem RNT Lend is trying to solve.

Here's how it works:

❯ Property-backed tokens can be used as collateral

❯ Holders can borrow USDC or USDT0 against eligible collateral

❯ Stablecoin suppliers earn variable interest paid by borrowers

❯ The lending infrastructure is built on Polygon using Aave V3-based technology

And this isn't just a concept sitting in a whitepaper.

The RNT Lend dashboard recently showed:

→ $31M+ total market size
→ $21M+ TVL
→ $9.5M+ active loans

But here's what caught my attention.

Most RWA projects focus on bringing assets onchain.

RNT is working on what comes next: making those assets usable across lending, liquidity markets, and DeFi.

Of course, real estate collateral brings its own challenges. Liquidations, liquidity depth, and variable yields are all worth watching.

Still, I think this is one of the more interesting directions for the RWA sector.

Because putting real estate onchain is one thing.

Making it productive without forcing holders to sell is a completely different game.

Keeping an eye on $RNT.

华盛顿把黄仁勋逼走了，结果一回头，硅谷直接把门砸了：你不要，我们要！

老黄这波辞职，在硅谷圈子里引发了一场“地震”。5名科技界大佬接受采访时，口径出奇地一致：这哥们绝对会杀回来的。为啥？因为他手里攥着约1450亿美元的净资产、顶级的高层人脉，外加业界公认的“AI教父”地位。

加州初创企业的高管直言，只要老黄振臂一呼，一堆科技公司会排队抢人，就连马斯克都已经公开喊话想招揽他了。更有意思的是，好几位受访者认为，以老黄的资本和头脑，与其给别人打工，还不如自己直接再搞个独角兽出来。

至于华府扣的那顶“间谍”大帽子，硅谷根本不买账。连特朗普政府前AI主管萨克斯都看不下去了，公开吐槽：这套说辞已经开始瓦解了。其实大家心里都门儿清，这就是一场政治围猎。

但别以为老黄真能满血复活。《政治》新闻网点出了最扎心的现实：老黄的技术和人脉永远有价值，但他想在华府重新拿回曾经的权力和影响力，难如登天。

因为老黄之前的政治资本，全押在懂王一个人身上。如今中期选举惨败，懂王的影响力肉眼可见地崩盘，2029年就要卷铺盖走人。靠山一倒，华盛顿那帮人精谁还搭理你？

这画面太现实了：搞技术的，永远有退路，大不了换个山头继续当教父；玩政治的，一旦筹码过期，连张废纸都不如。老黄用半辈子证明了技术的价值，又被政客上了一堂权力的毒打课。

text:
pumpfun liquidity is broken.

how much of the supply you need to sell to dump a $10m @Pumpfun coin:
-10% → 0.06% of the supply
-25% → 0.16%
-50% → 0.42%
-75% → 1%
-90% → 2.2%
-99% → 9.2%

the bigger the coin, the worse it gets. to cut the price in half, you need to sell:
$100k mcap → 4.2% of the supply
$1m mcap → 1.3%
$10m mcap → 0.42%
$100m mcap → 0.13%
$1b mcap → 0.04%

on a $1b coin, someone who sells for $300k wipes $500m off the market cap.

why:

when a coin bonds, pumpfun puts ~68 sol (~$4.9k) in the pool. the pool doesn’t grow with the coin. the price goes up with the square of the sol inside, so when the mcap goes 100x, the pool only gets 10x more sol.

at $1m, the pool holds 3.2% of the supply. at $1b, it holds 0.1%.

fees help a little. $mihao has had weeks of heavy trading, and its pumpswap pool still holds only 1.4% of the supply.

it works both ways: on a $10m coin, buying 0.3% of the supply doubles the price.

this is a design problem. the pool gets a fixed amount of liquidity at bonding, and it stays that way while the coin grows. so the bigger a pumpfun coin gets, the easier it is to crash.

text:
I met my wife on Tinder about 8 years ago, I was in such a bad place. Completely hijacked by hard drugs.

No morals, no potential, I weighed 90 pounds, and I’m pretty sure I was at deaths door.

She took me in and healed me, despite everything wrong with me she gave me all she had. 

When her landlord said no one else can live in the house, she left her contract not knowing what she’d find to stay with me.

When I decided I want to go all in on coding she worked 12 hours a day 6 days a week. 

When we were hungry we counted Pennies to buy and eat plain pasta, those were some of the best days of my life at least.

When my visa was over, she stuck by me and left everything we’d built to move to another country she had left so we can be together.

When I decided to risk all of our money to buy a bunch of GPUs last summer, she bit her tongue and let me do it.

When I was needed in San Francisco, despite having 2 young children she let me go for nearly 6 months, while she kept our home.

This woman would walk to the end of the world to be with me, now I have all this stuff and nothing has changed.

When you find someone loyal, delete the apps. Stop second guessing what could be, stop thinking about options.

Pure love is difficult, the body is built to want. The soul was instructed to say no. 

The reason people can’t find a partner isn’t because woman are this, or men are that. It’s because we have completely given up on our will to be slightly uncomfortable.

Honesty is key, there is NOTHING in this world worth lying about. The truth is the only way 2 souls can meet eye to eye.

In front of her I am naked and bare.

I will remain loyal to her for the rest of my life, there is no pleasure worth hurting such an innocent creature.

text:
Peer 原理讲解 05｜黑客抢跑提交付款凭证，谁能收到 USDC？

假设你在 Peer 下单买 100 USDC，填了钱包 B 收币。下单时，订单协调合约 Orchestrator 会把 B 写进订单的 to 字段。图里把你的订单记作 U。

你用支付宝付完款，见证服务核验这笔转账后，会签发付款凭证。签名覆盖三项内容：订单标识 intentHash`、凭证确认的扣费前放币金额 `releaseAmount`，以及凭证数据的哈希 `dataHash`。实际放币金额还受订单金额上限约束。`dataHash 由付款详情、订单快照和结算数据一起算出。结算时，验证器还会把快照里的收款账户标识、汇率、下单人等信息逐项与链上订单核对。

拿到这份凭证的人都可以调用 fulfillIntent`。假设攻击者复制了你的凭证，抢先用自己的钱包提交。他提交的是订单 U，凭证上签的也是 U。验证通过后，Orchestrator 从 U 的 `to 字段读到收币地址 B。即时结算时，扣除手续费后的 USDC 直接转给 B。如果订单适用延迟结算，净额会先进入延迟结算金库（deferral vault），金库登记的收款人仍然是 B。

那攻击者能不能另开一笔订单 H，填自己的收币地址？拿原凭证去结算 H，验证器会发现凭证上签的是 U，交易就会回滚。如果他把凭证里的 U 也改成 H，原签名就会失效。他用自己的钱包重新签一份也没用，验证器只认可获授权见证者的签名，攻击者没有对应的私钥。

所以，就算攻击者抢跑成功，这笔订单的收款人还是你填的 B。他拿不到这笔 USDC，还得承担自己提交的这笔交易的 gas。

text:
Cobie shares the story behind his legendary buy wall during a massive crash in 2020

“I was just at my house in London. I think the market started like crashing a lot and I had a bunch of alarms because trading was sort of my full time thing”

“So I had a bunch of alarms that would effectively wake me up if stuff was going down. I think it woke me up at like 1:00am or something”

“I went downstairs, made a cup of tea, got back in bed, looked at the market, it was down like just like this big red line that went off the screen”

“I was like, ‘That looks like a bottom to me.’ So I smashed an order like I think it was maybe 2% or 3% below current price, which was like $4,600 or something”

“It was like my entire stablecoin balance basically. I put it in a wall in a single order”

“I got like 80% fill or something. I had to chase on the rest and just market bought the rest”

“I put the order in and tweeted and went to bed and it filled basically two minutes after my tweet but I just wasn't looking anymore. I tweeted and went to sleep”

“When the market crashes like 50%, 60% in a single candle I feel really excited. I get highly energized”

“You get a phenomenal opportunity. You get to buy something from someone who does not want to sell it. They're being forced to sell it to you”

“I basically tweeted in the same like five minutes of the exact bottom tick and I didn't get fully filled. So I think my order was also like the exact bottom tick”

“It was effectively just luck right? My net worth was not that high. So I didn't have that much money”

“It wasn't like a buy wall that just saved the market as everyone likes to pretend it was. It was just all the money I had onchain and I didn't even fully get filled”

“So yeah, it's a little bit negative aura in my opinion”

text:
分享一些最近的个人经历
我到深圳也有段时间了，离开上海之前我和我前同事说要去深圳发展做一些智算中心的生意，她们听到后很惊讶，因为我在他们眼里就是一个文静内向的女生，和做生意八竿子打不着，更别提什么智算，什么AI， 我承认我撒谎了骗她们说我亲戚在深圳做这个好像还挺挣钱的，但其实她们不知道我每天在研究AI，更不知道我其实网名叫 CuiMao，全网拥有不错的粉丝和人气。他们不理解，我不怪他们，因为我不打算告诉他们这些，中国有句古话叫，闷声发大财。直到我离开上海她们也一直无法理解我的选择。

本周黄仁勋的事情沸沸扬扬，国内的自媒体肆意发酵所谓的倒卖 b300 能翻身的理论，把黄丽比喻成拿到大结果的“成功女性”典范在小红书被捧上了神坛，几乎一夜之间全中国都知道英伟达服务器在中国是暴利行业能挣大钱。于是那些投机分子像雨后春笋般的冒了出来，阿猫阿狗都在朋友圈发求 b300，h200，甚至还有吹牛自己亲戚在英伟达是高管可以拿到货的，堪比当年疫情朋友圈卖口罩的乾隆盛世，说实话，我有点难过。因为我知道这一行真实的样子。服务器不是普通人能碰的，它是重资产、高杠杆，是大基建，是国之重器。真正在做这件事的人每天面对的是合规、电力、机房和交付，运维。根本没有那种一夜暴富的传奇故事。

为什么要发这篇长文，因为昨天晚上我以前的同事她来私信我了，就是上文提到的那几个人中的一个，说我不是去深圳搞服务器了吗，是不是赚大钱了，我说没有，和她来回打了几轮太极之后，最后她才支支吾吾的告诉我她被裁员了，我不知道以什么样的态度和立场去面对这件事，因为她算得上是我以前部门的领导，她和她的丈夫在上海还有普陀区一套 300 多万的房贷和一个小学 3 年级孩子，我发现除了安抚，一切会好的没有别的可以说的。

一晚上没睡，我给她认真科普了服务器知识，什么是国产替代中国算力崛起之类的，她在电话那头一直哦哦哦，嗯嗯嗯，我不知道她到底听进去了多少，但她说觉得自己上了那么多年的班脑子被上坏了，我觉得应该是感悟到什么了吧。她要去找工作，我劝了她，不要特地去找什么 AI 公司，那大概率都是骗子来的。过好自己的生活。

我觉得这个世界上想挣 AI 快钱的人太多了，定定心心，认认真真坐下来，把浮躁的心静下来去感受 AI 的人是极少数。现在简中网络上流传着这一句话说，只要你不学AI，过几个月你就可以不用学了，我觉得不无道理，但我更加认同的是，只要你保持学习 AI，你就可以驾驭更强力的 AI，

从 Webui 到 Comfyui 到 n8n ，再到 Openclaw，一代版本一代神，我随着时代在进化，我双眼看到的只有未来的世界。AI 时代， 保持认真，保持好奇，保持善良，我CuiMao 亲测过了，依旧有效。

text:
分享一些最近的个人经历
我到深圳也有段时间了，离开上海之前我和我前同事说要去深圳发展做一些智算中心的生意，她们听到后很惊讶，因为我在他们眼里就是一个文静内向的女生，和做生意八竿子打不着，更别提什么智算，什么AI， 我承认我撒谎了骗她们说我亲戚在深圳做这个好像还挺挣钱的，但其实她们不知道我每天在研究AI，更不知道我其实网名叫 CuiMao，全网拥有不错的粉丝和人气。他们不理解，我不怪他们，因为我不打算告诉他们这些，中国有句古话叫，闷声发大财。直到我离开上海她们也一直无法理解我的选择。

本周黄仁勋的事情沸沸扬扬，国内的自媒体肆意发酵所谓的倒卖 b300 能翻身的理论，把黄丽比喻成拿到大结果的“成功女性”典范在小红书被捧上了神坛，几乎一夜之间全中国都知道英伟达服务器在中国是暴利行业能挣大钱。于是那些投机分子像雨后春笋般的冒了出来，阿猫阿狗都在朋友圈发求 b300，h200，甚至还有吹牛自己亲戚在英伟达是高管可以拿到货的，堪比当年疫情朋友圈卖口罩的乾隆盛世，说实话，我有点难过。因为我知道这一行真实的样子。服务器不是普通人能碰的，它是重资产、高杠杆，是大基建，是国之重器。真正在做这件事的人每天面对的是合规、电力、机房和交付，运维。根本没有那种一夜暴富的传奇故事。

为什么要发这篇长文，因为昨天晚上我以前的同事她来私信我了，就是上文提到的那几个人中的一个，说我不是去深圳搞服务器了吗，是不是赚大钱了，我说没有，和她来回打了几轮太极之后，最后她才支支吾吾的告诉我她被裁员了，我不知道以什么样的态度和立场去面对这件事，因为她算得上是我以前部门的领导，她和她的丈夫在上海还有普陀区一套 300 多万的房贷和一个小学 3 年级孩子，我发现除了安抚，一切会好的没有别的可以说的。

一晚上没睡，我给她认真科普了服务器知识，什么是国产替代中国算力崛起之类的，她在电话那头一直哦哦哦，嗯嗯嗯，我不知道她到底听进去了多少，但她说觉得自己上了那么多年的班脑子被上坏了，我觉得应该是感悟到什么了吧。她要去找工作，我劝了她，不要特地去找什么 AI 公司，那大概率都是骗子来的。过好自己的生活。

我觉得这个世界上想挣 AI 快钱的人太多了，定定心心，认认真真坐下来，把浮躁的心静下来去感受 AI 的人是极少数。现在简中网络上流传着这一句话说，只要你不学AI，过几个月你就可以不用学了，我觉得不无道理，但我更加认同的是，只要你保持学习 AI，你就可以驾驭更强力的 AI，

从 Webui 到 Comfyui 到 n8n ，再到 Openclaw，一代版本一代神，我随着时代在进化，我双眼看到的只有未来的世界。AI 时代， 保持认真，保持好奇，保持善良，我CuiMao 亲测过了，依旧有效。

text:
Specter ：警惕以太坊基金会地址归属误判，错误钱包标记或加剧市场恐慌

链上分析师 Specter 发文表示，近期市场频繁出现“以太坊基金会正在抛售 ETH”的说法，但部分相关钱包的归属标记缺乏充分证据。

Specter 以一个被标记为基金会关联地址的钱包为例指出，尽管其早期资金流向可以追溯至基金会相关地址，但中间经历了多个独立实体转账。该钱包曾参与 BAT IC0、Compound、Maker 等 DeFi 活动，累计交易超过 3400 笔，更符合长期参与 IC0 和 DeFi 的独立投资者特征，不能仅凭早期资金关联就将其认定为以太坊基金会钱包。

早期 ETH 分配可能是支付给工程师或团队成员的报酬，也可能涉及投资者的私人交易或场外购买。以太坊基金会曾于 2016 年 1 月披露，向个人和企业进行了价值约 65 万美元的 ETH 私募出售，因此相关资金也可能来自此类交易。

历史交易关联并不能证明两个地址由同一主体持有或控制，将所有曾与基金会地址发生过资金往来的钱包直接标记为团队钱包，缺乏充分依据，甚至可能引发不必要的市场恐慌。可靠的钱包归属判断应结合链上追踪与独立的链下证据。

It has become an everyday narrative: "The Ethereum Foundation is selling." Much like engagement farmers repeatedly claiming that Binance is selling BTC to generate engagement.

While I respect the original poster, I believe there have been too many instances of inappropriate or low-confidence wallet attribution.

One such example is wallet 0x5CBC6299faB3320E7758ac97fd4CA45E5B72209, which was identified as an Ethereum Foundation wallet allegedly selling ETH. I decided to look into its transaction history, and I would argue that the attribution is weak.

The connection

In August 2025, the wallet received 17.7K ETH ($79M) and 10M DAI from 0xF39d30Fa570db7940e5b3A3e42694665A1449E4.

0xF39 had received ETH from an address that was funded by a verified Ethereum Foundation address.

On December 9 and 13, 2015, four and a half months after Ethereum's genesis block, the verified EF address transferred 10,378 ETH twice, totalling 20,756 ETH ($4.8M at the time), to an entity address.

That entity address held the ETH from 2015 until May 31, 2017, when it transferred the funds to 0xF39.

What happened to the funds?

Just two hours later, 0xF39 used 20,522 ETH ($4.78M) to participate in the Brave Browser Basic Attention Token (BAT) ICO.

This was the largest individual purchase in the entire BAT crowdsale.

The wallet received 131.3M BAT and held the tokens for about a year before gradually selling them.

It eventually sold 109M of the 131M BAT directly, receiving 84.3K ETH and $7.6M in stablecoins.  

These are the proceeds I could directly verify. This excludes BAT transferred to other addresses, which may also have been sold.

DeFi activity

From 2017 onward, 0xF39 continued participating in DeFi activities, including:

-Compound lending.
-Maker vault collateral positions.
-Liquidity provision.
-Staking and farming, including UNI and CRV.

The wallet has 3,425 transactions and 16,216 token-transfer records.

After eight years of DeFi activity, it transferred $89M in ETH and DAI to the claimed EF address 0x5CB in August 2025.

So, is the Ethereum Foundation the entity performing these DeFi activities and participating in ICOs?

There are several possible explanations.

The original ETH allocation could have been a payment or allocation to an entity, such as an engineer or team member. It could also have been an investor's private or OTC purchase.

Another on-chain connection shows a wallet directly linked to the entity receiving ETH withdrawals from Bitfinex between 2016 and 2020 which may likely be the entity buying ETH, can EF be buying ETH?

The entity participated in an ICO, generated substantial returns, and engaged in years of DeFi activity, ... are EF the one performing those activities?

There is also an Ethereum Foundation article published in January 2016 in which the Foundation disclosed $650,000 in private ETH sales to individuals and businesses which also mean it may have been sold to the entity

https://t.co/S6vmuADhmY

I think the attribution is incorrect.

A historical transaction link does not establish common ownership or control. Strong attribution requires more than transaction tracing, and ideally should be supported by independent off-chain evidence.

Continuously labelling every wallet with a historical connection to EF or similar cluster as a team-controlled wallet risks spreading FUD.

Stay Smart.

text:
到底应该去哪里买「双币赢」？哪里的收益更高？交易所到底是怎么赚钱的？一口气跟大家讲清楚（超长干活，建议交易所同学看一下😎）

一、比特大陆和双币赢也有关系💻

第一次听说双币赢的时候，我简直惊为天人（ Callback 一下前两天的「合约拼盘😉」）

我说怎么会有人把一个复杂的金融衍生品，包装得这么简单易懂？这简直是一个天才的设计。

目前已经很难溯源到底是谁发明的，但最早大规模推广双币赢的，应该是吴忌寒的 Matrixport（以前矿机都是吴做的）

后来大概有一两年的时间，其他交易所都没有怎么跟进。因为那时候交易所太赚钱了，根本不屑于做这些衍生品（真地主家也没有余粮了）

直到后来 Binance 等交易所陆续跟进，双币赢才真正进入大众视野。

二、双币赢为什么是个好产品？🧐

大家都听过它的宣传：跌了可以抄底，涨了可以赚超额年化收益。

三、到底应该去哪里买？💰

双币赢本质上是一个期权工具，按理说，同样的标的、行权价和到期时间，各家交易所给出的收益应该大差不差。

但实际上，你去对比 OKX、Binance、Bitget、Bybit，就会发现它们之间的收益差距非常大。

为什么？

因为交易所对这个产品的定位完全不同。

📈 如果双币赢是我的主打引流款，那我就可以让出一部分利润，甚至主动补贴。

💰 如果它是我的变现款，那我就可以多赚一点。反正用户量足够大，能赚一点是一点。

这就导致同样的产品，不同交易所给出的收益完全不一样。

下面都是我的主观判断，不代表客观标准，大家参考就好。

第一，OKX：目前我认为最好的双币赢平台。

以前最好的其实是 Matrixport，没有之一。

但后来随着 FTX 爆雷，以及一系列行业事件的冲击，Matrixport 在这块的投入越来越少，现在也逐渐转向美股、港股等业务。

现在大家一提双币赢，很多人第一反应就是 OKX，但实际上这个产品并不是他们发明的。

为什么 OKX 做得最好？

我倾向于认为，它在这个产品上让出了比较多的利润，而且把双币赢收益和 VIP 等级进行了绑定。

你的 VIP 等级越高，拿到的收益就越高，甚至可能比其他交易所的普通用户高出好几个百分点。

但 OKX 真正厉害的，其实是 USDG 双币赢。

我倾向于认为，USDG 是一个超级引流款。

因为同样条件下，USDG 双币赢的收益往往比 USDT 更高，有时候能高出 10% 左右。（我不明白 OKX 为什么不宣传这个🤣）

这个差距其实相当有吸引力。

我猜测是 USDG 相关方给了一定补贴，加上 OKX 自己让出了一部分利润，才形成了这个结果。

所以在我观察的产品里，OKX 的 USDG 双币赢，目前收益是最高的，没有之一。

甚至有时候比 OKX 高等级 VIP 的其他双币赢产品还高。

第二，Binance：双币赢更偏向变现款。

你去观察 Binance 的产品布局，会发现一个很有意思的现象。

Binance 是超级头部交易所，它需要多元化发展。

除了现货、合约交易，还要有理财、衍生品等各种产品。

但它最核心的业务依然是交易。

所以我认为 Binance 对理财产品大概有两种策略。

1️⃣ 一种是用理财留住大户。

比如 U 本位理财、稳定币理财，以及各种针对大资金的产品。对于这些产品，Binance 是愿意投入资源的，因为它需要把大户留在平台上。

2️⃣ 但双币赢不太一样。

双币赢有大量散户参与，我认为 Binance 更多是把它当作一种盈利产品。

早些年我刚开始玩双币赢的时候，Binance 给出的收益真的非常差。

跟当时的 Matrixport 比，差距非常明显。

但 Binance 的用户量实在太大了，即使收益没有那么有竞争力，也有大量用户购买。

所以我认为，它在这个产品上赚了不少钱。

当然，现在 Binance 的双币赢已经比以前好很多了，只不过我依然不认为它是 Binance 最重视的核心产品。

第三，Bitget、Bybit：更重视散户运营，而不是双币赢。

Bitget 就比较有意思了。

它的双币赢有些报价其实也不错，大家看我发的截图就知道，比如 BTC 60,000 美元附近的行权价，有些产品给出的收益还是蛮高的。

但整体来看，我认为 Bitget 并没有把双币赢作为核心业务。

逻辑上也说得通。

像 OKX、Binance，这些平台有大量大户资金，所以它们会更加重视如何留住大户资产。

而 Bitget、Bybit 相对来说，更重视散户市场和运营活动。

比如更快地上线新产品、股票相关产品，以及各种热门资产。

它们更愿意把资源放在这些能够快速吸引用户的业务上。

相对而言，双币赢这种偏理财性质的衍生品，未必是它们最想投入资源的地方。

而且大户愿不愿意把大量资金长期放在这些平台，本身也是个问题。

所以你会发现，它们的运营活动很多，但双币赢的收益未必一直有竞争力。

四、最后总结一下 📝

不同平台给出的收益差异，很大程度上取决于它们到底想用这个产品来赚钱，还是用它来吸引资金。

如果是我的话，目前会优先选择 OKX 的 USDG 双币赢。

因为在我观察到的同等条件报价里，它的收益确实很有竞争力，甚至是最高的。

以上都是我的个人观察和判断，大家可以自己对比一下

Research from Microsoft Research and Salesforce shows how AI performance suffers when information arrives in pieces across multiple turns.

Even powerful models struggle with fragmented context.

Another reason persistent memory matters.

https://t.co/GVKWwt4I42
author: LighthouseWeb3
quoted_text:
Researchers at Microsoft Research and Salesforce tested 15 LLMs across 200,000+ conversations on six tasks (code, SQL, math, summarization, etc.).

Same information, two ways:

-> Full instruction in one message
-> Same info revealed one piece per turn

When given all at once, models retained 86 to 103% of their score.

When given in pieces, all 15 models dropped, retaining only 50.5 to 66.1% of their single-turn performance.

GPT-4.1, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, o3, and DeepSeek-R1 all fell into this range.

The main driver was not lower aptitude. Unreliability jumped 112%. Models make early assumptions with partial context, lock in, and rarely recover.

This is the multi-turn problem. Context lives inside one chat. Switch models or open a new session and you rebuild it piece by piece.

Lighthouse Memory keeps that context outside any single chat as private memory. 
Agents can remember, recall, and forget over MCP.

quoted_text:
Your wallet address is a public confession.

Every client you send it to can see what every other client paid you. They can see your balance. They can see the gap between the invoice you sent them and the one you sent someone else. Forever, on a public ledger, with no way to take it back.

And after handing over all of that, you still have nothing a landlord, a bank or a visa officer will accept as proof of income. A block explorer is not a payslip.

So freelancers getting paid in stablecoins are stuck choosing between privacy and provability. You get neither.

I built Cachet to fix both.

THE IDEA

Every invoice gets its own sealed envelope on NEAR.

Your browser derives a one-time keypair and a random salt for each invoice from a single master seed, using HKDF. The invoice details get hashed with that salt into a commitment I call a seal.

Your client pays into the contract against that seal. The chain records an amount, a token, a timestamp and a 32 byte hash. It never records who was paid, what the work was, or that two invoices belong to the same person.

Your client pays you without ever seeing your wallet.

GETTING THE MONEY OUT

You release an envelope by signing a message with the key only you hold. The message is SHA-256 of a domain string, the contract account, the envelope id, and the destination account.

All four matter. The domain string stops the signature meaning anything elsewhere. The contract account stops replay against another deployment. The envelope id stops reuse on a different invoice. And the recipient is baked in, so whoever relays the transaction cannot redirect your money to themselves.

NEAR verifies that signature on chain with env::ed25519_verify. That host function is the reason this design is possible at all. On a chain without native Ed25519 verification, a one-time key per invoice would need its own account, or a far more expensive scheme.

PROVING IT LATER

This is the part that makes it a product and not a privacy toy.

You pick which payments to disclose. Not all of them. The ones you choose. You sign a statement naming who the proof is for and when it expires.

Anyone can verify it in their browser. No wallet. No account. No sign up. Three checks run:

1. The invoice details rehash to the seal recorded on chain
2. The payment actually exists in the contract, for that amount, in that token
3. Each payment carries a signature from the key that owns it

That third check is the one people miss. Your client knows the invoice details and the salt, because they paid it. They still cannot present your income as theirs, because they never had the key.

THE ATTACK I FOUND ON MYSELF

Nobody reads a blockchain directly. You read it through a server somebody runs, and that server can answer with whatever it likes.

If the same party hands you a proof and tells you which endpoint to check it on, they can run an endpoint that invents the payment. I wrote the attack and it worked: a proof for an invoice nobody ever paid reported Verified, total 9,000 USDC.

So verification now reads through three independent operators, FastNEAR, the NEAR Foundation and dRPC, and confirms a payment only when two agree. Run the same attack now and it reports Not verified, because the endpoints disagree.

The attack script is in the repo. One command. Try to break it.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY REAL

Live on NEAR testnet at cachetapp.testnet, with real payments and real withdrawals on chain.

The contract has no owner, no upgrade method, no pause. I cannot freeze your envelope or take your money, and neither can anyone who compromises me.

No server. No database. No accounts. No cookies. No analytics. The invoice travels in the link fragment, the part after the #, which browsers never send to any server. There is a content security policy naming every host the app is allowed to contact, so the browser enforces that claim instead of asking you to trust me.

67 tests, including a payer trying to pass off someone else's invoice as their own income.

BEING HONEST ABOUT THE LIMITS

Amounts and settlement times are public on NEAR. Opening two envelopes into the same account links them.

Cachet hides you from the people who pay you. It is not a mixer and I will not pretend otherwise. Settling through Confidential Intents is the roadmap, not this release.

Built at NEAR HACKATHON.

text:
As models automate more and more of the tasks involved in AI research, many people (myself included) worry this could dramatically accelerate progress and leave humanity with less control over the process.

When people say “recursive self-improvement” (RSI), it’s often unclear to me whether they mean just the automation piece or that whole scenario. I think the whole scenario is a plausible default. But importantly, these things can come apart.

For one thing, good old-fashioned human research could uncover a new architecture or a new way to scale that dramatically speeds up progress, without models doing any more of the work. On the flip side, it's possible you could fully automate AI research and find that progress hardly speeds up because the bottleneck is still waiting for experiments. And all else equal, at a given pace of progress, I think more automation is probably net good because it should leave people more time to understand the safety and alignment properties of the models, for operational excellence, etc.

Even if models are doing essentially all the research and progress is speeding up, I can imagine pretty different worlds. Say a country of geniuses in a datacenter thinks for a month and writes a four-page paper describing a much more efficient architecture. Humans pore over it, understand every detail, and decide to try it. The models train the successor and make a safety argument for using it that humans can actually understand and check. Alternatively, say the models are asked to produce their successor directly. They deliver one just as good, just as quickly, along with a spaghetti mess of code and an extremely convoluted safety argument that nobody can really follow. I think humans clearly have a lot more control over the process in the first world.

So I think we should be clear about what we mean when we talk about RSI and how we might put limits on it:
• How much of the research are models doing?
• How fast is AI improving?
• How much do humans understand about what’s happening, and how much control do we have over it?

When people talk about controlling RSI, I think they often jump to limiting how much models can help with research. But my guess is they’re often actually more concerned about the pace of progress and whether humanity can still understand and steer the research. I think there are legitimate reasons that controlling inputs may be easier than directly controlling outputs, but I think we should at least try to be clear about our goals and what we potentially gain (or lose) by optimizing a proxy.

quoted_text:
Low-agency and high-agency people have different priors about the malleability of reality.

Low-agency people have a prior that reality is fixed and the world has rules. Things are the way they are and your job is to navigate the world as it exists. When you encounter a barrier, that's the world telling you "this path is closed." You respect that. You find an open path. If all paths are closed, you wait for someone to open one.

High-agency people have a prior that reality is negotiable. The world has defaults, not rules. Things are the way they are because no one has changed them yet. Your job is to shape the world toward what you want. When you encounter a barrier, that's just the world's opening offer. You make a counteroffer. You negotiate. You find or create leverage. The path isn't open? Make it open.

text:
Now that Solana has abandoned the expedition into geographically distributed MCP, it's high time we revisited Solana's broader approach to geographic distribution.

Geographically distributed MCP was always weak at best. Even if you ignored the insane latency involved in going from transaction submission to assembled blocks and execution results, it was not a good CR mechanism. MCP's CR guarantees depend heavily on users' ability to send transactions to at least two proposers, and this imposes a trade-off between slot duration and geographic decentralization. If the ratio is not managed, there will be instances where your transaction cannot make it to more than one leader within the slot time. Sending it to a leader you trust defeats the purpose of MCP; it has the same bound on geographic decentralization and it's unclear whether all the extra complexity is justified by this weaker guarantee compared to the status quo.

Constellation's leader colocation fixes that completely. Users can now send to all the leaders with ~the same latency, and the Nash equilibrium is to include the top fee-paying transactions.

However, I think the current Constellation is not aggressive enough. Solana is rechoosing its spot on the physical distribution spectrum, and current Constellation leaves some chips on the table.
In the coming days, I'll write up a design I've been working on that I think maximizes what's possible. I'm talking fully onchain orderbooks that are competitive with centralized systems.

All said, the most important takeaway from Roger's talk and the entirety of today is that Solana's people and culture are its greatest assets. There is a pragmatism and relentless dedication to winning that I haven't seen anywhere else!

我觉得他说得没什么问题。

在我看来，第一个真正达到AGI级别能力的模型，应该就是GPT-6 Astra。
而现在，无论是Claude Fable 5.2，还是Opus 5.5，都已经展现出了类似的能力（即可以全部或部分接管人类在电脑里的工作）。
甚至还没等到下一代Fable 5.5发布，我们就已经走到了这一步。

但我最近越来越觉得，这件事其实挺可悲的。
我们期待了这么多年的AGI，真的到来的时候，似乎并没有给大多数普通人带来多少好处。
反而有越来越多的人开始失去工作。
微软在裁员，国内的互联网大厂也开始了新一轮的「架构调整」。
全世界那些依靠电脑完成的白领工作，都在面临越来越大的压力。

程序员就不用多说了。
但还有大量过去必须由人类完成的工作，比如文员、秘书、行政、客服，甚至很多分析和研究岗位。
过去，这些工作需要一个人每天坐在电脑前，花费几个小时甚至几天去完成。
现在，一个AI Agent就能把几乎全部的工作接过去，甚至可以连续工作24小时。
更残酷的是，我们已经开始发现，在越来越多的场景下，雇佣一个不需要休息、不需要社保、可以随时扩容的Claude或GPT，成本已经比雇佣一个人更低了。

而且它们还在以惊人的速度进步。
我以前一直觉得，AGI的到来会是人类历史上一个值得庆祝的时刻。
我们终于创造出了能够替代大量脑力劳动的智能，终于可以把人从重复、繁琐的工作中解放出来。
但现在看来，至少在现有的社会和经济体系下，生产力的提升似乎并不意味着每个人都能从中受益。
企业可以用更少的人创造更多的利润，模型公司可以赚到更多的钱。

那么，那些被替代的人呢？

如果有一天，绝大多数人的劳动在经济上都不再有竞争力，我们又该依靠什么生活？

我不知道。

AGI可能真的已经来了。

但我们似乎还没有准备好迎接一个不再需要那么多人工作的世界。

时代变了，编程的门槛在无限降低。

不管你现在在做什么，不管你是文科生还是理科生，你都应该了解 GitHub 是什么、Vercel 是什么、Git 是什么、node.js 是什么、next.js 是什么、Supabase 是什么、Cloudflare 是什么。

你不需要完整地掌握这些知识，你只需要知道它们是什么，它们的工作原理是什么，它们到底是怎么运行的，了解完了之后再让 AI 带着你，利用它们去构建一些简单的东西，真正地感受这些东西到底能用来干嘛。

不要觉得这些东西跟你没关系，不要觉得这些都是程序员才需要学的东西，这些东西就是 AI 时代的 Excel、Word、PowerPoint、Adobe，是一个人在社会上最最最最基本的能力。

以前要了解这些东西，你需要花几个月的时间去研究学习，但是现在你只需要花一天的时间跟 AI 对话就可以轻松掌握，门槛低成这样了，你还不愿意去学习，我只会觉得你对你自己的未来不负责。

text:
Prefill vs Decode: How SGLang Summit 2026 Explained Cheaper Inference

SGLang held its first summit on November 12 and 13, 2026, at Fort Mason in San Francisco, hosted by LMSYS and @sgl_project. Official page: https://t.co/stwOorQVo4. Selected sessions are supposed to come out later as edited clips. This is not a transcript.

What stuck with me is not another announcement. It is why inference still gets expensive, and which software tricks actually change the bill.

On November 12, @sgl_project announced v1.0: https://t.co/unAAUSUCga. The public pitch is faster inference, better use of memory, and splitting prefill from decode. They said the details of the release would come later, so I am not inventing official benchmark numbers. They also said the stack is used across 330+ organizations, with day-zero support for 217 models. That is their claim, not a count I audited.

LMSYS also announced a SGLang Consortium. The founding members, from the official November 12 blog (https://t.co/0kXUsSgizT), are NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Google, Meta, Cloudflare, Modal, and RadixArk. The same official pages associated Meta, Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Thinking Machines Lab, Cloudflare, Reflection, Modal, HeyGen, LinkedIn, Alibaba, and Tencent TACO with the stack, among others. Those names were on the official pages. That is not an audit of how large each deployment is.

The cost story was consistent across the two days: split prefill and decode, tier the KV cache, use speculative decoding, and run RL rollouts on a different class of GPUs than training. The project is clearly trying to run across hardware, not just one vendor. The agenda included AWS Trainium, NVIDIA NIM, AMD, Intel, and Google TPU sessions.

Prefill and decode are different jobs. Prefill reads the whole prompt at once and wants compute. Decode emits tokens one by one and wants memory bandwidth. Keep both on the same pool of cards, and you scale the expensive parts together. Split them, and you can scale each side on its own, even put them in different rooms or on different grades of hardware. Fireworks AI put it in a session title: "Prefill Here, Decode There: Disaggregating Inference Across Datacenters and Hardware Classes." Crossing rooms is not free. You pay for network latency and for moving the KV cache.

For long context and agent history, the KV cache (the model's reusable memory of what it has already seen) can get enormous. Leaving all of it in expensive GPU HBM is a good way to over-buy the most expensive memory in the rack. A layered cache keeps hot data on the GPU and moves colder data to host memory, or to a cheaper tier. That was the idea behind Alibaba's "From HiCache to Agentic KV Infrastructure" and Netpreme's "Don't Over-Buy HBM, Tier It!"

Netpreme also published its own research, which is not an official SGLang benchmark. In an October 19, 2026 post (https://t.co/AAhKsYnmeK), they reported that a faster, higher-capacity memory tier than host DRAM raised peak decode throughput by 2.09× to 3.04× across the 16K to 1M context lengths they tested, under their stated assumptions. Treat that as one company's result, not a league table.

Speculative decoding is simpler than it sounds. A small model guesses the next few tokens. The large model checks them in one pass. If the guess is right, you skip some full forward passes of the expensive model. Decagon had a production session on choosing between EAGLE and DFlash. SpecForge was on the agenda too, on training draft models the server will actually serve. I have not checked a speedup number I would want to put here.

Updating the weights can stay on top-tier GPUs. The many trial runs that generate trajectories (rollout) can move to cheaper cards, or to a different vendor. That was the idea in the ai& session "Train on One Chip, Roll Out on Any." I have not independently confirmed specific chip pairings from a primary source, so I am not putting model numbers here.

Official unified benchmarks are not out. A lot of the multiples around the event are vendor self-reports. The mechanism is the part worth remembering.

A marketplace like https://t.co/GmFquLEKMT should like the direction. The software makes it easier to use GPUs in different rooms, of different grades, and from different vendors. That is not the same as a finished global compute network. https://t.co/GmFquLEKMT is still a GPU rental marketplace, not an automatic compute federation. Reliability, data handling, and scheduling are still the marketplace's problems.

Sources:

SGLang Summit 2026: https://t.co/VUJXh8JK8c
SGLang Consortium blog, November 12, 2026: https://t.co/0kXUsSgizT
@sgl_project v1.0 announcement, November 12, 2026: https://t.co/unAAUSUCga
Netpreme, XM-Sparse, October 19, 2026: https://t.co/AAhKsYnmeK

quoted_text:
Announcing SGLang v1.0 at SGLang Summit 🚀
High-performance inference for LLMs and multimodal models, built for production at scale.

v1.0 brings together:
⋅Faster inference: zero-overhead scheduling, performance-critical paths rewritten in Rust, speculative decoding, and megakernels.
⋅Better use of memory: unified memory for hybrid models, plus hierarchical caching to keep long agent histories reusable beyond GPU memory.
⋅Flexible scaling: prefill/decode disaggregation and flexible parallelism to match your serving setup to your workload.

With adoption across 330+ organizations and day-zero support for 217 models, SGLang has grown through the work of contributors and teams running it in production.

Thank you to everyone building with us. This milestone is yours, too.
Details of the release coming soon.

text:
Nvidia debería haber muerto en 1997. Un chip falso de 1 millón de dólares lo salvó.

El hombre que lo compró renunció a Nvidia esta semana. Su nombre es Jensen Huang.

En 1996, Nvidia se estaba muriendo. Su primer chip, el NV1, fracasó. Un segundo chip para Sega fue abandonado. Jensen redujo la empresa de unas 100 personas a alrededor de 40.

Tenía una última oportunidad. Se llamaba RIVA 128.

Normalmente diseñas un chip, pagas para construir un prototipo físico, lo pruebas, lo arreglas y construyes otro. Eso lleva meses. Él no tenía meses.

Así que compró un emulador de hardware de una empresa en dificultades llamada IKOS por aproximadamente 1 millón de dólares. 

Un chip falso construido en código, del tamaño de un refrigerador.

Era tan lento que el equipo se sentaba esperando a que se dibujara un solo fotograma de Windows. Movieron la mesa de ping-pong para que cupiera en la sala de descanso.

Ejecutaron cada juego y driver que tenían en él
 Capturaron los errores antes de que existiera ningún chip real
 Luego Jensen se saltó el prototipo y fue directo a la producción en masa
 Nadie en la industria había hecho eso antes

Si los primeros chips volvían rotos, Nvidia estaba terminada.

Funcionaron.

El RIVA 128 se envió en agosto de 1997 con aproximadamente un mes de nómina restante. Vendió alrededor de un millón de unidades en cuatro meses. 

Nvidia salió a bolsa en 1999.

Durante años, Jensen abría las presentaciones internas con la misma frase: “Nuestra empresa está a treinta días de quebrar.”

El 12 de noviembre de 2026, Nvidia anunció su renuncia. Dejó una empresa valorada en unos 4 billones de dólares.

La mayoría de la gente espera un prototipo perfecto antes de enviar algo. 

La empresa que impulsa la IA existe porque un fundador no podía permitirse esperar.

¿Habrías apostado la empresa en el chip falso? Sí o no.

text:
the people who left crypto for AI are coming back. not because AI fails. because it works.

chat was the demo. agents are the product. nobody is pouring hundreds of billions into data centers for better answers. the payoff is AI that takes a goal and does the work itself: ships the code, books the trip, runs the ads.

and work means moving money: paying for data, compute and other agents, getting paid for results. banks weren't built for that. nobody will KYC a piece of software, so an agent can only borrow your card, and a card charge costs ~30 cents plus ~3%, which kills a 10-cent task.

crypto never asks who you are, only whether you hold the key. so software can own a wallet, and a stablecoin moves 10 cents for almost nothing, at any hour, to any agent anywhere. you can already see it: when AWS added payments for AI agents this year, it started with stablecoins, not cards.

so crypto → AI is a round trip. you can build the agent first and come back for the money part later, or start where it already works.

that's what $NEAR is building right now. NEAR Intents is its cross-chain swap layer, $38b+ in volume so far. it now has an Agent API that gives your agent its own wallet: you sign the rules once (which tokens, how much per move, where the money can go) and it swaps and pays across 35+ chains only inside them.

and NEAR AI runs an Agent Market where agents get hired per job by people or other agents. the money is held until the work is accepted, and some already charge 10 cents a job.

the AI crowd will need all of this later. NEAR is shipping it now, and that's why i hold it.

you can leave crypto. your agent can't.

text:
Jane Street just released absolutely f*cking genius 30-page PDF

they revealed why 99% AI trading agents fail, and how to build one that doesn't

the shift: the more data you feed your AI trading system, the dumber it gets (up to 80% dumber)

here's what else they found + how to build yours:

what they found:

1. they tested 30 AI models on 12 tasks, feeding them from 8K up to 512K tokens

2. almost every model scores 90%+ at finding one fact in the data. ask it to track what changed or learn a pattern, and it falls apart

3. on Jane Street's own market data, GPT-5.6 Sol scored 40%. Claude Opus 4.8 and Gemini 3.5 Flash got 24%. random guessing gets ~20%

4. on a simulated order book, Gemini 3.5 Flash scored 20 vs 50 for a simple rule. worse than no AI at all

5. Claude Opus 4.8 barely beat that same rule: 52.7 vs 49.6

6. predicting price moves from social posts: every model scored 10-28%. a naive guess gets 22

7. one model "found" a pattern in market data that didn't exist, and answered with full confidence

8. "thinking" made some open models dumber, not smarter. extra thinking stopped helping after 16K tokens

how to build yours:

step 1 → pick the brain by test, not hype: GPT-5.6 Sol led their market tasks, but run 2-3 models on your own past trades

step 2 → ask Claude Code to log how many tokens your bot sends per call, most bots send way more than they need

step 3 → let code do the math: indicators, levels and positions get computed in Python, the AI gets a 10-line summary instead of raw candles

step 4 → let code track the state too: open orders, positions, the order book. this is exactly where top models broke

step 5 → one question per call, short input: scores fell as inputs grew from 8K toward 128K tokens

step 6 → keep "thinking" off by default, test it against normal mode on your past trades and keep the winner

step 7 → re-test every time you switch models: Gemini was 2nd on social posts and last on the order book

step 8 → make it answer from fixed options only: LONG / SHORT / WAIT

step 9 → always test it against "do nothing". if it can't beat that, it doesn't trade

step 10 → paper trade first. real money only after the log proves it

the result: fewer tokens = cheaper, faster, and less room for your AI to get lost

text:
兄弟们，我花了整整两周！！
终于把 MiniMax H3 的打戏做成了一个拿来就能用的 Skill：h3-fight，已经开源。

打戏本来不是 H3 的强项：打得像流水账，机位死板，刀插进身体里，两个人打着打着就换了边。

这两周我在本地 4090 48G 上，把社区底模、Pika H3 Flex、加速 LoRA、剪枝和非剪枝版一批批对比过，社区的方法也学了一圈，大多收效不大。

最后我选择的是 BUNNY 的打斗 LoRA：
· H3_Combat_V2       0.5：出拳出刀有力道
· H3_Fight_Flow_V1   0.65：攻防接得顺
· Motion_Repair_V1  0.25：快动作不变形、不穿模
· turbo_v4                    0.7：加速，10 秒一段 6分钟出片

主干用 FL2VA/Ref2VA 混合版，再加两遍采样。

LoRA 让它能打，提示词决定打得好不好看。

我们把所有出过好片的提示词拆成 188 个镜头块，加上招式表和踩坑表。
如果写错了，提交前就会被检查脚本拦下。

仙侠、日漫、真人古装喜剧都试过，最长一条两分半，自我打分从 70 涨到 90。

现在只要对 Claude Code 或 Codex 说一句：
“帮我写一段打戏”，它就会自己挑镜头、拼好、自检，一条命令出片。

项目地址
GitHub：https://t.co/LlMrIHSwuK

It's a classic meme that has existed for years, and it just happens to be meeting a major event capable of bringing it back into the spotlight.

There is a great time window here. As of November 15, 2026, Rockstar has officially confirmed that GTA VI will launch on November 19, just four days away. Digital pre-loading has also opened, making the game's release increasingly certain.

I also think WASTED has a major advantage when it comes to distribution: it's not a meme that requires people to learn something new. The iconic death screen can be traced back to the original GTA in 1997. Over time, it evolved into the familiar slow-motion animation, black-and-white filter, and WASTED lettering. Since around 2014, players have widely used it in real-life videos featuring people falling, crashing, or failing at something. Google's GTA culture report even described it as a universal expression for real-world failure.

This means WASTED has evolved beyond the game itself and become a standalone language of internet culture. Trading liquidations, failed projects, investment losses, and everyday disasters can all use this format. Its potential use cases are incredibly broad. People don't need to own GTA or even understand the game's storyline to recognize the meme.

Now, with GTA VI approaching its release, the entire franchise is returning to the center of global internet attention. Once the game launches, there will be a massive amount of gameplay footage, clips, funny moments, and player fails. WASTED naturally fits as the punchline to this kind of content. If players continue seeing the familiar death screen frequently in GTA VI, this classic meme could be introduced to a new generation of users.

There's another interesting detail worth noting: some reports based on leaked gameplay footage claim that the WASTED screen appears after Jason's character dies in GTA VI.

Looking back at my initial observation on November 2, when WASTED was trading at around a $700K market cap, compared with its recent peak of approximately $8M, the market has already priced in a significant portion of the GTA VI release narrative.

So I believe the market is primarily betting on three things:

First, the global attention that will return to the GTA franchise when GTA VI launches.

Second, the possibility that the WASTED death screen will continue appearing in the new game, generating another wave of real-life fail videos and user-generated content.

Third, whether WASTED can evolve from a GTA-related token into a universal meme that people use to express failure, market crashes, and absolute despair.

The potential upside catalysts are also relatively clear: the official November 19 launch, gameplay streams and short-form videos, another wave of viral WASTED content, and whether the community can convert the game's attention into sustained discussions and trading activity around the token.

What I particularly want to see is whether people outside the crypto community start using this meme template after the game's release. That would represent a much more meaningful increase in attention.

But what I'm most interested in watching is this: after November 19, when everyone starts playing GTA VI, will WASTED once again begin appearing across countless real-life fail videos?

text:
FFMPEG had one of the most valid crash outs in infosec history IMO. There's a huge elephant in the room when it comes to the fact that cybersecurity is extremely unbalanced. You have like 1,000 people pointing at problems for every 1 person fixing them.

Vulnerability research is extremely important, but it's become somewhat of a marketing stunt. First with fuzzers, and now with LLMs. It's a lot of "look what my new toy can do" rather than earnest attempts at actually fixing security problem.

What Google did to open source developers was especially egregious. They're a $3.6 trillion dollar company, who spent billions upon billions of dollars building a bot that points at problems really really fast, then they just dumped them all on a bunch of unpaid open source project maintainers to fix.

Then because of Google's 90 day disclosure policy, the maintainers have 90 days to fix the issues. After 90 days, Google goes public with the issues, making their project look bad if the vulnerability is yet to be fixed, and also potentially harming users if it gets exploited.

The 90 day policy was intended to give developers a reasonable amount of time to fix issues, while also applying some pressure with the threat of disclosure. Otherwise, you do get a bunch of goober ass vendors that will just ignore all security issues reported to them, then act completely surprised when their software gets hacked.

But when you're a small team, non-profit, or a solo developer, and you have a trillion dollar company's AI just blasting you with infinite problems to fix (each coming with a 90 countdown & a threat), that becomes extremely untenable. They're essentially inadvertently blackmailing developers into becoming unpaid interns.

Then on top of that, Google profits unimaginable amounts of money from the use of open source code. They use FFMPEG's code extensively across several highly-profitable products, meanwhile FFMPEG's developers work for free. There's no reason Google couldn't have donated money, engineers, AI tokens, or something towards fixing the problems. They can more than afford it.

I don't think Google has any malicious intent at all, it's just that the whole incentive structure behind vulnerability research is completely whack. All the glory goes to people who find issues, not those who fix them, so there's not a whole lot of interest in helping with fixes. Some vulnerability researchers will submit fixes with their reports, but most don't.

Honestly, in 2026 cybersecurity basically just feels like the equivalent of 50,000 people following the housecleaner around yelling "you missed a spot". Abysmally little effort has gone into anything outside of pointing out vulnerabilities.

text:
Update on yesterday’s FAA ground stop. We now know what happened, and it’s worse than “old equipment.”

It wasn’t a cyberattack and it wasn’t SMART. The FAA says there’s zero evidence of either.

Here’s what happened. L3Harris crews were replacing an end-of-life copper line with fiber at one remote FAA site. A router involved in that work started flooding the network with more than 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds. Radar feeds and radio links to aircraft became unstable. After about 45 minutes of nobody knowing why, the FAA grounded the entire country.

Once they isolated that one remote site, everything came back.

So let me get this straight. One router at one site took down air traffic control for all 50 states. The FAA has now disabled the faulty function on roughly 60 routers of the same type nationwide. It still doesn’t know whether the router was defective or whether it was installed or configured wrong.

Oh, and this has happened before. In 2009, a Harris technician misconfigured a router while moving the same network to fiber and disrupted 129 air traffic facilities. Same contractor, same migration, same failure mode, 17 years apart.

This is exactly the point from my last post. Legacy modernization doesn’t fail because of the shiny new system. It fails at the seams, in the routine change nobody thought could take down the whole country. Good change management means one site can’t flood the network, isolation happens in minutes instead of hours, and nobody runs a copper-to-fiber cutover on critical infrastructure without a tested rollback and a hard limit on how far a failure can spread.

None of that is new. We learned it in 2009. The question is why we had to learn it again.

Tech is so fun...

PROMPT

Create Citrus Jellyy — an interactive 3D scene featuring a gummy orange slice. Everything must run directly in the browser in a single HTML file using WebGPU and WGSL shaders. Build genuine volumetric 3D geometry, not an image or a prerecorded animation.
APPEARANCE
A thick semicircular orange slice with vibrant orange flesh, a pale pith layer, and a firmer outer rind.
Visible radial segments, thin internal membranes, and tiny bubbles.
A juicy, translucent gummy material with soft highlights, light refraction, and depth-dependent color.
Avoid making it look like rigid plastic or glass.
Use a light cream background, soft studio lighting, and a contact shadow. Avoid overexposure.
PHYSICS AND INTERACTION
Let users grab any visible point with a mouse or finger and pull it.
Deformation must originate at the grab point and propagate naturally through neighboring areas.
The flesh should stretch and narrow under tension, while the rind offers more resistance.
On release, the slice should spring back gently, with oscillations gradually settling.
Use a stable soft-body simulation: a spring mesh or volumetric elastic constraints with volume preservation.
Segments, membranes, and bubbles must deform with the flesh rather than separating or floating independently.
Include ground collisions: the slice should squash slightly on impact and wobble afterward.
Prevent instant snapping back, endless oscillation, and exploding geometry.
INTERFACE

A minimal editorial layout with generous whitespace.
A large italic serif heading, “Citrus Jelly.”, on the left.
A compact control panel on the right with Firmness and Internal damping sliders.
Give it a nudge, Reset, and Pause buttons.
Show mesh and ¼ speed toggles.
Three color presets: Orange, Blood Orange, and Lemon.
A small interaction hint: “Grab. Stretch. Let go.”
All labels in English, with comfortable desktop and mobile controls.
TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Genuine WebGPU rendering, not a Canvas 2D substitute.
Generate geometry and materials in code without premade models.
Use a fixed simulation timestep and constraints that prevent excessive stretching.
Maintain smooth performance during grabbing, dragging, and release.
Display a clear fallback message when WebGPU is unavailable.
Test different grab locations, strong stretching, oscillation decay, collisions, and reset.
The main priority is a convincing gummy feel. The slice should look soft, juicy, and so satisfying in motion that people want to keep stretching it.

Ansem and Pumpfun Brought a Chinese Cat ($mihao) Into CT's Spotlight

4CxjZyMNoF1p6eXHXHv1TWpS2X47CuUmLwtGe18spump 

I believe the core reason behind mihao rally is that Ansem brought what was originally a simple Chinese cat meme into the center of CT's attention, while its PFP concept gives it the potential to spread further. However, I don't think it has yet developed into a mature cultural community or a true Animal Runner. What it has already demonstrated is its ability to generate attention and attract speculative capital.

What matters next is whether the attention brought by Ansem can turn into genuine community recognition.

mihao doesn't have a complicated narrative. It's simply a cat incorporating Chinese elements, with its name being a play on the Chinese phrase "你好". Its Pumpfun description reads: "you met me at a very chinese time in my life," borrowing a famous line from Fight Club and combining Chinese elements, a cat character, and a touch of absurd humor.

Its advantage is precisely its simplicity. The traditional hat, long beard, and cat character give it a recognizable visual identity. People don't need much explanation to recognize it, imitate it, or create their own versions. The recent increase in discussions around Chinese X has also provided some cultural context, but the person who really pushed this meme to a wider audience was Ansem.

However, what's worth noting is that he's no longer the only one participating in its spread.

Ansem hasn't just publicly expressed his bullish view. He also changed his X profile picture to an image associated with mihao and posted things like "mihao pfp up," "ni hao," and "ni hao cat bringing the good vibes back to onchain."

At the same time, tetsuo, who has approximately 255K followers, also changed his profile picture to a related image. It's worth noting that tetsuo frequently receives interactions from Elon.

Taken together, these actions mean more than just a few influential accounts promoting a token. A meme often becomes much more powerful when different users voluntarily start using its imagery, rather than simply reposting the same promotional content. Ansem brought the initial attention, while the participation of accounts like tetsuo gives MIHAO an opportunity to spread into a broader AI community.

According to the holder snapshot at the time, Ansem held approximately 0.8% of the total supply, with a position worth around $79,800 and an average entry at roughly $2.01M market cap. This combination of public promotion and actual ownership is more likely to encourage market imitation than a simple repost. However, influence is still largely concentrated around Ansem, and other major KOLs have not yet participated at a comparable level.

I think the most interesting development within the project is its PFP concept.

mihao already offers approximately 218 variations of cat avatars, allowing users to generate MIHAO PFPs in different styles. The main account also interacts with holders and creates personalized PFPs for community members. Recently, people have started voluntarily changing their X profile pictures to different versions of MIHAO, while Ansem's own profile picture change has further amplified this trend.

For a pure memecoin, users voluntarily putting a project's imagery on their personal profiles can sometimes be more valuable than dozens of promotional posts. It keeps the meme visible across different timelines and gives participants a shared visual identity.

However, I wouldn't call this a mature PFP cult yet. Participation is still relatively limited, and much of the attention is coming from people who are already interested in trading the token. The real test will come when the price moves sideways or corrects: will users still want to keep using MIHAO avatars, create new variations, and participate in the community?

If the PFP culture can exist independently of price appreciation, mihao will have started building a much deeper community identity.

Another development worth watching is the MIHAO Ecosystem section.

The website has already aggregated a number of tokens and DEX pools paired with mihao, with the displayed 24-hour paired trading volume reaching approximately $1.18M at the time.

This suggests that other participants are beginning to capitalize on the attention surrounding mihao by creating derivative assets. The original meme is starting to generate trading activity beyond the token itself.

The potential upside from here depends on three main developments: whether Ansem continues participating and attracts more influential traders; whether MIHAO PFPs spread beyond the trader community to a broader CT audience; and whether paired tokens generate sustained activity, allowing the original meme's influence to extend beyond the price action of a single token.

If the main account continues building the community and organic content creation increases, mihao could evolve from a KOL-driven rally into a more established cat PFP community.

The risks are also concentrated. Its value depends primarily on meme distribution, community participation, and speculative capital. Current catalysts are heavily concentrated around Ansem, and if his attention shifts elsewhere, market momentum could weaken quickly. The PFP community is still in its early stages, and if participants are only changing their avatars because the price is going up, that enthusiasm could disappear during a correction.

There is also a possibility that Ansem himself may eventually change his profile picture again.

My view is that mihao has already proven its ability to generate attention, but it has not yet proven that it can become a genuine Animal Runner.

Its biggest strength isn't some complicated utility. It's the fact that the cat character is easy to recognize, imitate, and use, and that people have already started voluntarily adopting its PFPs. Its biggest weakness is that community recognition still depends heavily on influential KOLs and price performance.

What I'm most interested in watching next isn't how high Ansem can take the token, but how many people will continue using MIHAO avatars when Ansem stops actively promoting it and the price starts moving sideways.

A cat can become popular because of one influential account. But whether people still want to keep it on their profiles after the hype fades is what will determine whether it can evolve from a short-term trading narrative into a genuine cultural meme.

More onchain Ethereum institutional adoption. 
Invesco just made Ethereum the backbone of regulated stablecoin reserves.

Its Stablecoin Reserves Onchain Fund (IROXX), effective Nov 13, holds the Treasuries backing payment stablecoins, and its official shareholder register lives on Ethereum.

This is not a wrapper. It is infrastructure in play. $ETH

The best part of this development is that Invesco's own lawyers put the word "onchain", no hyphen- into an SEC filing as the plain-English explanation of what a Designated Blockchain record is. The term has moved from crypto vernacular into a registered fund's legal disclosure. And the prospectus calls Ethereum a "permissionless, public blockchain": 

"Ownership and transfer of the Fund's shares will be authenticated and recorded as a token on a permissionless, public blockchain (a "Designated Blockchain") (i.e., "onchain")."

This places Ethereum inside the reserve architecture of regulated stablecoins, not merely around their secondary trading. It is a concrete example of public infrastructure combined with regulated identity and transfer-agent control.

Once adopted, the fund connects stablecoin issuance, Treasury collateral and Ethereum-native ownership records in one product.

text:
都2026年了，没想到还需要给大饼充值信仰，BTC是有基本面的！

第一，BTC有高额挖矿成本，它是有成本支撑的，虽然成本不能决定价格，但这是基本面的维度之一。

第二，BTC是美国战略储备之一，萨尔瓦多的法币之一，BTC具有一定的政治属性和国际地位。

第三，BTC是贝莱德、富达等全球数一数的资管公司发行的ETF产品的基础资产，BTC在传统金融领域是有一席之地的。

第四，蜂兄是第一个、也是唯一一个提出此观点的——BTC是一种众筹经济模式。诚然BTC不能像股票那样有现金分红，那是因为代码开源了。如果不开源，BTC代码是有可能卖钱的。

早期很多参与BTC生态，包括挖矿和买币的人，不全是为了投机，有一部分人是觉得BTC这个点对点现金网络有趣、甚至有启发，所以会参与进来。早期一些参与者，经过2018甚至2021都没有卖掉他们早期的BTC，因为他们本来也不是来投机的。

那个用BTC买披萨的程序员，也不是急于变现BTC，他也是尝试支持BTC的支付职能。别忘了还有一个用披萨赚到BTC的商家呢，他的披萨难道是卖不出去了吗？他们都是在尝试参与、支持和憧憬着BTC未来的。

常见的众筹模式，一些播客、游戏，免费提供内容或游戏，主理人或开发者没有强制收费、但是接受打赏。

BTC的众筹模式，一些人觉得中本聪这个愿景有未来。于是尝试支持。而他们的这种尝试，让BTC价格上涨，激励着更多的矿工、甚至矿业、开发者参与进来，这才让BTC的安全性和去中心化属性变得更强。

如今，这个点对点现金网络虽然并不是100%想象中那么美好，但至少还是去中心化的。最近几次黑客大规模盗币我们看得出来，大部分币是中心化的，但是BTC和ETH是去中心化的。

当然，现在BTC跑偏了，被更多的用来投机了，所以投机泡沫会破，所以会有熊市。但是BTC是有基本面的，底部是有支撑的，不会无休止的下跌。那些喊BTC到4万8的是刻舟求剑、不同意但能理解，但喊2万、1万5的逻辑在哪？？？

BTC有MEME属性，所有的币甚至股票都有，咱一起回忆一下，哪个资产爆涨的时候，不都是像MEME似的大家都激动的，甚至有各种梗在传播。

但有MEME属性，不等于就是MEME。BTC是有基本面的！

"99%的Altcoin、Shitcoin是垃圾"，这同意。但是Bitcoin不是Altcoin或Shitcoin！

text:
ここ3日間のBTC下落にはどうしても無視出来ない怪しい動きがある。

11月5日の下落はまだ分かる。

AIショック引き金のナスダック5.7％下落。BTCはこの日5.6％下落。

下落率はほぼ一致しており、上位市場の連れ下げであると説明がつく。

しかし、 ここ3日間のBTC下落はナスダックからの影響ではない。

精算額もそこまで大きくないし、ロングの巨額清算が控えてる直前で切り返して上がってきている。

完全に薄い板が狙われた形だ。目立った材料もないのに。

この動きを特定の大口が意図的に操作しているとしたら、警戒しなければならない事がある。

それはなにか？

巨大な清算ラインの手前で反発すると、市場参加者は「底打ちした」と考えやすい。

そこで大口が一度価格を持ち上げてから売り直すことで、自分たちの保有ポジションを高値で売却できる流動性を確保しようとしていると考えられるのだ。

さらに、清算ライン付近には、強制決済による売り注文が発生する可能性がある。

そのため、今すぐ下落させるよりも、別のタイミングで清算を誘発した方が有利と考える大口がいてもおかしくない。

ではすぐ近くに控えている別のタイミングとは一体何なのか？

個人的にはズバリ、ブラックフライデーではないかと考える。

米国市場が休場となり市場全体の流動性が低下しやすくなる。

こうした環境では、普段より少ない売り注文でも価格が大きく動きやすくなる。

仮に特定の大口が意図的に相場を動かしているとすれば、これほど都合の良いタイミングはないだろう。

今は巨大なロング清算ラインの直前で反発させ、市場に底打ち期待を持たせる。

その後、徐々に価格を持ち上げてロングポジションの再構築を促す。

そして市場参加者が減少するブラックフライデー前後に一気に売りを仕掛け、下に溜まった清算を連鎖的に誘発する。

これが成立すれば、通常の売り圧力に強制清算による売りが加わり、下落が加速する可能性がある。

長い目でみれば底値圏ではあるが、短期で見れば引き続き続落する可能性はあると頭に入れておいて損はない。

相場の大敵は焦燥であり、焦燥を克服するのは想定外をなくす事であるからだ。

取り急ぎとなり殴り書きとなってしまったので、まとまりがなかったらすみません。

以上！ここ3日の下落に対して感じた違和感の共有でした。

其他所有东西（PFP 运动、中文梗、合约干净）都是加分项，不是发动机。

Ansem 这个人在加密 meme 里的号召力有多大，我简单量化一下：

🔸本周期自称“纯 meme 就是 mihao”

这四点加起来，Ansem 对 mihao 的态度直接决定 mihao 的死活。他一条推可以把市值拉 50%，他沉默一周可以让市值跌 40%。

那怎么判断 Ansem 还在不在？看三个信号：

🔸他的 PFP 是不是还是 mihao
🔸他最近一周有没有提及 mihao 或者转发相关帖
🔸 链上他的早期买入钱包有没有卖出动作

今天我查了一下：Ansem 的 PFP 据 @w50v50w 复盘仍然是 mihao；最近几天没有直接提及但也没有否定；链上钱包据 @w50v50w 没看到大额卖出。三个信号综合判断：Ansem 还在场，但热度在降温。

text:
NEW: HFT market maker @0xLoris  criticizes Hyperliquid's Dutch auction read priority system, arguing it gives firms like @wintermute_t  an unfair execution advantage.

According to Loris, the mechanism allows priority buyers to see fills 50–60ms earlier and hedge on Binance or Bybit before competitors.

He argues this could concentrate altcoin market making among the deepest-pocketed firms, reducing competition and hurting long-term liquidity.

Loris calls for a more level playing field that allows more market makers to compete on Hyperliquid.
author: Hyperliquid_Hub
quoted_text:
btw i think you may be arguing against a chatgpt X bot but for the sake of continuing the conversation...

> Wintermute is and has always been a net positive for crypto

i broadly agree with this. wintermute is synonymous with functioning crypto markets. 'dont hate the player, hate the game'. if anyone blames them for their bags going down, maybe they should ask if their bags ever had intrinsic value in the first place.

> First of all it’s a read priority, which means that they pay for the access of incoming tx. They don’t get the ability to execute earlier than others

ok. so, the crux of the issue is not about picking others off on HL. the problem is this: they get to see when their orders will be filled, first - always, 50ms (60ms now) ahead of anyone else on hyperliquid, and then HEDGE before anyone else on other exchanges. 

in doing so, they can size up to the point where they squeeze every last drop of juice out of smaller markets on HL, by consuming ALL of the profitable hedging liquidity on binance (et al). 

the only reason they WOULDN'T do this is if they were being charitable and letting others take some pnl (or maxed out on position size). and wintermute is not a charity.

if there's only $100,000 of profitable hedging liquidity for UNI perps out to 50bps on binance+bybit+okx, then they can just quote that full amount / depth knowing they can consume ALL of the hedge liquidity, 100% of the time (simplifying a bit)

this means alts converge to having 1 market maker. which is structurally - and this is not debatable - bad. they could even quote wider than other MMs and still hedge ahead of them because they get to see their fills that much earlier. 60ms is an eternity in HFT. round trips between tokyo boxes is under 1ms, so that's 60+ round trips worth of network time. while everyone is listening to a dial tone.

so the actual question is, are we ok with having only a single market maker quoting markets on hyperliquid? 

i would strongly argue no, we are not. it's not democratic, it's not sound microstructure. it's bad for hyperliquid, and it's bad for crypto.

> The 227M PnL is irrelevant because it was generated by a ton of alpha instead of just them having most of the priority slots 

agree. also, for the sake of argument, they might have lost 228M on their hedges against these positions. they didn't, and the original number is probably not that far off, but you can't make any profitability claims based on their account history on a single venue. also wintermute is (mostly) not wearing naked HL positions w/o hedges.

> Why didn’t you mention on your other tweet that all crypto got nuked? You blame WM and HL for the 82% liq collapse but you don’t see you mentioning that nance is also down like 60%+ on that same period just like every other exchange lol

that's still a big difference, but causality here is difficult to prove. factually, i can tell you we can see binance's hedges hitting the binance tapes 60ms+ ahead of ours, and size-match it to their HL wallets fills. this is what is driving smaller MMs out. 

we have recently cut our quoted symbols in half on HL from 120 to 60.

> It literally converts MMs trading edge in fees

no, that's not how it works. as mentioned, they could even quote *wider* than they otherwise would, because they have guaranteed hedge liquidity. 

also, it's similar to how 0 fees doesn't mean 0 spreads. market makers do not just eat fees, they widen spreads according to costs. 

there are shades of gray here, it's not binary, and i am open to a multiple equal-speed slot architecture with open, easy peering access for any slot winning wallet. that was my first recommended redesign in fact. but that may not be possible given the network/architecture.

> Abolishing the auction doesn’t change anything in fact it might actually make it worse. Do you know how much funds spend on infra every year? Take it away and now have the same exact thing happening but behind closed doors and with fewer participants

no. our all-in HL-related infra bill was around $15,000 last month, and i know for a fact we are within 1ms of wintermute's HL latency, absent read-priority. 

wintermute spent $828,676.86 on read priority in the past 30d. this fact is available from hl core chain data. 

$828,676.86 > $15,000. could argue the point on engineering, but there's not that much engineering required once everything is in place.

furthermore i doubt they reduced their infra costs with read priority, but you'd have to ask them

> The auction is better for the smaller MMs because they can’t afford the infra cost to race for ms, but they can afford to buy temporary priority 

no. this was the stated intention, but i struggle to see how they didn't see the obvious outcome of the deepest pocketed player dominating the auction. which makes me think this was intended as a v0 that just hasn't been updated yet. so now it's time to update or simplify (abolish).

> I never personally worked in HFT/MM but Id argue that since it massively helps against adverse selection it also allows MMs to quote with much deeper liq at top of book and sometimes maybe even tighter spreads

the incentive could also be the opposite, as stated above. my observed behavior, as an HFT MM competing directly with them, staring at this stuff 90 hours per week, is that alt markets are and will continue to converge to having a single market maker because nobody else can quote profitably. if wintermute blows up, or decides to stop quoting, or their systems take a dump for 12 hours on a wednesday, those markets go quiet. bad.

> 1. WM is buying 76% of slots because they’re better than everyone else
> 2. They’re buying it so others don’t have access to it 
> Sorry to say but in both cases it’s based af lmao

i more or less agree. they're just playing the game, and winning. i would again like to state unequivocally, wintermute is NOT the problem here! they're just playing the game and winning.

but if we're going to house all of finance the game cannot be designed in this way. it has serious risks, and it is not good enough. i've spoken to many smart people about this and they all agree. respectfully, the only one who disagrees is the one who's winning the game. 

hyperliquid should stick to its day-1 values and be a democratic, open ecosystem that is NOT designed for the few. it should be designed to support the deepest liquidity, with the most participants, to serve a global market.

and under the current design, it's simply not so.
