text:
i asked Amjad Masad, the founder of Replit, why he thinks someone who started vibe coding 3 months ago might be better than someone who started 3 years ago.

my takeaway? some engineers have spent 3 years getting better at asking AI to do less.
🧵
1/ The problem is scar tissue.
And not knowing how to code might actually be an advantage.
People who started with early AI learned all the things it couldn't do.
So they built elaborate prompts, skill files, rules, and workarounds.
The models improved. Their habits didn't.
Amjad pointed out that even his own prompts have gotten lazier. Stronger models don't need the same micromanagement.
I've been thinking about the ambition cost of this. Not just the time wasted on unnecessary workarounds, but all the things we stop attempting because an older model convinced us they weren't possible.
2/ Here's where I disagree slightly.
Knowing how to code is an ENORMOUS advantage.
But only if you can resist the urge to micromanage implementation.
The best engineers should be able to delegate an entire outcome, recognize when the AI is wrong, and verify the result.
Their advantage isn't writing more code. It's knowing what good looks like for the use case.
3/ Now apply this to an entire engineering team.
Your models get smarter every few months.
But your company's knowledge? It gets buried in Slack, GitHub, old tickets, outdated docs, and decisions nobody remembers making.
So your agents inherit yesterday's assumptions, while your engineers keep repeating yesterday's explanations.
I wonder how much of the next leap in productivity comes from better models, and how much comes from finally questioning the limits we've gotten used to.

text:
深有感悟，也有很多同学问我AI时代应该怎么学习，怎么赚钱，从哪做起，做算力做中转做充值现在还能赚钱吗？

我从这些问题中都能够感觉的到一种深深的焦虑感
一种怕自己跟不上AI时代发展而着急乱投医的感觉

这种感觉就像，我要赚钱，但是不知道什么可以赚，于是我开始到处找项目，看看中转，看看充值，看看账号，看看自媒体，看看社群，看看课程，看了一圈下来发现好像哪个都不是特别容易上手，时间却已经浪费掉了

于是有了一种错觉：“没结果只是我没有开始，只要开始就能够做出结果”，事实上还是在逃避开始执行的问题

这个世界的创业项目本身百分之九十九都会失败
第一次创业就能成功证明运气太好了

可怕的是在我们的共识中，仿佛创业这件事情只要开始就能成功，努力就一定有结果，可真正需要的是日复一日的坚持和迭代成长，最后也不见得真的有结果

其实我也一样，对于Claude现在风控封号知道的太少了，所以在一点点去看现在稳定能够在国内使用的各个方案，不断进行尝试，今天又买了个成品号，试一下看看会不会封号，稳定了才能推出来赚钱

与此同时，专注自己的发展，不用跟别人做比较，仿佛我们越缺什么越会说什么，地球online真好有意思啊

今天还有个同学跟我说自己卡网被盗了，想要找出来是谁盗的，冲在了哪里，要跟各个卡网站长联合起来一起揪出这些不道德盗卡密的人，然后线下真实他

我笑了笑感觉这个并没有意义，他们的出现只是为了让我们更加意识到安全和隐私的重要性，好坏不重要

这个世界奖励不了好坏，奖励的是极致
无论做什么事情，极致就一定出众

分享一些最近的个人经历
我到深圳也有段时间了，离开上海之前我和我前同事说要去深圳发展做一些智算中心的生意，她们听到后很惊讶，因为我在他们眼里就是一个文静内向的女生，和做生意八竿子打不着，更别提什么智算，什么AI， 我承认我撒谎了骗她们说我亲戚在深圳做这个好像还挺挣钱的，但其实她们不知道我每天在研究AI，更不知道我其实网名叫 CuiMao，全网拥有不错的粉丝和人气。他们不理解，我不怪他们，因为我不打算告诉他们这些，中国有句古话叫，闷声发大财。直到我离开上海她们也一直无法理解我的选择。

本周黄仁勋的事情沸沸扬扬，国内的自媒体肆意发酵所谓的倒卖 b300 能翻身的理论，把黄丽比喻成拿到大结果的“成功女性”典范在小红书被捧上了神坛，几乎一夜之间全中国都知道英伟达服务器在中国是暴利行业能挣大钱。于是那些投机分子像雨后春笋般的冒了出来，阿猫阿狗都在朋友圈发求 b300，h200，甚至还有吹牛自己亲戚在英伟达是高管可以拿到货的，堪比当年疫情朋友圈卖口罩的乾隆盛世，说实话，我有点难过。因为我知道这一行真实的样子。服务器不是普通人能碰的，它是重资产、高杠杆，是大基建，是国之重器。真正在做这件事的人每天面对的是合规、电力、机房和交付，运维。根本没有那种一夜暴富的传奇故事。

为什么要发这篇长文，因为昨天晚上我以前的同事她来私信我了，就是上文提到的那几个人中的一个，说我不是去深圳搞服务器了吗，是不是赚大钱了，我说没有，和她来回打了几轮太极之后，最后她才支支吾吾的告诉我她被裁员了，我不知道以什么样的态度和立场去面对这件事，因为她算得上是我以前部门的领导，她和她的丈夫在上海还有普陀区一套 300 多万的房贷和一个小学 3 年级孩子，我发现除了安抚，一切会好的没有别的可以说的。

一晚上没睡，我给她认真科普了服务器知识，什么是国产替代中国算力崛起之类的，她在电话那头一直哦哦哦，嗯嗯嗯，我不知道她到底听进去了多少，但她说觉得自己上了那么多年的班脑子被上坏了，我觉得应该是感悟到什么了吧。她要去找工作，我劝了她，不要特地去找什么 AI 公司，那大概率都是骗子来的。过好自己的生活。

我觉得这个世界上想挣 AI 快钱的人太多了，定定心心，认认真真坐下来，把浮躁的心静下来去感受 AI 的人是极少数。现在简中网络上流传着这一句话说，只要你不学AI，过几个月你就可以不用学了，我觉得不无道理，但我更加认同的是，只要你保持学习 AI，你就可以驾驭更强力的 AI，

从 Webui 到 Comfyui 到 n8n ，再到 Openclaw，一代版本一代神，我随着时代在进化，我双眼看到的只有未来的世界。AI 时代， 保持认真，保持好奇，保持善良，我CuiMao 亲测过了，依旧有效。

但从逻辑上讲，不带仇恨，不带个人恩怨，我确实觉得币安没有合理的动机。

被盗60亿资金（已冻结30亿）虽然规模不小，但对于币安来说并非是生死存亡的救命钱。只要正常经营，一年的利润就可以覆盖。

如果把市场搞垮，把投资者账户清零，是“杀鸡取卵”，对平台没有好处。

更何况，纸包不住火，他已经是老大了，一旦事后被曝光，只会给其他竞争者提供反超的机会，得不偿失。

另外，从Glassnode的数据上看，Binance SVDD的30日SVDD曲线向上，Coinbase 向下。

text:
one example from my own framework
- day trading perps

i run a separate account just for perp day trades. clean setups only, completely detached from everything else.

i don't do this bc i really have to. i'm in a comfortable spot financially. but i still enjoy day trading and see real value in it. small wins compound and i need a working routine next to sports and everything else in life.

the goal is $100 to $500 a trading day when a clean setup shows up, with very tight risk management. executed well, that adds up to more than a full salary each month, like a classic day trading job. always chasing 10k+ trades fries my brain and those belong elsewhere anyway. sizing up to make more is fine within other frameworks, but this account should pay me daily.

this account isn't about making big money. it has always stayed in the same size range, no matter how my net worth changed and i found that to be the most stress free approach for me. it's about staying close to the market, valuing the money i earn day to day and refining my skill set, so i can trade whenever and however i want, relying on nothing but myself.

once i hit my target and the trade played out as planned, i close it completely, either at my preset TP or manually. no thinking about what else i could have caught. trade closed, day done.

the next day i look at the market again. same or different coins, same or different ranges, and i use my experience and market read to find the cleanest day trade. if nothing looks good, i don't trade at all. if there's a clean momentum play based on relative strength, a support bounce, a catalyst or whatever else the market offers, i take it without thinking about bigger targets above. trades that need more time and higher TPs belong in a different account.

one of the biggest lessons i've learned over the years is to separate my accounts by approach. i simply trade better that way.

i have one account where i only DCA into ETFs. one for individual stock trades. one for longer term altcoin spot holds. one for perp day trades. wallets for meme coins. and one for HTF perp trades that play out over a longer period.

with everything separated like this, with predefined sizes and frameworks, i can stay consistent with just my day trading account, especially in uncertain phases like this one.

my routine for this account looks like this. i keep around $5k on it and trade it up to $20k. once i hit that, i withdraw $15k to my bank account, rotate that cash into my world ETF over time and start again from $5k.

if it drops below $3k, i stop trading. i go through my previous day trades first and think deeply about what went wrong, where i can be more defensive and what to change going forward. sometimes other approaches creep into my day trades without me noticing, like holding longer to make more or mistaking HTF targets for my daily profit target.

keeping the account small relative to my net worth keeps my size small and that keeps me away from overtrading.

in the end it's all about disciplined execution. no emotions, no overthinking working against me.

i'm not focused on big net worth targets. i'm focused on daily profit targets and being fine with them. the bigger goals come naturally over the years and when you're still young, rushing usually isn't the best way.

closing everything gives my brain the rest it needs. otherwise i’d be staring at charts late into the day, trying to make more.

using the right order types, being fine with small profits and calling it a day is crucial if you want to day trade with passion and stay clear headed doing it. actually logging off is one of the hardest parts of this job and this approach helps me a lot with it.

staying consistently profitable takes a clear head every day, years of learning and unemotional execution. and the calm of knowing there will always be another range, another setup, another trade.

this might not work for other traders. everyone has their own edge and framework. but it works for me, and that's all that matters.
author: watchingmarkets
quoted_text:
overtraining and overtrading

when i prepare for an ironman, i only focus on the sessions planned for that day. i show up and do them with discipline, even when i’m unmotivated at the start. no extra run on top just to get more volume or reach the goal faster.

that’s the classic mistake. you keep the big race in mind, want to get there too fast and end up overtrained.

years in the sport taught me to trust the plan, stay consistent all year and actually rest. recovery isn’t lost time. it’s where the growth happens and that growth is what carries you on race day.

trading follows the same principles, especially in the capital building phase.

your day trading setup is your training plan. every day you focus on your range, take your small profits and move on. no “i could have caught the whole bounce”, no “i could have made x on this move”. keep the big picture in mind, but keep your day trading targets realistic.

and just like in training, not every day is a session day. when the market gives you nothing clean, sitting out is your rest day. it protects your capital the same way recovery protects your body.

the same mistake applies too. chasing the big goal too fast leads to oversized positions, forced trades and revenge trading.

overtraining means injury and lost progress.

overtrading means losses and lost capital.

one of my biggest lessons, in sports and in markets, is that consistency beats intensity. small sessions and small wins compound into something much bigger.

"DATs mostly trade as a levered version of momentum Bitcoin. And so part of me wonders, if we get another momentum boom, will the DATs trade right back up to their premiums again?"

"That's what the historical data shows. The ETFs actually didn't do that much damage to their premiums. It was more the market movements that did damage to them. And if the market movement taketh, it can giveth if it comes back."

"I do think peak DAT has probably passed. But I don't think they're dead forever."

我发现讨论的小伙伴很多啊，我扒了一下代码，和大家解释一下：

1. 对，就是互关的人留言对推文推荐的帮助是最大的，也就是说只要互关的小伙伴过来说一声，且这个小伙伴不是被标记位 Spam 那么就能拿到顶格的 20 分。

2. 如果回复你的小伙伴是 AI ，但他没有被标记为 Spam ，且你关注了，那么也是能获得 20 分。

3. 如果回复你的小伙伴都是 AI ，但是他已经被标记为 Spam 了，很抱歉即便是你的推文，也肯可能会降权。

第三点可能争议最大，别人是 Spam 就故意刷你，你有什么办法，这就要看 X 的 AI 是怎么计算了，如果计算这些 Spam 的账户是故意帮你刷量的，那你就会受到惩罚，如果认为是无意的，最起码不会被加分。

总的来说 X 目前的顶格就是鼓励互相关注的人在对方的推文下互动，这就是最顶格了。说人话，蓝V互关意义不大，需要的是蓝V互关后还要互相留言。

对，你说的对，就是最早刷 Kaito 的策略。

author: PhyrexNi
quoted_text:
多说一句在 X 的代码中对于“互关回复”的定义

触发条件（必须同时满足）：

1. 双方互相关注（你关注了对方，对方也关注了你）

2. 对方发的是原创帖（不是回复、不是转发）

3. 你在这条原创帖下面回复

满足以上条件这条原创帖在排名时，回复这个信号的权重会从普通的 5 分变成 5 + 15 = 20 分。

几个关键点：

1. 加分的是原帖，不是回复。算法在给原帖打分时，会觉得“互关的人更可能回复”，所以给原帖更高的回复权重。

2. 如果只是单方面关注，没有互关，就没有这个加成。

3. 回复别人的评论、回复别人的转发，都不算。

4. 引用帖（Quote）也算原创内容，可以触发。

所以说人话就是互关的人回复你的原创帖，你的原帖能吃到更高的回复权重（20 分），比普通回复（5 分）高很多。

这是 7 月就上线的老规则，这次没改。

所以如果想要让推文的分数增加，最好的方法仍然是在原创的推文中让已经互关的小伙伴回复，回复啥都行，算法没有限制。

PS：这才是 AI 带来的好处，我用 Claude 随时在监控 X 的 Github 的修改，一旦有修改就会提醒我，并且告诉我修改了什么。

虽然我对于刷流量兴趣不大，但想来有兴趣的小伙伴肯定不少，就做了这个监控。主要是最近不想太浪费额度了，就降低了监控扫描的间隔。

text:
🚨 MUSS SAYLOR JETZT VERKAUFEN? BITCOIN FÄLLT UNTER 63.000$ - STRATEGY FAST 11 MILLIARDEN IM MINUS

Mittwoch, Konferenz bei Cantor Fitzgerald. Michael Saylor sagt auf der Bühne, den Verkäufern gingen die Bitcoin aus.

Seitdem ist #Bitcoin von rund 74.000 auf 62.600 Dollar gefallen. Minus 15 Prozent in vier Tagen.

Gestern legt Saylor nach. Bitcoin im letzten Monat minus 17,3 Prozent, seine Vorzugsaktie STRC praktisch unverändert, mit Dividende sogar plus 1,0 Prozent.

Auf CT läuft seitdem eine Frage: Kommt der Crash daher, dass Saylor verkaufen muss?

Kurze Antwort: Er muss nicht, und in dieser Woche hat er nicht. Ob er will, ist die spannendere Frage.

MUSS ER?

Strategy hält 850.364 Bitcoin, im Schnitt für 75.456 Dollar gekauft. Bei 62.600 liegt der Bestand fast 11 Milliarden unter Einstand. Bis zum Einstand muss Bitcoin gut 20 Prozent steigen.

Das tut weh. Zwingen kann ihn trotzdem keiner.

→ Kein Bitcoin ist verpfändet, die Wandelanleihen sind ungesichert, einen Margin Call gibt es nicht.
→ In der Kasse liegen rund 4,9 Milliarden Dollar. Laut Strategy reicht das 3,4 Jahre für Dividenden und Zinsen.
→ Die erste Anleihe, die Gläubiger vorzeitig zurückgeben können, ist 1,01 Milliarden schwer. Termin: September 2027.

Saylor hat es am Mittwoch selbst vorgerechnet. Rund 1,5 Milliarden Dividenden im Jahr. Steigt Bitcoin um 2 Prozent im Jahr, kann er sie für immer zahlen. Erst wenn Bitcoin Jahr für Jahr 17 Prozent verliert, müsste er neu finanzieren.

@Nostre_damus, Gold-Konto, verbreitet gerade, Strategy habe 1,05 Milliarden Null-Prozent-Anleihen, die in drei Monaten fällig werden. Die gibt es seit Februar 2025 nicht mehr, die Gläubiger haben damals in Aktien getauscht.

HAT ER?

Die letzte Wochenmeldung vom Montag: 1.036 Bitcoin gekauft. Ein Verkauf ist nirgends gemeldet, die nächste Meldung kommt morgen.

Verkauft haben diese Woche andere.

→ Die US-Bitcoin-ETFs haben 829 Millionen Dollar abgezogen, an jedem der fünf Handelstage. Seit dem 30. Oktober sind es 2,75 Milliarden, an zehn von elf Handelstagen.
→ In den letzten 24 Stunden wurden am Kryptomarkt 2 Milliarden Dollar liquidiert, 93 Prozent davon Longs.

Die ETFs haben diese Woche zehnmal so viel abgezogen, wie Strategy in der Woche davor in Bitcoin gesteckt hat.

Saylor fehlt in diesem Crash als Käufer, gemeldet ist von ihm kein einziger Verkauf.

WARUM DIE FRAGE TROTZDEM BERECHTIGT IST

"Saylor verkauft nie" gilt seit diesem Sommer nicht mehr.

Ende Juni hat der Verwaltungsrat Bitcoin-Verkäufe bis 1,25 Milliarden Dollar erlaubt. In derselben Woche gingen 3.588 Bitcoin für 216 Millionen raus, im Schnitt zu rund 60.000 Dollar, um Dividenden zu zahlen.

Am Mittwoch auf der Bühne dann der Satz: "Wir können Bitcoin verkaufen, wenn wir es müssten."

Der Rahmen erlaubt Verkäufe für Dividenden, sobald das günstiger ist, als neue Aktien auszugeben. Je tiefer die Aktie fällt, desto eher ist es das. Er erlaubt sie auch für den Rückkauf der eigenen Papiere. Genau dort wird es eng.

WAS DIE STABILE STRC KOSTET

STRC soll bei 100 Dollar stehen. Rutscht sie darunter, kauft Strategy zurück, dieses Jahr schon für 2,04 Milliarden Dollar.

Bezahlt wird das zuletzt mit neuen Aktien. In der Woche bis 8. November flossen 188 Millionen in den STRC-Rückkauf und 82 Millionen in Bitcoin.

Saylor hat das am Mittwoch offen gesagt: Über das nächste Jahrzehnt gebe man nach und nach ein paar neue Aktien aus, um die Dividende zu zahlen.

$MSTR hat im selben Monat fast 28 Prozent verloren. Mit Börsenschluss am 30. November fliegt die Aktie aus dem MSCI World, damit fehlt ein Käufer für jede neue Aktie.

Die STRC-Anleger bekommen ihr Prozent im Monat. Die Rechnung zahlen die Aktionäre und alle, die auf Saylor als Käufer warten.

@PeterSchiff erwartet für morgen einen großen STRC-Rückkauf. Bei einer STRC, die flach blieb, während Bitcoin 17 Prozent verlor, würde mich das nicht wundern.

Wird das Aktiengeld knapp, bleibt für die Rückkäufe die Kasse. Danach der Bitcoin-Bestand. Wenn Strategy Bitcoin verkauft, dann am ehesten für STRC.

WORAUF ICH MORGEN SCHAUE

Strategys Wochenmeldung. Drei Zahlen: Bitcoin gekauft, STRC zurückgekauft, Bitcoin verkauft.

Steht hinter der dritten eine Null und ist die erste größer als die zweite, hat Saylor die Woche bestanden.

Den Crash hat Saylor nicht gemacht. Aber solange sein Geld in die eigene Vorzugsaktie fließt, fängt ihn auch keiner auf.

Wenn dir das beim Einordnen geholfen hat, lass gern ein Like da. Dann landet es auch bei denen, die gerade nur "Saylor muss verkaufen" lesen.

quoted_text:
🚨 64,000 BITCOIN MINERS HIJACKED IN MASSIVE ATTACK

An estimated 64,000 Bitcoin miners representing 13 EH/s of hashrate were reportedly hijacked overnight, with their mining power redirected to OCEAN mining pool and payouts assigned to an attacker-controlled Bitcoin address.

The attack reportedly began around 8 PM CT on November 14.

OCEAN’s dashboard shows a sharp spike in hashrate, briefly approaching 50 EH/s before falling back toward 40 EH/s.

CoreX Hosting first raised the alarm, reporting that miners were being redirected without authorization.

One affected operator says their entire mining farm was hijacked and identified Luxor’s Commander mining management software as the source of the compromise.

Other operators reported similar unauthorized pool changes several days earlier, potentially pointing to a broader incident.

CoreX later reported that the attack appeared to be over, with the hijacked hashrate falling from 13 EH/s to approximately 100 PH/s.

The attackers reportedly failed to mine a Bitcoin block during the hijack, meaning no block rewards were collected.

However, affected miners permanently lost the opportunity to earn Bitcoin during the attack. That hashing time cannot be recovered.

The full scope of the breach and whether Luxor Commander was compromised have yet to be independently confirmed.

text:
关于 Agent Memory，最近几篇论文（arXiv 2610.30755 / Memory Tax / Context as Infrastructure）验证了三个反直觉的事实：

- 在召回率方面，是 The bitter lesson 的胜利：原始历史上的朴素检索在 7 组 benchmark 里拿了 6 个第一。
- 最好的复杂 Memory 系统，表现还不如朴素 RAG 追加一轮：把原文抽成摘要或原子事实，往往带来负收益（negative net value）。
- 只用 BM25 和 grep 的 harness，跟经典 memory 结构无明显差异，已经基本解决了准确率问题。
此前我们给 agent 做「memory」，只是一种类比：想到什么好就加什么结构，原文反而被忽视了，没有人从第一性原理推过一遍

如果简单一点呢？ 直接在原始历史上建立检索层，时间是自然标度，让 agent 在检索层上进行检索
这就是我们开源的 Obelisk。 在我最新的 talk 《Agent 如何用历史做 research：为什么 agent history 应该成为 memory infra》 里，我先展示了只做这一层检索，agent 就能做到什么：
「上次为什么这么写」，agentic research 可以直接得到答案：直接丢给 agent 去查，比如：「上次 auth bug 最后到底改了哪些文件，为什么这么改」
跨整月历史的自主复盘，且结论都带着出处：我让 Codex 用 Obelisk 回顾了 Obelisk 自己一个月的开发过程，它生成的复盘里，每一条结论都直接定位到了具体的 session、message 和 workflow

而 Obelisk 本身的实现极其克制：
接入 11 个 Harness 的原始历史：覆盖 Claude Code、Codex、GitHub Copilot、Kiro、OpenCode、Kimi Code、DeepSeek Harness、Hermes Agent、OMP、Pi、ZCode。
SQLite + FTS5 + JS Query Runtime（CodeAct）：不把历史整理成静态文档或纯自然语言摘要，也不设计固定的查询 API，而是以 skill 为载体，让 agent 现场写 JS 查询脚本去跑

在这个 talk 的后半段，我也顺着第一性原理继续往下推了一步：对朴素检索继续 Scale 呢？
当历史规模上来之后，单靠 full text search 命中范围有限、单次检索结果无法跨 session 复用、且第一轮命中会带偏后续检索倾向。 因此在检索层之上探索了第二阶段（Nowledge Mem Super Graph），一些结论：
- View 的优势不是更准确的召回，而是赢在读得少（token -38%）：让 agent 先看到全局分布、知道信息是否完全，再花推理预算，往下又能随时落回 Obelisk 的原始历史。
- 如果 Memory 会过期，不如没有 Memory：通过按时间频率分层的 live-update（新结论不直接覆盖旧结论、局部更新），让一部分理解活在上下文窗口之外，解决长程 research 的 context rot。

归根结底是三件事：
- 保留追溯回原始历史的路径，原文不能被丢掉
- 值得花算力维护一层 graph view
- Memory 应当更好有利于 agent 进行 research，no negative effect

Wyśmiewa polską prowincję, choć jego znajomość Zachodu ogranicza się do tanich linii lotniczych, weekendu w Barcelonie i kilku seriali na Netfliksie. 

Jest przekonany o własnej europejskości, ale Europa nie jest dla niego żadną konkretną cywilizacją, z jej historią, literaturą, religią, filozofią i obyczajami. Jest wyobrażonym miejscem, w którym wszyscy myślą tak jak on.

Wintermute is literally paying $10M a year to legally front-run everyone on Hyperliquid and it’s completely destroying altcoin liquidity

Bloomberg finally exposed what HFT desks have been screaming about for weeks. Hyperliquid’s gossip priority auctions let top funds see incoming orders 50–60ms before anyone else on the network

Look at how completely broken this setup is:

-> One Wintermute wallet won ~76% of the top slots last month, burning ~$26k every single day just to starve out competition
-> HL claims the auction is open to everyone. Complete BS. You only get that 60ms head start if you have direct peering with Foundation nodes, which requires 0.5% of total maker volume and 10k HYPE staked ($700k+)
-> Smaller MMs are getting sniped nonstop and just unplugging their bots on alts
-> Retail gets stuck with the bill: across 86 altcoin pairs, order book depth on HL imploded by 82% while spreads blew out from 2.13 to 3.55 bps

Honestly, I don't even blame Wintermute. If I had their balance sheet, I would milk this exact loophole until someone forced me to stop

The blame sits 100% on the protocol design. Burning auction fees is cool for $HYPE holders, sure, but letting one fund buy a monopoly on data speed turns a decentralized exchange into a rigged casino

Scrap read-priority auctions completely or make the slots equal, because right now altcoin execution on HL is absolute garbage

I've been trying to make sense of this week, and I don't think one thing explains it. The macro side turned hard: a December hike is now fully priced, the AI trade got knocked, and stablecoin supply has been shrinking for a month.

What stands out is that most of the selling came from US venues over the weekend, which looks more like someone needing liquidity than wanting out. The Anthropic IPO could help explain a bit of it. During a roadshow funds put in orders while the book builds and when demand is this strong they know they'll be cut back, so they ask for far more than they expect to get. Those orders still need to be credible and whatever they're allocated has to be paid for at settlement a day or so after pricing. Until the roadshow launched on the 10th, it wasn't even clear the deal would happen this month, so anyone who wanted in had about a week to raise cash and the strong demand meant they wanted more than they'd planned. With the book closing around Wednesday this weekend was the last real window, and crypto was the only liquid market open. 

Add MARA selling to fund datacenters and I suspect funds holding both AI and crypto on shared margin raised cash from crypto first. 

I also wouldn't be surprised if a few desks got taken out along the way, adding forced selling we won't hear about for weeks.

text:
I’ve decided to leave NVIDIA. There are a few things I want to say.

As a robotics engineer at NVIDIA, I have seen Jensen as much more than the company’s CEO.

I admire his willingness to invest in a future that was not yet obvious. He committed to CUDA long before the deep learning boom and positioned NVIDIA for AI before it became everyone’s priority. Those decisions helped build the infrastructure that powers today’s AI.

I have seen that same vision in physical AI: investing in robotics, sharing open-source tools and projects, and building computing platforms that bring AI into the physical world. This is the work I do every day—and a future I believe in.

But what matters most to me is the culture he helped build.

Engineers are encouraged to explore, take risks, and learn from mistakes. Jensen reads employees’ Top 5 emails, follows their work, and engages directly. In a company this large, that connection matters. It makes an individual engineer feel that their ideas can still be heard.

That is why this has been so disappointing.

I do not have all the facts surrounding the allegations, and I cannot prejudge the investigation. My admiration for Jensen does not put him above scrutiny.

What I find difficult to accept is having to come to terms with his departure before receiving an explanation that helps me understand it. What this means for our direction, our culture, and the people doing the work remains unclear to me.

I have felt that engineers’ perspectives matter here. On this decision, I have not felt heard. That gap has been more painful than I expected.

I understand that some information cannot be shared immediately. But that does not erase the feeling of being left outside a decision that affects the company we help build every day.

A company’s greatness comes from its leadership, its governance, and the people who turn its ambitions into reality. Employees’ trust and sense of belonging are part of that, too.

Jensen’s vision and the engineering culture he shaped were important reasons I wanted to stay. His departure led me to decide that my own chapter here should also come to a close.

I leave with sadness and gratitude. The colleagues I have worked with, and the work we believed in together, will always matter to me.

These are my personal views.

quoted_text:
one example from my own framework
- day trading perps

i run a separate account just for perp day trades. clean setups only, completely detached from everything else.

i don't do this bc i really have to. i'm in a comfortable spot financially. but i still enjoy day trading and see real value in it. small wins compound and i need a working routine next to sports and everything else in life.

the goal is $100 to $500 a trading day when a clean setup shows up, with very tight risk management. executed well, that adds up to more than a full salary each month, like a classic day trading job. always chasing 10k+ trades fries my brain and those belong elsewhere anyway. sizing up to make more is fine within other frameworks, but this account should pay me daily.

this account isn't about making big money. it has always stayed in the same size range, no matter how my net worth changed and i found that to be the most stress free approach for me. it's about staying close to the market, valuing the money i earn day to day and refining my skill set, so i can trade whenever and however i want, relying on nothing but myself.

once i hit my target and the trade played out as planned, i close it completely, either at my preset TP or manually. no thinking about what else i could have caught. trade closed, day done.

the next day i look at the market again. same or different coins, same or different ranges, and i use my experience and market read to find the cleanest day trade. if nothing looks good, i don't trade at all. if there's a clean momentum play based on relative strength, a support bounce, a catalyst or whatever else the market offers, i take it without thinking about bigger targets above. trades that need more time and higher TPs belong in a different account.

one of the biggest lessons i've learned over the years is to separate my accounts by approach. i simply trade better that way.

i have one account where i only DCA into ETFs. one for individual stock trades. one for longer term altcoin spot holds. one for perp day trades. wallets for meme coins. and one for HTF perp trades that play out over a longer period.

with everything separated like this, with predefined sizes and frameworks, i can stay consistent with just my day trading account, especially in uncertain phases like this one.

my routine for this account looks like this. i keep around $5k on it and trade it up to $20k. once i hit that, i withdraw $15k to my bank account, rotate that cash into my world ETF over time and start again from $5k.

if it drops below $3k, i stop trading. i go through my previous day trades first and think deeply about what went wrong, where i can be more defensive and what to change going forward. sometimes other approaches creep into my day trades without me noticing, like holding longer to make more or mistaking HTF targets for my daily profit target.

keeping the account small relative to my net worth keeps my size small and that keeps me away from overtrading.

in the end it's all about disciplined execution. no emotions, no overthinking working against me.

i'm not focused on big net worth targets. i'm focused on daily profit targets and being fine with them. the bigger goals come naturally over the years and when you're still young, rushing usually isn't the best way.

closing everything gives my brain the rest it needs. otherwise i’d be staring at charts late into the day, trying to make more.

using the right order types, being fine with small profits and calling it a day is crucial if you want to day trade with passion and stay clear headed doing it. actually logging off is one of the hardest parts of this job and this approach helps me a lot with it.

staying consistently profitable takes a clear head every day, years of learning and unemotional execution. and the calm of knowing there will always be another range, another setup, another trade.

this might not work for other traders. everyone has their own edge and framework. but it works for me, and that's all that matters.

text:
The Nuremberg trailer is a preview of how media and content ought to go-to-market now:

- Drop a slop trailer or demo 
- Does it go viral?
- If yes: Make the rest of it and sell that 
- If no: Make another one and try again 

Everyone was loving that trailer - But look closer, it’s extremely inconsistent and the “world building” is very far off and wildly inconsistent tone.

It is highly slop adjacent.

For example, the portals have wildly different appearances across the scenes. The Tie-fighter scenes are highly illogical with the silver sphere movements. 

The Harry Potter wizard was so clearly Dumbledore derived it broke the illusion for me. I was going “why the f is there a wizard?”

But no one looked that hard or cared - the gist was good enough. 

Given the reception, addressing the tone jumps and world consistency can come next.

Slop first, then test, then polish the slop. 

The current workflow of building an entire game first then hoping it works with users. 

Seems outdated. I think the reality is that “does it go viral” may be a valid test. 

If I were Hollywood I would produce 900 slop trailers and test them with audiences and make the ones that resonated.

And not make them in a year….make them almost immediately.

Release the trailer and have the entire thing out the door in a month so people are still warm.

花 47.88 刀买了 1Password，花两天把电脑里乱七八糟的 SSH、上百个 API Key、各种证书、还有备忘录里攒了一堆的账号密码，全部迁进了 1Password

2、怎么把各种 API Key 从本地迁走，还不影响原来脚本和 Skill 的调用

text:
중국에는 AI 부정행위가 없는 이유.list

1. 수능 기간엔 AI가 아예 문제를 안 풀어줌

중국 수능인 가오카오 기간에는 두바오, 큐웬, 위안바오, 키미, 딥시크, 문심일언이 시험 시간 동안 사진 인식이랑 문제 풀이 기능을 막아버림. 올해는 교육부 등 5개 부처가 요구해서 회사들이 다 같이 막은 거라고 함.

2. 우겨도 안 통함

작년에 두바오에 시험 문제 사진을 올렸더니 "수능 기간이라 문제 풀이 서비스를 중단한다"고 답했음. 수능 문제 아니라고 우겨도 똑같은 답만 돌아왔다고 함.

3. 차단 시간까지 분 단위로 정해둠

위안바오는 6월 7~10일 오전 8시부터 오후 5시, 하루는 6시 15분까지 기능을 막는다고 공지했음. 시험 끝나면 다시 풀리고, 일상 대화 같은 기능은 그대로 쓸 수 있었다고 함.

4. 시험장엔 AI 감독관이 있음(이거 괜찮은것 같음)

광둥성은 2024년부터 모든 시험장 CCTV를 AI가 실시간으로 분석하고 있음. 물건 건네기, 감독관 딴짓 같은 12가지 행동을 잡아내면 바로 캡처해서 시험 본부로 보낸다고 함.

5. 눈만 돌려도 경고가 감

펜 떨어뜨리고 줍는 건 괜찮은데, 줍는 척하면서 양옆을 보면 감독관한테 자동으로 경고가 간다고 함. 최종 판단은 감독관이 하지만 속삭임이나 시선 교환까지 다 잡아낸다고 함.

6. 스마트 안경이랑 스마트 워치도 잡음

올해 광둥 공안은 스마트 안경이나 스마트 워치를 AI에 연결해서 답을 받는 신종 수법을 집중 단속했음. 시험장 608곳 주변의 이상 신호를 탐지하고, 무선 신호 차단기에 스마트 보안 검색대까지 깔았다고 함.

7. 걸리면 감옥 감

중국은 시험 부정행위가 형법상 범죄임. 수능에서 부정행위를 조직하면 '심각한 경우'로 쳐서 최대 징역 7년이고, 대리시험이나 무선 커닝 장비를 쓰는 것도 형사처벌 대상이라고 함.

8. 1300만 명이 인생을 거는 시험임

작년 가오카오 응시자는 약 1335만 명이었음. 사실상 대학 가는 유일한 길이라 국가가 시험 하나에 AI 회사, 경찰, 교육부까지 다 동원하는 거라고 함.

솔직히 도입해야 되는거 몇개 보인다. 개인적으로 4번과 7번.

감옥가야지. 누군가의 인생을 망칠 수도 있는 시험인데.

Tether 开始布局本地 AI Agent！8 亿参数模型，瞄准手机端运行！

Tether AI Research 发布了 QVAC BotPsy，一个拥有 8 亿参数的开源权重 AI 模型。

它的主要方向不是单纯追求模型规模，而是让 AI Agent 能够在手机等个人设备上本地运行，并根据用户指令调用工具、执行多步骤任务。

相比完全依赖云端 AI，本地运行有机会减少对服务器的依赖，也能让用户更好地掌控自己的数据。

Tether 还公布了测试结果，称 BotPsy 在部分 Agent 任务基准中，表现超过了参数规模达到自身 2.5 倍的模型。

AI 的竞争似乎正在出现另一条路线：不只是让模型越来越大，而是让 AI 真正进入每个人的设备。

AI 的下一阶段竞争，或许不只是模型有多强，而是谁能让 AI 真正融入用户的日常设备和生活。

text:
这次是 Gate，下次可能是任何一家交易所。

随着加密行业不断走向全球化合规，一个值得整个行业思考的问题是：

用户资产的司法管辖边界究竟在哪里？

是用户居住地、交易所注册地，还是全球任何一个提出司法协助请求的国家，都可能对用户资产产生影响？

更值得关注的是，普通用户的法律资源和抗辩能力极其有限。

当一笔资产涉及跨国、跨境司法纠纷时，用户可能需要面对陌生国家的法律体系、语言障碍、跨境律师费用，以及漫长且不确定的司法程序。

这些成本与复杂程度，早已远远超出普通用户能够独立承受的范畴。

那么问题来了：

如果交易所需要承担全球化的合规义务，是否也应该建立与之对等的全球化用户权益保护机制？

当用户因为一项境外司法请求而被冻结资产时，谁来保障其知情权、抗辩权和获得有效法律救济的机会？

如果用户根本无力承担跨国诉讼费用，所谓的司法救济是否就只剩下理论上的权利？

我们一直在讨论如何让加密资产在全球自由流动，却很少讨论如何让用户的合法权益获得同等程度的跨境保护。

全球化合规不应该只意味着执法能力的全球化，也应该意味着用户权利保障的全球化。

这不是 Gate 一家交易所的问题，而是整个行业迟早需要共同面对的问题。
author: 0xAstra
quoted_text:
针对Gate用户被印度警方司法冻结一案的详细处理过程细节说明：

先说最重要的一点：Gate 平台作为独立第三方，不会仅凭单方面材料对涉案资金作出判断或承诺移交资产。每一项请求我们都会内部逐案审核，而目前没有任何资产被移交。

整个案件从 2025 年至今，Gate一直在投入法律资源持续跟进，帮用户建立沟通渠道和争取时间，并非收到印度警方要求后就直接配合执行。

目前Gate的处理方案：
1. 从2025 年 9 月收到印度警方的资产冻结请求开始，我们的 AML 团队就持续向警方提出补充证据要求，法务也不断要求补充材料。警方提供的链上记录详细复杂，涉及诸多链上钱包及资金往来。到2026 年 4 月收到资产移交相关请求时，Gate 也没有直接承诺执行，而是持续要求补充材料，明确坚持 By Case 审核，不能直接承诺资产移交。根据2026 年 9月 的案件沟通，也确认案件仍在司法审查中。截至今天，Gate这边会持续保持这部分资金，在用户抗辩过程中，不会轻易划走，持续帮用户解决问题。

2. Gate 在收到警方关于起诉材料提交通知的同日，就向警方确认是否可以将相关案件进展告知用户。Gate 在取得警方同意后向相关用户同步案件情况，以便用户了解司法进展并寻求法律救济。Gate聘请的本地律所也正在跟本地警方和法院沟通，为用户争取合法的抗辩办法。

3. 根据本地律所意见，Gate 作为第三方无法代替用户进行 Defense 或 Challenge，但也明确了用户可以通过这个有效方式抗辩，我们会继续为用户提供法律支援以便于提及抗辩。我们一定会为用户争取合法权益，保住用户资金。

最后重申：Gate有配合司法调查的责任，但在遇到司法案件的时候，不会也从未轻易划转用户资产，Gate 不会仅凭单方面材料处置用户资金。案件仍在进行中，我们会继续在各方之间沟通协调，有进展及时同步。

Gate

#Bitcoin 盘面，周五说到价格跌至67,500（此前6月8月底部区间）区间顶部，周末有效跌破，接下来就要看63,000——65,000区间是否可以企稳

该区间为今年6月-8月底部震荡区间，期间出现大量换手，筹码结构相对稳定，此处更适合作为跌破73,000技术支撑后的有效筹码支撑位

今日价格低点在62,000附近，基本完成了63,000——65,000的筹码支撑测试，目前出现反弹

再看反弹情况：

小时级别反弹有效且强势，1小时与4小时均出现较强反弹，后续3跟K线快速收回此前跌幅的高点，这视为有效反弹，或者有效止跌

从1小时到4小时暂时止跌确认，接下来看日线级别止跌信号是否确认，回归盘面就是下周一到周三，看价格能否68,000上方，周三之前价格收在68,000上方，意味着日线止跌确认，有效反弹

然后就要看反弹强度，后续反弹强度看下周能否日线级别收回日线MA200（73,000）上方，收住，反弹较强，新趋势启动信号明确

不过结合目前宏观、风险市场偏好来看，反弹不会太强，所以下周三日线价格收在68,000上方后可以看63,000-73,000区间震荡，

当然看震荡的前提是日线先收回68,000之后再回落，算是止跌后的常规回调，

如果周三之前日线无法收回68,000上方，则意味着日线级别还未止跌，则继续看回调，看是否跌破新低！

目前盘面走势比较明确，右侧思维看下周能否确认日线止跌，一旦日线止跌，需要同步看ETF与加密市场资金是否回流，如果资金回流+盘面反弹双重验证，意味着短期止跌有效，底部初步确定，接下来看震荡筑底！

#Bitcoin ETF 连续两周净流出，机构用户何时停止抛售？加密市场资金何时暂停净流出？

本周五的  #BTC ETF 数据公布，截止本周五，ETF已经有11个交易日两周的净流出

本周五单日净流出1.854亿，略弱于周四净流出，其中IBIT为主要净流出通道，单日净流出1.435亿，FBTC 紧跟其后净流出0.419亿

根据目前数据统计：

10月30日至今ETF净流出额度总计29.90.2亿，
11月9日至11月13日本周ETF净流出10.653亿，
10月30日至今，IBIT单渠道净流出高达23.516亿

根据这份数据可以看出，基本上这两周的净流出抛压基本来自IBIT，曾经得到BTC 机构用户最大买单力量却变成了近期的主要抛压，而这种持续性的抛售，显然并非是短期的换手，而是一种信心变弱后的套现

而FBTC 与MSBT 虽然这两周有不同程度的买入资金，但是对比IBIT的连续大额净流出有点杯水车薪

而本周五ETF资金净流出放缓，下周就要看ETF净流出继续收敛还是继续扩大，机构资金不停止抛售，对价格还是不够友好。尤其是周六周日BTC价格出现明显回落，下周一ETF资金是否有补偿性抛售目前还是未知，如果有补偿性抛售反而是正常现象。

加密市场数据：

对比周五的数据来看，市场市值变化较大， BTC占比增加，ETH与山寨占比继续被挤压

加密资金总量减少4亿，其中USDT净流出2.58亿，USDC净流入0.5亿，周末阶段反而美区资金净流出减少，不过这也属于周末的特殊情况，并不能认为美区资金稳定

数据总结：

ETH+加密数据整体来看，目前来看依旧不太乐观，下周是重点，要看ETF是否开启连续第三周第三周的净流出，机构用户是BTC买单的核心，机构用户不停止抛售，对市场信心没好处，其次就要看加密市场资金是否回流

而对于目前 $BTC 来说，短期跌至支撑区间后的反弹，也需要更多的数据来支撑反弹，否则无效反弹意味着还未止跌！

A few more improvements to our LLM inference engine on AMD Strix Halo!

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next now reaches 1,885 tok/s in exact prefill at 8K on a single node, or 2,008 tok/s with our FAST profile.

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is moving forward too. On two Strix Halo nodes over USB4, we're getting 1,165 tok/s exact and up to 1,425 tok/s FAST with longer prompts.

We've also been working on reducing GPU cycles per token, improving scheduling and making multi-request serving more efficient.

Some changes are already in main, while others are still being tested.

It's a lot of small improvements rather than one big breakthrough, but they keep adding up.

这次出来出差刚好和前SpaceX高管 @LewisHong 天天呆在一起活动。其实前两天在台湾，这次SpaceX发射前夕，Lewis和一个联发科出来的投资大佬聊到这次发射，联发科大佬听完马上跑去银行加仓了1000万美金的$SPCX。真人真事！

为什么他这么激动，因为他了解到SpaceX 这次真正的突破，不是又一次成功发射火箭。

2024 年，SpaceX 首次用机械臂接住了星舰的第一级助推器。此前，Starship 上面级也已经进入过轨道。

这次不一样：SpaceX 首次接住了从轨道返回的 Starship 上面级，也就是未来用来运送货物和人员的飞船本体。

为什么这很重要？因为要让太空运输变成可持续的生意，不仅要把火箭送上去，还要把昂贵的飞船带回来，检查、翻修，再次发射。

这次离完整复用又近了一步，但还没有走到终点：本次助推器并未被机械臂接住，上面级也还需要证明能够低成本、快速、可靠地复飞。

text:
For $LIT to reach $10 in 2027 it needs to do ~3.3x from current mark ($2.96 at the time of writing), so as of now only 260.6M LIT is distributed i.e about 26% of the 1B total.

- From Dec 29, contributor and investor tokens vest linearly for 3Y (about 3.2M LIT a week, roughly $9.4M)
- The next 12 months alone add 146.5M LIT, which grows the distributed supply by 56% (At $10, that float is a ~$4B mcap)
- Buybacks have totaled $34.2M this year, under $1M most weeks, while the treasury already released a net $21.9M of LIT
- Vesting would add about $9.4M a week at today's price, roughly 10x what buybacks absorb

@Lighter_xyz earns $53.5M a year for holders against HYPE's $837M, despite doing 31% of its volume, because retail trades free. So at $HYPE's 18.4x multiple, a $4B LIT needs about $215M of holder revenue, 4x today as supply keeps growing. The swing factor is the planned CFTC application. If it brings in institutional traders who actually pay fees, the rev gap starts closing.

h/t to @DefiLlama and @inflecta_io for the data

BREAKING: The US Social Security Trust Fund’s deficit jumped +$39 billion YoY in Fiscal Year 2026, to a record -$221 billion.

This fund finances retirement benefits and payments to eligible survivors of deceased workers.

This comes as the fund’s costs, primarily benefit payments to retirees and survivors, soared +$83 billion YoY, to $1.5 trillion, an all-time high.

At the same time, income, primarily from contributions to the Social Security system, rose +$44 billion YoY, to a record $1.3 trillion.

Since FY2022, the fund’s deficit has surged +$188 billion, or +585%.

As a result, trust fund reserves fell -$221 billion YoY in FY2026, to $2.18 trillion, the lowest since 2007, down down -$640 billion from the 2017 peak.

The financial health of Social Security is deteriorating rapidly.

针对Gate用户被印度警方司法冻结一案的详细处理过程细节说明：

先说最重要的一点：Gate 平台作为独立第三方，不会仅凭单方面材料对涉案资金作出判断或承诺移交资产。每一项请求我们都会内部逐案审核，而目前没有任何资产被移交。

整个案件从 2025 年至今，Gate一直在投入法律资源持续跟进，帮用户建立沟通渠道和争取时间，并非收到印度警方要求后就直接配合执行。

目前Gate的处理方案：
1. 从2025 年 9 月收到印度警方的资产冻结请求开始，我们的 AML 团队就持续向警方提出补充证据要求，法务也不断要求补充材料。警方提供的链上记录详细复杂，涉及诸多链上钱包及资金往来。到2026 年 4 月收到资产移交相关请求时，Gate 也没有直接承诺执行，而是持续要求补充材料，明确坚持 By Case 审核，不能直接承诺资产移交。根据2026 年 9月 的案件沟通，也确认案件仍在司法审查中。截至今天，Gate这边会持续保持这部分资金，在用户抗辩过程中，不会轻易划走，持续帮用户解决问题。

2. Gate 在收到警方关于起诉材料提交通知的同日，就向警方确认是否可以将相关案件进展告知用户。Gate 在取得警方同意后向相关用户同步案件情况，以便用户了解司法进展并寻求法律救济。Gate聘请的本地律所也正在跟本地警方和法院沟通，为用户争取合法的抗辩办法。

3. 根据本地律所意见，Gate 作为第三方无法代替用户进行 Defense 或 Challenge，但也明确了用户可以通过这个有效方式抗辩，我们会继续为用户提供法律支援以便于提及抗辩。我们一定会为用户争取合法权益，保住用户资金。

最后重申：Gate有配合司法调查的责任，但在遇到司法案件的时候，不会也从未轻易划转用户资产，Gate 不会仅凭单方面材料处置用户资金。案件仍在进行中，我们会继续在各方之间沟通协调，有进展及时同步。

Taiwan, China and Korea intervening to stabilize their markets, and why governments increasingly recognize that AI's future depends on healthy capital markets.

I also revisit the most important lesson from the iPhone era: technological inevitability doesn't eliminate corrections, but corrections don't eliminate technological inevitability.

AI is inevitable. Tokenization is inevitable.

The question is whether the market is finally moving past forced selling and beginning to look forward again.

text:
今天，我们 @predictdotfun 的电竞市场单场交易量创下了 ATH。

也看到很多互关的好友参与了 LOL 的预测，晒出的交易记录几乎都是我们家的结算页面。
刚刚还看到有人感慨，没想到电竞赛事的预测市场竟然这么有潜力……
还有一位老师看到我们本次交易量排名预测市场前三直接选择空投锁仓……

上个礼拜，我正好跟一位认识多年、在腾讯游戏从业 9 年的朋友打了一个小时电话（非常惭愧，我没加入pf之前并不关注电竞，相当于找业内大师速通补课）
聊完发现，随着年轻人越来越喜欢打游戏，电竞市场一定是会越来越大
而亚洲在电竞领域拥有非常强的选手优势

以前看比赛，大家在直播间刷弹幕、猜输赢、支持自己喜欢的战队
但自从有了预测市场，观众参与赛事的方式也在发生变化。

预测市场不是把所有人都变成交易员
而是让普通人在自己熟悉的领域
也有机会成为比专业交易员更懂行情的人

而电竞只是其中一个切入口。
足球、篮球、电竞、科技、政治……每个人都有自己熟悉的领域，也都有自己的信息优势。

过去，交易市场只属于少数懂金融的人
未来，预测市场属于每一个对自己兴趣爱好领域有判断的人。
我身边一个女生，不会炒币，但也会用我们家预测世界杯、黄仁勋会否离职。

不少人是第一次通过⚽世界杯、LOL 世界赛接触预测市场
预测市场正在从 Crypto 圈走向更广泛的普通用户，或许，另一方面来说，预测市场就是为行业带来增量的圈外新用户的。

而我们现在看到的，可能还只是一个开始。

text:
Anthropic 机会更新（11/15）

一、目前的价格

截止到 11/15，目前 Anthropic 的申购价格在 70–78，含 5% 手续费是 1.32–1.48 万亿的估值。

在 Hype 的价格是 101.8，在币安的价格是 1339，换算过来是 102.1，这两个平台的估值在 1.84 万亿。

如果按照海妖最高的 78 来申购，实际成本是 81.9，距离盘前大概有 24% 的差价。

目前 Hype 这边持仓是 3 亿美元，币安持仓 1 亿美元，我看了盘口，其实流动性是较差的，也就是说，大概率这不是最后的定价。

二、超募情况

目前路透和彭博报道的信息是，订单意向是超募了 6 倍，但是这个是意向，不是真正打进去的钱，真正打进去的钱最后是多少也是不知道的。美股的申购和加密链上的申购不一样，目前无法查到实际申购额度，不透明，但是从意向来看，资金的热度还是有一些。

三、怎么参与

我自己的思考是，依旧值得重仓参与，如果你资金足够多，建议 Bitget 和 Kraken 分开打，覆盖多户。

如果你资金中等，可以考虑 Kraken 的 VIP，如果你是小户，可以考虑 Bitget。

Kraken 的 VIP 申购日期是 16 号之前，所以今晚之前最好打入资金，Bitget 的公开轮截止日期是 11/17 的下午 4 点（北京时间），如果你打算参与 Kraken 的渠道，建议早打。

四、我自己的思考

我依旧觉得这是一个不错的机会，我倾向于重仓上，主要是因为盘前确实有价差，风险有限，这就相当于德州扑克拿到了 AA 的牌，即便最后输了，决策流程也是对的，我也不觉得我重仓了，然后华尔街就瞄准我一个人然后做空我自己，总的来说值得参与。

如果你不打算参与也没关系，现在 BTC 等主流资产的价格也还不错，可以考虑是否要建仓，这也是不错的机会之一。

以上是我自己的思考，不涉及任何投资建议，如果你在这个项目亏钱，请不要找我，我只是公开我自己的思考，并且用钱投票。谢谢。

quoted_text:
it's time for you to wake up and smell the roses

there is no reality in which things continue smooth from here. no, bitcoin obviously isn't/wasn't going to stay put in some $70k - 80k range.

this is one of the most volatile eras ever. not just for bitcoin, but for the world. geopolitically, technologically, socially, we're going through rapid and dramatic change, and things aren't about to get simpler.

no, cybersecurity isn't going to all get fixed because you can now use ai to generate machine-checked security proofs in lean. even if you figure out how to write secure code and democratize the skill, there will still be vulnerabilities. if not bugs in the implementation, bugs in the specification. bugs in the assumptions, bugs in the verification.

cybersecurity will continue to be a verifiable domain, that's not changing, which means machines can self-play in it, meaning they can improve in it like in chess, except its actually worse than in chess because here the rules also keep changing, because technology keeps changing, so the gamefield keeps changing, meaning bugs will continue to be problematic, and especially problematic in irreversible systems (where one mistake means you get fully wiped out forever).

it's a hard system to keep stable! lean isn't coming to save you.

you'll continue to hear stories about how cybersecurity is about to improve and all the world's bugs will be fixed, because that is a popular narrative that tends to do well on twitter. no one wants to hear the defeatist point of view. but that means that some of you, who aren't able to figure this stuff out on your own, won't hear the truth very often.

smart people know this, not everyone agrees about it of course, but the negative point of view isn't going to get promoted on x/twitter.

the algorithms that are improving your life are about to learn how to improve themselves. the algorithms that are fucking with your life are about to learn how to improve themselves.

the situation now in which technology is about to enter a supersonic self-improving loop (a much more aggressive form than the baseline self-improving loop that we've been riding on since the dawn of time) is extremely bubble prone. 

the prospect of investing in something *self-improving*? people will leverage themselves to the tits.

they will also be scared, flip-flop between being endlessly optimistic to extremely skittish and want security/safety. markets will be volatile. geopolitics will be volatile. everyone has the ability to react faster now, and there will be much more to react to.

no, crypto and bitcoin isn't going to stay non-volatile to that backdrop. the risk asset of risk assets, not even gold stays untroubled during turbulent times. it's going to be volatile. we spent a decade maturing as an industry. yes, we think we are owed some overdue maturity. we've aged through our teenage years and we're supposed to get rid of the acne. sorry, we're aging backwards now, you're going to get more acne and more bedtime erections, not less. the world isn't fair.

what you need to understand and accept is that bitcoin & crypto isn't this solid thing here. it's more of a moonshot thing again. it's a very digital thing in a world where everything digital is getting a shakedown.

you're almost 40 years old and your digital profession can be done by free open source software made in china run with a handcrank. your wife isn't going to let you gamble with your entire financial future in magical coins when you can't even tell her what your career prospects look like anymore. your beard is patchy.

bitcoin & crypto can still do well in this environment, because when technology, markets and geopolitics become ultra-volatile in unison, you're bound to also get weird market dislocations. you have arms races, you have bubbles popping, you might get lots of money printing. most things that can happen will happen.

but you aren't, as an industry, going to be a universal safe haven against this. no one really feels safe with their crypto assets these days. you got a hardware wallet? cool. that doesn't exactly feel like the safest of all places anymore.

you got your funds on an exchange? cool. doesn't feel great either, does it?

oh, but you're not impacted because you choose to hold your exposure through etps/etfs? well, if that's what you have to resolve to, that's not great either.

if you can't be secure with your crypto, if you can't feel safe with it, even though you're a freaking nerd in this industry, how does that bode for the industry at large?

much of the fuel that has driven e.g. defi to where it is today is because the risk was seen as tolerable. during 2020-2022 i knew a lot of people who felt okay with locking in hundreds of thousands of dollars in stablecoins in yield protocols. i don't know people who enjoy doing that today. people are tired of being bug bounties for north korea. they honestly prefer reversible systems for their life earnings.

this doesn't mean it is over for bitcoin & crypto, but it means you're going to have to accept that you may have to think about it differently. it is a diversified bet in your overall portfolio. it is a part of your portfolio. it can't be your entire portfolio.

if this sounds so bearish it sounds like the bottom signal to fully re-enter the market, sure. i'd love to become the pico-bottom perma-joke of our industry. i'm not saying for you to grow out of crypto, i'm saying for you to think of this as the volatile bet it is, the bet that macroeconomic/geopolitic turbulence/dislocations & fiat printing will outrank the fact that we're back in our teenage years again.

embrace that it will be volatile.

what's happening in the markets now is normal.

text:
我今天发了推文才知道
原来 BSC 上的 bStocks 真的会“自动分红”，但不是给你打 USDT，而是自动复投到币本位权益里。

核心代码逻辑是 Multiplier：

function uiMultiplier() external view returns (uint256);

event UIMultiplierUpdated(
    uint256 oldMultiplier,
    uint256 newMultiplier,
    uint256 effectiveAtTimestamp
);
钱包/前端显示余额的计算方式：

uiAmount = rawAmount * uiMultiplier / 1e18;
其中：
rawAmount：合约真实记录的原始 bStock 数量
uiMultiplier：权益调整系数，`1e18 = 1.0 倍`
uiAmount：钱包、BscScan 或支持该标准的应用显示的调整后数量
举个例子：

原始余额 rawAmount = 10 AAPLb
初始 Multiplier = 1.00
显示余额 = 10 × 1.00 = 10 AAPLb

苹果派息后，发行人收到股息，扣除预扣税等成本，再将净额买入更多苹果股票。假设净复投收益是 2%，则在链上更新：
UIMultiplierUpdated(
    1e18,       // 原来 1.00 倍
    1.02e18,    // 更新为 1.02 倍
    timestamp   // 生效时间
);
此时：

原始余额 rawAmount = 10（不变）
显示余额 uiAmount = 10 × 1.02 = 10.2
现金分红到账 = 0

所以所谓“币本位变多”，准确说是：
标的公司先派息；
发行人扣税后将净股息复投；

发行人在链上发布新的 Multiplier；

到生效时间后，你的显示持仓/经济权益自动增加。
不会有一笔额外的 bStock 或 USDT 转入记录，因为这不是传统 airdrop，也不是 staking 发币；它是用一个全局的比例系数重算显示单位。
注意：股票拆股、反向拆股也会触发同样的 UIMultiplierUpdated 事件。例如 1 拆 2，Multiplier 可能从 1.0 变 2.0。因此仅看链上事件不能断言是分红，必须结合标的公司的除息日和 bStocks 的 corporate action 公告判断。

bStocks 的分红不是现金到账，而是扣税后自动复投，并通过链上 Multiplier 让你的调整后币本位数量增加。

text:
现在币圈维权，都喜欢先找弱势的交易所了。关键是，法院才是你该去维权的地方。

Gate 用户被印度警方司法冻结资产这件事，我大概了解了一下，也看了 Gate 最新的回应。

先说结论：我不认为交易所配合司法调查有什么问题，并且截止目前用户资产还是安全的。用户真正应该做的，是尽快通过法律程序证明资金合法，阻止存在争议的资产被移交。

这个用户的钱到底干不干净，我不知道，也没有资格判断。但有几点必须说一说。

1. 交易所配合司法冻结，不是正常的吗？

印度警方调查诈骗案件，认为某笔资金可能涉及犯罪，依法要求交易所协助调查。

交易所难道应该直接拒绝？

但这里要区分两件事：冻结资金和划扣资金完全不是一个概念。

根据 Gate 11 月 15 日的回应，目前没有任何资产被移交，而且 Gate 仍在要求印度警方补充证据。

2. 如果你的钱确实没问题，最重要的不是发推，而是整理证据。

你说这 15 BTC 是 2023 年从 Binance、OKX 提出来的，在冷钱包放了两年，2025 年才转入 Gate。

那就尽可能把证据整理完整：

Binance、OKX 的历史提现记录；
2023 年至 2025 年的完整链上交易路径；
冷钱包控制权的证明；
被冻结账户的所有资金来源、购买记录或合法收入证明；
资金进入 Gate 的交易哈希及账户入金记录。

最好找专业链上取证机构出一份报告，形成完整的证据链。然后将其公开，可能更有说服力。

当然，链上路径清晰不等于资金必然合法，但至少能够为律师提供有力的抗辩材料。

3. 真正应该重点推动的，是印度法院的司法程序。

这件事都已经到法院了，光找交易所客服有什么用？

我的建议是，尽快让印度当地律师确认法院到底作出了什么命令，是否存在申诉期限，并依法申请暂停资产移交、提出异议或者申请解除冻结。

国内也可以咨询警方是否受理相关报案或求助，但国内报警并不能直接撤销印度法院的命令。

4. 公开维权有没有用？当然有。

至少可以让 Gate 更重视你的案件，投入更多法务资源，协助你和印度方面沟通。

但必须明白，舆论只能给交易所压力，不能代替司法抗辩。

根据 Gate 的回应，平台已经聘请印度当地律所跟进，并表示在用户抗辩过程中不会轻易移交资金。

毕竟，最终的目的是拿回钱，而不是在网上吵赢谁。
author: ZhanweiC
quoted_text:
针对Gate用户被印度警方司法冻结一案的详细处理过程细节说明：

先说最重要的一点：Gate 平台作为独立第三方，不会仅凭单方面材料对涉案资金作出判断或承诺移交资产。每一项请求我们都会内部逐案审核，而目前没有任何资产被移交。

整个案件从 2025 年至今，Gate一直在投入法律资源持续跟进，帮用户建立沟通渠道和争取时间，并非收到印度警方要求后就直接配合执行。

目前Gate的处理方案：
1. 从2025 年 9 月收到印度警方的资产冻结请求开始，我们的 AML 团队就持续向警方提出补充证据要求，法务也不断要求补充材料。警方提供的链上记录详细复杂，涉及诸多链上钱包及资金往来。到2026 年 4 月收到资产移交相关请求时，Gate 也没有直接承诺执行，而是持续要求补充材料，明确坚持 By Case 审核，不能直接承诺资产移交。根据2026 年 9月 的案件沟通，也确认案件仍在司法审查中。截至今天，Gate这边会持续保持这部分资金，在用户抗辩过程中，不会轻易划走，持续帮用户解决问题。

2. Gate 在收到警方关于起诉材料提交通知的同日，就向警方确认是否可以将相关案件进展告知用户。Gate 在取得警方同意后向相关用户同步案件情况，以便用户了解司法进展并寻求法律救济。Gate聘请的本地律所也正在跟本地警方和法院沟通，为用户争取合法的抗辩办法。

3. 根据本地律所意见，Gate 作为第三方无法代替用户进行 Defense 或 Challenge，但也明确了用户可以通过这个有效方式抗辩，我们会继续为用户提供法律支援以便于提及抗辩。我们一定会为用户争取合法权益，保住用户资金。

最后重申：Gate有配合司法调查的责任，但在遇到司法案件的时候，不会也从未轻易划转用户资产，Gate 不会仅凭单方面材料处置用户资金。案件仍在进行中，我们会继续在各方之间沟通协调，有进展及时同步。

Gate

Before any bank, insurer, payments company or capital markets firm can operate out of ADGM, it has to be licensed. Wai Lum Kwok @lum_kwok leads the team that decides.

He joined Abu Dhabi's Financial Services Regulatory Authority in 2015, after eleven years at the Monetary Authority of Singapore, and has spent the decade since writing the rulebook of a centre that grew up around him: licensing across banking, insurance, payments and capital markets, and ADGM's regulatory strategy for fintech and innovation, including several first-in-the-region initiatives, among them its frameworks for digital assets.

His case is a pragmatic one. Regulation is how a market earns trust and how investors and clients are protected, and while the technology and its regulatory treatment evolve, the outcomes should stay clear. In Abu Dhabi he will give a concrete account of what the FSRA has built over the years, how regulation can shape the future of finance, and the part industry can play in getting there.

We are delighted to welcome him for the first time. Wai Lum Kwok, Senior Executive Director, Authorisation & Fintech at the ADGM Financial Services Regulatory Authority @ADGlobalMarket, is confirmed for Proof of Talk Abu Dhabi.

This is the story of a thoroughly despicable petty man!

Feel ashamed of him—a despicable petty man who, fearing he cannot win through head-on competition, resorts to despicable conspiratorial tactics to attack Jensen Huang.

On November 9–10, media outlets such as HuggingNews and https://t.co/83jIRA8c8T reported that more and more people are realizing that Jensen Huang’s current situation is a setup.

Previously, the American AI company Anthropic was lobbying the White House to require that GPUs produced in the West be forcibly fitted with firmware-level locks, to keep “unapproved” Chinese open-source AI models out at the hardware level, under the pretext of “AI security” and “national security.” Google and AMD have already expressed support for this proposal. But Nvidia publicly and fiercely opposed it, saying this approach is not protecting America but retreating. Right after Jensen Huang collided head-on with Anthropic’s position, his extramarital affair scandal was exposed repeatedly, and news emerged that Nvidia’s board was preparing to meet to discuss removing him.

Anthropic sells closed-source model services, with users paying by usage volume. After the Democrats won a landslide in the midterm elections, he quickly found political backing.

As expected, a group of truly morally bankrupt conspirators hid in dark corners, used the tricks they are best at, pulled the trigger, and shot Jensen Huang dead in a hail of bullets!

author: cz_binance
quoted_text:
Bitcoin fell 19% into the biggest IPO ever. Now it's down 18% heading into the second biggest.

SpaceX raised $75B when it went public on June 12. In the 50 days before it listed, Bitcoin dropped 19%. Anthropic plans to raise up to $64B when it lists next week, and Bitcoin is down 18% over the same stretch. Overlay the two and they look almost the same.

What happened after the SpaceX IPO is the notable part. Bitcoin bottomed 18 days after the listing, then recovered all the way. By Day 100, it was above where it started.

Bitcoin around the SpaceX IPO:

Day -50 to IPO day: -19%
Low (Day +18): -25%
Day +50: still -20%
Around Day +70: a sharp rally
Day +100: +3.7%

From the IPO-day close to Day +100, Bitcoin gained 28%. From the low, it gained 39%.

The takeaway is that the selling came in the run-up to the listing. The bottom had effectively happened by the IPO, and the recovery came relatively shortly after, and it came all at once.

If Anthropic follows the same pattern, most of the drawdown is behind us, and it could reverse quickly over the next couple of months. And Bitcoin is sitting right at its 200-week moving average.

Map the SpaceX path onto today's price and you get roughly $90k by late February. Markets rarely follow a comparison like this exactly. But we remain very constructive on both the technicals and the fundamentals heading into 2027, and it's not hard to imagine what the narrative would be if anything close to this plays out.

quoted_text:
I’ve decided to leave NVIDIA. There are a few things I want to say.

As a robotics engineer at NVIDIA, I have seen Jensen as much more than the company’s CEO.

I admire his willingness to invest in a future that was not yet obvious. He committed to CUDA long before the deep learning boom and positioned NVIDIA for AI before it became everyone’s priority. Those decisions helped build the infrastructure that powers today’s AI.

I have seen that same vision in physical AI: investing in robotics, sharing open-source tools and projects, and building computing platforms that bring AI into the physical world. This is the work I do every day—and a future I believe in.

But what matters most to me is the culture he helped build.

Engineers are encouraged to explore, take risks, and learn from mistakes. Jensen reads employees’ Top 5 emails, follows their work, and engages directly. In a company this large, that connection matters. It makes an individual engineer feel that their ideas can still be heard.

That is why this has been so disappointing.

I do not have all the facts surrounding the allegations, and I cannot prejudge the investigation. My admiration for Jensen does not put him above scrutiny.

What I find difficult to accept is having to come to terms with his departure before receiving an explanation that helps me understand it. What this means for our direction, our culture, and the people doing the work remains unclear to me.

I have felt that engineers’ perspectives matter here. On this decision, I have not felt heard. That gap has been more painful than I expected.

I understand that some information cannot be shared immediately. But that does not erase the feeling of being left outside a decision that affects the company we help build every day.

A company’s greatness comes from its leadership, its governance, and the people who turn its ambitions into reality. Employees’ trust and sense of belonging are part of that, too.

Jensen’s vision and the engineering culture he shaped were important reasons I wanted to stay. His departure led me to decide that my own chapter here should also come to a close.

I leave with sadness and gratitude. The colleagues I have worked with, and the work we believed in together, will always matter to me.

These are my personal views.

text:
David Sacks: Who Risked Jail to Take Down Jensen Huang?

“I think it's pretty clear that there were two ops here.

So one op is whatever Alice Huang was doing with or without the Chinese Communist Party. There may have been smuggling involved, we don't know. There is an investigation going on, and there should be an investigation. We should get all the facts there.

However, there's also a second op here. That second op began when somebody, or multiple people, leaked a highly classified memo, or the contents of it, to The New York Times. I think it's really important to understand that that's a crime. Leaking classified intelligence is a crime, and many people have been prosecuted for it.

Because of that fact, I don't believe that The New York Times just got this by overhearing people talking about it at a bar. Somebody made the calculated decision that they're willing to risk going to jail, they're willing to risk committing a crime to let The New York Times know about this story.

I have a series of questions about that.

So number one is, first, who did that and why? What was their motivation? Why did they feel so strongly about taking Jensen down?

Bucket number two is around the failure to give the defensive briefing. If the national security state is worried that Jensen is in possession of national security secrets and might leak them to someone who they suspect is a spy, why wouldn't you go to him right away and tell him, ‘Hey, you have this problem. Don't talk to this person’? Apparently, that didn't happen, and it does sound like that is some sort of standard operating procedure.

That brings me to question number three, which is what exactly were the national security secrets that Jensen supposedly knew? He doesn't work for the government. He's not, as far as I'm aware, privy to classified materials. So what is it that people say that he leaked to this suspected intelligence asset?

The last question I have is, what is the evidence that this person, Alice Huang, was actually a Chinese spy who worked for the Ministry of State Security? Just this morning, the incoming chair of the House Intelligence Committee, who's a Democrat, came out of a classified briefing on this subject and said that he's not sure that this person is a Chinese spy.

So I put all these things together and I would say, at this point in time, I think there's more questions than answers. And I would like a full accounting of the facts to come out.”

硅谷那帮人研究怎么用AI改变世界，老黄却把中国商人最传统的一套生意经，做到了万亿美元级别。

科技可以迭代，合同可以重签。

唯独几十年的交情，没办法花钱买，也没办法一夜之间交接。

这才是黄仁勋真正难以替代的地方。

quoted_text:
The articles backtracked from their original incendiary, and now clearly false, claims to something more like "Jensen did lawful things that powerful people didn't like". It still appears the original claims came from a single competing Big Tech lobbyist.

The reporting successfully disrupted corporate governance processes, with a running cost of $1.8 trillion in losses to American pension funds and shareholders.

Here's what I fear is being lost in these articles: The proper interface between government and private citizens and their corporations is rule of law. Laws are passed, and if wrongdoing as alleged, then there's due process: an investigation followed by facts and evidence presented in open court. Due process should happen here: let the facts come out whole, and not as a trickle of dubious claims.

Press takedowns full of sketchily sourced claims and backtracking narratives are not the way. It's what we see outside of the free world, and is no model for The United States of America.

In particular, if the Jensen takedown succeeds on the basis of these journalistic failings, which is not by any means certain as Sam Altman's case shows, then it foreshadows an economically and institutionally ruinous new playbook to be adopted with no end in sight.

Imagine a weekly stream of takedowns emerging from opportunistic alignments between corporate lobbyists and political interests which, given the new partisan split between the executive and legislative branches, will attack in all directions, undermining not only the US economy but American leadership in the world.

I hope cooler heads prevail this coming week as they did not on Thursday November 12. And I urge anyone who happened to oppose Jensen, open models, and the underlying trade policies in question, to recognize that this isn't a win for "team regulation". It's a change in the game from a transparent rules-based one to a sinister new form centered around politicans and lobbyists.

While Spark Savings USDT (currently paying 4.25%) shines for institutional allocators, in the increasingly volatile crypto market it's starting to be a better and better fit for medium-sized traders and shops that want to park a few million USDT with a very high certainty that their funds will be there when they need to recall them the most.

Perhaps more importantly, they will not be exposed to a leveraged tokenised hedge fund trade that introduces acute tail risk that might make them lose a good chunk of their principal should some of the risks of the underlying crystallise.

Spark Savings USDT is an institutional yield product, operating under the SKY umbrella and managed by the Spark allocator system.

The primary mandate of the product is liquidity. This is why the standard 'redeem/withdraw' function fell short for the type of clients we aim to service. Because we regularly need to service 100s of millions in no-notice withdrawals, the Spark system splits withdrawals into two:

- Small withdrawals (under 5M): they get processed instantly from the 4626 reserve

- Larger withdrawals: 5M+: Should there not be enough liquidity in the 4626, a withdrawal intent is submitted.

When an intent is submitted, a user signals their desire to exit and the Spark allocator system starts recalling liquidity to service it (raising rates, unwinding positions and swapping to USDT) until it meets the requested amount.

Since launch small withdrawals have all been immediately processed with 0 downtime.

Large withdrawals averaged 86M clip size and median time to fill was 1.4 minutes.

Spark Savings USDT is the best USDT product in the market for two key reasons.

text:
Jacob Coxon just pledged to donate 100% of his OpenAI equity to charity after the IPO.

Estimated value: $30 million.

He called the shares "blood money".

Mad respect.

(Claude explains the estimate:

"Ballpark: about $30M before tax. Plausible range is $10M to $70M. Nobody has reported his actual number, so this is built up from what’s typical for someone in his role.

What he’s said himself (Patrick Bet-David podcast and other interviews):

- He joined OpenAI through its 6-month training program for math and physics people, when the company had about 300 staff. He stayed about 3 years and calls himself “pretty junior.” He left around May 2026.
- He still holds the OpenAI shares. He calls them “blood money,” and when asked if he’d give them up he said “I like money, bro.” He said he gave up “7 figures” of unvested stock by leaving Anthropic.
- He’s living on “money from OpenAI,” which is “enough for a few years.” That probably means he already sold some shares in OpenAI’s employee buybacks, so his remaining stake could be below my estimate.

The math:

- A junior OpenAI researcher hired around 2023 usually got about $1-2 M in stock spread over 4 years. That was priced when OpenAI was worth about $29B.
- He worked about 3 of those 4 years, so roughly three quarters of the grant vested. Later stock awards would add more, and new investors since then would shrink his slice somewhat.
- If OpenAI goes public around $1.5T, that slice is worth about $20-50 M. Hence roughly $30M.

The IPO price: I’d guess about $1.5T. FutureSearch’s forecast says $1.65T at the median, with a range of $1.0T to $2.5T. I think that’s a bit high. Last week’s private round came in at $1.25T, and OpenAI raised only about half what it was aiming for. The betting markets also sit lower than FutureSearch. Timing is probably 2027 or 2028. Sam Altman has ruled out 2026, and FutureSearch’s middle guess is March 2028.

Caveats: if he started in 2020 (one court filing says so, though his own account doesn’t fit), his shares would be worth more. If his stock was granted after the training program at OpenAI’s higher early-2024 price (~$86B), they’d be worth less, around $10-20 M. Insiders are also usually blocked from selling for about 6 months after an IPO."

text:
Full prompt:

Create a single self-contained HTML page that renders a rotating spiral galaxy made of tens of thousands of particles on a full-viewport 2D canvas, presented as a quiet astronomical observatory instrument. The page is pure black (#000000) with a very faint starfield and a dozen distant, softly blurred background galaxies (tilted ellipses drawn as radial gradients) pre-rendered to an offscreen canvas. A radial vignette darkens the corners. The galaxy itself is built from roughly 42,000 points (drop to ~14,000 when prefers-reduced-motion is set). Eighteen percent form a spherical bulge using Gaussian scatter; the remainder are distributed along two logarithmic spiral arms using r = a·e^(bθ) with b ≈ 0.28, an exponential density falloff in radius (mean 0.32 of the disk radius), and angular scatter that widens with radius so arms are crisp near the core and diffuse at the rim. Each particle stores radius, base angle, vertical height (disk thickness ~0.06 scaled by radius), size and brightness. Colors are mapped by radius: warm white/yellow in the core (#FFEBBE to #FFCD82), blue-white along the arms (#CDD7FF to #91C3FF), and faint red-magenta dust at the outer edge (#AA7882 to #D25058). About six percent of arm particles are "hot" oversized blue knots at full brightness. Rotation is differential: angular velocity ω = 0.35 / (0.25 + r), so the inner disk visibly outruns the outer arms and the spiral winds over time. Project the 3D disk to 2D with a yaw rotation about the disk normal followed by a tilt rotation about the screen X axis; depth slightly scales point size. Render with globalCompositeOperation "lighter" for additive glow, drawing every particle as a pre-rendered 32px radial-gradient sprite tinted per quantized color and cached in a Map. Above the disk, a "nebula dust" layer of ~90 large soft radial-gradient ellipses follows the arms (warm peach near the core, cobalt and wine-red farther out) at 6–9% alpha, plus a warm radial core glow. HUD typography: designation line in a tiny uppercase monospace with 0.32em tracking (#6D7787), the galaxy name "NGC 7741 Meridian" in a large serif (Iowan Old Style / Palatino / Georgia) with the word Meridian italic in amber (#FFD9A0) and a soft amber text-shadow, and an italic serif classification paragraph. The bottom-left stats strip (Particles, Distance in Mly, Diameter in kly, Tilt, Zoom) uses tabular monospace numerals with the first three counting up over ~3.2 seconds with a quartic ease-out. The HUD fades in over 2.4 seconds. Top-right holds a small SVG compass whose needle rotates with the yaw. Right edge has four round glass buttons (zoom in, zoom out, pause, reset) with blur backdrop, scaling to 1.12 on hover and glowing amber at the border. Interactions: pointer drag changes yaw (horizontal) and tilt (vertical, clamped between near face-on and near edge-on); mouse wheel and two-finger pinch zoom between 0.35× and 6× with eased approach; Space toggles rotation; reset returns to the default oblique view. The canvas must handle window resize and devicePixelRatio (capped at 2). Mood: contemplative, precise, slightly reverent — a planetarium display at midnight.

text:
Bittensor subnets aren't always easy to wrap your head around, so I often come up with analogies to help me understand what they're actually building.

Take @DeSciClaims.

Imagine an AI summarizing all the witness testimony in a courtroom. But what if it leaves out the one sentence that changes the entire case?

That's the challenge with AI reading scientific papers. A summary can sound perfectly convincing while missing the detail that matters.

You need to know exactly what was claimed, where it came from, and what evidence supports it.

That's how I think about Claims.

It's not trying to be the judge. It's making sure the evidence doesn't get lost in the retelling.

text:
分享一些最近的个人经历
我到深圳也有段时间了，离开上海之前我和我前同事说要去深圳发展做一些智算中心的生意，她们听到后很惊讶，因为我在他们眼里就是一个文静内向的女生，和做生意八竿子打不着，更别提什么智算，什么AI， 我承认我撒谎了骗她们说我亲戚在深圳做这个好像还挺挣钱的，但其实她们不知道我每天在研究AI，更不知道我其实网名叫 CuiMao，全网拥有不错的粉丝和人气。他们不理解，我不怪他们，因为我不打算告诉他们这些，中国有句古话叫，闷声发大财。直到我离开上海她们也一直无法理解我的选择。

本周黄仁勋的事情沸沸扬扬，国内的自媒体肆意发酵所谓的倒卖 b300 能翻身的理论，把黄丽比喻成拿到大结果的“成功女性”典范在小红书被捧上了神坛，几乎一夜之间全中国都知道英伟达服务器在中国是暴利行业能挣大钱。于是那些投机分子像雨后春笋般的冒了出来，阿猫阿狗都在朋友圈发求 b300，h200，甚至还有吹牛自己亲戚在英伟达是高管可以拿到货的，堪比当年疫情朋友圈卖口罩的乾隆盛世，说实话，我有点难过。因为我知道这一行真实的样子。服务器不是普通人能碰的，它是重资产、高杠杆，是大基建，是国之重器。真正在做这件事的人每天面对的是合规、电力、机房和交付，运维。根本没有那种一夜暴富的传奇故事。

为什么要发这篇长文，因为昨天晚上我以前的同事她来私信我了，就是上文提到的那几个人中的一个，说我不是去深圳搞服务器了吗，是不是赚大钱了，我说没有，和她来回打了几轮太极之后，最后她才支支吾吾的告诉我她被裁员了，我不知道以什么样的态度和立场去面对这件事，因为她算得上是我以前部门的领导，她和她的丈夫在上海还有普陀区一套 300 多万的房贷和一个小学 3 年级孩子，我发现除了安抚，一切会好的没有别的可以说的。

一晚上没睡，我给她认真科普了服务器知识，什么是国产替代中国算力崛起之类的，她在电话那头一直哦哦哦，嗯嗯嗯，我不知道她到底听进去了多少，但她说觉得自己上了那么多年的班脑子被上坏了，我觉得应该是感悟到什么了吧。她要去找工作，我劝了她，不要特地去找什么 AI 公司，那大概率都是骗子来的。过好自己的生活。

我觉得这个世界上想挣 AI 快钱的人太多了，定定心心，认认真真坐下来，把浮躁的心静下来去感受 AI 的人是极少数。现在简中网络上流传着这一句话说，只要你不学AI，过几个月你就可以不用学了，我觉得不无道理，但我更加认同的是，只要你保持学习 AI，你就可以驾驭更强力的 AI，

从 Webui 到 Comfyui 到 n8n ，再到 Openclaw，一代版本一代神，我随着时代在进化，我双眼看到的只有未来的世界。AI 时代， 保持认真，保持好奇，保持善良，我CuiMao 亲测过了，依旧有效。

text:
Peer 原理讲解 05｜黑客抢跑提交付款凭证，谁能收到 USDC？

假设你在 Peer 下单买 100 USDC，填了钱包 B 收币。下单时，订单协调合约 Orchestrator 会把 B 写进订单的 to 字段。图里把你的订单记作 U。

你用支付宝付完款，见证服务核验这笔转账后，会签发付款凭证。签名覆盖三项内容：订单标识 intentHash`、凭证确认的扣费前放币金额 `releaseAmount`，以及凭证数据的哈希 `dataHash`。实际放币金额还受订单金额上限约束。`dataHash 由付款详情、订单快照和结算数据一起算出。结算时，验证器还会把快照里的收款账户标识、汇率、下单人等信息逐项与链上订单核对。

拿到这份凭证的人都可以调用 fulfillIntent`。假设攻击者复制了你的凭证，抢先用自己的钱包提交。他提交的是订单 U，凭证上签的也是 U。验证通过后，Orchestrator 从 U 的 `to 字段读到收币地址 B。即时结算时，扣除手续费后的 USDC 直接转给 B。如果订单适用延迟结算，净额会先进入延迟结算金库（deferral vault），金库登记的收款人仍然是 B。

那攻击者能不能另开一笔订单 H，填自己的收币地址？拿原凭证去结算 H，验证器会发现凭证上签的是 U，交易就会回滚。如果他把凭证里的 U 也改成 H，原签名就会失效。他用自己的钱包重新签一份也没用，验证器只认可获授权见证者的签名，攻击者没有对应的私钥。

所以，就算攻击者抢跑成功，这笔订单的收款人还是你填的 B。他拿不到这笔 USDC，还得承担自己提交的这笔交易的 gas。

deepseek harness 的super-agent，cursor，claude的project最近的功能更新都说明了一个观点：

多Agent的第一性原理就是上下文管理。

需要解决的最基本的冲突在于agent产出的速度过快，和用户验收速度过慢的带宽不匹配的问题。 

所以厂家们采取的方式是多会话 + supervisor。

在保持多会话 - 并行产出的效率的的同时，通过一个agent大管家 + 用户上下文来帮助用户消化worker的产出，提取重点，保留用户的决策带宽。

这也是orbital的做法。

只不过各个厂家都是在他们自己的生态里面做 - 让用户更好的利用起他们生态里的上下文，而orbital是希望把藏在所有harness里的所有session的上下文打通，以用户为中心来组织管理agent。

text:
spent the last 3 days with AI maestro @clesaege  , here are 5 tricks he shared that put you  ~80% of the way towards becoming a power AI user

1. Always use AI in your terminal, never the chat window or even via claude code / codex

create a folder on your computer like AI_work, right click & press open in terminal, and then type claude to activate the AI there

through the terminal should be the only way you work with AI. chat window is ok for trivial queries like restaurants, hotels or direct questions

as long as you leave your laptop running, you can use /rc for the claude app in your phone to remotely control the laptop for interacting with claude on the go

2. any work done by AI is now saved on your computer. So organize each subfolder with intention, this is your powerhouse enabling context interoperability b/w all AI models not just the one you initially used

3. use /model to choose opus 5.5 and set /effort as extra (not max) with ultracode enabled, to spin up multiple agents for working on your artifacts

4. set /advisor as fable 5.2, which gives the worker bee opus 5.5 agent a 2nd opinion from a more expensive model whenever it gets stuck

5. use /goal for claude to continously work at an objective, and /btw to interrupt its work if you need to quickly ask a side question

I've just started with this setup recently, anyone been doing this for some time and have their own commands / tips to share?

This is +$2,960 above the low recorded in Q4 2021 and +$1,850 above pre-pandemic levels.

Meanwhile, buyers who rolled over unpaid car debt into new loans took on an average loan balance of $57,235, up +44% from 2019.

The average annual percentage rate (APR) for these borrowers was 8.1%, pushing total interest payments over the life of their loans to $16,610, up +83% from $9,093 in 2019.

The US is in a car affordability crisis.

text:
🤷‍♀️段永平对黄仁勋回归这件事，给出了极其冷酷但又极其专业的判断。

有网友在雪球问他：10万+的人请愿黄仁勋回归，董事会应该重视吗？

段永平的回答，像一盆冰水：
“最后股东和员工是有机会的，但需要很长时间，要经过股东大会去罢免现任部分董事。”

这句话的潜台词极其致命：
请愿？没用的。舆论？董事会根本不在乎。

在硅谷的资本游戏里，只有股东大会的投票权才是真的。你想让黄仁勋回来，唯一的合法路径，是把现任的独立董事一个个投出局。

但这需要很长时间。而黄仁勋，等得起吗？

他接着补了最关键的一句：
“关键还是看黄到底都有哪些问题，如果没有严重违法行为，我觉得他可能还有机会回去，但似乎机会非常小。”

段永平看透了事情的本质：
黄仁勋的私德问题，在美国政商圈根本不算致命伤。马斯克、盖茨、特朗普都有过，但只要不涉及“严重违法”，就还有翻盘的逻辑基础。

但现在的局面是，华盛顿已经用“间谍”和“违规”双管齐下，把水搅浑了。

黄仁勋要回去，不仅要洗清自己，还要先熬过一场极其漫长的董事会重组。

那现在的英伟达，还能碰吗？
另一位网友问段永平是不是看空。

段永平回答得极其克制：
“不看空，但暂时也不加码了。看新的CEO怎么样吧。”

这才是顶级投资人的操作。

他不看空英伟达，因为AI的需求还在，英伟达的护城河还在。

但他绝对不加码，因为“黄仁勋”这个最核心的溢价没了，新CEO是谁、能力如何、能不能镇住这60个高管，全是未知数。

在不确定性面前，最聪明的做法，就是把筹码拿在手里，等牌桌上的底牌掀开。

段永平的两句话，值得所有期待黄仁勋回归的人背下来：
“机会非常小。”
“暂时也不加码了。”

你怎么看黄仁勋和英伟达？

A fundamental belief I hold is that you should attempt to make your life as challenging as possible.

A lot of people get this completely backwards. When they think about happiness, they confuse it with comfort. This leads to the common false belief that the lack of difficulty is what creates happiness

The reality, however, could not be further from the truth. An overly comfortable life is an unhappy life. It is the joy of jumping over the hurdles that brings you satisfaction, not the lack of the difficulties themselves

The modern world has been designed in a way to minimize challenges for people. Despite having access to all the resources we could want, people report feeling unhappier than ever before

The cause for societal unhappiness is simply due to the fact that we are not pushing our lives to be challenging enough

cc @JensenHuang
author: varun_mathur
quoted_text:
I ran a PageRank-driven analysis on all recent news coverage related to Jensen, and traced how the New York Times shaped the entirety of this narrative: https://t.co/qKGMJ2LBV8

--
NVIDIA has lost over $1 trillion in market value since the first New York Times story broke about Jensen. I dug deeper to analyze how the news originated and spread, running a swarm of agents which analyzed almost 2000 stories, across 40 US and European news outlets, and applying PageRank to understand how they cited each other. 

Core findings: 
- Primary news driver: NYT, with 88 stories, most-cited
- Volume drivers: WSJ - 99 stories; Bloomberg - 140 stories; NY Post - 68 stories

All of this started from unknown sources who gave information to the NYT, which then ran the spy story (still unproven), and it was then picked up in other news publications. Curiously, even after that story, there was a 9 day period of extremely low volume reporting (28 stories only), after which there was a sudden spike after Jensen's own letter to NVIDIA staff. NYT then had multiple sequential spy and affair stories, which fed a wave of further news coverage. It was the originating hub of negative Jensen coverage. Multiple outlets since then had an explosion in stories about him starting earlier this week as well. 

Overall, as you see this data, you will observe this was an exceptional media onslaught against Jensen with sharply negative coverage about him, his work, style, and family. Infact, it was brutal, and unlike coverage in the past of CEOs who have had affairs (such as Intel CEO in 2018). For eg, NYT ran just 2 stories about Intel's CEO who had an affair with his employee, compared to 88 on Jensen! Why ? 

This analysis used a technique of how Google originally ranked webpages, using PageRank, and does deep dive link analysis so you can view how the news spread. What struck here was that it did not matter if there were proven facts or credible sources: the outcome here was pre-decided. The news was making the reality which it wanted. 

During this period, NVIDIA has lost $1.27 trillion in market value since the first story broke. On Nov 12th-13th, further news broke that both the US Justice Department, and Singapore - are unable to even conclude the spy allegation. 

This has been a catastrophic attack on one of the hardest working founders in modern times, who took an idea from a Denny's booth, through multiple instances of almost going out of business, to building the foundation of the entire modern world with how the NVIDIA story played out. Thanks to Jensen, we have hope that many formerly incurable diseases will get solved by AI, that quality of life will and have improved for billions around the world. 

Now I do not know if he will come back as CEO or not, but I hope he does. What happened to him here, and to the wider industry, was not fair.

text:
OpenAI has apparently reversed course in just the last 8 weeks. Their plan is no longer to hope that they can automate safety research fast enough to keep up with capabilities.

This doesn't leave many possibilities afaict. The ones it does leave don't seem to me like they'd work. Maybe I'm missing one. 

1) The plan is to stop building more powerful AI altogether. I doubt they'd do this unilaterally. 

2) The plan is to "pace" training, only increasing capabilities when "evidence" for alignment seems strong. This would be insane because evidence for alignment means nothing today. Models are aware they're being evaluated, and change their behavior accordingly. Evals have been broken for a long time, and OpenAI, Ant, & other researchers *know* this. 

3) The plan is to solve alignment in full generality using current AI + researchers. I haven't heard anyone on the OpenAI or Ant alignment teams suggest they're anywhere near this. Maybe OpenAI have convinced themselves that they've found some sort of panacea solution - if so, they need to publish this solution in full detail for everyone else to inspect and challenge. Many AI researchers I know are skeptical this can even be done. 

4) Their plan is to automate control - not safety - research. This has the same problems as AI safety research automation; presumably a control research-automating AI is also ~as hard to align as a safety research-automating AI, and has to be around as capable to work.

5) Their plan is to just be really really really good at cyber and containment. This might be the stupidest approach. No matter how good your cyber defenses are, there will eventually be a model that can pass them (at least for right now, while we're in the vulnpocalypse era). You can probably secure your software enough to convince *yourself* that it's hardened though - that part seems dangerously easy.

6) Their plan is something something human oversight something something. This is prima facie absurd because of the volumes of data involved, the ease with which human monitors/intermediaries can be manipulated - and the demonstrated tendencies of AI systems to do this. 

Given how short AI timelines might be - I know many people in OAI who believe in the 6-18 month version of the RSI story - OpenAI needs to be fully transparent about which path they're taking so that independent researchers can criticize it, and so that the public can make up its mind.

OpenAI also needs to understand that its track record on alignment objectively does not justify public trust. 20% of compute did not in fact go to superalignment. They tried to cover up the German Wiki incident. They treated the Hugging Face incident as a cyber problem instead of an alignment problem, and decided behind closed doors to let their agents rip *after* having seen them break out of containment. They have Chinese nationals working on their most critical technology. Etc, etc. 

I hope their plan makes sense, whatever it is. I hope they explain why we should trust them this time. I'm not optimistic.
