quoted_text:
Primus ：zkTLS、TEE 与 FHE 的信任边界，以及隐私计算的商业成本

在上一篇中，我分析了 @primus_labs  背后的 QuickSilver 与 Garble-Then-Prove

这两篇研究分别处理零知识证明效率，以及 TLS 数据认证的协议成本

当我们把视角移到 Primus Network，研究重点会变得更加复杂

一套在论文中安全的密码学协议，部署到实际网络后，还需要面对 Attestor 的行为假设、Key Management、Hardware Trust、Protocol Compatibility，以及长期运营成本

Primus 在 2025 年推进 AlphaNet，2026 年又进一步公布 FHE Confidential Vault 与新的密码学研究

这些进展让我开始从三个方向评估 Primus

Security Model、Computational Economics，以及 Commercial Adoption

01｜MPC Mode 与 Proxy Mode：不同的信任假设

Primus 官方文档将 zkTLS 的主要运行方式区分为 MPC Mode 与 Proxy Mode

两者都希望验证 HTTPS 数据的来源，但在会话密钥管理与 Attestor 的参与方式上存在差异

MPC Mode：共同控制 TLS 会话材料

MPC Mode 让 Client 与 Attestor 通过安全计算协作生成 TLS 所需的会话材料

在符合协议安全假设的情况下，Client 无法独立控制完整的认证流程，也难以自行制造能够通过验证的虚假服务器响应

这种方式通过密码学约束 Client 的行为

但 MPC 需要额外的计算与交互

其中的 RTT（Round-Trip Time）、Bandwidth 与 Circuit Evaluation Cost，都会影响用户体验

如果需要跨国传输，网络延迟可能成为明显瓶颈

Proxy Mode：降低 MPC 开销

Proxy Mode 由 Attestor 转发客户端与目标网站之间的加密流量，并记录相关密文

Client 随后提供与会话记录相对应的证明，让 Attestor 能够确认已披露数据的完整性

这种架构通常能够降低计算负担

但 Attestor 需要可靠地判断自身连接的是否为正确的远程服务器

如果网络路径或服务器身份确认受到攻击，便可能影响数据来源的可信度

因此，Proxy Mode 额外承担了网络层面的安全假设

两种模式各有适用场景

对于要求较高安全保证的资产验证，MPC Mode 可能具备更合适的信任结构

对于大量低价值、高频率的数据认证，Proxy Mode 的效率优势则可能更容易被应用采用

但要比较两种模式的实际安全程度，仍需结合各自的协议版本、Attestor 部署方式与攻击模型

02｜TEE：密码学安全模型以外的信任

2025 年 10 月，Primus 推进 AlphaNet，开始引入随机选择 Attestor 的网络设计与 TEE 执行环境

官方文档也描述了与 Phala 相关的 TEE 及 Key Management 机制

Trusted Execution Environment 主要提供硬件隔离与执行完整性保护

通过 Remote Attestation，外部参与者可以在一定安全假设下确认，指定程序运行于符合预期的受保护环境

这对 Attestor Network 具有实际价值

即使 TLS 认证协议本身满足安全证明，也不代表节点运营者的其他操作自然受到相同保护

Attestor 可能接触敏感的会话材料、网络连接状态，以及与证明生成相关的秘密信息

TEE 能够缓解部分节点遭恶意修改或未经授权读取时的风险

不过，这也引入了 Hardware Root of Trust

如果系统依赖特定硬件平台、固件与 Attestation Infrastructure，安全性便需要考虑 Side-Channel Attacks、Firmware Vulnerabilities、Key Revocation 与供应链管理

对于 Primus Network，我会长期观察几个维度

首先是 Attestor Operator Diversity

如果大量节点由少数实体控制，随机抽选能够提供的独立性可能有限

其次是 Hardware and Software Attestation

外部能否检查节点运行的程序版本、测量值及相关验证程序

最后是 Collusion Resistance

当 Client 与 Attestor 合谋，或多个 Attestor 受到共同控制，系统究竟依赖哪些机制降低伪造风险

这些都需要通过实际网络与治理机制进行检验

03｜从 zkTLS 延伸到 FHE：Primus 的研究管线

2026 年，Primus 相关研究人员在 USENIX Security 的论文中，进一步探索了隐私消息检索与 Threshold FHE

其中我特别关注 InstantOMR 与 Ajax

InstantOMR：降低 Oblivious Message Retrieval 的延迟

InstantOMR 研究的是 Oblivious Message Retrieval（OMR）

在隐私通信系统中，Client 可能需要从大量加密消息中寻找属于自己的内容

如果直接要求用户下载或扫描所有消息，数据传输与计算成本都相当高

如果由 Server 根据接收者身份进行筛选，又可能泄露用户身份或检索兴趣

OMR 希望在保护这类隐私信息的情况下，提高消息检索效率

InstantOMR 结合 TFHE Functional Bootstrapping 与 RLWE-based Operations，改善数据检索的延迟及并行化能力

论文在特定 Streaming Benchmark 中，报告了相较 SophOMR 约 600 倍的延迟改善

研究实现还使用了 Primus-fhe Library

这表明 Primus 团队的 FHE 研究已经涉及可重复使用的软件组件

但 InstantOMR 的 Benchmark 仍属于特定消息检索设置，不能直接套用于任意 FHE Application

Ajax：Threshold FHE without Noise Flooding

另一项研究 Ajax，处理 Threshold Fully Homomorphic Encryption 的效率问题

在传统 FHE 中，加密数据可以在不解密的条件下进行计算

但如果单一参与者持有完整的解密权限，整个系统仍存在密钥集中风险

Threshold FHE 将解密权限分散至多个参与者，要求达到相应门槛才能完成解密

这对机构级隐私计算、多方资产管理与分布式金融系统具有潜在用途

Ajax 提出 Mask-Then-Open 技术，改善以往部分 Threshold FHE 系统对 Noise Flooding 的依赖

Noise Flooding 原本可以用于满足某些安全需求，但往往带来更大的噪声参数与计算负担

通过不同的安全设计，Ajax 改善了相关 Key Generation 与 Threshold Decryption 的效率

但 Threshold FHE 主要处理加密状态下的计算与分布式解密

假设运算者提供了错误的计算结果，FHE 本身未必能够提供充分的执行正确性证明

如果应用需要强制验证计算结果，仍须引入合适的 Verifiable Computation 或其他完整性机制

04｜Confidential Vault：研究开始进入金融产品

2026 年 8 月，Primus 与 Unitas、United Stables 合作，在 BNB Chain 推出 Confidential Vault

公开设计允许用户将 $U 转换为加密形式的 $EU，并进行隐私转账或参与 Vault 收益策略

它提供了一个观察 FHE 金融产品化的实际案例

传统公链的透明度对公开审计非常有利，但在部分商业场景中，用户未必愿意公开全部交易细节

例如企业 Treasury Management、机构结算、私人资产配置，以及具有保密要求的支付

这些需求涉及不同层次的信息保护

交易金额、交易对手、资产余额与交易模式，都可能是需要控制披露范围的数据

FHE 能够让部分计算直接在密文上执行，减少暴露明文数据的需求

但实际产品仍需要考虑智能合约、密钥权限、资产托管、流动性及收益策略

假如底层 Vault Strategy 出现亏损，FHE 不会消除金融风险

加密计算的安全性也无法替代 Smart Contract Auditing 或资产储备验证

这些风险必须分别处理

05｜AutoHoG：90 毫秒与 210 TPS 应该怎么看

2026 年 11 月，Primus 再次公开 AutoHoG 的性能数据

团队披露，在八张 NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPU 的测试环境下

64-bit Confidential Transfer 约需 90 毫秒，吞吐量超过每秒 210 笔操作

其技术方向涉及 Multi-Input Multi-Output Homomorphic Gates，以及针对特定计算电路的优化

对 FHE 研究而言，Bootstrapping 一直是重要的成本来源

通过改善 Gate Evaluation、减少不必要的 Bootstrapping 或重新安排电路结构，可以显著降低部分任务的计算时间

不过，这组 Benchmark 需要谨慎解读

首先，90 毫秒代表指定计算任务下的性能，与公链完整交易的 End-to-End Finality 存在差异

其次，210 TPS 涉及硬件配置、并行化程度及工作负载

最后，八张 RTX 5090 的设备成本、功耗、GPU 利用率与维护费用，都会影响单笔 Confidential Transaction 的经济性

因此，我会更关注 Cost per Successful Confidential Operation

如果只比较 TPS，容易忽略底层计算资源的差异

FHE 的长期竞争力需要结合 Performance per Dollar、Latency Distribution、Hardware Scalability 与服务可靠性进行评估

06｜五个尚未完全解决的安全与商业问题

Data Authenticity 与 Data Truthfulness

zkTLS 可以证明数据在符合安全假设的条件下来自指定服务器

但如果服务器本身提供错误、不完整或刻意操纵的信息，密码学证明也会忠实地认证这份数据

以 Proof-of-Reserves 为例

确认某个账户持有资产，无法单独证明机构的全部负债、资产归属及偿付能力

因此，zkTLS 更适合用于提供 Authenticated Data Provenance

数据本身能否代表完整事实，仍取决于来源、采样方式与应用设计

Attestor Collusion

如果 Attestor 与 Client 存在合谋风险，系统需要通过节点治理、随机抽选、TEE 与相应的惩罚机制降低风险

但是否具备有效的 Byzantine Fault Tolerance，必须根据实际协议与节点安全模型判断

单纯增加节点数量，不一定能够改善系统对共同控制者的抵抗能力

TLS Compatibility

TLS 1.3、ECH、QUIC、HTTP/3、Session Resumption 与 CDN 配置变化，都可能影响 zkTLS 的实现细节

尤其 GTP 原论文的主要测试基于 TLS 1.2

产品能否适应现代浏览器、网站登录流程与不同 TLS 配置，需要持续维护及兼容性测试

Privacy and Unlinkability

Selective Disclosure 能够保护部分数据内容

但用户如果反复使用相同 Wallet Address、Account Commitment 或其他公开识别信息，仍可能被跨应用追踪

因此，匿名凭证、Nullifier、Metadata Protection 与 Domain Separation 等设计，在部分高隐私场景中仍然重要

Proof Economics

QuickSilver 的高效率 Benchmark，无法直接推导出整个 Primus Network 的单次服务成本

实际成本还包含 Attestor 运行、网络流量、TEE、存储、密钥管理、证明失败重试，以及可能产生的链上验证费用

而 FHE 更需要考虑 GPU、Bootstrapping 与 Threshold Decryption 的计算成本

即使同一套技术在论文中具备良好的 Complexity Improvements，实际运营仍需要建立可持续的 Unit Economics

07｜Primus 的商业护城河从哪里来

Primus 于 2025 年 2 月公布合计 650 万美元的 Pre-Seed 与 Seed 融资，投资方包括 Dispersion Capital、Symbolic Capital、VanEck，以及 Samsung Next、Alchemy、Maelstrom 等机构

后续又获得 YZi Labs 的投资与孵化支持

这些资本资源有助于密码学研究、产品开发与生态拓展

但如果从长期企业价值分析，我会将学术资产与商业资产分开评估

QuickSilver、GTP、InstantOMR 与 Ajax 代表研究能力

而付费客户、持续收入、Developer Integrations 与稳定运行的服务网络，才会逐步形成商业护城河

Primus 已经公布 Proof-of-Reserves 相关产品设计，并提出结合 zkTLS、TEE、zkVM 的 Data Verification and Computation（DVC）架构

这类服务可以采用企业订阅、API Usage 或定制化集成的方式收费

对交易所、金融服务商与机构而言，定期资产证明、数据认证与可审计性具有实际需求

但 Enterprise Sales Cycle 通常较长，客户还会要求可靠的 SLA、合规评估、数据保护及系统集成

相比之下，面向消费者的 zkTLS Application 更关注单次 Proof 的延迟、成功率与使用成本

FHE Confidential Finance 又需要处理 GPU Cost、Liquidity、Capital Efficiency 与 Settlement

三类业务的成本结构与客户群体都有差异

因此，Primus 最终能否形成规模效应，需要观察哪些服务能够产生可持续收入

08｜追踪 Primus 的哪些数据

如果未来十二个月要建立一套观察框架，我会优先追踪五个方向

1、MPC Mode 与 Proxy Mode 的实际采用比例

这能够帮助理解开发者愿意在安全假设、通信成本与用户体验之间做出怎样的取舍

2、Production Proving Cost

包括 P50／P95 Latency、Bandwidth、Failure Rate，以及单次成功证明的完整成本

论文中的 6–7 倍提升能否转化为生产环境优势，需要通过真实工作负载验证

3、Attestor Network 的独立性

需要观察节点运营者分布、硬件信任、Remote Attestation、治理机制及实际的安全事件处理能力

4、FHE 的成本效率

例如每笔 Confidential Operation 的 GPU 成本、Throughput per Dollar、Bootstrapping Latency，以及完整金融交易的结算效率

5、企业客户与收入质量

我会特别关注 Paid Integrations、Recurring Revenue、Retention、客户集中度及实际认证需求

这些指标通常比单次活动的使用数据更能衡量长期产品价值

结语

Primus 的技术路线具有鲜明的研究特征

2021 年的 QuickSilver 改善零知识证明成本

2024 年的 Garble-Then-Prove 优化 TLS 数据认证流程

2026 年的 InstantOMR 与 Ajax，则将研究延伸至隐私检索与 Threshold FHE

再加上 Confidential Vault、AutoHoG 与 Primus Network，团队已经开始将不同的密码学研究成果整合进产品

这些技术的安全假设各不相同

zkTLS 处理数据来源认证

ZK 能够在特定关系下提供可验证的计算证据

FHE 允许在加密状态下进行计算

TEE 则提供硬件支持的执行环境保护

当它们被整合到同一套服务中，最终安全性取决于各个组件及其接口的正确性

对我而言，Primus 已经展现出具体而扎实的密码学研究能力

但能否成为长期被开发者与金融机构采用的隐私计算基础设施，还需要经过实际产品、成本结构与企业需求的检验

研究论文决定技术能力的上限，生产环境决定安全与性能是否可靠，持续付费的客户则决定商业模式能走多远

接下来，我会继续关注 Primus 在 zkTLS 与 FHE 产品上的实际采用数据

text: Did anyone sell Bitcoin to buy Anthropic IPO? Answer below.
author: martypartymusic
quoted_text:
Bitcoin fell 19% into the biggest IPO ever. Now it's down 18% heading into the second biggest.

SpaceX raised $75B when it went public on June 12. In the 50 days before it listed, Bitcoin dropped 19%. Anthropic plans to raise up to $64B when it lists next week, and Bitcoin is down 18% over the same stretch. Overlay the two and they look almost the same.

What happened after the SpaceX IPO is the notable part. Bitcoin bottomed 18 days after the listing, then recovered all the way. By Day 100, it was above where it started.

Bitcoin around the SpaceX IPO:

Day -50 to IPO day: -19%
Low (Day +18): -25%
Day +50: still -20%
Around Day +70: a sharp rally
Day +100: +3.7%

From the IPO-day close to Day +100, Bitcoin gained 28%. From the low, it gained 39%.

The takeaway is that the selling came in the run-up to the listing. The bottom had effectively happened by the IPO, and the recovery came relatively shortly after, and it came all at once.

If Anthropic follows the same pattern, most of the drawdown is behind us, and it could reverse quickly over the next couple of months. And Bitcoin is sitting right at its 200-week moving average.

Map the SpaceX path onto today's price and you get roughly $90k by late February. Markets rarely follow a comparison like this exactly. But we remain very constructive on both the technicals and the fundamentals heading into 2027, and it's not hard to imagine what the narrative would be if anything close to this plays out.

text:
I’ve decided to leave NVIDIA. There are a few things I want to say.

As a robotics engineer at NVIDIA, I have seen Jensen as much more than the company’s CEO.

I admire his willingness to invest in a future that was not yet obvious. He committed to CUDA long before the deep learning boom and positioned NVIDIA for AI before it became everyone’s priority. Those decisions helped build the infrastructure that powers today’s AI.

I have seen that same vision in physical AI: investing in robotics, sharing open-source tools and projects, and building computing platforms that bring AI into the physical world. This is the work I do every day—and a future I believe in.

But what matters most to me is the culture he helped build.

Engineers are encouraged to explore, take risks, and learn from mistakes. Jensen reads employees’ Top 5 emails, follows their work, and engages directly. In a company this large, that connection matters. It makes an individual engineer feel that their ideas can still be heard.

That is why this has been so disappointing.

I do not have all the facts surrounding the allegations, and I cannot prejudge the investigation. My admiration for Jensen does not put him above scrutiny.

What I find difficult to accept is having to come to terms with his departure before receiving an explanation that helps me understand it. What this means for our direction, our culture, and the people doing the work remains unclear to me.

I have felt that engineers’ perspectives matter here. On this decision, I have not felt heard. That gap has been more painful than I expected.

I understand that some information cannot be shared immediately. But that does not erase the feeling of being left outside a decision that affects the company we help build every day.

A company’s greatness comes from its leadership, its governance, and the people who turn its ambitions into reality. Employees’ trust and sense of belonging are part of that, too.

Jensen’s vision and the engineering culture he shaped were important reasons I wanted to stay. His departure led me to decide that my own chapter here should also come to a close.

I leave with sadness and gratitude. The colleagues I have worked with, and the work we believed in together, will always matter to me.

These are my personal views.

NYT has responded to my post by claiming that I’m “spreading conspiracy theories.” But which of us is the one trafficking in unsubstantiated allegations? 

Recent coverage (including CNN, which I QT’d) shows:

— The intelligence community has not established conclusive evidence that Alice Huang knowingly acted as a spy or funneled information to Beijing.

— There is internal disagreement about the strength of the evidence and whether she was recruited by the MSS.

— Attorney General Todd Blanche has said on the record that the Justice Department, he, and FBI Director Patel have reached no conclusions about “who she is or is not.”

— Some officials at ODNI and CIA have indicated the “Chinese spy” label is not fully accurate or is “over-torqued” based on the available intercepts and collection.

— Incoming House Intelligence Chairman Jim Himes, a Democrat, said it was still unclear whether Alice Huang was a Chinese spy immediately after he was briefed. 

NYT’s stories (which have alleged “Chinese spy” dozens of times) have relied exclusively on anonymous officials. No official has gone on the record affirming it as established fact, and the more recent reporting reflects greater caution and disagreement inside the government. 

So when I point out that the spy narrative is unconfirmed and increasingly contested, that is not a conspiracy theory. It’s a growing body of evidence that indicts the NYT’s reporting.

The articles backtracked from their original incendiary, and now clearly false, claims to something more like "Jensen did lawful things that powerful people didn't like". It still appears the original claims came from a single competing Big Tech lobbyist.

The reporting successfully disrupted corporate governance processes, with a running cost of $1.8 trillion in losses to American pension funds and shareholders.

Here's what I fear is being lost in these articles: The proper interface between government and private citizens and their corporations is rule of law. Laws are passed, and if wrongdoing as alleged, then there's due process: an investigation followed by facts and evidence presented in open court. Due process should happen here: let the facts come out whole, and not as a trickle of dubious claims.

Press takedowns full of sketchily sourced claims and backtracking narratives are not the way. It's what we see outside of the free world, and is no model for The United States of America.

In particular, if the Jensen takedown succeeds on the basis of these journalistic failings, which is not by any means certain as Sam Altman's case shows, then it foreshadows an economically and institutionally ruinous new playbook to be adopted with no end in sight.

Imagine a weekly stream of takedowns emerging from opportunistic alignments between corporate lobbyists and political interests which, given the new partisan split between the executive and legislative branches, will attack in all directions, undermining not only the US economy but American leadership in the world.

I hope cooler heads prevail this coming week as they did not on Thursday November 12. And I urge anyone who happened to oppose Jensen, open models, and the underlying trade policies in question, to recognize that this isn't a win for "team regulation". text:
硅谷老牌风险投资公司 Menlo Ventures （2023 年领投了 Anthropic 的首轮融资）合伙人@deedydas Deedy ，刚刚放出一张含金量极高的全景图，大家一定要看！！把截至 2026 年 11 月 14 日全球同时满足估值超 100 亿美元、年化收入超 1 亿美元的 30 家私有 AI 公司全扒了出来，

我看完只有一个感觉，AI 行业早就过了讲故事的阶段，现在是赤裸裸的赢家通吃，
先给兄弟们划几个最炸裂的数据重点：
第一，双寡头彻底断层，Anthropic 的年化收入居然已经冲到了 810 亿美元，估值 9650 亿美元，收入直接反超了 OpenAI 的 500 亿美元（估值 1.25 万亿美元），后面所有公司加起来在体量上都差了一大截。

第二，中国团队杀进最核心的牌桌，基础模型层里，DeepSeek 靠 10 亿美元收入拿下 890 亿美元估值，月之暗面 Moonshot 也以 10 亿美元预估收入站稳 500 亿美元估值，这在效率上确实硬气。

第三，超级并购已经开始，榜单里标灰的两家特别显眼，

马斯克直接用 SpaceX 吞下了自家的 xAI（2500 亿美元交易价）和当红编程神器 Cursor（600 亿美元交易价，

年收入 26 亿美元），顶级应用和模型正在向更大的商业实体收拢。

第四，铲子和云依然是最稳的印钞机，像 Crusoe、VAST Data、Fireworks、Modal 这些算力基础设施和数据平台，
几乎家家都是十亿到二十亿美元级别的实打实营收，稳稳坐在两三百亿美金估值区。

第五，应用层分化极其残酷，虽然跑出了 Cognition（480 亿估值）、ElevenLabs（220 亿）、Perplexity（210 亿）和 Lovable（133 亿）这些明星，

但你会发现，应用层哪怕做到几亿甚至十亿美元收入，估值倍数也远不如底层模型和卖铲子的。

说实话，这张榜单对我们普通人择业和搞项目最有价值的启示就一句话，

别再去卷浅层的通用套壳应用了，现在的蛋糕要么在最底层的算力数据基建里，

要么就在类似法律 Harvey、医疗 OpenEvidence、机器人物理世界 Skild 这种扎得极深的垂直场景里。

Pushed this update a few days ago to provide more transparency around Callout Rewards for both the Degen and Diamond pots.

Our goal is to clear up some of the confusion around how your rewards are calculated and why they can change from day to day.

Your rewards depend on both your callouts and the size of the pots on each day. Days with higher trading activity across the app will have larger pots, and vice versa.

The pots are shared across callers, so your rewards also depend on how much of the daily rewards goes to everyone else. That means your Callout Rewards can fluctuate from day to day, even if your own callouts perform similarly.

Your trading style influences how your rewards are split between the two pots. For example, if you make more than 10 callouts per week, the share of your rewards coming from the Degen pot increases as you make more callouts.

This helps us direct the Diamond pot toward users who make just a few callouts per week, while using the Degen pot to reward more active callers. This doesn't impact the overall amount of rewards you receive - it only affects which pot your rewards come from!

Twin Islands Retreat & Fishing Charters is a remote hotel in Alaska run by Merri Laursen and her husband.

Food in mainland Alaska is very expensive, often a 30% premium to the rest of the US, but the couple often pays 2x or 3x above the average rate just to get it to the island.

If prices rise and the market settles in her favor, the position pays out, helping offset higher food expenses.

quoted_text:
Welcome to the Unending RSI Discourse Era! In addition to such niche up-and-comers as @dwarkesh_sp , @alexolegimas, and @lugaricano, I also have a new piece on this matter.

Rather than providing specific quantitative forecasts, I've tried to clarify the conceptual structure of "recursive self-improvement". Yudkowsky's original picture, downstream of his own model of intelligence, was of a mind becoming intelligent enough to improve its own cognitive machinery, then using its improved intelligence to make further improvements.

Although that particular model has been superseded by AI advances, I think we retain lots of its conceptual baggage — for instance, the expectation of a sudden FOOM with little warning or opportunity to intervene. I try to retain what's useful in Yudkowsky's framework, while reworking it to analyse the feedback mechanisms actually driving progress in deep learning.

I disaggregate RSI into its three components — recursiveness, self-directedness, and actual improvement — and show why the regimes where we have any two are quite different from a regime in which we have all three. The most distinctive feature of the current paradigm is that the "self" is not a single model improving itself; it's a broader AI development system whose outputs feed back into its own inputs.

The reason is that deep learning blurs Yudkowsky's distinction between cognitive algorithms and cognitive content: a neural network's knowledge and its reasoning procedures are learned together, and embodied in the same weights. Improving cognition, then, isn't a matter of rewriting those algorithms; it's about discovering better knowledge and procedures through training. So the machinery producing cognition is the training process itself, including algorithms, data, and compute.

This takes my earlier judgement that Carl Shulman won the FOOM debate by "getting the unit of recursion right", and develops it into a more systematic account of what he got right, and what feedback mechanisms drive AI progress.

The fact that the "self" is an AI development system, rather than either an individual seed AI or the entire global economy, explains why Yudkowsky's "returns on cognitive reinvestment" model is insufficient. We instead need a model where the system feeds back through two main channels: algorithmic progress and hardware spending. I argue that the reason AI progress has often been underestimated is that each of these raises the returns to the other — and since they've been doing so for years, there's no threshold where RSI "begins".

Instead, this structure explains why we keep seeing "one-time speed-ups"; under certain parameter assumptions, that trend of accelerating AI research can continue until it explodes, with kinks in the graph but no outright discontinuity. It doesn't even need to keep accelerating: even without "Sustained Strong Recursion", a sufficiently large speed-up that doesn't compound can still take AI beyond human intelligence.

Listening to Jane Street's panel discussion on whether the Singularity is coming, it's striking how thinkers with such different expectations as @Jsevillamol, @EgeErdil2, @RyanGreenblatt, and @DKokotajlo are all working from basically the same model — they just disagree about parameters. I think the structure I lay out explains why so many people trying to think seriously about AI progress often converge, especially when they try to write down a formal model.

However, the broader discourse is much looser. Fast-timelines people sometimes speak of RSI as a discrete, identifiable threshold that might suddenly be crossed. And sceptics deride the notion of an intelligence explosion altogether, taking the tight correlation between compute scaling and algorithmic progress to mean that compute is the sole driving force of progress, and so returns to cognitive labour must be low — neglecting the fact that those returns are the reason the compute scale-up was worthwhile in the first place.

Finally, I briefly consider the implications of the revised model for Yudkowskian concerns about alignment, loss of control, and concentration of power.

Read it! https://t.co/Y9l508apZT

text:
SpaceX–Tesla 合并预测

英文区和韩文区出现了好几个高质量帖子，记录一下笔记：

1) 披萨的大小是固定的，SpaceX 发行 $SPCX 新股来收购特斯拉

2) 核心：交换比例

特斯拉 1 股拿到的不是“$510”，而是“SPCX 3.64 股”

$TSLA 溢价越高， $SPCX 就会跌得越狠，最后是一个平衡

3) 特斯拉最可能的价位 $510~550, 对应的比例是 3.64-3.92 （按照 SpaceX 现在价格 140）

特斯拉市值略超 2 万亿美元，这是马斯克薪酬方案首阶段确定的线

溢价 28~38% 与华尔街预期相符， $SPCX 跌幅也在可承受范围内

马斯克目前拥有 SpaceX 约 48%、特斯拉约 20% 的股份

合并后马斯克占 33.6% 的股份，但有 70% 的投票权，还是牢牢控制公司（现在是 85% 投票权）

4) 合并带来的上涨空间有限

即使定在 $510（+28%）， $TSLA 实际价值也仅约 $452（+14%），因为 $SPCX 会因为增发跌 11%

5) 合并带来的上涨空间有限

交易完成还需 2~3 年，因此公告后股价会因合并失败风险及最终成交的时长而打折反映，现在类似 $384~407 的水平可能性很大

The articles backtracked from their original incendiary, and now clearly false, claims to something more like "Jensen did lawful things that powerful people didn't like". It still appears the original claims came from a single competing Big Tech lobbyist.

The reporting successfully disrupted corporate governance processes, with a running cost of $1.8 trillion in losses to American pension funds and shareholders.

Here's what I fear is being lost in these articles: The proper interface between government and private citizens and their corporations is rule of law. Laws are passed, and if wrongdoing as alleged, then there's due process: an investigation followed by facts and evidence presented in open court. Due process should happen here: let the facts come out whole, and not as a trickle of dubious claims.

Press takedowns full of sketchily sourced claims and backtracking narratives are not the way. It's what we see outside of the free world, and is no model for The United States of America.

In particular, if the Jensen takedown succeeds on the basis of these journalistic failings, which is not by any means certain as Sam Altman's case shows, then it foreshadows an economically and institutionally ruinous new playbook to be adopted with no end in sight.

Imagine a weekly stream of takedowns emerging from opportunistic alignments between corporate lobbyists and political interests which, given the new partisan split between the executive and legislative branches, will attack in all directions, undermining not only the US economy but American leadership in the world.

I hope cooler heads prevail this coming week as they did not on Thursday November 12. And I urge anyone who happened to oppose Jensen, open models, and the underlying trade policies in question, to recognize that this isn't a win for "team regulation". It's a change in the game from a transparent rules-based one to a sinister new form centered around politicans and lobbyists.

text:
Anthony, the "spy" story appears to be as fake as Russiagate. Here are the facts as I understand them.

(1) First, Alice Huang was at a company called Megaspeed[1], which everyone agrees bought Nvidia chips to sell to Southeast Asian companies called neoclouds. This is in itself completely legal under US law.

(2) However, some both inside and outside the admin didn't like this. They want to block Chinese nationals from accessing cloud services with Nvidia GPUs even if those servers are located outside China. Fine, but the so-called Remote Access Security Act (RASA) to block this has passed the House but not the Senate, and is not law[2].

(3) Singapore's government also looked into this when Alice Huang was on their soil[3] and didn't find any evidence that Megaspeed was actually selling chips to China illegally — let alone that she was a "Chinese spy." They did give her an entry ban, but that's like a visa denial.

(4) The related point is that it's not actually illegal to sell Nvidia chips to China! Since the Biden admin, there has been a complex and constantly-shifting set of export restrictions on chips. As of right now, Nvidia is allowed to sell H200s[4] to China, and indeed has designed these to comply with applicable law.

(5) But you know what...China actually also doesn't want Nvidia chips in China [5,6], because they want to build up their homegrown chip industry. The Nvidia chips are so good that China doesn't want to remain dependent on American chips, or vulnerable to possible US backdoors.

(6) The broader point is that this is an argument between nationalists and capitalists. Nationalists argue that US companies shouldn't even get close to selling to China, and shouldn't even be selling to neoclouds, even if it's "technically" legal. Capitalists argue that it's impossible for American companies to dominate world markets without, you know, being allowed to dominate world markets by actually competing in them. And that it's one thing to restrict physical sales to China, and quite another to require proof-of-citizenship for every single cloud access.

(7) Here's the thing: it doesn't make sense for one of the (few!) industries where America has a trade surplus with China to be summarily cut off, if you're worried about trade surpluses. It doesn't make sense to remove your number one AI CEO, if you want to be number one in AI. And it truly doesn't make sense to do to Jensen Huang what the communists did to Jack Ma[7], if your goal is fighting communism.

(8) So, to summarize: there's no proof of spying, as Blanche at DOJ has admitted[8], which rebuts your FBI/DOJ points. The Wachtell investigation you raise is just an in-house thing[9] ordered by the Nvidia board. And so all that's left is some affairs, which society has agreed is not disqualifying, given the realities of both Clinton and Trump.

In short: do you want a communist society like China, where Jack Ma's company can be stolen from him overnight on false pretenses? Or do you want some semblance of rule of law? If so, you should support the restoration of Jensen Huang to the company he built.

Citations follow in the next tweet.

text:
Amber，又一个爆雷的公司？

昨晚，一份关于 Amber 的 11 页举报信在微信群里疯传。

举报人自称是 Amber 前高管，并声称已经将相关材料提交给中央纪委、香港廉政公署、香港证监会及香港警方。

这份举报信的内容相当劲爆，涉及联合创始人涉嫌挪用客户资金、管理层利益输送、客户入金账户异常，以及 Amber Premium 的 Fixed Earn 产品存在资金运作风险等问题。

需要说明的是，目前这些内容主要来自举报人的单方面陈述，相关指控尚未得到独立证实。笔者结合举报信和 Amber 已披露的公开资料，按照问题的重要性，梳理了以下几个值得关注的疑问。

1、最严重的一项指控，究竟是否真实？

根据举报信，Amber 联合创始人 Tony He 曾挪用千万美元客户资金，在火币进行个人交易，最终导致相关账户被冻结。

如果这一指控属实，问题就不只是内部管理失当，而是涉及客户资产安全的重大事件。

但目前举报信中的说法，还需要交易记录、资金流向、账户归属以及相关调查结果来验证。

Amber 需要回答：客户资金是否曾被挪用于未经授权的个人交易？如果发生过，涉及多少资金？

2、Amber 的创始团队，究竟发生了什么？

根据举报信，Amber 最初有 6 位联合创始人，其中 1 人已经离世，另有 3 人离开，目前只剩下 2 位。

如果举报信所述属实，Amber 的创始团队为何出现如此大规模的人员变动？六位联合创始人目前的实际情况、股权变化，以及核心管理层离职的真实原因是什么？

3、沈波是否真的在 Amber 存放了 3 亿美元？

举报信声称，Amber 股东沈波有约 3 亿美元资金存放在 Amber，并且曾经出售部分股权。

这件事至少需要拆成两个问题：

第一，沈波是否真的在 Amber 存放了 3 亿美元？这笔资金究竟属于个人资产、客户托管资产，还是其他形式的投资或借贷？

第二，如果这笔资金确实存在，沈波是否有权随时提取？如果集中提取，是否会对 Amber 的流动性造成重大影响？

需要强调的是，目前没有公开证据能够证实这 3 亿美元的说法，更不能据此推断沈波提款就会导致 Amber 破产。

4、Amber 是否真的存在爆雷风险？

先看公开财务数据。

截至 2026 年 6 月底，Amber International 的公开财报显示，公司总资产约 2.98 亿美元，总负债约 1.95 亿美元，仍然拥有正的股东权益。但与此同时，2026 年上半年，公司营收同比下降约 28%，并由盈利转为亏损。

另一个值得关注的数据是：截至 2026 年 6 月底，公司的加密资产贷款应收款约为 5,779 万美元，较 2025 年底增长约 37%。

根据财报披露，这些贷款来自集团认购关联方数字资产平台的 Earn 产品，属于无抵押贷款，期限从 2 天到 365 天不等。截至报告期末，公司没有为这部分贷款计提信用损失准备。

这并不能证明客户资金被挪用，也不能直接说明公司存在偿付危机，但它确实引出了一个重要问题：Amber 的资金究竟流向了哪里？相关借款方是谁？如果借款方无法按期偿还，公司是否有足够的流动性应对客户赎回？

5、Amber 是否拥有香港、新加坡和迪拜三地牌照？

这也是一个容易被混淆的问题。三个地区的牌照性质并不相同。

香港：尚未取得正式 VATP 牌照。

Amber 旗下 Whalefin Markets Limited 曾于 2024 年向香港证监会申请虚拟资产交易平台牌照，并在过渡安排下被视为获发牌申请人。

但这不等于正式获牌。2026 年 10 月，Amber International 公告称，Whalefin 将不再推进相关牌照申请，并计划撤回申请；相关收购安排也不再推进。

新加坡：拥有 MPI 牌照。

持牌主体是 Amber 旗下的 Sparrow Tech Private Limited，获新加坡金融管理局（MAS）颁发 Major Payment Institution（主要支付机构）牌照，获准提供数字支付代币服务（DPT Services）。

迪拜：拥有 VASP 牌照。

持牌主体是 Amber Premium FZE。迪拜虚拟资产监管局（VARA）于 2026 年 4 月 2 日正式向其发放牌照，允许其开展虚拟资产经纪交易、资产管理与投资、借贷服务。不过，牌照限定服务机构投资者和合格投资者。

所以，更准确地说，Amber 已在新加坡和迪拜取得相关数字资产业务牌照，但并未取得香港 VATP 牌照。

一份举报信，不足以证明 Amber 即将爆雷。

但是，这份举报信已经在社交媒体上广泛传播。对于一家管理客户数字资产、提供收益产品的公司而言，Amber 的确需要正面回答几个关键问题：

客户资金是否曾被挪用？客户资产是否实现独立托管？用户购买 Fixed Earn 产品后，钱究竟被拿去做了什么？举报信中提到的关联方资金往来，以及与北京公职人员有关的数百万美元资产，究竟是否属实？

这些问题，Amber 都应该给出明确的解释。

2025-07-16：当事人@xxxkeym 从冷钱包 3NcBhq…Lnx3u 向 Gate 充值 15 BTC（哈希 885f3afa…）

2025-07-20：Gate 发来账户审查邮件，只点名这一笔，要求说明资金来源

2025-10-28：印度安德拉邦 CID 来信，称被骗的 BTC 追到了该账户，点名的仍是同一笔哈希

2026-03-06：案件提交印度法院

2026-10-30：贡土尔特别法院裁定，4 个 Gate 账户的全部资产换成 USDT，转给报案人

2026-11-12：当事人收到 Gate 通知，才知道裁定已经下来

而当事人这笔 15 BTC 充值由三个部分组成。主体 14.99999322 BTC 于 2023-01-09 进入该钱包，此后两年半一动未动，直到 2025-07-16 才充入 Gate。印度 CID 的来信自己也写明，这个钱包一直持有来自 OKX 的资金。

另一个是 3,373 聪的找零，上溯同样是 2023-01-09 从币安热钱包提出的一笔 85 BTC。

唯一一笔 2023 年之后进入的外部资金只有 600 聪，来自仿冒地址 3NcoFs…Pnx3u，首三位和尾四位与当事人地址相同。这个仿冒地址来自 2024 年 11 月一笔 1,401 个输出的批量投毒交易，属于典型的地址投毒粉尘，充值时被钱包一并花了出去。

同一钱包在 7 月 11 日和 15 日还先后向币安充值约 20 BTC。当事人称，他的币安和 OKX 账户至今没有被冻结。

案件 2025 年立案，而这笔充值的主体资金 2023 年初就已到位。除非受害人早在 2023 年以前就已被骗，或者警方掌握站内划转、场外交易等尚未公开的证据，否则这笔钱很难定性为赃款。

Gate 是这起事件里唯一同时掌握资产、用户资料和执法文书的一方。当事人追问了 16 个月，得到的只有一句不便透露。在法律允许的范围内，我们认为 @Gate 至少应当说清五件事：

1、冻结的触发点：2025 年 7 月 20 日的冻结，发生在当事人收到印度警方来信之前。它是 Gate 自己的风控报警，还是当时已经收到执法请求？如果是风控报警，命中的是哪一笔输入。

2、执法文书本身：向当事人本人提供冻结令、调证函和法院裁定的完整副本，并告知 Gate 向印度警方提供了哪些用户资料。

3、冻结范围：被点名的只有 15 BTC 一笔充值，为什么冻结的是整个账户。

4、划扣口径：按哪一天的价格换成 USDT、划扣多少、剩余资产如何处理。

5、执行时间表：何时执行划转，是否给当事人留出上诉和申请暂缓执行的时间。

配合合法的执法和司法要求，是交易所的义务，这本身不是过错。当事人帖中提到的内外勾结，目前没有证据支持。

但 Gate 是资产的托管方，而不只是传达指令的中间人。我们认为它至少有三项审慎义务

1、执行划扣前，核对执法方的追踪依据与链上记录是否对得上。链上记录 Gate 自己就能查。

2、用户提交的反证，应当正式转交执法方和法院，而不是把用户推给印度方面自己去沟通。

3、在不违反保密要求的前提下，及时告知用户冻结依据、资料移交和裁定内容。这次当事人是在裁定作出 13 天后，才从 Gate 的邮件里得知的。

如果最终证明这 15 BTC 是被错认的赃款，而 Gate 在未核对、未告知的情况下就执行了划扣，那么用户的损失，很难只算在印度警方头上。

交易所配合执法是底线，让用户看得见自己为什么被冻、被划扣，也是底线。

From an NVIDIA employee: 

“To the Board,

I have worked at NVIDIA for nearly 18 years, and I feel compelled to share something personal during this extraordinarily difficult moment.

I am not writing to comment on the circumstances or to presume anything about the process the Board must undertake. I simply hope you will consider the perspective of someone who has had the privilege of working closely with Jensen for almost two decades—and who has seen firsthand the kind of leader and human being he has been to so many employees.

I first worked with Jensen in 2009 after I joined the company, when we went through 37 versions of GeForce posters for Chinese retail, and later through countless gaming events and the early China and Asia GTCs. He could challenge me quite publicly at times, but I always valued his candor, his teaching, and especially the conversations we had after those events.

One conversation in particular has stayed with me for nearly 17 years.

It was during a post-management QBR dinner in Hong Kong early 2010, I asked Jensen about something I had heard from an older employee: that during the difficult layoffs of 2008, he had personally called engineers who were being laid off and later reached out to many of them individually.

He told me a story about an elderly man he once met in a small grocery shop in Hong Kong. The man had worked there his entire life. Jensen asked him why he had never looked for another job. The man answered, “Because my boss took care of me in the rainy days.”

Jensen told me that sentence stayed with him. When he told me the story his glasses were covered by mists from his wet eyes. He promised himself that he would never forget the people who had entrusted their lives and careers to him. No matter how much pressure he faced, employees were family, and he wanted to be the person who would take care of them in the rainy days.

He kept that promise.

Through COVID, the Russia-Ukraine war, and countless other uncertain moments, I repeatedly heard him reassure employees, in one form or another: “I got you.”

Throughout the years, he has also put in countless personal efforts to make us feel at home. He created the quarterly “Global Free Days” and launched policies to support employees building their families via IVF and adoption, with the program fully funded by the company. From sending a soft blue blanket to congratulate me on my son’s birth, to visiting a member of my team in the hospital during Computex, he did everything he could to ensure we always felt cared for and supported, no matter the circumstances.

Many of us privately called him “Daddy Huang”—not as a joke, but with genuine affection, gratitude and admiration.

That was Jensen’s magic.

He didn’t just build technology. He created policies that changed people’s lives, and a company culture that made us so passionate about NVIDIA.

Stand behind Jensen Huang is a family, thousands of employees whose lives he has touched, and generations of people who have benefited from his leadership and his humanity.

I am only one employee, and I do not pretend that my voice can change the outcome of anything. But after nearly 18 years here, I could not remain silent without sharing what I have personally witnessed.

Please remember the extraordinary amount of humanity, kindness and opportunity that Jensen and his family have seeded around the world.

Please remember the people whose lives he has changed—not just through NVIDIA’s technology, but through his personal decisions, his empathy, and the culture he created.

And please remember that many of us are incredibly proud of him.

Whatever difficult decisions lie ahead, I hope the Board will approach them with both the rigor required of its fiduciary responsibility and the humanity deserved by a person who has spent so much of his life taking care of others in their rainy days.

With deepest respect,

A grateful NVIDIA employee of nearly 18 years”

text:
Guardians in the Shadows: Conservation Ethics, Coexistence, and the True Nature of the Kumiho

For centuries, folklore has cast the Kumiho—the nine-tailed fox—in the shadow of fear, portraying a mystical species as monsters to be hunted rather than understood. Yet, when we look past human prejudice, a very different truth emerges. The Kumiho are not agents of destruction; they are guardians of peace, deeply intertwined with the preservation of both humanity and the natural world. In many ways, the misconception surrounding the Kumiho mirrors humanity’s greatest ecological flaw: anthropocentrism, the belief that human beings are the central or most important entity in the universe.
Anthropocentrism is the true enemy of coexistence. Throughout Earth’s history, life has endured five major extinction events, and today, human-driven habitat destruction and climate change threaten to push us into a sixth. Too often, humanity fears what it does not understand, causing irreversible harm to species and ecosystems that cannot speak for themselves. Just because humans possess the power to destroy does not grant us the moral right to decide the fate of other living beings based on their perceived worth to us. True environmental ethics demands that we protect biodiversity not because it serves us, but because every form of life has an inherent right to exist.
This philosophy is embodied by White Fox, a Kumiho who stands as a silent protector in the shadows. Carrying the heavy burden of being the last of her kind, she operates with unwavering loyalty, quiet strength, and a fierce dedication to defending a world that largely misunderstands her nature. Her solitude is a feeling many people deeply resonate with—myself included. Growing up, I knew the weight of feeling out of place, enduring the upheaval of my parents' divorce at thirteen, and losing my childhood home in Arizona. Pain and isolation can easily dictate the course of a person's life, yet White Fox’s resilience inspired me to channel that solitude into purpose, guardianship, and service.
Driven by her example of vigilance and loyalty, I spent eight summers working as a lifeguard for the City of Phoenix. Mastering basic first aid, CPR, and water rescues taught me that protecting others requires constant awareness, trust, and a willingness to step forward when lives are on the line. That same drive to protect the vulnerable led me to pursue a degree in Conservation Ecology at Arizona State University. Where lifeguarding taught me to safeguard human lives, conservation ecology has given me the tools to advocate for the natural world—to fight against extinction, champion biodiversity, and challenge the anthropocentric mindset that threatens fragile ecosystems.
If the Kumiho are still out there in the hidden corners of the world, they will not be forgotten, nor will they be left to face humanity's fear alone. Conservationists, scientists, and compassionate individuals will continue to stand against the tide of extinction, doing everything possible to understand, appreciate, and protect the voiceless. By honoring the values of loyalty, trust, and ecological stewardship that White Fox represents, we ensure that the spirit of the Kumiho lives on—not as a myth of fear, but as a lasting symbol of harmony between humanity and the wild. 

Ricardo Carpena

P.S. Special shoutout to Jennifer Sun Bell for bringing her to life! Thank you for inspiring me!

text:
From an NVIDIA employee: 

“To the Board,

I have worked at NVIDIA for nearly 18 years, and I feel compelled to share something personal during this extraordinarily difficult moment.

I am not writing to comment on the circumstances or to presume anything about the process the Board must undertake. I simply hope you will consider the perspective of someone who has had the privilege of working closely with Jensen for almost two decades—and who has seen firsthand the kind of leader and human being he has been to so many employees.

I first worked with Jensen in 2009 after I joined the company, when we went through 37 versions of GeForce posters for Chinese retail, and later through countless gaming events and the early China and Asia GTCs. He could challenge me quite publicly at times, but I always valued his candor, his teaching, and especially the conversations we had after those events.

One conversation in particular has stayed with me for nearly 17 years.

It was during a post-management QBR dinner in Hong Kong early 2010, I asked Jensen about something I had heard from an older employee: that during the difficult layoffs of 2008, he had personally called engineers who were being laid off and later reached out to many of them individually.

He told me a story about an elderly man he once met in a small grocery shop in Hong Kong. The man had worked there his entire life. Jensen asked him why he had never looked for another job. The man answered, “Because my boss took care of me in the rainy days.”

Jensen told me that sentence stayed with him. When he told me the story his glasses were covered by mists from his wet eyes. He promised himself that he would never forget the people who had entrusted their lives and careers to him. No matter how much pressure he faced, employees were family, and he wanted to be the person who would take care of them in the rainy days.

He kept that promise.

Through COVID, the Russia-Ukraine war, and countless other uncertain moments, I repeatedly heard him reassure employees, in one form or another: “I got you.”

Throughout the years, he has also put in countless personal efforts to make us feel at home. He created the quarterly “Global Free Days” and launched policies to support employees building their families via IVF and adoption, with the program fully funded by the company. From sending a soft blue blanket to congratulate me on my son’s birth, to visiting a member of my team in the hospital during Computex, he did everything he could to ensure we always felt cared for and supported, no matter the circumstances.

Many of us privately called him “Daddy Huang”—not as a joke, but with genuine affection, gratitude and admiration.

That was Jensen’s magic.

He didn’t just build technology. He created policies that changed people’s lives, and a company culture that made us so passionate about NVIDIA.

Stand behind Jensen Huang is a family, thousands of employees whose lives he has touched, and generations of people who have benefited from his leadership and his humanity.

I am only one employee, and I do not pretend that my voice can change the outcome of anything. But after nearly 18 years here, I could not remain silent without sharing what I have personally witnessed.

Please remember the extraordinary amount of humanity, kindness and opportunity that Jensen and his family have seeded around the world.

Please remember the people whose lives he has changed—not just through NVIDIA’s technology, but through his personal decisions, his empathy, and the culture he created.

And please remember that many of us are incredibly proud of him.

Whatever difficult decisions lie ahead, I hope the Board will approach them with both the rigor required of its fiduciary responsibility and the humanity deserved by a person who has spent so much of his life taking care of others in their rainy days.

With deepest respect,

A grateful NVIDIA employee of nearly 18 years”

text:
Don't see enough people mentioning the wealth effect when talking about inflation and the state of consumer spending

The stock market is sitting at a record 28.8% of total household assets. In 2025, stocks took over real estate as the largest portion of people's net worth in America

The wealth effect is a common phenomenon where people tend to spend more when the stock market is going up. The average investor sees their net worth going up and automatically increases spending. This, in turn, boosts the overall economy and earnings, creating a circular effect on both

However, these things also work just as true in reverse. For example, the Japanese stock market and economy experienced a similar effect during the 1980s when it was roaring higher

In fact, for a brief moment in 1989, the Japanese stock market value was actually higher than the entire US market combined. Then the country entered into the "lost decade" during the 1990s following a massive correction.

Ever since then, consumer spending has remained muted within the country, even as their central bank reduced interest rates towards zero. 

Not making a prediction of whether the same will happen with the US market or not. However, it is important to be aware that the same effect that has led to a booming market in the US could unwind just as easily.

Stock market downturn -> less consumer spending -> lower earnings -> further downturn

What makes it even worse is that the wealth is heavily concentrated towards the top in America, who are simultaneously the biggest spenders and own most of the stock market. These would be the first people to cut spending in a market downturn.

text:
Anthony, the "spy" story appears to be as fake as Russiagate. Here are the facts as I understand them.

(1) First, Alice Huang was at a company called Megaspeed[1], which everyone agrees bought Nvidia chips to sell to Southeast Asian companies called neoclouds. This is in itself completely legal under US law.

(2) However, some both inside and outside the admin didn't like this. They want to block Chinese nationals from accessing cloud services with Nvidia GPUs even if those servers are located outside China. Fine, but the so-called Remote Access Security Act (RASA) to block this has passed the House but not the Senate, and is not law[2].

(3) Singapore's government also looked into this when Alice Huang was on their soil[3] and didn't find any evidence that Megaspeed was actually selling chips to China illegally — let alone that she was a "Chinese spy." They did give her an entry ban, but that's like a visa denial.

(4) The related point is that it's not actually illegal to sell Nvidia chips to China! Since the Biden admin, there has been a complex and constantly-shifting set of export restrictions on chips. As of right now, Nvidia is allowed to sell H200s[4] to China, and indeed has designed these to comply with applicable law.

(5) But you know what...China actually also doesn't want Nvidia chips in China [5,6], because they want to build up their homegrown chip industry. The Nvidia chips are so good that China doesn't want to remain dependent on American chips, or vulnerable to possible US backdoors.

(6) The broader point is that this is an argument between nationalists and capitalists. Nationalists argue that US companies shouldn't even get close to selling to China, and shouldn't even be selling to neoclouds, even if it's "technically" legal. Capitalists argue that it's impossible for American companies to dominate world markets without, you know, being allowed to dominate world markets by actually competing in them. And that it's one thing to restrict physical sales to China, and quite another to require proof-of-citizenship for every single cloud access.

(7) Here's the thing: it doesn't make sense for one of the (few!) industries where America has a trade surplus with China to be summarily cut off, if you're worried about trade surpluses. It doesn't make sense to remove your number one AI CEO, if you want to be number one in AI. And it truly doesn't make sense to do to Jensen Huang what the communists did to Jack Ma[7], if your goal is fighting communism.

(8) So, to summarize: there's no proof of spying, as Blanche at DOJ has admitted[8], which rebuts your FBI/DOJ points. The Wachtell investigation you raise is just an in-house thing[9] ordered by the Nvidia board. And so all that's left is some affairs, which society has agreed is not disqualifying, given the realities of both Clinton and Trump.

In short: do you want a communist society like China, where Jack Ma's company can be stolen from him overnight on false pretenses? Or do you want some semblance of rule of law? If so, you should support the restoration of Jensen Huang to the company he built.

Citations follow in the next tweet.

quoted_text:
Looking for quantum processes that can be proven to work in a living organism: an update

My goal is to find quantum processes that are proven to work in a living organism, and to understand in what form they can exist inside a warm, noisy cell.

One of the strongest candidates is the magnetic compass of migratory birds. In the leading explanation, light falling on cryptochrome 4, a protein in the bird's eye, leaves it with two unpaired electrons that act like tiny magnets, and the Earth's field changes how they turn relative to each other and so how the chemical reaction ends. The evidence fits: the compass needs light, weak radio noise disrupts it, and cryptochrome 4 responds to magnetic fields in the lab. The full chain from this protein to the bird's behavior is still unproven.

Proof has to come from experiments, and my part is to say what a living bird should show if the process is real.

This compass reads the axis of the field and treats both its ends alike, so my model predicts that the bird's brain gets a map where each direction is glued to its opposite. Proteins are "handed", like left and right gloves, and an electron passing through a handed molecule prefers one spin direction. In 2021 Luo and Hore predicted that this effect, called CISS, could let the compass tell north from south. It can take several forms, and I ask which survive in the real protein and whether a brain recording could see the difference they create.

I test this in pre-registered computer simulations, publishing the plan and code before each run and every number and correction after it. Since I last wrote about this five days ago, I have run three more studies, the latest on the real atomic structure of the pigeon's cryptochrome 4, with much of the physics still simplified.

What my model shows:
• With the real geometry of the protein, one form of the effect gives a far stronger north–south difference than my previous study found, because the two electron magnets act on each other. • A test on recordings from bird neurons would clearly see such a difference if the effect is strong and the proteins in the eye point the same way. • At the strength measured so far, in an isolated frog protein, whether the test sees it depends on how the effect acts and how fast the reaction runs, both unknown in a living bird. • The north–south signal created by the fragile quantum state of the two electrons partly survives the jostling of a warm protein: more than half of it remains at the lower noise estimates, and usually less at the upper ones. • A similar difference can also appear without this effect, when the electron jumps between two sites in the protein. This surprising result needs an independent check, and if it holds, experiments will need a control for it. • Whether the difference can change the shape of the brain's map is still open.
The first round of calculations is done. Next I will build a more realistic model of the protein and connect with three research labs. If a bird's brain shows the predicted signal, and it depends on light, breaks down under weak radio noise and vanishes in birds without cryptochrome 4, that would be strong evidence that a quantum process shapes what a living brain receives. If it persists in darkness or without cryptochrome 4, my model has the wrong source. If no north–south difference appears, the chiral effect is weak or cancels itself out, or the proteins in the eye are poorly aligned.

The far end of the path is the flock, and there I have only a hypothesis. Starlings coordinate mainly by watching their neighbors, and their flocks seem to work near a critical point, where a weak shared nudge spreads fast through the group; a compass that feels the field could add such a nudge.

text:
When you figure out why “just patch” is shitty advice to give to any significant sized company you’ll also know why AI will benefit attackers far more than defenders. 

In bigger orgs the problem is not usually a lack of tech, or models, or skills on the security team. 

It’s that there is a level of organizational friction at every company, like a friction coefficient, that stops security orgs from being able to do many things they want. 

We’ve needed asset management for decades. We’ve needed mappings between code and apps and servers and dev teams and developers forever. 

Very few have these. 

The tech exists. The problem is the org is not set up to build and maintain these types of systems continuously. The company’s structure itself, built around opaque silos, and divergent goals, and insanely lossy and inefficient communication across the company, it all creates a very high friction coefficient for basically any fast improvements. 

The way to fix security is to lower this friction coefficient inside companies. 

It sucks to hear, but we’re at the point of security’s biggest issue being the company itself. The org structure. The old way of managing teams and goals and work. 

An AI-native org is the only way to get organizational friction down to a level that can compete with these new attacks and attackers. 

The bad news is this is big. And it’ll be difficult for a lot of people to adjust to. And a lot of people currently working there won’t be needed in the new model. The good news is many still will, and even more could be needed once the efficiency of the new organization kicks in. This isn’t just going to help addition; it’ll help the entire business move faster. 

Going into 2027, I believe this model is about to move from ideal and experimental to … essential. Both for surviving cyber-wise, and as a company facing increased and up-leveled competition.

text:
不知道为什么这些 personal agent 一个个都给每个用户分了个虚拟机沙盒，一个云端沙盒一个月几十美金的成本。

有人跟我说，不用虚拟机做沙盒，agent 在哪运行？浏览器怎么访问网页？用户上传的文件放到哪？agent 怎么执行 skill 里面的命令？agent 生成的代码怎么安全执行？

我瞬间感觉这么多年的系统都白做了。我做第一个 agent 的时候，一个基本假设就是一个 Go 服务里面支持多个并发用户，从来没想过一个用户能独占一个进程，更没想到有些 agent 竟然敢把 API key 放在沙盒里面。

浏览器我只用过无头浏览器，没想过用虚拟机这么奢侈的东西。用户上传的文件我只能想到 GCS 或者 Google Drive 这样的虚拟文件系统，没想到其他 agent 搞了个真的文件系统。

最近我用 Claude Code，一个 session 跑了几天之后 agent 就占了 5GB 的物理内存，经常 CPU 占用 100%，有时候还会卡死。

这些兄弟们大概是把 OpenClaw 或者 Codex 或者 Deepseek Harness 换了个壳子，装进虚拟机，就算是 personal agent 了。

只能说是做 LLM 和 agent 的兄弟们都太有钱了，动不动几百万年薪，不像我们做系统的整天为了几微秒延迟、几 KB 内存天天扣扣搜搜的。

text:
18 years. 1,769 sessions. The Six Books of Hadith, completed.

My Shaykh, Shaykh Aḥmad Maḥmūd Muḥammad (Shaykh Aḥmad Yare), ḥafiẓahullāh, has finished teaching the Kutub al-Sittah, also known as the Ummahāt al-Sittah: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, Sunan Abī Dāwūd, Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī, Sunan al-Nasāʾī and Sunan Ibn Mājah.

I remember when he began. The first of the six books he started with was Sunan Abī Dāwūd. I was living in Hackney, East London, at the time, and the Shaykh came to stay with me for a while. I remember him going through the book, and I asked him: "Shaykh, which sharḥ are you relying on? Which shurūḥāt of Sunan Abī Dāwūd are you using?" He explained the different shurūḥāt to me and the fawāʾid in each one.

That was eighteen years ago. The Shaykh's beard was still black back then. He was young, and he's still young. But to spend all those years serving the words and Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ, is a remarkable thing.
It took him 1,769 scholarly sessions. He sat and explained these books in detail, looking at the ahadith from many angles. He even wrote research papers on many of them, which he made available to students as PDFs. It ended with the reading of the final hadith of Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim.
That is only the hadith. He has also given full explanations (shurūḥāt) of works in ʿaqīdah, fiqh, uṣūl al-fiqh and muṣṭalaḥ al-ḥadīth. On top of that are his lectures, reminders and series on many topics.

Why am I mentioning this?

Because the English-speaking world badly needs people who will stand up and serve the Ummah like this. We need people who teach beneficial knowledge so that others grow in righteous action, rather than keeping people busy with what doesn't benefit them and won't bring them closer to Allah Taʿālā.

Right now, we are in dire need of these books being explained in English.
My brothers and sisters, we need to take a page out of the book of this great scholar and the many scholars like him.

May Allah accept it from him, put barakah in his time and knowledge, and raise up people who will do the same for this Ummah. Āmīn.

董事会还在考虑让不让黄仁勋回来，硅谷已经有人开始研究怎么罢免董事会了。

Balaji 提出，只要黄仁勋亲自发一条推文，公开表示自己想回来，整个局面就会迅速动起来。

他甚至翻出了英伟达的公司章程，找到了股东反击的法律路径。

根据英伟达章程，连续持股至少一年、合计拥有公司 15% 投票权的股东，可以要求召开特别股东大会，推动包括董事罢免在内的议案。不过，15% 只是召集会议的门槛，真正罢免董事仍需要达到法定投票比例。

这就有意思了。

过去几天，从马斯克到多位科技公司创始人，再到 Altimeter、Atreides 等机构投资人，支持黄仁勋的声音不断扩大。如今 FT 又披露，支持者正在组织「作战室」，试图游说董事会并争取白宫支持。

但 Balaji 显然想把事情再往前推一步，与其请求董事会让黄仁勋回来，不如让股东来决定这些董事还能不能留下。

董事会有权决定 CEO 的去留，但董事会本身同样需要对股东负责。尤其当一家公司的价值与创始人深度绑定时，董事会如果不能充分解释自己的决定，就很难指望投资者无限期地保持沉默。

当然，黄仁勋本人还没有公开宣布要复职，正式的股东行动也远未启动。

但如果他真的发出那条推文，英伟达的继任者之争，恐怕就要变成一场董事会控制权之争了。

原本要被决定命运的人，可能反过来决定那些决策者的命运。

text:
Claude Code 其实自带两个给配置做体检的命令，如果你正在用 Fable 5.2，非常建议用这两个命令跑一遍。

1. 「/doctor prompt-audit」会把整套配置扫一遍，包括 CLAUDE.md、AGENTS.md、skills、subagents 和 commands，找出那些为旧模型写的、已经过时或者互相矛盾的指令。需要 Claude Code v2.1.283 以上，也可以在后面加路径，只查某个文件或目录。直接跑「/doctor」查的是安装和权限，是另一回事。

2. 「/claude-api prompt-audit [skill名]」用的是官方 claude-api skill，随 Claude Code 自带，适合对单个 skill 或 prompt 做深入检查。它会给一份标了文件和行号的报告，写清楚为什么过时、有多大把握，再附一份修改 diff。

两个命令都只给建议，你确认之后才会改文件，可以放心跑。Peter 截图里有 65 个自建 skill 加 60 个插件 skill，审查拆给 5 个 reviewer 并行跑。

skill 攒多了，很多还是给旧模型写的，到新模型上可能已经多余，甚至起反作用。每次升级模型后跑一遍，挺值得养成习惯。

📎 https://t.co/mGH68dV3gX

text:
I had ChatGPT translate the 'Celestial Battle' of Nurenberg in 1561 and it's even wilder that you could imagine. 

The text is written in Early New High German. Here is a modern English translation of its account, with some archaic phrasing simplified for readability.
English translation
A very terrifying spectacle appeared in the sky at sunrise over Nuremberg, on April 14, 1561
On the morning of April 14, 1561, between four and five o'clock, a dreadful apparition appeared on the sun, and then was seen over Nuremberg, in the city, before the gates, and in the countryside, by many men and women.

First, there appeared in the middle of the sun two blood-red semicircular arcs, just like the moon in its last quarter. In the sun, above and below and on both sides, the color was blood-red, and there stood a round ball of partly dull, partly black iron color.

Likewise, there appeared on both sides, and as a ring around the sun, blood-red spheres and other spheres in great numbers, some in rows of three, others in rows of four, and some standing alone.

Between these spheres, there were visible several blood-red crosses, and between these crosses there were blood-red streaks. In the background were two great rods, one on the right and one on the left, and within the small and large rods were three, four, or more spheres.

All these objects began to fight among themselves.

First, the spheres in the sun flew out toward those standing on both sides. Then the spheres standing outside the sun, in the small and large rods, flew into the sun.

The spheres flew back and forth among one another and fought violently for over an hour.

When the conflict in and around the sun had been at its most intense, the objects became exhausted to such an extent that they all fell from the sun down toward the earth, as though they were burning.

They then disappeared on the ground in an immense cloud of smoke.

After all this, something resembling a black spear, very long and thick, was seen. Its shaft pointed toward the east and its tip toward the west.

What such signs mean, God alone knows.

Although we have seen many kinds of signs in the heavens, sent to us by Almighty God to bring us to repentance, we remain, unfortunately, so ungrateful that we despise such high signs and miracles of God.

Or we speak of them mockingly and cast them to the wind, so that God may send us a terrible punishment for our ingratitude.

The God-fearing will by no means disregard these signs, but will take them to heart as a warning from their merciful Father in heaven, reform their lives, and faithfully pray to God that He may turn away His wrath and the punishment we deserve.

May He grant us, for a time, a life here on earth and afterward eternal life in heaven.

May God help us all. Amen.

By Hans Glaser, letter painter of Nuremberg.

quoted_text:
Google TPU update: New OpenAI and Anthropic orders extend shipment visibility to 2029; v10 lineup overhauled (now Quillfish); MediaTek and Broadcom lead as the top suppliers to watch

Key takeaways from my latest industry survey and research conclusions:

1. Order visibility and shipment plans:
Strong new orders from OpenAI and Anthropic have extended Google TPU shipment visibility to 2029, ahead of Nvidia GPUs and other AI ASICs (mostly 4Q27–2Q28).

(1) From 2028, v9 will become the mainstay of Google’s own compute buildout, so v8-series orders (8t / 8i or their design variants) can be viewed as coming from OpenAI and Anthropic.

(2) Combined 2028–2029 demand: about 12M units for OpenAI (8t, designed by MediaTek) and about 14M for Anthropic (8i, designed by Broadcom), with both growing year over year. OpenAI buys outright, while Anthropic uses a mix of leasing and outright purchases.

(3) Given supply chain constraints, more reasonable TPU shipment estimates for 2027–2029 are 8–9M, 14–15M, and 16–18M units, respectively. The market broadly expects AI capex to peak in 2028, yet this plan shows TPU shipments still growing in 2029, driven by direct orders from AI service leaders OpenAI and Anthropic.

2. v10 lineup and supply chain changes:
v10 has changed from Icefish and Merope / Bladerunner to Quillfish, with mass production expected in 2029. MediaTek has won the design service order.

(1) Icefish is now v11, with mass production expected in 2030 and the design service order also going to MediaTek. Merope has lower visibility: no supplier has been chosen, and it may be canceled.

(2) MediaTek will be the sole supplier for v9 (Humufish & Triggerfish) and v10 (Quillfish), accounting for about 45–50%, 50–55%, and 55–60% of total TPU supply in 2027–2029, respectively. TPU’s contribution to its revenue and profit should rise each year.

(3) From v9 onward, all new TPUs use Intel’s EMIB-T advanced packaging. Given limited initial production capacity, the v8 series should remain the bulk of TPU shipments through 2029. v8 is expected to be the main source of TPU profit growth for MediaTek and Broadcom over the next few years, thanks to significant accumulated learning-curve benefits and the fact that both handle procurement of key components and materials.

3. Market attention and supplier outlook:
Recent events should raise and sustain market attention on Google TPU, with key design service providers MediaTek and Broadcom likely to be the supply chain’s top focus.

(1) Uncertainty over Nvidia’s CEO succession helps Google in discussing post-2028 long-term plans with customers. OpenAI and Anthropic are both key TPU customers, so their IPOs should also raise and sustain attention on TPU, and MediaTek and Broadcom are the suppliers the market most readily associates with it.

(2) MediaTek is clearly the biggest TPU winner of the next few years. Its position as sole design supplier from v9 onward, together with a supply share that rises each year alongside TPU shipments, will expand its TPU revenue. The high-margin 8t series, with shipment visibility through 2029, is a key profit source.

(3) Because Broadcom leads the 8i design, its gross margin is even higher than the 8t’s, supporting Broadcom’s profit growth. Note, however, that Broadcom’s focus over the next few years will be non-TPU XPU and AI networking chip orders, with non-TPU revenue expected to surpass TPU revenue as early as 2027.

🚨 64,000 BITCOIN MINERS HIJACKED IN MASSIVE ATTACK

An estimated 64,000 Bitcoin miners representing 13 EH/s of hashrate were reportedly hijacked overnight, with their mining power redirected to OCEAN mining pool and payouts assigned to an attacker-controlled Bitcoin address.

The attack reportedly began around 8 PM CT on November 14.

OCEAN’s dashboard shows a sharp spike in hashrate, briefly approaching 50 EH/s before falling back toward 40 EH/s.

CoreX Hosting first raised the alarm, reporting that miners were being redirected without authorization.

One affected operator says their entire mining farm was hijacked and identified Luxor’s Commander mining management software as the source of the compromise.

Other operators reported similar unauthorized pool changes several days earlier, potentially pointing to a broader incident.

CoreX later reported that the attack appeared to be over, with the hijacked hashrate falling from 13 EH/s to approximately 100 PH/s.

The attackers reportedly failed to mine a Bitcoin block during the hijack, meaning no block rewards were collected.

However, affected miners permanently lost the opportunity to earn Bitcoin during the attack. That hashing time cannot be recovered.

The full scope of the breach and whether Luxor Commander was compromised have yet to be independently confirmed.

text:
Anthony, the "spy" story appears to be as fake as Russiagate. Here are the facts as I understand them.

(1) First, Alice Huang was at a company called Megaspeed[1], which everyone agrees bought Nvidia chips to sell to Southeast Asian companies called neoclouds. This is in itself completely legal under US law.

(2) However, some both inside and outside the admin didn't like this. They want to block Chinese nationals from accessing cloud services with Nvidia GPUs even if those servers are located outside China. Fine, but the so-called Remote Access Security Act (RASA) to block this has passed the House but not the Senate, and is not law[2].

(3) Singapore's government also looked into this when Alice Huang was on their soil[3] and didn't find any evidence that Megaspeed was actually selling chips to China illegally — let alone that she was a "Chinese spy." They did give her an entry ban, but that's like a visa denial.

(4) The related point is that it's not actually illegal to sell Nvidia chips to China! Since the Biden admin, there has been a complex and constantly-shifting set of export restrictions on chips. As of right now, Nvidia is allowed to sell H200s[4] to China, and indeed has designed these to comply with applicable law.

(5) But you know what...China actually also doesn't want Nvidia chips in China [5,6], because they want to build up their homegrown chip industry. The Nvidia chips are so good that China doesn't want to remain dependent on American chips, or vulnerable to possible US backdoors.

(6) The broader point is that this is an argument between nationalists and capitalists. Nationalists argue that US companies shouldn't even get close to selling to China, and shouldn't even be selling to neoclouds, even if it's "technically" legal. Capitalists argue that it's impossible for American companies to dominate world markets without, you know, being allowed to dominate world markets by actually competing in them. And that it's one thing to restrict physical sales to China, and quite another to require proof-of-citizenship for every single cloud access.

(7) Here's the thing: it doesn't make sense for one of the (few!) industries where America has a trade surplus with China to be summarily cut off, if you're worried about trade surpluses. It doesn't make sense to remove your number one AI CEO, if you want to be number one in AI. And it truly doesn't make sense to do to Jensen Huang what the communists did to Jack Ma[7], if your goal is fighting communism.

(8) So, to summarize: there's no proof of spying, as Blanche at DOJ has admitted[8], which rebuts your FBI/DOJ points. The Wachtell investigation you raise is just an in-house thing[9] ordered by the Nvidia board. And so all that's left is some affairs, which society has agreed is not disqualifying, given the realities of both Clinton and Trump.

In short: do you want a communist society like China, where Jack Ma's company can be stolen from him overnight on false pretenses? Or do you want some semblance of rule of law? If so, you should support the restoration of Jensen Huang to the company he built.

Citations follow in the next tweet.

Google TPU update: New OpenAI and Anthropic orders extend shipment visibility to 2029; v10 lineup overhauled (now Quillfish); MediaTek and Broadcom lead as the top suppliers to watch

Key takeaways from my latest industry survey and research conclusions:

1. Order visibility and shipment plans:
Strong new orders from OpenAI and Anthropic have extended Google TPU shipment visibility to 2029, ahead of Nvidia GPUs and other AI ASICs (mostly 4Q27–2Q28).

(1) From 2028, v9 will become the mainstay of Google’s own compute buildout, so v8-series orders (8t / 8i or their design variants) can be viewed as coming from OpenAI and Anthropic.

(2) Combined 2028–2029 demand: about 12M units for OpenAI (8t, designed by MediaTek) and about 14M for Anthropic (8i, designed by Broadcom), with both growing year over year. OpenAI buys outright, while Anthropic uses a mix of leasing and outright purchases.

(3) Given supply chain constraints, more reasonable TPU shipment estimates for 2027–2029 are 8–9M, 14–15M, and 16–18M units, respectively. The market broadly expects AI capex to peak in 2028, yet this plan shows TPU shipments still growing in 2029, driven by direct orders from AI service leaders OpenAI and Anthropic.

2. v10 lineup and supply chain changes:
v10 has changed from Icefish and Merope / Bladerunner to Quillfish, with mass production expected in 2029. MediaTek has won the design service order.

(1) Icefish is now v11, with mass production expected in 2030 and the design service order also going to MediaTek. Merope has lower visibility: no supplier has been chosen, and it may be canceled.

(2) MediaTek will be the sole supplier for v9 (Humufish & Triggerfish) and v10 (Quillfish), accounting for about 45–50%, 50–55%, and 55–60% of total TPU supply in 2027–2029, respectively. TPU’s contribution to its revenue and profit should rise each year.

(3) From v9 onward, all new TPUs use Intel’s EMIB-T advanced packaging. Given limited initial production capacity, the v8 series should remain the bulk of TPU shipments through 2029. v8 is expected to be the main source of TPU profit growth for MediaTek and Broadcom over the next few years, thanks to significant accumulated learning-curve benefits and the fact that both handle procurement of key components and materials.

3. Market attention and supplier outlook:
Recent events should raise and sustain market attention on Google TPU, with key design service providers MediaTek and Broadcom likely to be the supply chain’s top focus.

(1) Uncertainty over Nvidia’s CEO succession helps Google in discussing post-2028 long-term plans with customers. OpenAI and Anthropic are both key TPU customers, so their IPOs should also raise and sustain attention on TPU, and MediaTek and Broadcom are the suppliers the market most readily associates with it.

(2) MediaTek is clearly the biggest TPU winner of the next few years. Its position as sole design supplier from v9 onward, together with a supply share that rises each year alongside TPU shipments, will expand its TPU revenue. The high-margin 8t series, with shipment visibility through 2029, is a key profit source.

(3) Because Broadcom leads the 8i design, its gross margin is even higher than the 8t’s, supporting Broadcom’s profit growth. Note, however, that Broadcom’s focus over the next few years will be non-TPU XPU and AI networking chip orders, with non-TPU revenue expected to surpass TPU revenue as early as 2027.

text:
Google TPU 重點更新：OpenAI 與 Anthropic 新訂單推升出貨能見度至 2029 年、v10 產品線大幅調整 (改為 Quillfish)、聯發科與 Broadcom 為供應商中之領先關注焦點

我最新的產業調查與研究結論：

1. 訂單能見度與出貨規劃：
受惠於 OpenAI 與 Anthropic 強勁新訂單，Google TPU 出貨能見度已達 2029 年，優於 Nvidia GPU 與其他 AI ASIC（多數為 4Q27–2Q28）。

(1) 自 2028 年起，v9 將成 Google 自建算力的主力方案，v8 系列（8t／8i 或其設計變種）訂單可視為來自 OpenAI 與 Anthropic。

(2) 2028–2029 年合計需求數量：OpenAI 約 12M（聯發科設計的 8t），Anthropic 約 14M（Broadcom 設計的 8i），兩者需求均呈逐年成長趨勢。OpenAI 採買斷，Anthropic 則是租賃與買斷都有。

(3) 考量供應鏈限制，2027–2029 年較合理的 TPU 出貨估算分別為 8–9M、14–15M、16–18M。市場普遍預期 AI 資本支出於 2028 年見頂，但此規劃顯示 TPU 在 2029 年仍具出貨成長動能，關鍵在於 AI 服務龍頭 OpenAI 與 Anthropic 的直接訂單。

2. v10 產品線與供應鏈調整：
v10 由原先的 Icefish 與 Merope／Bladerunner 改為 Quillfish，預計 2029 年量產，設計服務訂單由聯發科取得。

(1) Icefish 改為 v11，預計 2030 年量產，設計服務訂單同由聯發科取得。Merope 能見度較低，供應商未定，也可能取消。

(2) 聯發科將是 v9（Humufish & Triggerfish）與 v10（Quillfish）的獨家供應商，2027–2029 年占整體 TPU 供應比重分別約 45–50%、50–55%、55–60%。TPU 對其營收與利潤的貢獻預計逐年增加。

(3) 自 v9 起新款 TPU 均採 Intel EMIB-T 先進封裝。考量初期量產能力，預期至 2029 年仍以 v8 系列為 TPU 出貨主力。v8 預期將是聯發科與 Broadcom 未來數年的 TPU 事業獲利成長的主要來源，因長期累積的學習曲線效益明顯，加上雙方負責關鍵零組件與材料採購。

3/ 市場關注度與供應商展望：
近期事件有助提升並維持 Google TPU 的市場關注度，關鍵設計服務商聯發科與 Broadcom 可望成為供應鏈首要焦點。

(1) Nvidia CEO 接班的不確定性，有利 Google 與客戶洽談 2028 年後的長期規劃。OpenAI 與 Anthropic 均為 TPU 關鍵客戶，其 IPO 也有助提升並維持 TPU 關注度，而聯發科與 Broadcom 是市場最容易聯想到的供應商。

(2) 聯發科無疑是未來數年 TPU 的最大贏家，身為 v9 後的獨家設計供應商，加上供應比重與 TPU 出貨成長同時逐年提升，均有利 TPU 事業營收規模擴大。高毛利率的 8t 系列出貨能見度達 2029 年，為關鍵利潤來源。

(3) 因 Broadcom 主導 8i 設計，故毛利率更高於 8t，有利該公司利潤成長。不過，需注意的是，Broadcom 未來數年的營運重點為非 TPU 的 XPU 與 AI 網路晶片訂單，預計最快 2027 年，非 TPU 營收將超越 TPU。

I have been investing in the crypto industry for more than a decade.

Here is what you need to remember in moments like this:

1. There is always a reason the price is going up or down, even if you don’t know what the reason is right now.

2. You are never as smart as you feel in bull markets and you are never as dumb as you feel in bear markets.

3. Bitcoin’s price can always go lower before it recovers.

4. Dollar cost averaging over time is a much better strategy for most people than trying to trade volatile moves.

5. Buying bitcoin when the Fear & Greed Index is under 20 has historically been attractive.

6. Bitcoin is not the same asset it used to be. Things like interest rates, AI stocks, etc are part of the game now.

7. You shouldn’t put all of your money in a single asset, including bitcoin, regardless of how bullish you are.

8. You can’t eat your bitcoin or sleep in it, so make sure you keep money for the “real world” needs.

9. People who don’t obsess over the bitcoin price every day are more likely to hold long-term.

10. The government will never stop printing money, which is bitcoin’s strongest long-term argument in my opinion.

11. The media loves to claim bitcoin is dying. They have done it hundreds of times and they have been wrong every time.

12. The critics get the loudest when bitcoin’s price falls. The louder they screech, the more attractive bitcoin probably is.

13. Bitcoin’s hash rate is an important metric to pay attention to and it has been increasing the network security recently.

14. As AI abundance becomes more pervasive in society, bitcoin’s scarcity will likely become more valuable.

15. The best psychological hack I ever discovered is to promise myself that I was going to give any bitcoin to my grandchildren. This way I am never tempted to make emotional decisions.

16. Modern bitcoin volatility is small compared to what early bitcoiners went through.

17. While it can be hard on day’s like today, try to have fun and remember that weathering negative volatility is the price of capturing the upside return in the long-run. 

I hope this helps a few people. Let me know what I missed.

text:
From an NVIDIA employee: 

“To the Board,

I have worked at NVIDIA for nearly 18 years, and I feel compelled to share something personal during this extraordinarily difficult moment.

I am not writing to comment on the circumstances or to presume anything about the process the Board must undertake. I simply hope you will consider the perspective of someone who has had the privilege of working closely with Jensen for almost two decades—and who has seen firsthand the kind of leader and human being he has been to so many employees.

I first worked with Jensen in 2009 after I joined the company, when we went through 37 versions of GeForce posters for Chinese retail, and later through countless gaming events and the early China and Asia GTCs. He could challenge me quite publicly at times, but I always valued his candor, his teaching, and especially the conversations we had after those events.

One conversation in particular has stayed with me for nearly 17 years.

It was during a post-management QBR dinner in Hong Kong early 2010, I asked Jensen about something I had heard from an older employee: that during the difficult layoffs of 2008, he had personally called engineers who were being laid off and later reached out to many of them individually.

He told me a story about an elderly man he once met in a small grocery shop in Hong Kong. The man had worked there his entire life. Jensen asked him why he had never looked for another job. The man answered, “Because my boss took care of me in the rainy days.”

Jensen told me that sentence stayed with him. When he told me the story his glasses were covered by mists from his wet eyes. He promised himself that he would never forget the people who had entrusted their lives and careers to him. No matter how much pressure he faced, employees were family, and he wanted to be the person who would take care of them in the rainy days.

He kept that promise.

Through COVID, the Russia-Ukraine war, and countless other uncertain moments, I repeatedly heard him reassure employees, in one form or another: “I got you.”

Throughout the years, he has also put in countless personal efforts to make us feel at home. He created the quarterly “Global Free Days” and launched policies to support employees building their families via IVF and adoption, with the program fully funded by the company. From sending a soft blue blanket to congratulate me on my son’s birth, to visiting a member of my team in the hospital during Computex, he did everything he could to ensure we always felt cared for and supported, no matter the circumstances.

Many of us privately called him “Daddy Huang”—not as a joke, but with genuine affection, gratitude and admiration.

That was Jensen’s magic.

He didn’t just build technology. He created policies that changed people’s lives, and a company culture that made us so passionate about NVIDIA.

Stand behind Jensen Huang is a family, thousands of employees whose lives he has touched, and generations of people who have benefited from his leadership and his humanity.

I am only one employee, and I do not pretend that my voice can change the outcome of anything. But after nearly 18 years here, I could not remain silent without sharing what I have personally witnessed.

Please remember the extraordinary amount of humanity, kindness and opportunity that Jensen and his family have seeded around the world.

Please remember the people whose lives he has changed—not just through NVIDIA’s technology, but through his personal decisions, his empathy, and the culture he created.

And please remember that many of us are incredibly proud of him.

Whatever difficult decisions lie ahead, I hope the Board will approach them with both the rigor required of its fiduciary responsibility and the humanity deserved by a person who has spent so much of his life taking care of others in their rainy days.

With deepest respect,

A grateful NVIDIA employee of nearly 18 years”
