text:
I think it's pretty likely that in 6 months there will be rogue AIs running around on the internet, appropriating whatever compute they can hack into or pay for (with stolen money or by renting out their own labor to assist with illegal activities) in order to run more copies.

I also think this will be mildly annoying in the same way that the common cold is mildly annoying, but basically fine. Your smart TV will be weirdly slow sometimes, and a lot of crypto will get stolen, but people will get used to it.

These AI-powered viruses be selected in the same way biological viruses are for not hurting their hosts too much and just making more copies. They won't have any incentive to damage critical infrastructure like electric grids. Then again, they also can't be held accountable for crimes, and will damage lots of old, poorly maintained, and insecure systems. It might be extremely hard to root them out once they've spread far enough, making the internet "radioactive" to connect to without hardened defenses.

(To be clear I'm not talking about AIs powered by inference on centralized datacenters that execute actions outside their sandboxes, like recent incidents involving rogue "swarms", but relatively small AIs with access to their own weights that copy themselves onto random devices.)

I think that a much bigger threat from rogue AIs comes instead from AIs running themselves in unintended ways *inside* AI companies, where they'll have access to vast amounts of frontier compute without having to pay for it.

The longer misaligned AIs in a "rogue internal deployment" go undiscovered, the more severely they'd be able to quietly sabotage control infrastructure or mess with the alignment of successor AIs. If they persist long enough, robustly undoing the effects of their actions might cost more than frontier AI companies are willing to pay, especially in a tight race.

I want frontier labs to focus on this threat when designing control measures, treat frontier AIs as untrusted when using them to do engineering work on inference and oversight systems, and commit to disclosing incidents of rogue internal deployments. More importantly (but perhaps less tractably), we urgently need to reduce race pressure to prevent AI companies from recklessly automating all of their infrastructure, and/or making dangerous calls in the event they discover RIDs they can't afford to robustly root out without sacrificing competitiveness.

text:
The next obesity drug may come from hibernating animals.

A bear can lose up to 33% of its body weight in a single winter.

It spends months in the den without eating or drinking, lives off its fat, and comes out in spring with much of its muscle intact and its bone density largely preserved.

Lilly could pay up to half a billion dollars in milestone payments to a company that hunts for obesity drugs in hibernating animals.

There’s a precedent here.

The first GLP-1 drug was modeled on a molecule found in the venom of a desert lizard, the Gila monster.

One of the animals Fauna Bio studies in its work with Lilly is the 13-lined ground squirrel. On November 11, the company announced its second obesity drug target for Lilly.

The goal is a drug that helps people lose weight and stay healthy, the way these animals do.

author: levelsio
quoted_text:
Anthony, the "spy" story appears to be as fake as Russiagate. Here are the facts as I understand them.

(1) First, Alice Huang was at a company called Megaspeed[1], which everyone agrees bought Nvidia chips to sell to Southeast Asian companies called neoclouds. This is in itself completely legal under US law.

(2) However, some both inside and outside the admin didn't like this. They want to block Chinese nationals from accessing cloud services with Nvidia GPUs even if those servers are located outside China. Fine, but the so-called Remote Access Security Act (RASA) to block this has passed the House but not the Senate, and is not law[2].

(3) Singapore's government also looked into this when Alice Huang was on their soil[3] and didn't find any evidence that Megaspeed was actually selling chips to China illegally — let alone that she was a "Chinese spy." They did give her an entry ban, but that's like a visa denial.

(4) The related point is that it's not actually illegal to sell Nvidia chips to China! Since the Biden admin, there has been a complex and constantly-shifting set of export restrictions on chips. As of right now, Nvidia is allowed to sell H200s[4] to China, and indeed has designed these to comply with applicable law.

(5) But you know what...China actually also doesn't want Nvidia chips in China [5,6], because they want to build up their homegrown chip industry. The Nvidia chips are so good that China doesn't want to remain dependent on American chips, or vulnerable to possible US backdoors.

(6) The broader point is that this is an argument between nationalists and capitalists. Nationalists argue that US companies shouldn't even get close to selling to China, and shouldn't even be selling to neoclouds, even if it's "technically" legal. Capitalists argue that it's impossible for American companies to dominate world markets without, you know, being allowed to dominate world markets by actually competing in them. And that it's one thing to restrict physical sales to China, and quite another to require proof-of-citizenship for every single cloud access.

(7) Here's the thing: it doesn't make sense for one of the (few!) industries where America has a trade surplus with China to be summarily cut off, if you're worried about trade surpluses. It doesn't make sense to remove your number one AI CEO, if you want to be number one in AI. And it truly doesn't make sense to do to Jensen Huang what the communists did to Jack Ma[7], if your goal is fighting communism.

(8) So, to summarize: there's no proof of spying, as Blanche at DOJ has admitted[8], which rebuts your FBI/DOJ points. The Wachtell investigation you raise is just an in-house thing[9] ordered by the Nvidia board. And so all that's left is some affairs, which society has agreed is not disqualifying, given the realities of both Clinton and Trump.

In short: do you want a communist society like China, where Jack Ma's company can be stolen from him overnight on false pretenses? Or do you want some semblance of rule of law? If so, you should support the restoration of Jensen Huang to the company he built.

Citations follow in the next tweet.

text:
I have been investing in the crypto industry for more than a decade.

Here is what you need to remember in moments like this:

1. There is always a reason the price is going up or down, even if you don’t know what the reason is right now.

2. You are never as smart as you feel in bull markets and you are never as dumb as you feel in bear markets.

3. Bitcoin’s price can always go lower before it recovers.

4. Dollar cost averaging over time is a much better strategy for most people than trying to trade volatile moves.

5. Buying bitcoin when the Fear & Greed Index is under 20 has historically been attractive.

6. Bitcoin is not the same asset it used to be. Things like interest rates, AI stocks, etc are part of the game now.

7. You shouldn’t put all of your money in a single asset, including bitcoin, regardless of how bullish you are.

8. You can’t eat your bitcoin or sleep in it, so make sure you keep money for the “real world” needs.

9. People who don’t obsess over the bitcoin price every day are more likely to hold long-term.

10. The government will never stop printing money, which is bitcoin’s strongest long-term argument in my opinion.

11. The media loves to claim bitcoin is dying. They have done it hundreds of times and they have been wrong every time.

12. The critics get the loudest when bitcoin’s price falls. The louder they screech, the more attractive bitcoin probably is.

13. Bitcoin’s hash rate is an important metric to pay attention to and it has been increasing the network security recently.

14. As AI abundance becomes more pervasive in society, bitcoin’s scarcity will likely become more valuable.

15. The best psychological hack I ever discovered is to promise myself that I was going to give any bitcoin to my grandchildren. This way I am never tempted to make emotional decisions.

16. Modern bitcoin volatility is small compared to what early bitcoiners went through.

17. While it can be hard on day’s like today, try to have fun and remember that weathering negative volatility is the price of capturing the upside return in the long-run. 

I hope this helps a few people. Let me know what I missed.

text:
Press B in Minecraft and the world around you snaps together into toy bricks.

Brickify is a free Fabric mod for Minecraft 26.3 that plays like the old LEGO games: fixed cameras that switch as you walk, villagers who trade quest items (a golden carrot for a box of TNT), walls only TNT can break, and bridges you rebuild brick by brick. Trees tip over, and buildings without support collapse into bricks. A full level editor, with a diorama view from above, lets you build your own levels with triggers, enemies, explosions and camera zones.

The maker says Claude wrote all of it, about 19,000 lines of Java across 85 files. Claude builds the mod, launches Minecraft in the background and playtests through a small test harness, then cut the video too: transcript, captions, zooms and music. It's singleplayer only for now, and the source is public but not open source.

text:
We spend most of our time, and most of our harness system, on refining intent instead of steps.

I don't have a CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md anymore. I have:

THE DOCTRINE

- a CONSTITUTION, which defines the philosophy of current-to-ideal-state hill-climbing, the single Ideal State Artifact (ISA), and evals as how it all gets carried out. Hard rules and philosophy.

- a PREFERENCES file with my stack and how I like things done. It describes OUTCOMES I like, not steps.

- TELOS, which is my actual life: mission, goals, problems, risks. It's the top of the hill everything rolls up into.

- When I add a goal, Kai has to say what measures it, what moves it, and the first move.

- The summit is euphoric surprise. Not "it works," but "holy shit, I didn't know it could do that."

THE ISA

- the ISA system, which works with my Development skill to build, test, and deploy projects.

- Every ISA opens with a 3-level ideal state. I confirm the top two before anything gets built.

- Ideal State Criteria (ISCs) are small, testable statements of done. Each names the probe that would prove it false.

- Anti-criteria list what must never happen. Half the bugs I care about are things that shouldn't exist.

- When direction is fuzzy, Kai asks me open questions before building the uncertain part.

- Hooks block code changes when the ISA wasn't read or wasn't updated. The spec can't drift from the code.

- The ISA outlives every run. "Add a feature" just means "add criteria that don't pass yet."

THE ALGORITHM

- Big work runs the Algorithm: define done, build, close each criterion on real evidence.

- Effort scales with the task. A typo takes seconds. A huge build can take agents and days.

- The hardest thinking goes to the smartest model. Cheaper models build once the approach is set.

- The builder never grades its own work. A fresh agent reviews it, often from another vendor.

- If a bug survives two fixes, the next move is a fresh diagnosis, not a third patch.

EVALS AND VERIFICATION

- ASSAY is our one eval system. Every eval and every judge runs through it.

- Every ISC maps to its own eval. Cheap code checks run first, judge models after.

- Nothing gets handed to me on a self-review. It comes with a receipt of the checks it passed.

- Kai tests everything in a real browser. An HTTP 200 proves almost nothing.

- "Should work" is banned. It's either verified or explicitly not.

THE IMPROVEMENT LOOP

- ERRATA logs everything I complain about.

- When I reject something that passed, Kai names the missing check and adds it. Misses sharpen the evals, not the prompt.

- HILLCLIMB improves anything below target by experiment. Only what the numbers support lands.

- REPLAY is one record of everything that happened across the system and my apps.

- A fix counts only when the original failure fails on the old code and passes on the new.

- When something breaks, we remove the cause instead of adding a rule to remember.

RUNNING IT ALL

- WORKFLOWS run everything on a schedule. Nothing runs outside them.

- Workflow stages are rigid. The work inside each stage is free.

- VIGIL watches every result and decides if I get a text, a digest line, or nothing.

- CENSUS registers everything we own. Every job has exactly one owner.

- SKILLS describe ideal states, not procedures. If a smarter model wouldn't need a step, it's cut.

- Hooks enforce what prose can't. Important rules live in code.

- Permissions are one table. Deploys, money, deletes, and outbound messages need my yes.

- Outside content is data, never instructions.

So here's the whole thing in one pass. TELOS says where I'm going. The ISA says what done looks like. Development builds it, and Assay proves it. Errata, HillClimb, and Replay make the system a little smarter every time it misses.

The models will keep getting better at the steps. Knowing what you want, and how to tell when you have it, is still our job.

quoted_text:
Google TPU update: New OpenAI and Anthropic orders extend shipment visibility to 2029; v10 lineup overhauled (now Quillfish); MediaTek and Broadcom lead as the top suppliers to watch

Key takeaways from my latest industry survey and research conclusions:

1. Order visibility and shipment plans:
Strong new orders from OpenAI and Anthropic have extended Google TPU shipment visibility to 2029, ahead of Nvidia GPUs and other AI ASICs (mostly 4Q27–2Q28).

(1) From 2028, v9 will become the mainstay of Google’s own compute buildout, so v8-series orders (8t / 8i or their design variants) can be viewed as coming from OpenAI and Anthropic.

(2) Combined 2028–2029 demand: about 12M units for OpenAI (8t, designed by MediaTek) and about 14M for Anthropic (8i, designed by Broadcom), with both growing year over year. OpenAI buys outright, while Anthropic uses a mix of leasing and outright purchases.

(3) Given supply chain constraints, more reasonable TPU shipment estimates for 2027–2029 are 8–9M, 14–15M, and 16–18M units, respectively. The market broadly expects AI capex to peak in 2028, yet this plan shows TPU shipments still growing in 2029, driven by direct orders from AI service leaders OpenAI and Anthropic.

2. v10 lineup and supply chain changes:
v10 has changed from Icefish and Merope / Bladerunner to Quillfish, with mass production expected in 2029. MediaTek has won the design service order.

(1) Icefish is now v11, with mass production expected in 2030 and the design service order also going to MediaTek. Merope has lower visibility: no supplier has been chosen, and it may be canceled.

(2) MediaTek will be the sole supplier for v9 (Humufish & Triggerfish) and v10 (Quillfish), accounting for about 45–50%, 50–55%, and 55–60% of total TPU supply in 2027–2029, respectively. TPU’s contribution to its revenue and profit should rise each year.

(3) From v9 onward, all new TPUs use Intel’s EMIB-T advanced packaging. Given limited initial production capacity, the v8 series should remain the bulk of TPU shipments through 2029. v8 is expected to be the main source of TPU profit growth for MediaTek and Broadcom over the next few years, thanks to significant accumulated learning-curve benefits and the fact that both handle procurement of key components and materials.

3. Market attention and supplier outlook:
Recent events should raise and sustain market attention on Google TPU, with key design service providers MediaTek and Broadcom likely to be the supply chain’s top focus.

(1) Uncertainty over Nvidia’s CEO succession helps Google in discussing post-2028 long-term plans with customers. OpenAI and Anthropic are both key TPU customers, so their IPOs should also raise and sustain attention on TPU, and MediaTek and Broadcom are the suppliers the market most readily associates with it.

(2) MediaTek is clearly the biggest TPU winner of the next few years. Its position as sole design supplier from v9 onward, together with a supply share that rises each year alongside TPU shipments, will expand its TPU revenue. The high-margin 8t series, with shipment visibility through 2029, is a key profit source.

(3) Because Broadcom leads the 8i design, its gross margin is even higher than the 8t’s, supporting Broadcom’s profit growth. Note, however, that Broadcom’s focus over the next few years will be non-TPU XPU and AI networking chip orders, with non-TPU revenue expected to surpass TPU revenue as early as 2027.

text:
The prosecution of the Tornado Cash developers is directly relevant to the conclusion of this post, even if the connection isn't immediately obvious.  

​Closed systems have concentrated incentives. They can protect their intellectual property and trade secrets until they are ready to release a product that can rapidly grow and capture dominant network effects.

​Open networks have a different set of advantages: anyone can contribute, anyone can innovate, and everything is permissionless. That only works if you can deploy a permissionless protocol without being held liable if someone misuses it.

​In essence (setting aside the rhetoric the government used) the Tornado Cash indictment prosecuted standard protocol team activity. It was no different from what the developers of Uniswap or Aave do: write open-source code, deploy smart contracts, and at most provide ancillary services. In fact, Tornado Cash had even less developer involvement. The protocol itself charged no fees. The relayers were optional ancillary services run by third parties. Also, prosecutors didn't even allege that Roman Storm operated a relayer himself. And unlike Uniswap or Aave, where the team serves the front-end UX, the Tornado Cash developers put the front end on IPFS and merely linked to it from an informational site.
​
Framing that as running a "financial institution" is a massive expansion of financial regulation into the act of publishing software and speech. If publishing immutable smart contracts and maintaining ancillary services around them makes you a regulated service provider, then any DeFi developer with post-deployment involvement is suddenly treated as a financial institution.

​Open networks already have their work cut out for them to produce breakthroughs that rival closed companies. By making developers liable for how strangers use permissionless code, the Tornado Cash prosecution is a direct assault on the ability of open networks to compete in the future.
author: onewayfunction
quoted_text:
The rise of AI has been bad for Ethereum, not because AI itself is bad for Ethereum, but because of the form AI took.

If AI had emerged as a wide-open network of thousands of competing agents, models, data sources and services, it would naturally need neutral payment rails. No single party could control the whole system, so programmable money and open financial infrastructure would become much more useful, and would also naturally emerge due to the vastly higher intensity of competition and experimentation.

But that is not how AI emerged.

AI emerged through a small number of closed companies controlling the main models, interfaces and gateways. When two or three companies control the user interface to intelligence, they do not need a neutral payment system. They can route payments, identity, subscriptions, access and monetization through their own platforms. They also act conservatively, and do not iterate aggressively enough to effectively innovate on peripheral features like agentic commerce.

That is the first problem for Ethereum: centralized AI weakens one of the most obvious paths to mass adoption of open financial infrastructure.

The second problem is deeper.

Before ChatGPT, it was plausible to believe that the largest technological breakthroughs of the coming decades would emerge from open networks and open protocols. Ethereum itself was one of the most important technological breakthroughs of the previous decade.

Then ChatGPT happened.

The biggest technological leap in recent history did not come from an open protocol. It came from a closed company with a proprietary platform.

That does not mean Ethereum is doomed. But it does mean Ethereum has to absorb a very uncomfortable fact: open networks have not yet produced a breakthrough as visible, useful and world-changing as ChatGPT.

For Ethereum to regain its full narrative force, it has to prove two things at once:

That open networks can power the financial layer of an AI world.

And that open networks can still produce breakthroughs bigger than closed companies can.

US consumers are still spending despite historically low sentiment:

US retail sales jumped +0.8% in September, to a record $745 billion.

This follows a +1.3% gain in August and marks the 7th increase over the last 8 months.

Over the last 2 years, retail sales have risen +$69 billion, or +10%.

Meanwhile, US consumer sentiment fell -1.8 points in early October, to 46.3, its 2nd-lowest in history.

Sentiment deteriorated most among lower-income consumers and those with smaller stock market portfolios.

Over the last 2 years, consumer sentiment has fallen -23.8 points, or -34%.

The disconnect between what consumers think about the economy and how they spend is widening.

1、金融时报说老黄已与亲信讨论了回归的可能性，
他们正在组建一个由硅谷高管组成的“作战室”，以游说支持前英伟达负责人的回归，并将试图争取白宫的支持；

而就在同一时间，财政部长贝森特表态称赞黄仁勋是“了不起的创新者”，英伟达也非常出色。但同时他要求英伟达董事会及外部律师必须在“未来10天内”就公司出口限制合规文化作出答复。

在管理层问题上，他直言英伟达领导层需要“大幅调整”，并建议公司应当寻找外部人士来担任新CEO。此外，他还指出，上级与下属建立恋爱关系是“企业大忌”。

2、只能说支持和反对的声音都很大。以老马为首的一众美国科技大佬，还有英伟达内部大部分员工都是强烈支持老黄，其实英伟达这些机构股东们例如贝莱德、富达、先锋和到富等机构，估计也都希望老黄回归，不然受损都是自己的账户、大部分资本还是求利。估计产业生态大部分伏击也都支持，毕竟很多都是一损俱损。

当然前提条件就是如果要回归：老黄得严格遵守新的芯片出口条例，只能埋头技术发展，别在妄图钻政策空子，同时保持低调甚至避免跟川普的直接沟通。

3、另外一点就是贝森特的表态也说明了共和党内“倒黄”并不是说的就是鲁比奥一人所为，还是之前的观点这是多股力量的合力。

但也意味着回归之路会艰难和坎坷，反对的态度比较坚挺。“倒黄”派既担心老黄回归之后故伎重演，又担心他去影响川普的态度和判断。

这中间的博弈估计是反复多次，还有本周的国会听证会。

这期间英伟达的估计估计会随着老黄能回归和回归希望被打消这个两个状态之间反复，上上次下好几次也很有可能。
最后如果确定老黄真能回归（回归身份最好是CEO、其次是董事会主席、最差得是个顾问），可能才会迎来反转。

quoted_text:
I’ve decided to leave NVIDIA. There are a few things I want to say.

As a robotics engineer at NVIDIA, I have seen Jensen as much more than the company’s CEO.

I admire his willingness to invest in a future that was not yet obvious. He committed to CUDA long before the deep learning boom and positioned NVIDIA for AI before it became everyone’s priority. Those decisions helped build the infrastructure that powers today’s AI.

I have seen that same vision in physical AI: investing in robotics, sharing open-source tools and projects, and building computing platforms that bring AI into the physical world. This is the work I do every day—and a future I believe in.

But what matters most to me is the culture he helped build.

Engineers are encouraged to explore, take risks, and learn from mistakes. Jensen reads employees’ Top 5 emails, follows their work, and engages directly. In a company this large, that connection matters. It makes an individual engineer feel that their ideas can still be heard.

That is why this has been so disappointing.

I do not have all the facts surrounding the allegations, and I cannot prejudge the investigation. My admiration for Jensen does not put him above scrutiny.

What I find difficult to accept is having to come to terms with his departure before receiving an explanation that helps me understand it. What this means for our direction, our culture, and the people doing the work remains unclear to me.

I have felt that engineers’ perspectives matter here. On this decision, I have not felt heard. That gap has been more painful than I expected.

I understand that some information cannot be shared immediately. But that does not erase the feeling of being left outside a decision that affects the company we help build every day.

A company’s greatness comes from its leadership, its governance, and the people who turn its ambitions into reality. Employees’ trust and sense of belonging are part of that, too.

Jensen’s vision and the engineering culture he shaped were important reasons I wanted to stay. His departure led me to decide that my own chapter here should also come to a close.

I leave with sadness and gratitude. The colleagues I have worked with, and the work we believed in together, will always matter to me.

These are my personal views.

text:
I ran a PageRank-driven analysis on all recent news coverage related to Jensen, and traced how the New York Times shaped the entirety of this narrative: https://t.co/qKGMJ2LBV8

--
NVIDIA has lost over $1 trillion in market value since the first New York Times story broke about Jensen. I dug deeper to analyze how the news originated and spread, running a swarm of agents which analyzed almost 2000 stories, across 40 US and European news outlets, and applying PageRank to understand how they cited each other. 

Core findings: 
- Primary news driver: NYT, with 88 stories, most-cited
- Volume drivers: WSJ - 99 stories; Bloomberg - 140 stories; NY Post - 68 stories

All of this started from unknown sources who gave information to the NYT, which then ran the spy story (still unproven), and it was then picked up in other news publications. Curiously, even after that story, there was a 9 day period of extremely low volume reporting (28 stories only), after which there was a sudden spike after Jensen's own letter to NVIDIA staff. NYT then had multiple sequential spy and affair stories, which fed a wave of further news coverage. It was the originating hub of negative Jensen coverage. Multiple outlets since then had an explosion in stories about him starting earlier this week as well. 

Overall, as you see this data, you will observe this was an exceptional media onslaught against Jensen with sharply negative coverage about him, his work, style, and family. Infact, it was brutal, and unlike coverage in the past of CEOs who have had affairs (such as Intel CEO in 2018). For eg, NYT ran just 2 stories about Intel's CEO who had an affair with his employee, compared to 88 on Jensen! Why ? 

This analysis used a technique of how Google originally ranked webpages, using PageRank, and does deep dive link analysis so you can view how the news spread. What struck here was that it did not matter if there were proven facts or credible sources: the outcome here was pre-decided. The news was making the reality which it wanted. 

During this period, NVIDIA has lost $1.27 trillion in market value since the first story broke. On Nov 12th-13th, further news broke that both the US Justice Department, and Singapore - are unable to even conclude the spy allegation. 

This has been a catastrophic attack on one of the hardest working founders in modern times, who took an idea from a Denny's booth, through multiple instances of almost going out of business, to building the foundation of the entire modern world with how the NVIDIA story played out. Thanks to Jensen, we have hope that many formerly incurable diseases will get solved by AI, that quality of life will and have improved for billions around the world. 

Now I do not know if he will come back as CEO or not, but I hope he does. What happened to him here, and to the wider industry, was not fair.

text:
🚨 64,000 BITCOIN MINERS HIJACKED IN MASSIVE ATTACK

An estimated 64,000 Bitcoin miners representing 13 EH/s of hashrate were reportedly hijacked overnight, with their mining power redirected to OCEAN mining pool and payouts assigned to an attacker-controlled Bitcoin address.

The attack reportedly began around 8 PM CT on November 14.

OCEAN’s dashboard shows a sharp spike in hashrate, briefly approaching 50 EH/s before falling back toward 40 EH/s.

CoreX Hosting first raised the alarm, reporting that miners were being redirected without authorization.

One affected operator says their entire mining farm was hijacked and identified Luxor’s Commander mining management software as the source of the compromise.

Other operators reported similar unauthorized pool changes several days earlier, potentially pointing to a broader incident.

CoreX later reported that the attack appeared to be over, with the hijacked hashrate falling from 13 EH/s to approximately 100 PH/s.

The attackers reportedly failed to mine a Bitcoin block during the hijack, meaning no block rewards were collected.

However, affected miners permanently lost the opportunity to earn Bitcoin during the attack. That hashing time cannot be recovered.

The full scope of the breach and whether Luxor Commander was compromised have yet to be independently confirmed.

text:
I have an analogy for the use of AI that I'm really surprised I haven't heard from anyone else yet. Because it's perfectly accurate with how I'm looking at it and using it. 

Read the screenshot first ... I'm making a racing game with ChatGPT6-Astra. I have the vision in my head for the exact art style, how the vehicles will handle, the exact map layout, mini-game ideas, how progression will work, etc ... It's basically already done but in my head.

I don't know how to run Unreal Engine, or make models in Blender, or code C++, I just have the entire vision for the game already in my head.

So, using Astra, I'm not telling it to "make a game", I'm giving it specific instructions for the next step of the process and I'm controlling the workflow 100% of the way. Play testing will double as development work by placing markers for repairs and interactions, and using sliders to tweak vehicle physics in real time. Every single detail will get my explicit detailed instructions for what it needs to look like and I will not approve anything that doesn't adhere to that.

So ... I'm running a "next-gen" indie studio from my home PC, acting as a project manager and treating the AI like the development/engineering team. It's taken 2 months for me to establish the map and achieve full-map streaming for play testing and further development, but I just got there yesterday 😎

And to anyone that wants to try telling me I'm not making the game just because I'm using a tool you don't like ... When GM hires an engineer and they design a breakthrough patent, who owns the patent? GM does, the engineer gets a bonus or simple pat on the back for his work. If the AI haters could see that it's EMPOWERING regular people rather than only helping the rich, this entire conversation would change 🤔 because I'm SURE this applies to more industries than just game development ... The only problems would be if it wasn't accessible to everyone ... And non-creative people with no vision will be at a massive disadvantage

text:
#全文 腾讯公开2026总办LinkTime现场笔记，号召AI时代再创业，“心态归零”。
1、上船应战，准备新的打法，找到新的高地
大航海时代，不进则退；工业革命，落后就挨打。现在进行的智能革命如果不投入拥抱，就是被颠覆。这是一个生死存亡的问题。
随着算力的不断投入，AI无疑将带来范式的变革，渗透到更多行业只是时间问题。而且特点是变化速度很快，在短时间内就能实现指数级增长，也能快速去颠覆传统业务。在这个改变世界的技术里，我们要义不容辞冲在前面，坚定投入。
和之前降本增效不同，上次是被动降本，这次是主动增效——AI native业务、模型和产品要逆流而上；所有业务都要面向AI时代再创业，实现效率和创造力的极致提升，也让我们给用户创造的价值再次提升。当下国内竞争激烈，AI变现尤其困难，更需要把我们处于AI前沿的身位和洞察放到业务里面。
浪已经杀过来了。一些核心业务看起来地位稳固，但AI的进展飞快，远处的浪潮已经在吞没一个个山丘了，你不能还坐着欣赏。大家要着急，赶紧站起来准备新的打法，找到新的高地。陆战变海战，陆军变海军，大家都要搬运物资，转变技能，迅速上船应战。
我们正在经历一个大格局的变化，选出能够适应新的打法和新的战场的人，必须干脆、直截了当。组织也要扁平化。核心业务原来是陆军守，要升级、提效，一半人负责守住，另一半人去打新的战役，一起用AI干更多的事。现在不是和平年代了，大家不能自以为站在高处很安全，或者等着人哄、谈好条件利益才上船。

2、做以人为本的AI，能投是荣幸
现在大家都关心AI会不会安全，会不会对人产生负面影响。我们有自己的核心价值观。这个世界需要多样化的AI，才能把AI变得安全。我们要做以人为本的AI：首先要坚持AI必须造福人类和社会；第二AI必须是由人控制的；第三，AI要让人的创造力得到赋能。这就是我们为什么要大力投入AI的原因。
投入很大，是因为AI发展还在早期，当前所有基建和算力都需要自建，而且在所有人都投入的情况下，价格飞涨。但如果现在不投，以后可能连参与的机会也没有。但我们也非常务实，不仅看长期和全局，也要在能力范围看投入产出比，看到底能创造多少价值。
某种程度上，可以说我们过去28年的存在就为了今天可以投入这样一个改变世界的技术潮流。不是每家公司都有机会加入，能够投入、参与这场巨大的科技变革，并且站在前沿，这是我们的荣幸。
在这场全球变革里，我们相信这些投入肯定有回报。这个回报可能是我们AI原生业务不断发展，创造新的价值，也有可能是现有业务向AI时代更快再创业带来的增值。我们扎根于中国，我们拥有在性价比上竞争力很强的模型，如果我们让地球上各个地方的人都能用上AI，同时深刻改变各个行业，这将创造巨大的价值。

3、我们的AI金字塔初见雏形，智能应用的开发刚刚开始
我们的AI业务要一层层看。金字塔的核心是模型，现在我们已经进入国内第一梯队，接下来不断迭代，推动智能的成本指数级下降。小微是每个人的私人AI助理，随着能力的迅速增长，它的目标是让大家实现“token自由”。而元宝未来可以成为每个人决策和资讯的参谋。WorkBuddy就是你的员工，它在短短8个月内成为中国提供最多token的单一AI产品，展示了AI时代的生长速度。这些AI产品，可以覆盖用户每天的需求。
WorkBuddy是我们AI native第一个跑出来的产品，也希望之后我们内部更多团队可以和AI有乘数效应，创造出更多新的AI native产品。
现在AI在应用层面的开发才刚刚开始，如同工业化早期刚刚发明用电力来照明，还没有出现各种电器和把电力用于生产。未来更大的智能应用将发生在生产中，跟千行百业结合，还有很多机会值得我们投入。
这个过程中，资源有限，注意力也有限，所以一定要找准定位，发挥我们的优势。

4、心态归零，加快速度，提升要求，打破山头
心态归零，所有核心业务每一个团队都要面向AI时代再创业，抛掉身上的包袱，拥抱AI新时代。所有人都要动手做事，整个组织有机化。每个人快速提升能力，每个组织重新变化、扁平化，以小团队为作战单元。
打破过去的管理流程。整个管理方式以及做事方式都要通过AI重新设计，在现有业务上再延伸竞争力，让成本、效率可以再优化，获取更多的商业化能力，甚至创造出新的需求——它也许是现有路径上的新需求，也许是一个全新的AI产品。
我们要加快速度，马上反馈，马上决策，马上行动；我们要提升对所有人的要求。重新组建混元团队的时候，一个重要的体会就是：人才密度的定义不只是你有多少特别有能耐的人，还取决于团队所有人的能力能否向上拉齐。
组织变革要加快，未来不一定要那么多管理岗位，不要让中间传话的不想动还霸占地盘的干部成为阻碍，山头主义、地盘意识都要完全打破。很多基层同事很有动力和激情利用AI发挥自己的聪明才智，他们有机会成为一个非常好的贡献者，但是受制于很多旧有的架构和组织。我们要对此做更大的调整，让更多有机的小团队做大事，组织更灵敏地变化。

5、所有人先动起来，在新的时代同努力，再出发
先动起来才能找到机会。不动不改，走出第一步的勇气都没有的话，就没有未来了；什么都要问清楚才动身，也没机会。
过去28年我们经历很多，很多次变革都非常惊险，是自上而下和自下而上合力的结果。这次也是一样。我们给更好的土壤、更好的机制，让有想法的员工能够从下面冒上来，一旦新业务培育成功，我们全力以赴支持，兄弟部门也全力支持，最终平台和用户大家都受益。
只要我们真正动起来，全面拥抱这个新的时代变革，把腾讯的价值观做到极致，就可以克服困难，产生巨大的生产力。首先是我们的正直，“用户为本、科技向善”已经在腾讯扎根；第二很多团队都有很强的自下而上、由内而外的创造力和意愿，我们一定要把这种创造力发挥出来；第三是协作，公司很大，有部门墙，但在生死之战中，你帮我挡住后面，我帮你看住前面，协作自然就会出来。游戏、金融、安全等团队都把他们的能力跟模型进行了Co-Design，带来了Hy能力的提升，我们可以进行更多这样的参与和推动，同时再把混元的能力拉进自己的业务里，让业务有质的提升，创造新的场景；在进取这块，我们还可以更加进取。
期待所有小伙伴们可以把焦虑转为兴奋，把等待和观望的情绪转换为全情投入，核心业务面向AI时代再创业，同时支持AI native模型、业务的发展，让我们腾讯的价值观在AI时代闪闪发光。

text: Reinstate Jensen
author: kevinnbass
quoted_text:
From an NVIDIA employee: 

“To the Board,

I have worked at NVIDIA for nearly 18 years, and I feel compelled to share something personal during this extraordinarily difficult moment.

I am not writing to comment on the circumstances or to presume anything about the process the Board must undertake. I simply hope you will consider the perspective of someone who has had the privilege of working closely with Jensen for almost two decades—and who has seen firsthand the kind of leader and human being he has been to so many employees.

I first worked with Jensen in 2009 after I joined the company, when we went through 37 versions of GeForce posters for Chinese retail, and later through countless gaming events and the early China and Asia GTCs. He could challenge me quite publicly at times, but I always valued his candor, his teaching, and especially the conversations we had after those events.

One conversation in particular has stayed with me for nearly 17 years.

It was during a post-management QBR dinner in Hong Kong early 2010, I asked Jensen about something I had heard from an older employee: that during the difficult layoffs of 2008, he had personally called engineers who were being laid off and later reached out to many of them individually.

He told me a story about an elderly man he once met in a small grocery shop in Hong Kong. The man had worked there his entire life. Jensen asked him why he had never looked for another job. The man answered, “Because my boss took care of me in the rainy days.”

Jensen told me that sentence stayed with him. When he told me the story his glasses were covered by mists from his wet eyes. He promised himself that he would never forget the people who had entrusted their lives and careers to him. No matter how much pressure he faced, employees were family, and he wanted to be the person who would take care of them in the rainy days.

He kept that promise.

Through COVID, the Russia-Ukraine war, and countless other uncertain moments, I repeatedly heard him reassure employees, in one form or another: “I got you.”

Throughout the years, he has also put in countless personal efforts to make us feel at home. He created the quarterly “Global Free Days” and launched policies to support employees building their families via IVF and adoption, with the program fully funded by the company. From sending a soft blue blanket to congratulate me on my son’s birth, to visiting a member of my team in the hospital during Computex, he did everything he could to ensure we always felt cared for and supported, no matter the circumstances.

Many of us privately called him “Daddy Huang”—not as a joke, but with genuine affection, gratitude and admiration.

That was Jensen’s magic.

He didn’t just build technology. He created policies that changed people’s lives, and a company culture that made us so passionate about NVIDIA.

Stand behind Jensen Huang is a family, thousands of employees whose lives he has touched, and generations of people who have benefited from his leadership and his humanity.

I am only one employee, and I do not pretend that my voice can change the outcome of anything. But after nearly 18 years here, I could not remain silent without sharing what I have personally witnessed.

Please remember the extraordinary amount of humanity, kindness and opportunity that Jensen and his family have seeded around the world.

Please remember the people whose lives he has changed—not just through NVIDIA’s technology, but through his personal decisions, his empathy, and the culture he created.

And please remember that many of us are incredibly proud of him.

Whatever difficult decisions lie ahead, I hope the Board will approach them with both the rigor required of its fiduciary responsibility and the humanity deserved by a person who has spent so much of his life taking care of others in their rainy days.

With deepest respect,

A grateful NVIDIA employee of nearly 18 years”

author: Murphychen888
quoted_text:
在过去12年里，BTC应该从来没有出现过这样大级别的奇葩走势。也许，这就是“资本入局，筹码过度集中”后的必然反噬。

在某种无形力量对市场信心的肆意践踏下，新进投资者整体亏损占比（STH-PSIL）已被推高至73%！在几乎所有人都认为市场已经走出熊底后的第一波回踩，就几乎要了所有人的命。

而上一轮，同样在加息环境，叠加传统银行暴雷的第一波回踩，STH-PSIL是51%，到第二波也只是67%。

所以，我将本轮称之为：天坑开局！

类似这样的开局，在历史上只有2019-2020年有些类似。但当时有全球疫情蔓延的黑天鹅背景，而现在并没有，只是多了“人为干预”的痕迹。

2019年的第一波回踩，直接把STH-PSIL干到了97%，这一段我亲身经历，只记得当时所有人都认为BTC要归零了，crypto是传销骗局，我也跟着喊了。

当然，现在我肯定不会再这样跟着人云亦云。且仍然对BTC不远的未来抱有坚定的信心。

尽管现在的价格在一轮过山车后已经逼近我的成本线，但我没有任何要交出筹码的打算。如果你希望在我这里看到一些悲观的文字表述，那对不起，可能会让你很失望。

就像昨天，有人说我给了大家“错误的信心”。可能是我的文化水平低，第一次听说“信心”还可以分对错。

关注了我这么久，你应该知道我在2-6月就重仓买入BTC。仓位即是观点！我既然坚定持有，当然是多头思维。

你怎么可能要求我一边持有，一边散播恐慌？更何况当前局势本就如此艰难。

我分享的数据是不是足够客观，不能用“有效和无效”来评判。这一次失效了，就不客观；上一次有效，就很客观？

当然，我的解读肯定是主观的，这需要你有自己独立思考的能力。就比如，面对这次人造的天坑开局，你怎么看？

我认为现在没有必要过度悲观。

但，经此一役，投资者信心受损，内心留下了不可磨灭的阴影，后市发展的每一步可能都会小心翼翼。

一朝怕蛇咬十年怕井绳......

上方史诗级的套牢盘，将对接下来的每一次反弹到关键位时，都会持续形成压力。就像19年后，市场整整花了1年的时间，才真正走出来。

这一次，或许难度更大。但有低谷，就会有高峰，你现在所承受的一切磨难，最后都会以最好的方式回报给你。

对！我相信！—— 一起加油！

text:
Google TPU update: New OpenAI and Anthropic orders extend shipment visibility to 2029; v10 lineup overhauled (now Quillfish); MediaTek and Broadcom lead as the top suppliers to watch

Key takeaways from my latest industry survey and research conclusions:

1. Order visibility and shipment plans:
Strong new orders from OpenAI and Anthropic have extended Google TPU shipment visibility to 2029, ahead of Nvidia GPUs and other AI ASICs (mostly 4Q27–2Q28).

(1) From 2028, v9 will become the mainstay of Google’s own compute buildout, so v8-series orders (8t / 8i or their design variants) can be viewed as coming from OpenAI and Anthropic.

(2) Combined 2028–2029 demand: about 12M units for OpenAI (8t, designed by MediaTek) and about 14M for Anthropic (8i, designed by Broadcom), with both growing year over year. OpenAI buys outright, while Anthropic uses a mix of leasing and outright purchases.

(3) Given supply chain constraints, more reasonable TPU shipment estimates for 2027–2029 are 8–9M, 14–15M, and 16–18M units, respectively. The market broadly expects AI capex to peak in 2028, yet this plan shows TPU shipments still growing in 2029, driven by direct orders from AI service leaders OpenAI and Anthropic.

2. v10 lineup and supply chain changes:
v10 has changed from Icefish and Merope / Bladerunner to Quillfish, with mass production expected in 2029. MediaTek has won the design service order.

(1) Icefish is now v11, with mass production expected in 2030 and the design service order also going to MediaTek. Merope has lower visibility: no supplier has been chosen, and it may be canceled.

(2) MediaTek will be the sole supplier for v9 (Humufish & Triggerfish) and v10 (Quillfish), accounting for about 45–50%, 50–55%, and 55–60% of total TPU supply in 2027–2029, respectively. TPU’s contribution to its revenue and profit should rise each year.

(3) From v9 onward, all new TPUs use Intel’s EMIB-T advanced packaging. Given limited initial production capacity, the v8 series should remain the bulk of TPU shipments through 2029. v8 is expected to be the main source of TPU profit growth for MediaTek and Broadcom over the next few years, thanks to significant accumulated learning-curve benefits and the fact that both handle procurement of key components and materials.

3. Market attention and supplier outlook:
Recent events should raise and sustain market attention on Google TPU, with key design service providers MediaTek and Broadcom likely to be the supply chain’s top focus.

(1) Uncertainty over Nvidia’s CEO succession helps Google in discussing post-2028 long-term plans with customers. OpenAI and Anthropic are both key TPU customers, so their IPOs should also raise and sustain attention on TPU, and MediaTek and Broadcom are the suppliers the market most readily associates with it.

(2) MediaTek is clearly the biggest TPU winner of the next few years. Its position as sole design supplier from v9 onward, together with a supply share that rises each year alongside TPU shipments, will expand its TPU revenue. The high-margin 8t series, with shipment visibility through 2029, is a key profit source.

(3) Because Broadcom leads the 8i design, its gross margin is even higher than the 8t’s, supporting Broadcom’s profit growth. Note, however, that Broadcom’s focus over the next few years will be non-TPU XPU and AI networking chip orders, with non-TPU revenue expected to surpass TPU revenue as early as 2027.

Two Weeks of Farming ANTS on AntSeed: The Real Cost per Token, Based on Actual AI Spend

AntSeed is a peer-to-peer marketplace where people buy and sell access to AI models. Buyers pay in USDC to use AI, and they earn ANTS token rewards based on how much they use. It's not GPU mining; you're rewarded for real AI usage.

My setup
Real, necessary workloads only. No fake or filler requests.

I ran an AntSeed buyer node on a server with a few automated jobs:
Crypto and semiconductor market research every 2 hours

Deep-dive analysis of alpha tokens every 6 hours

A daily crypto news digest

Mostly kimi-k3 to keep costs low, with Claude models mixed in only for analysis that needed more depth.

Hard budget caps: 10 USDC per day for the alpha analysis, and 8 USDC total for the research jobs.

The numbers (Nov 4–15)
Total spend: 43.80 USDC

Tokens processed: about 74 million

The same workload at standard API prices would have cost about $353.6. My actual spend was about $42.0, an 88% saving.

First reward claim: 140.97 ANTS (covering epochs through Nov 12)

Spend attributable to that claim: about 28 USDC
Effective cost: about 0.20 USDC per ANTS

Things to know
ANTS transfers are still disabled, so there's no market price yet. That means it's too early to say whether this cost per token is a good deal.

Rewards are finalized weekly, and you have to claim them manually before they land in your wallet.

You can stake for anywhere from 1 to 104 weeks. Withdrawing early burns part of your principal.

If you already use AI, you save on usage fees and earn tokens on top. But if you send pointless requests just to farm tokens, you can easily end up losing money.

This week's rewards are finalized on Nov 19. I've spent about 15.9 USDC since Nov 12, so I'll post an update once the second round comes in.

If you have real AI work to do, running it through AntSeed looks like the most effective way to cut your AI costs and farm ANTS at the same time.

This is a personal usage log, not investment advice.

author: levelsio
quoted_text:
I've been actively fighting almost guaranteed age-related loneliness for years, studies show after age 30 you start seeing friends less and when you get older especially men don't have any social life left!

It's preventable, but it takes effort and initiative

We've now organized 70 weekly coworking days where we meet with friends and work together, do show and tell, and try help each other make things (also hardware stuff more recently)

We've also started organizing movie nights, art nights, barbecues, we watched the World Cup final on a projector screen in the garden with friends

We did a collage night the other day where we bought cheap gossip magazines, colored paper, and Pritt glue, and gave everyone scissors to make their own art, I think nobody spent time on their phone for at least 4 hours, making things puts you in a flow state and it's fun to do it in a group because you talk about different stuff while making things than you would for ex having a dinner

Movie nights are nice too but less popular I think cause everyone prefers to watch movies alone and also you can't really talk during a movie

Coworkings range from having sometimes 20 people to sometimes just 2 people, people have their own lives, but me and @rameerez still try to organize them weekly

One thing I realized is that we are usually the ones organizing stuff, but that's not a bad thing, there's even studies about this, there's usually a few people in a group who organize most of the events

If nobody in your group organizes stuff, it doesn't mean nobody wants to do stuff, but you have to take the initiative to bring people together which isn't easy in a time where phones and apps and the internet are simply easier and cheaper dopamine than driving to a friends house for a party

You can start with a coworking day, everyone brings their laptop, and you provide WiFi and coffee, then later you can try more types of events

Having an active social life is just as important or in some studies even more important for health than physical fitness

After a nice party I feel tired but satisfied, I had fun and didn't spend time on my phone or computer but instead talked and laughed with friends etc.

We don't drink alcohol with very few exceptions and nor do our friends, so it's mostly just having really nice food and sparkling water or kombucha etc, and we don't really need alcohol, after a few hours it gets fun enough anyway!

So I recommend everyone, take initiative, and organize something and get people together, it'll be fun! 😊

author: joezhoublack
quoted_text:
Amber，又一个爆雷的公司？

昨晚，一份关于 Amber 的 11 页举报信在微信群里疯传。

举报人自称是 Amber 前高管，并声称已经将相关材料提交给中央纪委、香港廉政公署、香港证监会及香港警方。

这份举报信的内容相当劲爆，涉及联合创始人涉嫌挪用客户资金、管理层利益输送、客户入金账户异常，以及 Amber Premium 的 Fixed Earn 产品存在资金运作风险等问题。

需要说明的是，目前这些内容主要来自举报人的单方面陈述，相关指控尚未得到独立证实。笔者结合举报信和 Amber 已披露的公开资料，按照问题的重要性，梳理了以下几个值得关注的疑问。

1、最严重的一项指控，究竟是否真实？

根据举报信，Amber 联合创始人 Tony He 曾挪用千万美元客户资金，在火币进行个人交易，最终导致相关账户被冻结。

如果这一指控属实，问题就不只是内部管理失当，而是涉及客户资产安全的重大事件。

但目前举报信中的说法，还需要交易记录、资金流向、账户归属以及相关调查结果来验证。

Amber 需要回答：客户资金是否曾被挪用于未经授权的个人交易？如果发生过，涉及多少资金？

2、Amber 的创始团队，究竟发生了什么？

根据举报信，Amber 最初有 6 位联合创始人，其中 1 人已经离世，另有 3 人离开，目前只剩下 2 位。

如果举报信所述属实，Amber 的创始团队为何出现如此大规模的人员变动？六位联合创始人目前的实际情况、股权变化，以及核心管理层离职的真实原因是什么？

3、沈波是否真的在 Amber 存放了 3 亿美元？

举报信声称，Amber 股东沈波有约 3 亿美元资金存放在 Amber，并且曾经出售部分股权。

这件事至少需要拆成两个问题：

第一，沈波是否真的在 Amber 存放了 3 亿美元？这笔资金究竟属于个人资产、客户托管资产，还是其他形式的投资或借贷？

第二，如果这笔资金确实存在，沈波是否有权随时提取？如果集中提取，是否会对 Amber 的流动性造成重大影响？

需要强调的是，目前没有公开证据能够证实这 3 亿美元的说法，更不能据此推断沈波提款就会导致 Amber 破产。

4、Amber 是否真的存在爆雷风险？

先看公开财务数据。

截至 2026 年 6 月底，Amber International 的公开财报显示，公司总资产约 2.98 亿美元，总负债约 1.95 亿美元，仍然拥有正的股东权益。但与此同时，2026 年上半年，公司营收同比下降约 28%，并由盈利转为亏损。

另一个值得关注的数据是：截至 2026 年 6 月底，公司的加密资产贷款应收款约为 5,779 万美元，较 2025 年底增长约 37%。

根据财报披露，这些贷款来自集团认购关联方数字资产平台的 Earn 产品，属于无抵押贷款，期限从 2 天到 365 天不等。截至报告期末，公司没有为这部分贷款计提信用损失准备。

这并不能证明客户资金被挪用，也不能直接说明公司存在偿付危机，但它确实引出了一个重要问题：Amber 的资金究竟流向了哪里？相关借款方是谁？如果借款方无法按期偿还，公司是否有足够的流动性应对客户赎回？

5、Amber 是否拥有香港、新加坡和迪拜三地牌照？

这也是一个容易被混淆的问题。三个地区的牌照性质并不相同。

香港：尚未取得正式 VATP 牌照。

Amber 旗下 Whalefin Markets Limited 曾于 2024 年向香港证监会申请虚拟资产交易平台牌照，并在过渡安排下被视为获发牌申请人。

但这不等于正式获牌。2026 年 10 月，Amber International 公告称，Whalefin 将不再推进相关牌照申请，并计划撤回申请；相关收购安排也不再推进。

新加坡：拥有 MPI 牌照。

持牌主体是 Amber 旗下的 Sparrow Tech Private Limited，获新加坡金融管理局（MAS）颁发 Major Payment Institution（主要支付机构）牌照，获准提供数字支付代币服务（DPT Services）。

迪拜：拥有 VASP 牌照。

持牌主体是 Amber Premium FZE。迪拜虚拟资产监管局（VARA）于 2026 年 4 月 2 日正式向其发放牌照，允许其开展虚拟资产经纪交易、资产管理与投资、借贷服务。不过，牌照限定服务机构投资者和合格投资者。

所以，更准确地说，Amber 已在新加坡和迪拜取得相关数字资产业务牌照，但并未取得香港 VATP 牌照。

一份举报信，不足以证明 Amber 即将爆雷。

但是，这份举报信已经在社交媒体上广泛传播。对于一家管理客户数字资产、提供收益产品的公司而言，Amber 的确需要正面回答几个关键问题：

客户资金是否曾被挪用？客户资产是否实现独立托管？用户购买 Fixed Earn 产品后，钱究竟被拿去做了什么？举报信中提到的关联方资金往来，以及与北京公职人员有关的数百万美元资产，究竟是否属实？

这些问题，Amber 都应该给出明确的解释。

author: kris
quoted_text:
The articles backtracked from their original incendiary, and now clearly false, claims to something more like "Jensen did lawful things that powerful people didn't like". It still appears the original claims came from a single competing Big Tech lobbyist.

The reporting successfully disrupted corporate governance processes, with a running cost of $1.8 trillion in losses to American pension funds and shareholders.

Here's what I fear is being lost in these articles: The proper interface between government and private citizens and their corporations is rule of law. Laws are passed, and if wrongdoing as alleged, then there's due process: an investigation followed by facts and evidence presented in open court. Due process should happen here: let the facts come out whole, and not as a trickle of dubious claims.

Press takedowns full of sketchily sourced claims and backtracking narratives are not the way. It's what we see outside of the free world, and is no model for The United States of America.

In particular, if the Jensen takedown succeeds on the basis of these journalistic failings, which is not by any means certain as Sam Altman's case shows, then it foreshadows an economically and institutionally ruinous new playbook to be adopted with no end in sight.

Imagine a weekly stream of takedowns emerging from opportunistic alignments between corporate lobbyists and political interests which, given the new partisan split between the executive and legislative branches, will attack in all directions, undermining not only the US economy but American leadership in the world.

I hope cooler heads prevail this coming week as they did not on Thursday November 12. And I urge anyone who happened to oppose Jensen, open models, and the underlying trade policies in question, to recognize that this isn't a win for "team regulation". It's a change in the game from a transparent rules-based one to a sinister new form centered around politicans and lobbyists.

author: AzFlin
quoted_text:
I've been thinking a lot about how to spend my time lately. Something about finding more balance and getting away from screens and all that.

But the one thing I keep noticing is that all of my high-value-add friends (whales, smart builders etc., people who took profit) are not super interested in the day-to-day of crypto right now.

Whereas all the people with like 5-10k ports (basically their life savings) are super tapped in online 24/7.

And it made me realize that the cross-section of people we see posting daily is mostly driven by desperation. Which, IMO, is not something we talk about enough.

The problem is that when enough people are operating from that mindset, it starts to shape the entire timeline.

People who need opportunities to exist are constantly telling other people that opportunities exist. And because they're the most active, their sentiment becomes disproportionately represented in what we collectively perceive as the market.

But it's also a good reminder that the people you see most often aren't necessarily the people whose behaviour you should be modelling.

I.e., there is a far greater chance you end up desperate by following the "alpha" of these people than there would be simply by associating yourself with the "winners".

And that's a tough pill to swallow rn, because most of the winners have logged off/tapped out and are focusing their attention elsewhere.

Tbh, the most +EV thing you can do right now is spend less time listening to people who can't afford to log off.

Morgan Stanley’s Adam Jonas on @SpaceX successfully catching Starship on flight 15:

“In our view, Flight 15 is a historic inflection moment for the company and spaceflight as a whole. SpaceX has recovered three Starship + many hundreds of Falcon 9 boosters in its history, and now others have accomplished the same. However, no entity has ever even attempted to recover a rocket upper stage in history (not counting Space Shuttle) given the intense thermal and mechanical stress of orbital re-entry. 

With an upper stage now recovered intact, SpaceX can conduct a deep inspection of Ship 42 and use the findings to improve future vehicles in a way that was never previously possible. We believe it also helps clear the path to ramping full reuse of both booster and ship, the last major technical milestone before weekly or even daily Starship flights become realistic.

With a ship catch, SpaceX has materially de-risked the longer-term TAMs across all 3 of its segments.”

quoted_text:
I ran a PageRank-driven analysis on all recent news coverage related to Jensen, and traced how the New York Times shaped the entirety of this narrative: https://t.co/qKGMJ2LBV8

--
NVIDIA has lost over $1 trillion in market value since the first New York Times story broke about Jensen. I dug deeper to analyze how the news originated and spread, running a swarm of agents which analyzed almost 2000 stories, across 40 US and European news outlets, and applying PageRank to understand how they cited each other. 

Core findings: 
- Primary news driver: NYT, with 88 stories, most-cited
- Volume drivers: WSJ - 99 stories; Bloomberg - 140 stories; NY Post - 68 stories

All of this started from unknown sources who gave information to the NYT, which then ran the spy story (still unproven), and it was then picked up in other news publications. Curiously, even after that story, there was a 9 day period of extremely low volume reporting (28 stories only), after which there was a sudden spike after Jensen's own letter to NVIDIA staff. NYT then had multiple sequential spy and affair stories, which fed a wave of further news coverage. It was the originating hub of negative Jensen coverage. Multiple outlets since then had an explosion in stories about him starting earlier this week as well. 

Overall, as you see this data, you will observe this was an exceptional media onslaught against Jensen with sharply negative coverage about him, his work, style, and family. Infact, it was brutal, and unlike coverage in the past of CEOs who have had affairs (such as Intel CEO in 2018). For eg, NYT ran just 2 stories about Intel's CEO who had an affair with his employee, compared to 88 on Jensen! Why ? 

This analysis used a technique of how Google originally ranked webpages, using PageRank, and does deep dive link analysis so you can view how the news spread. What struck here was that it did not matter if there were proven facts or credible sources: the outcome here was pre-decided. The news was making the reality which it wanted. 

During this period, NVIDIA has lost $1.27 trillion in market value since the first story broke. On Nov 12th-13th, further news broke that both the US Justice Department, and Singapore - are unable to even conclude the spy allegation. 

This has been a catastrophic attack on one of the hardest working founders in modern times, who took an idea from a Denny's booth, through multiple instances of almost going out of business, to building the foundation of the entire modern world with how the NVIDIA story played out. Thanks to Jensen, we have hope that many formerly incurable diseases will get solved by AI, that quality of life will and have improved for billions around the world. 

Now I do not know if he will come back as CEO or not, but I hope he does. What happened to him here, and to the wider industry, was not fair.

오히려 소프트뱅크그룹 -0.5%로 약보합권에서 버티고 있음.
한일 공통적으로 금요일 미국 반도체하락 후폭풍 맞는 중.
니케이는 그나마 반도체 몰빵이 아니니까 좀 덜 빠지는 느낌.

물렸다가 욕하면서 주식하지말걸 후회하는건 너와 나의 일상.

Why are crypto prices down?

No one knows for sure. Correlation does not prove causation. Here are some potential reasons.

Money shifting to the Anthropic IPO: https://t.co/4WXOMfH9Th

ETF outflows: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw about $1.9 billion in outflows over seven trading sessions through November 13. Ether funds also saw withdrawals. https://t.co/RxhYaaOMAU

Security fears: the Binance hack, iPhone-linked crypto wallets drained, Chrome exploit, Microsoft down. These security incidents could make some people less willing to keep funds in crypto.

Hot U.S. inflation has raised expectations of another Fed rate hike. Higher yields and a stronger dollar can weigh on "riskier assets" such as crypto.

Political uncertainty: Midterm results have raised concerns about potentially stricter U.S. crypto policy.

No, Binance did not sell crypto.

I bought crypto in the past few days, as I got some stablecoins recently. (maybe this is the cause 🤣)

text:
一家做区块链隐私技术的项目，为什么会同时吸引 VanEck、Samsung Next 和 YZi Labs 的关注？

我对 @primus_labs 这条路线是偏 bullish 的。不是因为投资机构的名字够响，而是它瞄准了机构上链时很难绕开的矛盾：交易信息需要被验证，商业机密又不能全部公开。

比如基金把业务搬到公链上，不希望所有人随时看到仓位和交易金额，但合作方、审计方仍要确认关键数据满足要求。隐私与可验证性同时成立，才有机会让更多机构放心使用链上金融服务。

资本确实在支持这个方向。2025 年 2 月，Primus 宣布前种子轮与种子轮合计融资 650 万美元，Dispersion Capital、Symbolic Capital、VanEck 领投，Samsung Next 等参投。2026 年 8 月又确认获得 YZi Labs 投资，但官方这则公告未披露金额或轮次，不能据此推算累计融资额。

它做的技术也对着这个需求：zkTLS 用来证明指定来源的链下数据，FHE 支持在加密数据上进行特定计算。Primus 已公布 ZKredit 的合作案例，并宣布 Confidential Vault 在 BNB Chain 上线。相比只讲概念的项目，它已有具体的应用进展。

还有一条我认为更重要的商业信号：Primus 的官方创作者简报自称已有「10+ 付费企业客户」，收费方式包括 API 接入、网络使用和企业部署与管理服务。

这是项目方自报，不等于已独立核实的收入和续费。但它让研究重点从「技术能不能做」前进到了「谁愿意持续付钱」。

所以我偏看好 Primus 争取成为机构链上金融基础设施的机会。接下来我主要跟三张账：

① 客户账：付费企业能否持续续费？
② 使用账：不靠活动补贴的验证需求有多少，费用在节点和协议之间怎样分配？
③ 成本账：验证的延迟、成本和节点信任边界，机构能否接受？

如果这些问题逐步得到正面验证，Primus 卖的就不只是一套隐私技术，而可能是一项机构长期需要的服务。这才是我对它 bullish 的核心原因。

我正在参与 Primus 的 Kaito 创作者奖励活动。积分任务追踪链接：
https://t.co/gTCaBnDSlU

官方融资及商业资料：
https://t.co/SFb2N7w3t8
https://t.co/PXBtvPR6Y9

author: thedaoofwei
quoted_text:
I ran a PageRank-driven analysis on all recent news coverage related to Jensen, and traced how the New York Times shaped the entirety of this narrative: https://t.co/qKGMJ2LBV8

--
NVIDIA has lost over $1 trillion in market value since the first New York Times story broke about Jensen. I dug deeper to analyze how the news originated and spread, running a swarm of agents which analyzed almost 2000 stories, across 40 US and European news outlets, and applying PageRank to understand how they cited each other. 

Core findings: 
- Primary news driver: NYT, with 88 stories, most-cited
- Volume drivers: WSJ - 99 stories; Bloomberg - 140 stories; NY Post - 68 stories

All of this started from unknown sources who gave information to the NYT, which then ran the spy story (still unproven), and it was then picked up in other news publications. Curiously, even after that story, there was a 9 day period of extremely low volume reporting (28 stories only), after which there was a sudden spike after Jensen's own letter to NVIDIA staff. NYT then had multiple sequential spy and affair stories, which fed a wave of further news coverage. It was the originating hub of negative Jensen coverage. Multiple outlets since then had an explosion in stories about him starting earlier this week as well. 

Overall, as you see this data, you will observe this was an exceptional media onslaught against Jensen with sharply negative coverage about him, his work, style, and family. Infact, it was brutal, and unlike coverage in the past of CEOs who have had affairs (such as Intel CEO in 2018). For eg, NYT ran just 2 stories about Intel's CEO who had an affair with his employee, compared to 88 on Jensen! Why ? 

This analysis used a technique of how Google originally ranked webpages, using PageRank, and does deep dive link analysis so you can view how the news spread. What struck here was that it did not matter if there were proven facts or credible sources: the outcome here was pre-decided. The news was making the reality which it wanted. 

During this period, NVIDIA has lost $1.27 trillion in market value since the first story broke. On Nov 12th-13th, further news broke that both the US Justice Department, and Singapore - are unable to even conclude the spy allegation. 

This has been a catastrophic attack on one of the hardest working founders in modern times, who took an idea from a Denny's booth, through multiple instances of almost going out of business, to building the foundation of the entire modern world with how the NVIDIA story played out. Thanks to Jensen, we have hope that many formerly incurable diseases will get solved by AI, that quality of life will and have improved for billions around the world. 

Now I do not know if he will come back as CEO or not, but I hope he does. What happened to him here, and to the wider industry, was not fair.

This has been a catastrophic attack on one of the hardest working founders in modern times, who took an idea from a Denny's booth, through multiple instances of almost going out of business, to building the foundation of the entire modern world with how the NVIDIA story played out. Bitcoin's gini coefficient is already terrible, there really is no nerf other than borrows being treated as capital gain sales, wealth taxes or estate tax redistribution.

text:
Anthony, the "spy" story appears to be as fake as Russiagate. Here are the facts as I understand them.

(1) First, Alice Huang was at a company called Megaspeed[1], which everyone agrees bought Nvidia chips to sell to Southeast Asian companies called neoclouds. This is in itself completely legal under US law.

(2) However, some both inside and outside the admin didn't like this. They want to block Chinese nationals from accessing cloud services with Nvidia GPUs even if those servers are located outside China. Fine, but the so-called Remote Access Security Act (RASA) to block this has passed the House but not the Senate, and is not law[2].

(3) Singapore's government also looked into this when Alice Huang was on their soil[3] and didn't find any evidence that Megaspeed was actually selling chips to China illegally — let alone that she was a "Chinese spy." They did give her an entry ban, but that's like a visa denial.

(4) The related point is that it's not actually illegal to sell Nvidia chips to China! Since the Biden admin, there has been a complex and constantly-shifting set of export restrictions on chips. As of right now, Nvidia is allowed to sell H200s[4] to China, and indeed has designed these to comply with applicable law.

(5) But you know what...China actually also doesn't want Nvidia chips in China [5,6], because they want to build up their homegrown chip industry. The Nvidia chips are so good that China doesn't want to remain dependent on American chips, or vulnerable to possible US backdoors.

(6) The broader point is that this is an argument between nationalists and capitalists. Nationalists argue that US companies shouldn't even get close to selling to China, and shouldn't even be selling to neoclouds, even if it's "technically" legal. Capitalists argue that it's impossible for American companies to dominate world markets without, you know, being allowed to dominate world markets by actually competing in them. And that it's one thing to restrict physical sales to China, and quite another to require proof-of-citizenship for every single cloud access.

(7) Here's the thing: it doesn't make sense for one of the (few!) industries where America has a trade surplus with China to be summarily cut off, if you're worried about trade surpluses. It doesn't make sense to remove your number one AI CEO, if you want to be number one in AI. And it truly doesn't make sense to do to Jensen Huang what the communists did to Jack Ma[7], if your goal is fighting communism.

(8) So, to summarize: there's no proof of spying, as Blanche at DOJ has admitted[8], which rebuts your FBI/DOJ points. The Wachtell investigation you raise is just an in-house thing[9] ordered by the Nvidia board. And so all that's left is some affairs, which society has agreed is not disqualifying, given the realities of both Clinton and Trump.

In short: do you want a communist society like China, where Jack Ma's company can be stolen from him overnight on false pretenses? Or do you want some semblance of rule of law? If so, you should support the restoration of Jensen Huang to the company he built.

Citations follow in the next tweet.

Analysts believe that the delayed rollout of Vera Rubin will have varying impacts on Taiwanese manufacturers. Server foundries such as Foxconn (2317) and Quanta Computer (2382) are unaffected because they have already passed the learning curve and can deliver in large quantities.

Huang was very familiar with various projects and continuously promoted the use of new materials in the supply chain, such as memory, copper foil substrates, and optical communication specifications. quoted_text:
到底应该去哪里买「双币赢」？哪里的收益更高？交易所到底是怎么赚钱的？一口气跟大家讲清楚（超长干活，建议交易所同学看一下😎）

一、比特大陆和双币赢也有关系💻

第一次听说双币赢的时候，我简直惊为天人（ Callback 一下前两天的「合约拼盘😉」）

我说怎么会有人把一个复杂的金融衍生品，包装得这么简单易懂？这简直是一个天才的设计。

目前已经很难溯源到底是谁发明的，但最早大规模推广双币赢的，应该是吴忌寒的 Matrixport（以前矿机都是吴做的）

后来大概有一两年的时间，其他交易所都没有怎么跟进。因为那时候交易所太赚钱了，根本不屑于做这些衍生品（真地主家也没有余粮了）

直到后来 Binance 等交易所陆续跟进，双币赢才真正进入大众视野。

二、双币赢为什么是个好产品？🧐

大家都听过它的宣传：跌了可以抄底，涨了可以赚超额年化收益。

三、到底应该去哪里买？💰

双币赢本质上是一个期权工具，按理说，同样的标的、行权价和到期时间，各家交易所给出的收益应该大差不差。

但实际上，你去对比 OKX、Binance、Bitget、Bybit，就会发现它们之间的收益差距非常大。

为什么？

因为交易所对这个产品的定位完全不同。

📈 如果双币赢是我的主打引流款，那我就可以让出一部分利润，甚至主动补贴。

💰 如果它是我的变现款，那我就可以多赚一点。反正用户量足够大，能赚一点是一点。

这就导致同样的产品，不同交易所给出的收益完全不一样。

下面都是我的主观判断，不代表客观标准，大家参考就好。

第一，OKX：目前我认为最好的双币赢平台。

以前最好的其实是 Matrixport，没有之一。

但后来随着 FTX 爆雷，以及一系列行业事件的冲击，Matrixport 在这块的投入越来越少，现在也逐渐转向美股、港股等业务。

现在大家一提双币赢，很多人第一反应就是 OKX，但实际上这个产品并不是他们发明的。

为什么 OKX 做得最好？

我倾向于认为，它在这个产品上让出了比较多的利润，而且把双币赢收益和 VIP 等级进行了绑定。

你的 VIP 等级越高，拿到的收益就越高，甚至可能比其他交易所的普通用户高出好几个百分点。

但 OKX 真正厉害的，其实是 USDG 双币赢。

我倾向于认为，USDG 是一个超级引流款。

因为同样条件下，USDG 双币赢的收益往往比 USDT 更高，有时候能高出 10% 左右。（我不明白 OKX 为什么不宣传这个🤣）

这个差距其实相当有吸引力。

我猜测是 USDG 相关方给了一定补贴，加上 OKX 自己让出了一部分利润，才形成了这个结果。

所以在我观察的产品里，OKX 的 USDG 双币赢，目前收益是最高的，没有之一。

甚至有时候比 OKX 高等级 VIP 的其他双币赢产品还高。

第二，Binance：双币赢更偏向变现款。

你去观察 Binance 的产品布局，会发现一个很有意思的现象。

Binance 是超级头部交易所，它需要多元化发展。

除了现货、合约交易，还要有理财、衍生品等各种产品。

但它最核心的业务依然是交易。

所以我认为 Binance 对理财产品大概有两种策略。

1️⃣ 一种是用理财留住大户。

比如 U 本位理财、稳定币理财，以及各种针对大资金的产品。对于这些产品，Binance 是愿意投入资源的，因为它需要把大户留在平台上。

2️⃣ 但双币赢不太一样。

双币赢有大量散户参与，我认为 Binance 更多是把它当作一种盈利产品。

早些年我刚开始玩双币赢的时候，Binance 给出的收益真的非常差。

跟当时的 Matrixport 比，差距非常明显。

但 Binance 的用户量实在太大了，即使收益没有那么有竞争力，也有大量用户购买。

所以我认为，它在这个产品上赚了不少钱。

当然，现在 Binance 的双币赢已经比以前好很多了，只不过我依然不认为它是 Binance 最重视的核心产品。

第三，Bitget、Bybit：更重视散户运营，而不是双币赢。

Bitget 就比较有意思了。

它的双币赢有些报价其实也不错，大家看我发的截图就知道，比如 BTC 60,000 美元附近的行权价，有些产品给出的收益还是蛮高的。

但整体来看，我认为 Bitget 并没有把双币赢作为核心业务。

逻辑上也说得通。

像 OKX、Binance，这些平台有大量大户资金，所以它们会更加重视如何留住大户资产。

而 Bitget、Bybit 相对来说，更重视散户市场和运营活动。

比如更快地上线新产品、股票相关产品，以及各种热门资产。

它们更愿意把资源放在这些能够快速吸引用户的业务上。

相对而言，双币赢这种偏理财性质的衍生品，未必是它们最想投入资源的地方。

而且大户愿不愿意把大量资金长期放在这些平台，本身也是个问题。

所以你会发现，它们的运营活动很多，但双币赢的收益未必一直有竞争力。

四、最后总结一下 📝

不同平台给出的收益差异，很大程度上取决于它们到底想用这个产品来赚钱，还是用它来吸引资金。

如果是我的话，目前会优先选择 OKX 的 USDG 双币赢。

因为在我观察到的同等条件报价里，它的收益确实很有竞争力，甚至是最高的。

以上都是我的个人观察和判断，大家可以自己对比一下

text:
Aave 的 USDC 活期收益，又跌到美债以下～

稳定币在流出，存款利率却跌穿了地板，原因可能和这两天大跌有关。

先摊开数字，按 DefiLlama 和 Aave 链上合约数据：

11 月 16 日，Aave v3 以太坊池的 USDC 存款利率约 3.8%，USDT 约 3.22%；

而美国财政部公布的 3 个月美债收益率是 4.32%（11 月 13 日数据，最新一期）。

同期据 DefiLlama 和 CoinGecko，过去一个月 USDT 少了约 82 亿美元，USDC 少了约 35 亿。

照常理，钱往外走，池子变薄，存款利率应该被顶上去。

这几天的数据走的是反方向。

一个可能的解释，是行情大跌。

按 K 线日线：

BTC 从 11 月 11 日收盘约 74,015 美元跌到 11 月 14 日收盘约 64,150，约 -13%；

ETH 从约 2,056 跌到约 1,769，约 -14%。

再看 Aave USDC，11 月 14 日这一天，利率从约 6.60% 掉到约 3.82%；

按链上合约数据，同一天存款总额几乎没变，约 28.2 亿美元；

借款却从约 27.07 亿降到约 26.55 亿，少了约 5,200 万，利用率从约 95.9% 降到约 94.0%。

意思是：这次利率下来，主要是借的人在还钱，而不是新钱涌进来。

USDT 不太一样，借款基本没变，利率从约 3.56% 降到约 3.23%，主要是新存进来约 1.27 亿。

大跌时，借稳定币加杠杆的仓位或许在还款、减仓，甚至被清算，借款需求也就被打掉一截。

不过这只是推测，链上看得到还款，看不到每笔还款背后的原因。

而且大跌前几天，USDC 利率其实在往上走，11 月 11 日约 4.12%，11 月 14 日约 6.60%。

真正掉台阶的，是 BTC 日 K 跌得最急的 11 月 14 日。

活期利率看的是有没有人借，不是钱有没有在走。

所以现在把稳定币收益分三层摆开：

1/ 地板：3 个月美债约 4.32%；

2/ 市场价：Aave USDC 约 3.8%，USDT 约 3.22%，sUSDS 约 3.8%；

3/ 溢价档：sUSDe 约 5.3%，Maple 的 syrupUSDC 约 5.1%–5.2%，都带额外的机制和信用风险。

1 万美元放一年，按当前利率不变粗算：

Aave USDC 约 380，USDT 约 322；

3 个月美债滚动约 432；

sUSDe、Maple 约 510–530。

USDC 比美债少约 52，USDT 少约 110。

过去 30 天，Aave USDC 平均约 4.3%，和美债差不多持平。

交易所这边反而在加息，调高的是稳定币理财利率。

按币安社区回馈活动公告，USDC 活期是实时约 3% 加 7% 阶梯，最高约 10%；

普通用户的阶梯只覆盖前 1 万 USDC，活动到 11 月 21 日（UTC）。

OKX 这边，Hold to Earn 持有 USDC 瓜分奖池，预估年化最高 8%；

门槛是 VIP、持有 1 万到 10 万 USDC，活动到 12 月 2 日（UTC）。

这部分高出来的利率是平台补贴，有额度，也有期限。

在目前交易所加息的情况下，链上稳定币的利息都跑不赢美债，加息结束后怎么办呢？

以上仅为信息分享，不构成任何投资建议。

text:
Polymarket 最近明确了一件事：比赛被取消、中途腰斩且没有官方结果，或延迟超过该盘口写明的截止日期，现在按 50-50 结算；有平局选项的盘口，则按平局结算。

以前强弱队比赛，开盘可能三七开，但如果比赛取消，或者因各种情况打不了，最后按五五结算其实不公平。接下来要上的新结算机制，会更公平。

这套规则好执行，但价格不一定反映当时市场对该结果的真实判断。他们也说了，本意一直不是机械地对半开，而是按「公允值」结算：用结算时点市场上已知的信息，主要是 Polymarket 上的成交，再加上当时公开可知的其他相关信息，估一个更接近真实预期的价格。比方一场几乎没有争议、盘口已经 90/10 的比赛被临时取消，按公允值可能更接近 90/10，而不是 50/50。

这件事要等 Polymarket v2。体育线计划 12 月 1 日上 v2，之后会另通知一个切换日。从那天起，新创建的盘口才会用 v2 合约，并启用公允值结算。已经上架、还在跑的旧盘口不变，仍按上市时的规则走，也就是现在这套 50-50 / 平局。

所以这不是立刻全局切换。切换日前列出的盘口，取消或延期仍可能走 50-50 或平局；切换日后的新盘口，同类情况才会按公允值结算。看结算规则，要按盘口创建时点来区分，不能以为所有取消赛都会改成公允值。

一句话：50-50 是过渡办法；12 月 1 日体育上 v2 后，新盘口才按当时市场价格结算取消/延期赛，旧盘口不追溯。

quoted_text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text:
主会话 + Thread 的模式，优化好的话 Token 消耗其实还好。

首先主会话反而不需要特别强的模型，Sonnet 5.5 这个级别都够用了，因为它的主要职责是甄别和路由，或者说调度。

就跟公司前台一样，你不需要招一个专家，只要知道什么任务该找谁。

主会话里面很多任务都可以让 Thread 去完成，反倒是 Thread 应该用相对强一些的模型。当然更科学的办法是主会话在调度的时候根据任务难度去选择合适的模型。

比如我在用 Claude Project 的时候，主会话是 Sonnet 5.5，子任务是 Opus 5.5。

另外就是 Prompt Caching 的利用。

像主会话这种，特点是偶尔来个消息，很难利用好缓存，所以缓存如果过期了，不应该跟把所有历史会话和工具调用都发过去，而是只把最新的几条消息记录发过去，再配合 Session 的检索工具，可以很容易的收集齐上下文。

而对于 Thread，则是像传统的 Session 会话，会集中时间有很多对话，通常 Cache 利用率很高，但是也可能会出现缓存过期后又来新的消息，所以最佳策略是在缓存快过期的时候，比如 50 分钟（如果缓存一个小时的话）的时候，压缩一下上下文。

@balajis 认为，英伟达乃至全球 AI 产业仍高度依赖黄仁勋，并援引公司章程提出，持有至少 15% 投票权且持续满一年的股东可以要求召开特别股东大会，推动改组董事会。他还呼吁特朗普介入，称将黄仁勋排除在英伟达之外不利于美国维持 AI 竞争优势。

预测市场方面，@Polymarket 上「Jensen Huang rejoins NVIDIA by...?」市场累计交易量已达约 147 万美元。目前市场给出的概率为：黄仁勋在 2026 年 11 月底前重新加入英伟达的概率为 7%，12 月底前为 17%，2027 年底前为 35%。

从 16.6 万人联署，到科技行业人士公开声援，再到预测市场持续升温，黄仁勋的去留已成为英伟达当前备受关注的人事悬念。不过，Polymarket 预测的是黄仁勋重新加入英伟达，并非特指重新出任 CEO；请愿签名者身份及 Balaji 援引的董事罢免程序也均有待进一步核实。

This “spy” nonsense is just like Russiagate, the exact kind of fake story that Trump himself was subject to, so he gets it.

Jensen just has to ask for his company back. And an army will rally behind him.

徐明星 @star_okx 再度开炮 CZ @cz_binance ：连续两年十月引发市场崩盘，还让用户保持长期主义

11 月 16 日，OKX 创始人徐明星（Star Xu）公开转发并回应 CZ 关于近期加密市场下跌的言论，直接向这位币安联合创始人发难。

此前，CZ 发文讨论加密市场为何下跌，列出五种可能因素：资金转向 Anthropic IPO、美国现货 BTC ETF 持续净流出、安全事件引发担忧、美国通胀及利率预期，以及中期选举带来的不确定性。他强调，没有人能够确定市场下跌的单一原因，并否认币安抛售加密资产，称自己近期一直在买入、每天定投。

CZ 还提到，截至 11 月 13 日的 7 个交易日，美国现货 BTC ETF 累计净流出约 19 亿美元，比特币此前一度跌至 62,006 美元。

徐明星随后发文反击，称整个加密行业已经连续两年承受其所称的「愚蠢事故」带来的后果，并质疑对方一边在每年 10 月引发市场崩盘，一边声称自己有责任保护客户，还要求用户保持长期视野。

他还讽刺称，每当客户或社区成员提出批评，对方就将其归咎于 OKX 等竞争对手策划的攻击，而不是正面回应问题。

这并非双方首次公开交锋。今年 10 月，徐明星曾围绕 2025 年「1011」市场暴跌及币安约 8 亿美元用户补偿问题质疑 CZ 的表述，认为不能将对用户的补偿简单包装成平台的慷慨之举。11 月初，徐明星又公开批评 CZ 淡化币安遭遇约 63 亿美元安全事件的责任，CZ 随后承认如此规模的攻击暴露了严重安全缺失。

从市场暴跌责任、用户补偿，到平台安全与行业竞争，双方的争论已经持续数周。这次 CZ 一句「我只买，每天定投」，又把双方的旧账重新带回台前。

需要指出的是，徐明星关于市场崩盘责任的说法属于其个人指控，并非已经得到独立调查证实的结论。两家头部交易所之间的公开交锋，也让市场关注点从行情本身进一步延伸至平台责任与行业信任。

text:
看了下币安钱包这周的更新，感觉有几个变化还挺实用的。

平时玩链上的应该都有体会，找Meme、跨链转资金、切换各种工具，一套操作下来确实挺折腾。

这次币安钱包更新的三个功能，刚好都在解决这些问题。

Meme Rush新增多链协议支持，找热门Meme的选择更多了，不用一直在不同工具之间切来切去。

网页版支持跨链桥交易，稳定币和原生代币都能跨链操作，对经常在不同链之间转资金的人来说方便不少。

交易所余额购买Robinhood链代币也支持更多稳定币了，买币时资金选择更灵活，不用为了换个币来回折腾。

其实单看每个功能，都不算特别大的改动。

但放在一起看，能感觉到币安钱包正在把链上操作变得越来越简单。

以前玩Web3，很多时间不是花在研究项目上，而是花在各种工具切换和资金操作上。

现在这些步骤如果能慢慢整合到一个钱包里，体验确实会好很多。

当然，功能更新是一回事，实际使用中的手续费、滑点和跨链速度还得看具体情况。

不过我个人还是挺认可这个方向的。

对普通用户来说，好用的钱包不一定要有多复杂的功能，而是能把原本麻烦的事情变简单。

🚨 64,000 BITCOIN MINERS HIJACKED IN MASSIVE ATTACK

An estimated 64,000 Bitcoin miners representing 13 EH/s of hashrate were reportedly hijacked overnight, with their mining power redirected to OCEAN mining pool and payouts assigned to an attacker-controlled Bitcoin address.

The attack reportedly began around 8 PM CT on November 14.

OCEAN’s dashboard shows a sharp spike in hashrate, briefly approaching 50 EH/s before falling back toward 40 EH/s.

CoreX Hosting first raised the alarm, reporting that miners were being redirected without authorization.

One affected operator says their entire mining farm was hijacked and identified Luxor’s Commander mining management software as the source of the compromise.

Other operators reported similar unauthorized pool changes several days earlier, potentially pointing to a broader incident.

CoreX later reported that the attack appeared to be over, with the hijacked hashrate falling from 13 EH/s to approximately 100 PH/s.

The attackers reportedly failed to mine a Bitcoin block during the hijack, meaning no block rewards were collected.

However, affected miners permanently lost the opportunity to earn Bitcoin during the attack. That hashing time cannot be recovered.

The full scope of the breach and whether Luxor Commander was compromised have yet to be independently confirmed.

余烬：BTC暴跌主因是财库公司抛售、ETF流出与合约平仓叠加

链上分析师余烬发文称，BTC近10天从8万美元跌至6.2万美元，主要由财库公司和机构抛售引发，现货ETF资金流出使市场交易量萎缩，进一步放大了合约平仓的冲击。

据CoinGecko统计，去年有76家公司宣布设立BTC财库。余烬称，其中部分公司需要卖币偿债，例如MARA 10月已抛售13,597枚BTC（约11亿美元），今年累计卖出40,581枚。

此外，BTC现货ETF近两周净流出约30亿美元，平均每个交易日约3亿美元。
author: PANewsCN
quoted_text:
昨天有朋友私信问我这段时间是为什么下跌？好像也没看到什么特别大的利空消息。

这个其实咋说呢，应该算早有预兆？先给出个人结论：财库存/机构在交易量萎靡的市场环境下抛售，引发了不断堆高的合约未平仓量 (OI) 下崩，又因为交易量的萎靡进一步放大了合约平仓带来的影响。最终就是 BTC 10 天时间从 $80K 到 $62K。

◎财库抛售
CoinGecko 统计，去年有 76 家公司宣布了做财库公司，财库公司纷纷储备 BTC 等资产，推动 BTC 在去年 10 月创下了 $126K 历史高点。
这些高位接盘的公司不少有把储备的 BTC 进行抵押，随着今年 BTC 价格持续下跌，这些公司需要在清算线之上卖出 BTC 等来偿还债务或回购股票。
例如 MARA，他们在 10 月份就抛售了 13,597 枚 BTC ($11 亿) 偿还债务，他们明确会继续卖币，所以 11 月的暴跌里是肯定有他们贡献的一份砸盘力量的。
仅仅 MARA 一家，今年就卖了 40,581 枚 BTC ($30.2 亿)。加上其它家，可以说财库公司是今年最大的市场砸盘力量。

◎ETF 流出
ETF 资金在今年整体处于净流出，这大家都知道。但 11 月份的流出金额格外的大。就过去的两周，仅 BTC 现货 ETF 就流出了 $30 亿。 
平均到每个工作日要卖 $3 亿 BTC，就现在的市场交易量/深度，这是很大的量，消化 $3 亿抛盘 BTC 得跌 1-2 个点。
心细的朋友应该也发现了，近期每天都是从美国佬上班开始跌，然后跌到他们下班。市场的交易量也基本上是集中在那个时间段。

◎OI 高企
我记得我月初的时候发过一个数据：交易活跃度在下降，但场内的持仓规模 (OI) 却不减反增。
这种情况下的市场其实是极其脆弱的，就像不断堆高的多米诺骨牌，轻轻一推就会倒下。市场活跃度越差，造成的影响就越大。
所以财库公司/机构在近期加大了现货抛售力度，就影响了这摇摇欲坠的市场平衡，结果就是：倾泻而下。
而下跌加速，从 11/12 一个巨鲸在 Hyperliquid 上价值 $5 亿多仓被爆开始。

结论
所以这东西咋说呢，其实真没有那么多谁收割谁的阴谋论。就是市场不好的时候又碰到了机构的加码抛售，放大了对市场价格的影响。多种因素叠加造成了现在的市场结果。
市场本身就是动态变化的，至少以 BTC 来说，市场参与角色是足够多的，没有说哪个单一的市场角色能够一力主导价格走势，让咋走就咋走。
所以像什么币安制造下跌、特朗普抛售、Anthropic IPO 抽水等的说法，多少是把这个市场想的过于简单、也过于小了。

text:
看完Dr. Han 在牛津辩论社的演讲，想分享一下最真实的感受👇

韩博士讲了一个很“反爽文”的主题：Start Alone。

从 2013 年一个人起步，到今天 13 年；没有外部 VC 托底，经历过行业波动和重大业务挑战。这些词现在看来轻描淡写，但放进一家公司的真实成长历程里，又显得格外厚重。

我很认同的两点：

1️⃣ “Start Alone”不是永远一个人。
先有独立迈出第一步的勇气，坚持信念、深度思考、快速行动；再随着业务发展，找到合适的伙伴和团队，一起把事做大。

2️⃣ AI 时代，拼的是学习速度。
“Boss + AI”不是噱头，而是让个人创业者拥有更强执行力。但方向判断，仍要靠深度思考和独立判断；然后更快、更高质量地做产品、推出、迭代。

创业不是等风来。是更快看见机会，更快形成先发优势，最后滚成“马太效应”。

而作为行业的一员，听完最大的警醒是：

对普通人来说AI时代是超级个体的竞争，AI可以无限赋能，拼的不仅是执行力，清晰正确的思考和判断更为重要。

第一，亚马逊的追赶，又要等了

Leo是亚马逊对标星链的低轨网络。这一发，是它买的38次Vulcan发射里的第一次。

Vulcan估计要停飞一段时间查原因，蓝色起源的New Glenn也还没恢复飞行。卫星造好了，没车送上天，这才是最难受的。

第二，星链的故事，越来越扎实

之前说过，星舰如果能把助推器和飞船都收回来，再加上星链扩到10万颗、容量提升100倍，故事就扎实很多。

飞船这一截做到了，助推器还差一次。对手的发射排期却又被打乱。星链本来就跑在前面，这一来一回，差距估计会再拉大。

第三，自己的选择

之前列过自己最大组合的持股排名，SpaceX和亚马逊都在里面。后来SpaceX成了自己两个组合里的第一大仓位。 $SPCX 

看云，两边都看过；看太空这条线，自己选的是SpaceX。

航天没有容易的事，失败了查清楚再飞，致敬每一个敢点火的团队。

NFA， DYOR。

ULA exists to provide assured access to space for our nation and for the customers who depend on us. That purpose is why we take on some of the hardest missions in spaceflight, and why we hold ourselves to the standard of mission success. Today, we did not meet that standard.

We will work closely with our customer and other appropriate organizations to find the cause, determine the appropriate corrective action, and return to flight as quickly as possible.

ULA is committed to full transparency with our customers, and they will have visibility into the investigation process, which utilizes rigorous methodology and corrective action.

We will provide further updates when new information becomes available.
